## Not API drift — the federated identity cannot read the tailnet

The lane's token exchange succeeds; the token it gets back carries almost no read scope.

**Evidence.** Running the same `TestLiveContract` locally against `m7kni.io` with a full-read
OAuth token passes **all 18 ops**, including every one the lane reports as failing:

```
--- PASS: TestLiveContract (1.82s)
    --- PASS: TestLiveContract/listTailnetDevices (0.35s)
    --- PASS: TestLiveContract/listUsers (0.02s)
    --- PASS: TestLiveContract/getPolicyFile (0.09s)
    ... 18/18 PASS
```

So no consumed GET has drifted. The two ops that pass in CI — `listTailnetKeys` and
`getTailnetSettings` — are exactly the two whose scopes the identity still has; everything
else answers 403 `calling actor does not have enough permissions` or 404.

**Cause.** `TS_WIF_CLIENT_ID` / `TS_WIF_AUDIENCE` were rotated on **2026-08-08 10:02 UTC**.
The last green run was 2026-08-08 **07:33** — the last one on the old identity. Every run
since (08-09, 08-10) has failed. The replacement federated identity was created with far
narrower grants than the one it replaced.

**Fix (admin console, tailnet-side — not a repo change).** Grant the federated identity
behind `secrets.TS_WIF_CLIENT_ID` read scope — `all:read`, matching what the lane had before
the rotation — then re-run the lane with `workflow_dispatch`. A clean run auto-resolves this
issue.

**Repo-side change landed meanwhile** (`47382f7`): the lane now probes
`GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/devices?fields=all` with the minted token *before* running the
contract, and fails with the real cause. A missing-scope token no longer runs the contract
and no longer files a drift issue that says the API changed when it did not.

Leaving this open until the identity is granted read scope.

## Correction: nothing needs granting — the secrets point at the wrong credential

My previous comment said to grant the identity `all:read`. **That was wrong.** The correct
credential already has `all:read` and still exists; the repo secrets were simply overwritten to
point at a different one.

`GET /tailnet/-/keys?all=true` (federated credentials are `keyType: "federated"` entries there —
there is no `/workload-identity-*` endpoint) returns three:

| id | created | scopes | subject |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `…-kPoqG7uoM621CNTRL` — "tailscale2otel CI federated read" | 2026-07-28 10:41 | **`all:read`** | `repo:rknightion/tailscale2otel:ref:refs/heads/main` |
| `…-kM6aVCf4Js11CNTRL` — "github-actions openbao token broker issue 23" | 2026-08-08 08:58 | `auth_keys` (`tag:gha`) | `repo:rknightion*` |
| `…-koGwNyLrhD11CNTRL` — brewmdm broker | 2026-08-08 09:39 | `auth_keys` (`tag:gha`) | `repo:brewmdm*` |

The first was created at **10:41 on 2026-07-28**, matching this repo's secret `created_at` of
`10:41:22`/`10:41:23` exactly. On **2026-08-08 10:02** both secrets were rewritten — an hour
after the shared owner-level broker credential was created at 08:58. The lane has since been
authenticating as the **`auth_keys` broker identity**, which is why `listTailnetKeys` and
`getTailnetSettings` are the only two ops that pass: they are the only ones an auth-key scope
reaches.

**Do not widen the broker credential.** `repo:rknightion*` covers every repo in the account, so
giving it `all:read` would hand every rknightion workflow read of the whole tailnet. The fix is
to point this repo back at its own credential:

```sh
gh secret set TS_WIF_CLIENT_ID -R rknightion/tailscale2otel \
  --body 'TBkeySVEB121CNTRL-kPoqG7uoM621CNTRL'
gh secret set TS_WIF_AUDIENCE  -R rknightion/tailscale2otel \
  --body 'api.tailscale.com/TBkeySVEB121CNTRL-kPoqG7uoM621CNTRL'
gh workflow run live-contract.yml -R rknightion/tailscale2otel
```

Both values are identifiers, not credentials — possession grants nothing without a
GitHub-signed OIDC token whose `sub` matches the pinned subject.

A clean run auto-resolves this issue.
Lane `live-contract` is green again — closing automatically. See https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/actions/runs/31381798050.

## What

Migrate this repo's documentation to the inverted model. It stops carrying a full Zensical site and ships **content plus a manifest**; the m7kni.io hub generates the rest at build time.

Pilot for rknightion/m7kni-net-site#35. Infrastructure landed there in 72d1f09.

## Why

The previous approach copied a shared kit into all twelve repos. It drifted: the server-side SEO template `docs/overrides/main.html` now exists in two versions across the fleet (three repos serve the stale one), the shared stylesheet in nine, and all twelve configs differ despite ~180 identical boilerplate lines each.

## Changes

- [ ] Add `docs.toml` — identity, keywords, nav and assets, the things only this repo can know
- [ ] Delete `zensical.toml` — generated by the hub from `docs.toml` + the fleet base
- [ ] Delete `docs/overrides/main.html` and `docs/stylesheets/brand.css` — hub-owned, copied in at build time
- [ ] Rename `docs/stylesheets/extra.css` to `project.css` — this repo keeps only its own component styles, never branding
- [ ] Point `trigger-docs-sync.yml` at `docs.toml` instead of `zensical.toml`

## Acceptance

Built output must be byte-identical to the current hand-maintained build, ignoring the stylesheet rename. Verified before this issue was filed: every rendered page matched.

## Note

This repo can no longer build a standalone docs site — that is the accepted trade of the inverted model, decided on m7kni-net-site#35.
title: docs: migrate to the m7kni.io inverted docs model (content + manifest)

comments.body:
## Probe result: no node emits a sample yet

Probed all 39 lab-tailnet nodes for `tailscaled_serve_{inbound,outbound}_bytes_total`
(`http://<ip>:5252/metrics`, 2026-08-10):

| outcome | nodes |
| --- | --- |
| family declared, **zero samples** | arcane, forgejo, <host-2>, n8n, n8n-funnel, openbao, runners (all 1.102.x) |
| metrics endpoint up, family absent | <host-1> (1.98.10 — predates the metric) |
| no `:5252` endpoint | the other 31, including every k8s operator proxy |

The tailnet does host 11 Tailscale Services (`svc:alloy-*`, `svc:argocd`, `svc:envoy-gateway`,
`svc:grpc`, `svc:ingress-nginx`, `svc:istio-gateway`, `svc:robknight`) — but they are all
operator-managed and fronted by `ingress-proxies-0/1`, which run **1.98.9**. That predates the
metric *and* exposes no metrics endpoint, so the nodes carrying the actual Serve traffic are
precisely the ones that cannot report it.

That keeps the verdict at **parked**, now for a concrete reason rather than an assumed one: the
HELP text says "labeled by Tailscale Service name" but does not give the label **key**, and
there is no sample anywhere to read it from. Curating blind would pin a guessed key into a
catalog metric and a dashboard panel — the exact shape of a silently-empty panel.

Revisit when the operator proxies reach ≥1.102: one `curl` against an ingress proxy then gives
the key, and the curation is a two-line addition to `curatedCounters`. Note the raw series are
already forwarded verbatim by the node_metrics passthrough today, so nothing is being missed in
the meantime.

Evidence pinned into the baseline note in `ac187aa`.

body:
Rebooting the OPNsense box takes 10-15 minutes, and while it is down the whole LAN loses its route to Grafana Cloud - the exporter keeps running but nothing reaches the stack. Four rules here are exposed. Each one that fires creates an IRM alert group, and an IRM route posts to its MS Teams channel the instant the group is created; the `homelab` escalation chain's 15-minute wait step delays the personal page but not the channel post. So the fix has to be rule-side.

Measured on the 2026-08-01 17:09-17:25 reboot (boot at 17:15, ~7 min of downtime, i.e. a short one). `Exporter down`, `Config invalid`, `Collector scrape stale` and `Collector scrape failing` all went Pending on NoData. Only the reboot being short kept them out of Alerting.

Unlike `rknightion/opnsense2otel`, this repo has no `--stack` build step - `grafana-sync.yml` pushes the committed manifests as-is. That is fine here: these manifests already carry the deployment's IRM contract labels (`domain: observability`) in git, so the committed profile is already stack-specific and editing it directly is the intended path, not a generic-default change.

## Two different fixes, because the rules fail differently

**`for` 5m -> 10m** where NoData genuinely is the signal:

- `ts2o-exporter-down` (`noDataState: Alerting`) - no data IS the alert, so the pending window is the only lever
- `ts2o-config-invalid` (`noDataState: NoData`) - config validity is only knowable while the exporter is up, so its NoData is already redundant with exporter-down; the window is the simpler lever

**`noDataState: NoData` -> `Ok`, `for` left as authored**, on the two multi-window burn-rate rules:

- `ts2o-slo-availability-fast-burn` (`for: 2m`)
- `ts2o-slo-freshness-fast-burn` (`for: 5m`)

Their short pending windows are deliberate - the dual 5m/1h window requirement is what does the debouncing, as the availability rule's own description says ("Requiring BOTH windows is what stops a single restart from paging"). Raising `for` to 10m would blunt fast-burn detection to fix a problem fast-burn does not have. The reboot noise on these comes purely from NoData, and a genuinely dead exporter is already covered by `ts2o-exporter-down` - so NoData on a burn-rate query is duplicate noise with no signal of its own.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ts2o-exporter-down` and `ts2o-config-invalid` at `for: 10m0s`, `noDataState` unchanged
- [ ] `ts2o-slo-availability-fast-burn` and `ts2o-slo-freshness-fast-burn` at `noDataState: Ok`, `for` unchanged at 2m / 5m
- [ ] No other rule in `deploy/alerts/grafana-managed/` changes
- [ ] CI drift gate green
- [ ] Values verified live in the stack after grafana-sync runs

## Note

All four were patched live on 2026-08-01 as immediate relief, but the two SLO rules were patched the wrong way (`for` raised to 10m). Correcting those live is part of this issue.
title: Alert rules trip on a firewall reboot: floor 'for' at 10m, and drop NoData on the burn-rate rules

body:
Follow-up from #526, deliberately left out of scope there.

## The gap

`internal/catalog`'s coverage gate derives `visualized` from *"a panel **or template variable** in the
deploy/grafana dashboard family references this signal"*. A hidden presence sentinel is a template
variable, and its query is `label_values(<metric>, __name__)` — so **a signal referenced only by a
sentinel counts as visualized while appearing on no panel any operator can see.**

#526's acceptance bar was "all 310 catalog signals appear on ≥1 panel". The gate as written proves
something weaker.

## It is not theoretical

`tailscale.subnet_routes.advertised` was in exactly this state. Its only reference anywhere was
`sentinel("has_subnet", "tailscale_subnet_routes_advertised", ...)` in the old `tabs/fleet.py`. It
had **never** been on a panel, and the manifest recorded it as `visualized` throughout.

It only surfaced because #526 wave 3 merged away the row that sentinel gated, which deleted the
sentinel, which finally dropped the signal below the gate. Had that row survived, the signal would
still read as covered today. The failure mode is a signal that is invisible to operators and
invisible to the gate at the same time — and the gate is quieter about it the longer the sentinel
lives.

It now has a real panel ("Advertised subnet routes", on
`tailscale2otel-tailnet` > Fleet & Network > Devices > Connectivity & Routing), so the gate is
currently green and honest. This issue is about making it stay honest.

## Proposed fix

Split the derivation:

- **`visualized`** — referenced by a PANEL query. This is what the acceptance bar means.
- **`gates_a_row`** (or similar, derived, non-satisfying) — referenced only by a template variable.
  Worth recording rather than discarding: it is genuinely true, and it is how the dead-sentinel
  direction already works.

`TestEverySignalReachesAPanel` then keys on the narrower value.

## Expected fallout

Unknown until measured, and measuring it is the first task — there may be other signals sitting on
a sentinel reference alone. Any that turn up need a panel, not an exemption: #526 deleted
`raw_only`, `omitted` and the transitional `pending_panel` precisely so a coverage failure could not
be resolved by re-labelling, and there is deliberately no disposition left that means "does not need
a panel".

## Acceptance

- [ ] `visualized` is derived from panel queries only; template-variable references are recorded
      under a separate derived value
- [ ] `TestEverySignalReachesAPanel` keys on the narrower value
- [ ] The extractor distinguishes the two without a per-signal list (it already walks
      `spec.variables` separately from `spec.elements`)
- [ ] Every signal the change newly exposes has a panel — no new exemptions, no new dispositions
- [ ] `signal_dispositions.json` and `docs/signal-coverage.md` regenerated
- [ ] Full gate green: `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...`, `golangci-lint run`,
      `scripts/verify-modules.sh`
title: Coverage gate counts a template-variable query as "visualized"

body:
> Tracking issue for the dashboard re-architecture. This body IS the source of truth —
> the design was drafted in `docs/superpowers/specs/`, which is gitignored and therefore
> does not exist on any other clone. Everything needed to execute is below.

**Date:** 2026-07-31
**Status:** design approved, ready for implementation planning
**Scope:** `deploy/grafana/`, `internal/catalog/` gates, `docs/` regeneration

## Goal

Replace the single 437-panel `tailscale2otel-overview` dashboard with two world-class
dashboards — one for tailnet/product data, one for the exporter's own health — while
cutting the dashboard-level variable count from 82 to roughly 14 by moving variables to
the row or tab that consumes them, and hardening the coverage gate so no emitted signal
can go unpanelled.

## Verified facts (do not re-derive)

Established by real pushes and renders against the `m7kni` stack on 2026-07-31, every
probe deleted afterwards. These were verified rather than read off the schema because
this repo has been burned before by an offline gate agreeing with its own wrong
assumption (see the `execErrState: "Ok"` note in the root `CLAUDE.md`).

| claim | verdict | how |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TabsLayoutTabSpec.variables` persists | **yes** | push + read-back, name survived |
| `RowsLayoutRowSpec.variables` persists | **yes** | push + read-back |
| tab-scoped `AdhocVariable` incl. `baseFilters` persists | **yes** | push + read-back, `baseFilters` intact |
| tab-scoped `GroupByVariable` / `SwitchVariable` persist | **yes** | push + read-back |
| a **tab-scoped** hidden sentinel drives its rows' `conditionalRendering` | **yes, both directions** | rendered PNG: satisfied row present, unsatisfied row absent |
| four grouping levels render (domain→leaf→sub-tab→row→panel) | **yes** | rendered PNG, all four bars stacked |
| `AutoGridLayout` reflows responsively | **yes** | rendered PNG, 3 panels wrapped to 2 columns at 1400px |

Two traps found while establishing the above:

- **`v2alpha1` has no grouping-level `variables` at all.** Only `v2beta1` and `v2` carry
  `variables?: [...VariableKind]` on `RowsLayoutRowSpec`/`TabsLayoutTabSpec`. The
  generator's `dashboard.grafana.app/v2` apiVersion is therefore load-bearing — do not
  "simplify" it to an alpha version.
- **`AdhocVariableKind` puts `datasource` and a required `group` at the KIND level**, as
  siblings of `spec`, unlike `QueryVariable` which nests its datasource inside the query.
  Getting this wrong produces a 422 whose CUE disjunction error names
  `layout.kind` and never mentions the variable — the real cause is masked. Bisect from a
  known-valid fragment when a v2 push 422s.

Documentation says a maximum of three grouping levels. Four render correctly, so that
limit is enforced by the dashboard *editor*, not the renderer or the API. These artifacts
are generated and never hand-edited, so relying on the fourth level is acceptable — but
it is beyond documented support, so a Grafana upgrade could begin enforcing it. The
mitigation is that only three leaves use the fourth level, and collapsing them to
sibling leaves is a mechanical change if that ever happens.

## Decisions

All ten were put to Rob and answered on 2026-07-31. Recorded with reasons so they are not
re-litigated.

1. **Coverage bar — structural exemptions only.** Every one of the 310 catalog signals
   must appear on at least one panel. The `raw_only` and `omitted` dispositions are
   deleted outright. Only three exemption classes survive, and each is structural rather
   than a judgement call:
   - histogram/summary base names, which are only ever queried via `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count`;
   - templated event names with no literal selector (`tailscale.webhook.<type>`);
   - signals consumed **only** by a recording rule, where the rule's *output* metric is
     itself panelled. **This class matches zero signals today** — no signal is currently
     `recorded` without also being `visualized`. It is a forward-looking rule so the gate
     does not have to be reopened later; do not go looking for members of it.
2. **Product dashboard keeps a health strip.** A permanent 4-panel "is the exporter
   feeding this healthy?" strip on the Overview, plus a detail row that renders only when
   a degradation sentinel fires. Without it, a broken collector reads as a quiet tailnet.
3. **Device filters — hybrid.** `os_type` and `host_name` stay explicit dropdowns, scoped
   to the tabs that use them. `device_user`, `device_tag` and `posture_attr` fold into one
   tab-scoped `AdhocVariable` with `baseFilters` pinned to the device metric family.
4. **Both dashboards renamed.** `tailscale2otel-tailnet` and `tailscale2otel-health`.
   Honest names beat preserving links to `-overview`.
5. **Domains at level 1, leaves at level 2, sub-tabs only for oversized leaves.** A fourth
   level costs ~100px of stacked tab chrome, so it is spent only where a leaf exceeds ~35
   panels. `Tailnets` (3 panels) folds into the Overview rather than surviving as a tab.
6. **AutoGrid for uniform rows, fixed grid for bespoke.** Rows that are N same-size panels
   become `AutoGridLayout` and reflow; rows with deliberate asymmetry (a wide timeseries
   beside two stats) keep explicit `GridLayout`.
7. **Consolidate redundant panels, keep the coverage floor.** Merge near-duplicates and
   the many single-panel rows; never at the cost of a signal losing its last panel.
8. **Health dashboard organised by pipeline stage**, following where a failure actually
   occurs in *this* exporter, not opnsense's shape.
9. **Events & Logs is split and does not survive as a product tab.** ~34 of its 43 panels
   are exporter pipeline health and move to the health dashboard's Ingestion/Delivery
   domains; the ~9 genuine tailnet-event panels fold into the Overview and the relevant
   domain tabs.
10. **Key/identity overlap resolved by question, not by deletion.** Policy & Config owns
    the configuration view (what keys and OAuth apps exist, their scopes). Security &
    Audit owns the risk view (what is expiring, what is over-scoped). The same signal
    legitimately appears on both, answering different questions — which also serves the
    "ideally more than one panel" goal.

## The real size of the coverage gap

**42 of 310 signals currently reach no panel**, not the 35 implied by the `raw_only` +
`omitted` count. Measured breakdown — 27 self-obs, 15 operational:

| class | count | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw_only` | 33 | deliberately query-only today; all need a panel |
| `omitted` | 2 | `process.cpu.time`, `process.uptime` |
| **`alertable` only** | **7** | **on an alert rule but on no panel** |

The 7 alertable-only signals are the worst of the three classes and were missed by the
per-family inventory tests entirely: an operator can be **paged by something they cannot
then see on any dashboard**. They are `tailscale.device.attribute.expiry`,
`tailscale.geoip.database.build_time`, `tailscale.key.scope_class`,
`tailscale.key.tag_scope`, `tailscale.posture_integration.error`,
`tailscale2otel.tls.cert.not_after` and `tailscale2otel.tls.cert.reload.failures`. Every
one of these must land on a panel, and each should be reachable from the alert that fires
on it. None is covered by any of the three structural exemption classes.

## Target structure

### `tailscale2otel-tailnet` (product, ~285 panels pre-consolidation)

```
Overview                          (tailnet health, activity, capabilities, security
                                   scorecard, multi-tailnet summary, folded-in Tailnets
                                   panels, 4-panel exporter-health strip + degraded row)
Fleet & Network
  ├─ Devices          → Inventory & Hygiene | Posture & Security | Connectivity & Routing
  ├─ Flows
  └─ Node Metrics
Security & Policy
  ├─ Security & Audit → Audit Trail | Risk & ACL | Posture & Compliance | Identity & Keys
  ├─ Policy & Config  → Access & ACL | DNS & Settings | Identity & Credentials | Integrations
  └─ Kubernetes Audit
```

**Overview budget.** Overview absorbs the folded-in Tailnets panels, the health strip and
some Events panels, which would push it from 23 (after its 11 self-obs panels leave) to
~39 — over the ≤35 ceiling the rest of the dashboard obeys. Resolution: Overview takes the
4-panel health strip, the 3 Tailnets panels and only the **event-rate summary**; the log
explorer and the per-signal log panels (flow, posture) go to their owning domain tabs
instead. Target Overview ≤30 panels after consolidation.

**Node Metrics "Scraper health" (5 panels) is exporter health, not node health**, so its
detail moves to the health dashboard's Collection domain. Two summary tiles stay on the
product Node Metrics tab so a reader can tell "no node data" from "scraper broken" without
leaving. This was ambiguous in the first draft of this spec and is now settled.

Sub-tab groupings are derived from the existing row titles, not invented. `Devices`
splits 18 rows into Inventory & Hygiene (~28 panels: inventory, authorization & sharing,
trends, fleet hygiene, device health), Posture & Security (~12: security flags, posture,
key-expiry distribution) and Connectivity & Routing (~19: connectivity + detail, needs-relay,
DERP, exit nodes + inventory, subnet redundancy + routes). Seven of those rows currently
hold a single panel each and are prime consolidation targets.

### `tailscale2otel-health` (self-observability, ~152 panels pre-consolidation)

```
Overview        (golden signals, up, collector rollup, degradation summary)
Collection      (scrape/poll, API requests + retries + rate-limit wait, capability/scope preflight)
Ingestion       (object store, ingress WAL, receivers, stream, dedup, subrequest fan-out, freshness)
Delivery        (OTLP export, SIEM log shipping, PII filter, annotations)
Runtime         (Go runtime, GC, profiling upload, TLS cert reload)
Cost & Cardinality
```

This is where the **27 self-obs signals that currently reach no panel** get their homes —
profiling upload, TLS cert reload (including the two alertable-only cert signals),
processor queue, metrics-endpoint scrape, log truncation, annotation publish/drop.

## Variable architecture

Today: 82 dashboard-level variables, 16 visible and 66 hidden sentinels. Measured
breakdown of the 66:

- **3 gate a tab** (`has_k8s_audit`, `has_nodemetrics`, `has_multitailnet`) and must stay
  dashboard-level. A tab cannot gate itself on a variable scoped to itself — the variable
  only exists once the tab renders.
- **50 are used by rows in exactly one tab** → become tab-scoped.
- **9 span more than one tab.** Several stop spanning once the split separates product
  from health (`has_selfobs` and `has_multitailnet` both currently straddle it). Rule:
  a sentinel consumed by rows in ≥3 tabs on the same dashboard stays dashboard-level;
  ≤2 is duplicated at tab scope.
- **5 are dead** — `has_posture_int`, `pii_ext_ips`, `pii_host`, `pii_int_ips`,
  `pii_ts_ips` are declared and shipped in the artifact but referenced by no row or tab.
  `has_posture_int` is a near-duplicate of the live `has_posture_integration`. Delete
  them, and add a gate that fails on any declared-but-unconsumed sentinel so this cannot
  recur.

Visible controls drop from 16 to ~5 on the product dashboard: `ds_prometheus`, `ds_loki`,
`topn`, `tailnet`, `provider`. `ds_tempo` (5 references, Exporter Diagnostics only) and
`collector` (8 references, same) leave the product dashboard entirely and live on health.
`net_transport`/`traffic_type` scope to Flows; `log_event`/`log_filter` scope to the tabs
that read Loki.

**Unverified assumption to check during implementation:** whether two different tabs may
each declare a tab-scoped variable with the *same* name. The ≤2-tab duplication rule
depends on it. If Grafana rejects duplicate names, those variables stay dashboard-level
instead — a smaller reduction, not a broken design.

## Gating

The coverage gate lives in **Go**, extending `internal/catalog/dashboardrefs_test.go`,
because `internal/catalog` is the source of truth for what the exporter emits and the
test already parses the built dashboard JSON. It rides the existing `go test -race ./...`
run, so no new CI workflow is needed.

Required changes:

- `dashboardPath` becomes a **slice of both dashboard paths**. This mirrors the single
  most important lesson from opnsense-exporter: its `coverage()` is variadic over the
  dashboard *family* precisely because scoping it to one file makes splitting content
  structurally impossible — the moment a panel moves to the second dashboard its metric
  reads as missing on the first. Take the union.
- Add the **catalog → panel** direction (every signal reaches ≥1 panel), which does not
  currently exist as a global gate; today it is approximated by frozen per-family
  inventories in `deploy/grafana/gen/test_*.py`.
- Keep the existing **panel → catalog** direction (a panel querying a name the exporter
  cannot emit).
- Add the **dead-sentinel** direction (a declared sentinel no row or tab consumes).
- `signal_dispositions.json` derivation unions both dashboards. `raw_only` and `omitted`
  are removed from the disposition enum; the three structural exemption classes are
  expressed as explicit, individually-justified entries.

Accepted limitation, recorded so it is not re-derived: this is a substring/token match
over expressions. It proves a metric name appears in some query, not that an operator can
ever see the result — a panel on a row whose sentinel is never satisfied still counts.
That is deliberate. Evaluating conditional rendering needs a fixture of a hypothetical
tailnet, and the honest stronger check is the live-contract lane. The gate's claim is the
narrower "nothing was forgotten entirely", which is worth having at that strength. Do not
widen it with per-panel visibility heuristics.

The Python-side tests keep their role: unit consistency, CVD/palette, panel descriptions,
query budget, empty-state contract, fingerprints. The frozen per-family inventories in
`test_selfobs_coverage.py` become redundant once the global catalog→panel gate lands and
should be reduced to the assertions that check *placement* (which dashboard and tab a
family lands on) rather than mere presence.

## Generator architecture

`deploy/grafana/gen/build.py` currently hardcodes one dashboard. It grows a small spec
object per dashboard — uid, title, tags, description, output path, tab list — and builds
both in one invocation, so the coverage union is computed over both in a single process.
Follow opnsense's shape here; it already solved this.

Seams to freeze before any parallel work starts, since every tab module codes against them:

- the dashboard-spec object's fields;
- the tab-module signature, and how a module declares tab-scoped vs dashboard-level
  sentinels (today `builder.sentinel()` registers globally as a side effect — it needs a
  scope argument);
- `builder.autogrid_row()` alongside the existing `builder.row()`;
- the sub-tab helper for the fourth grouping level;
- the adhoc-filter helper, including the kind-level `group`/`datasource` placement trap;
- the cross-link helper (see below).

**The `--flat` and `--tab` preview flags need a `--dashboard` selector.** They exist so a
single tab can be snapshot-rendered in isolation, and both currently assume one dashboard.
Without the selector, `--tab "Collection"` is ambiguous the moment two dashboards have tabs.
`regen_dashboards()` in `scripts/regen-generated.sh` is likewise a single-artifact function
and must write both files, since `ci.yml`'s `dashboards-drift` job gates whatever that
script produces.

**Cross-links, currently absent.** `spec.links` is `[]` on today's artifact — there is no
cross-navigation at all. Each dashboard gets a link to the other, propagating time range
and shared variables, following the opnsense pattern:
`/d/<uid>?${__url_time_range}&${tailnet:queryparam}&${ds_prometheus:queryparam}` with
`placement: inControlsMenu`. The health dashboard's link is the one that matters most — it
is how an operator gets from "this panel is empty" to "is the exporter broken?".

One file, one owner. `build.py`, `builder.py` and `variables.py` are integration files
edited by a single wiring pass, never in parallel. The plan should decompose into waves:
(1) seams + gate rewrite, (2) health dashboard, (3) product dashboard tabs, (4) wiring +
consolidation pass + live verification. Waves 2 and 3 parallelise by tab module; wave 1
must land first and alone.

## Post-deploy cleanup

Renaming orphans the currently-deployed `tailscale2otel-overview`. `gcx resources push`
is additive, so it will keep evaluating until deleted by hand. Delete it once the new pair
is verified live, then run `python3 scripts/verify_deployment.py` (read-only; exit 0 in
sync, 1 drift, 2 unreachable) to confirm no orphans remain. Dashboard pushes and deletes
of resources the repo no longer ships are pre-authorized.

`deploy/alerts/grafana-managed/_folder.json` owns the `tailscale2otel` UID, so neither new
dashboard UID collides with it — the reason the old dashboard was `-overview` in the first
place.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Two committed artifacts, both `dashboard.grafana.app/v2`, both regenerated
      byte-identically by `scripts/regen-generated.sh dashboards`.
- [x] `ci.yml`'s `dashboards-drift` job covers both files.
- [x] All 310 catalog signals appear on ≥1 panel across the two dashboards; the only
      exemptions are the three structural classes, each with a written reason. This closes
      the measured gap of **42** signals, including the 7 alertable-only ones.
- [x] Each of the 7 formerly alertable-only signals is on a panel reachable from the alert
      that fires on it.
- [x] `raw_only` and `omitted` no longer exist as dispositions.
- [x] Dead sentinels deleted; a gate fails on any declared-but-unconsumed sentinel.
- [x] Product dashboard has ≤15 dashboard-level variables and ≤6 visible controls.
- [x] No leaf tab or sub-tab exceeds ~35 panels; Overview ≤30.
- [x] Both dashboards carry a cross-link to the other, propagating time range and shared
      variables.
- [x] `--flat`/`--tab` preview flags take a `--dashboard` selector; `regen_dashboards()`
      writes both artifacts.
- [x] Every panel keeps a description (existing `test_panel_descriptions.py` gate).
- [x] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` green;
      `golangci-lint run` clean; `scripts/verify-modules.sh` green.
- [x] Both dashboards pushed live and snapshot-rendered; the old `-overview` UID deleted
      and `verify_deployment.py` reports no orphans.
- [x] `docs/metrics.md`, `docs/env-vars.md`, `docs/signal-coverage.md` regenerated.

## Out of scope

Alert-rule changes beyond what the disposition manifest's derivation requires. Metric
renames or new instrumentation — this is a presentation-layer re-architecture; if a
signal is awkward to panel, it gets panelled awkwardly and a follow-up issue is filed.
Reintroducing any Grafana v1/Classic export path.

comments.body:
## Wave 1a landed — the split and the frozen seams (`372b169`)

The artifact is now a family of two. `git rm deploy/grafana/tailscale2otel.json`; in its place:

| artifact | uid | panels | dashboard-level vars | visible |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `tailscale2otel-tailnet.json` | `tailscale2otel-tailnet` | 334 | 75 | 16 |
| `tailscale2otel-health.json` | `tailscale2otel-health` | 103 | 25 | 16 |
| | | **437** | | |

The union is exactly the 437 measured before, and no panel was added, dropped or edited — this
commit is a move plus the seams. The variable counts are untouched on purpose: nothing is
re-scoped yet, so the ≤15/≤6 budgets are Wave 3 work.

### Deviation from the wave sketch, with its reason

The issue has Wave 1 as "seams + gate rewrite". This commit additionally performs the physical
split, by moving `Exporter Diagnostics` and `Cardinality & Cost` across unchanged. Reason: the
gate rewrite's whole point is the union over two paths, and a union over one real file and one
absent file is a vacuous gate — the exact failure mode the issue's own Gating section warns
about. No decision in the issue is altered. Content re-organisation is still Waves 2–3.

### Seams frozen (later lanes code against these)

- **`gen/dashboards.py`** owns what dashboards exist and what is on each: `DashboardSpec`,
  `TabDef`, `DomainDef`, `SubTabbedDef`. `build.py` loops over `dashboards.ALL` and emits both
  in one process.
- **Tab-module signature is `tab_x(scope) -> list[row]`.** `sentinel()`, `pii_sentinel()` and
  `raw_sentinel()` take `scope` as a **required** third argument — no default, so a module
  cannot forget it and silently rebuild the dashboard-level pile. Wave 1 passes
  `builder.DASHBOARD` everywhere, which is what made the pure-move check possible.
- `builder.autogrid_row()`; `variables=` on `row`/`tab`/`tab_group`; `variables.adhoc_var()`
  (owns the kind-level `group`/`datasource` placement); `builder.dashboard_link()`.
- `--flat`/`--tab` now **require** `--dashboard`.

Verified the migration was genuinely mechanical: regenerating after adding `scope` to all 11
modules and all 67 sentinel call sites produced a **byte-identical** artifact.

### Three things the issue does not mention, all forced by the rename

1. **`deploy/alerts/gen/build_rules.py`** resolved every alert's `__dashboardUid__`/`__panelId__`
   by panel *title* against the one file, taking the uid from that file. Panel ids restart per
   dashboard, so the uid now travels with the id, and a title present on both artifacts is an
   error rather than a pick-first. **92 alert links now resolve 57 tailnet / 35 health**, none at
   the retired uid. This is also the mechanism for the "reachable from the alert that fires on
   it" criterion.
2. **`tools/promqlcheck`** parsed a hardcoded single path. Its entire job is that no expression
   ships unparsed, and it was about to stop seeing 103 panels' worth. It walks the family now,
   with a test that puts the broken fixture *only* in the last artifact — the other tests all
   put theirs in the first slot, so without it a regression to single-file checking would pass.
3. **`.github/workflows/grafana-sync.yml`** publishes to GitSync repo `rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni`
   under a UID-derived filename. **This changes the post-deploy cleanup step**: retiring the live
   `-overview` dashboard means *deleting `networking/tailscale2otel-overview.json` from the
   GitSync repo* as well — a `gcx dashboards delete` on its own is undone by the next sync,
   which re-creates it from the file still sitting there.

### A correction to the "dead sentinel" item

> Delete them, and add a gate that fails on any declared-but-unconsumed sentinel so this cannot recur.

**That gate already exists** — `test_sentinel_registry.py::test_every_registered_sentinel_is_referenced_or_known_dead`
— and the five dead names sit in an explicit `KNOWN_DEAD_SENTINELS` allowlist, each with a
written reason. The four `pii_*` ones are deliberate: *"no panel anywhere renders a raw address,
so there is nothing for them to gate, and wiring them would mean ADDING an address-rendering
panel."* So the work is **deleting the five and deleting the allowlist**, which makes the
existing gate absolute. That is Wave 1b, not a new gate. Flagging rather than quietly doing
something different from what the issue says.

### Two sentinels straddled the split

`has_selfobs` (declared by `diagnostics.py`, consumed by `overview.py` and `events.py`) and
`has_multitailnet` (declared by `tailnets.py`, consumed by `diagnostics.py`) each ended up with
their declaration on one dashboard and a consumer on the other. The registry resets per
dashboard, so those rows would have rendered **permanently hidden — indistinguishable from a
correctly-gated row**. Both are now declared on both sides, and the registry test checks
per-dashboard rather than over the union, which is what caught them.

### Gate evidence

```
go build ./... && go vet ./...      OK
go test -race ./...                 exit 0, 68 packages ok, 0 FAIL
golangci-lint run                   0 issues
scripts/verify-modules.sh           exit 0 — all 4 modules (. apidrift configcheck metricscatalog promqlcheck)
python3 -m unittest deploy/grafana/gen   179 tests OK
python3 -m unittest deploy/alerts/gen    107 tests OK
regeneration idempotent             re-running scripts/regen-generated.sh dashboards changes nothing
```

`verify-modules.sh` earned its keep here: root `go build ./...` never reaches the tool modules,
so `promqlcheck` was broken for a while with a completely green root gate.

### Next

Wave 1b, before any tab work: delete the 5 dead sentinels + the allowlist, add the catalog→panel
direction over the union, seed the shrink-only `pending_panel` ledger with the measured gap, and
delete `raw_only`/`omitted`. Then the live probe of duplicate tab-scoped variable names, whose
answer decides whether the ≤2-tab duplication rule survives.

## Wave 1b landed — the coverage gate (`4617b10`)

`internal/catalog/coverage_test.go` now checks the catalog→panel direction over the union of both
artifacts. It was written independently of the issue's analysis, and it measures the gap at
**exactly 42 of 310** — the same figure, arrived at by a different route. All **7 alertable-only**
signals it names are the 7 the issue names:

```
tailscale.device.attribute.expiry          tailscale2otel.tls.cert.not_after
tailscale.geoip.database.build_time        tailscale2otel.tls.cert.reload.failures
tailscale.key.scope_class
tailscale.key.tag_scope
tailscale.posture_integration.error
```

Current state: **41 on the `pending_panel` ledger, 1 structurally exempt** (42 total), 7 of the 41
alertable-only. Every ledger row names the dashboard and tab its panel is scheduled for, taken from
the issue's target structure — so Waves 2–3 have a per-signal worklist rather than a count.

### `raw_only` and `omitted` are gone

Replaced by a single transitional `pending_panel` with a shrink-only ceiling
(`TestPendingPanelLedgerOnlyShrinks`). The point of the ceiling: a lane cannot make a coverage
failure go away by adding a row, which is exactly what the deleted values permitted. The ledger,
the constant and that test are deleted together when the last panel lands.

**A modelling error worth recording, because it defeated the gate's own purpose.** I first made
`pending_panel` mutually exclusive with all three derived dispositions, mirroring how `raw_only`
worked. Regeneration then silently dropped the ledger row for anything already `alertable` — i.e.
**precisely the 7 alertable-only signals**, the worst class and the reason the gate exists. It is
now mutually exclusive with `visualized` alone and coexists with `alertable`/`recorded` by design:
"paged by something nothing charts" is the case being drained, not a contradiction to reject.

### Structural exemptions: 1 member, and two classes legitimately empty

Only `tailscale.webhook.<type>` (`templated_event`) — the name is built at emit time, so no literal
`event_name="..."` selector can equal it. The webhook panels select the family by regex, which a
token match cannot attribute back, and widening the extractor to try would start matching unrelated
names by prefix.

The other two have **no members, for reasons worth writing down**:

- **`histogram_base` — empty for a mechanical reason.** `ArtifactRefs.references` already credits a
  query on `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count` back to the base signal, so a histogram whose buckets are
  charted is `visualized` outright. The class stays defined because that crediting is a property of
  the extractor, not a guarantee. The issue expected this class to have members; it does not.
- **`recorded_only` — empty exactly as the issue predicts.** Nothing is `recorded` without also
  being `visualized`. Confirmed, not assumed. Not going looking for members.

### Dead sentinels: the gate existed; the allowlist was the hole

As flagged in the previous comment: the five are deleted, and `KNOWN_DEAD_SENTINELS` is deleted with
them, which is what actually stops recurrence — the gate was never missing, the door was. A sentinel
that gates nothing now fails the build with nowhere to add a name. Tailnet dashboard-level variables
**75 → 70**.

The four `pii_*` deletions carry a note saying re-adding one is only correct **in the same commit as
a panel that renders the address it redacts** — that was the original reason they gated nothing, and
it still holds.

### Gate evidence

```
go build ./... && go vet ./...      OK
go test -race ./...                 exit 0, 0 FAIL
golangci-lint run                   0 issues
scripts/verify-modules.sh           exit 0 — all 4 modules
python3 -m unittest deploy/grafana/gen   179 OK
python3 -m unittest deploy/alerts/gen    107 OK
regeneration idempotent             yes
```

### Acceptance criteria now satisfiable

- [x] `ci.yml`'s `dashboards-drift` job covers both files
- [x] `raw_only` and `omitted` no longer exist as dispositions
- [x] Dead sentinels deleted; a gate fails on any declared-but-unconsumed sentinel
- [x] `--flat`/`--tab` preview flags take a `--dashboard` selector; `regen_dashboards()` writes both
- [x] Both dashboards carry a cross-link to the other, propagating time range and shared variables

Still open and unchanged: the 310-signal bar (41 to go), the ≤15/≤6 variable budgets, the ≤35/≤30
panel ceilings, live push + orphan deletion.

### Next, and the one thing that needs deciding before Wave 3

The live probe of **duplicate tab-scoped variable names**. The generator now permits the same name
in two different tab scopes; whether *Grafana* does is unverified, and the ≤2-tab duplication rule —
and with it the ≤15 dashboard-level variable budget — depends on the answer. If it is rejected,
those variables stay dashboard-level and I will recompute the budget and report here before
proceeding rather than quietly missing a stated criterion.

## Live probe results — both unverified assumptions now settled

Probed against the `m7kni` stack, both probes deleted afterwards and their absence confirmed by
`gcx dashboards list`.

### 1. Duplicate tab-scoped variable names — **VERIFIED, and more strongly than asked**

> **Unverified assumption to check during implementation:** whether two different tabs may each
> declare a tab-scoped variable with the *same* name.

Persistence alone would not have been enough. The failure mode that actually matters is Grafana
resolving the name **globally** — last-declaration-wins — which persists perfectly and then gates
the wrong rows. So the probe was built to separate the two:

- tab `Alpha` declares `has_dup` → `label_values(tailscale_devices_count_ratio, __name__)` — **5 live series**
- tab `Beta` declares `has_dup` → `label_values(ts2_probe_metric_that_does_not_exist, __name__)` — **no series**

Same name, opposite truth, each gating its own row.

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| both declarations survive push + read-back, with their **own** queries | yes |
| `Alpha` rendered first → its row **renders** | yes (PNG) |
| `Beta` rendered first → its row is **absent** | yes (PNG) |

Grafana resolves tab-scoped variables **per tab**. **The ≤2-tab duplication rule stands, and the
≤15 dashboard-level variable budget stays reachable.** No fallback needed and no re-planning
required.

### 2. Adhoc variable with kind-level `group`/`datasource` — **VERIFIED**

Pushed `variables.adhoc_var()` output verbatim, tab-scoped. No 422 — and specifically not the
`layout.kind` CUE error the issue warns masks this. Read-back:

```
kind        : AdhocVariable
group       : prometheus                      <- KIND level
datasource  : {'name': '${ds_prometheus}'}    <- KIND level
spec keys   : allowCustomValue, baseFilters, defaultKeys, description,
              filters, hide, label, name, skipUrlSync
baseFilters : [{'key': '__name__', 'operator': '=~', 'value': 'tailscale_device_.*'}]
```

`baseFilters` intact, and neither `group` nor `datasource` inside `spec`. The shape in
`gen/variables.py:adhoc_var()` is the correct one, now confirmed against the API rather than
against a reading of the schema.

### Also confirmed, for the Wave 4 cleanup

`gcx dashboards search tailscale` finds the live **`tailscale2otel-overview`**, so the orphan is
real and still deployed. Its retirement needs **both** halves, per the earlier comment: remove
`networking/tailscale2otel-overview.json` from `rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni` *and* delete the
dashboard — a delete alone gets undone by the next GitSync run.

One operational note for later steps: `gcx dashboards delete` refuses in agent mode without
`--force`, and the refusal is easy to miss because the surrounding hint line looks like normal
output. Both probe deletions initially no-opped for exactly that reason; verify deletions by
listing, never by the command's exit.

**Wave 1 is complete** — seams, split, gate, dead sentinels, and both probes. Waves 2 and 3 are
unblocked with no design changes.

## Wave 2 landed — the health dashboard, rebuilt by pipeline stage (`6a16821`)

`tailscale2otel-health` is now **158 panels over 7 leaves**, organised by where a failure actually
occurs rather than by which subsystem emitted the metric:

| leaf | panels |
| --- | ---: |
| Overview | 21 |
| Collection | 29 |
| Ingestion | 34 |
| Delivery | 19 |
| Runtime | 21 |
| Cost & Cardinality | 20 |
| Exporter internals | 14 |

No leaf exceeds the ~35 ceiling. Built by five parallel lanes, one file each, with
`diagnostics.py`/`events.py`/`cardinality.py` read-only for all of them — the wiring pass below was
the only thing that touched shared files.

### The self-observability half of the coverage gap is closed

**Pending ledger 41 → 14, and all 14 remaining are product-dashboard signals.** Among the 25
drained: profiling upload (5), TLS cert reload (4), processor queue (3), metrics-endpoint scrape (5),
log truncation (2), annotations (3), export spans/diagnostics (2), process CPU/uptime (2).

**Both alertable-only TLS signals are now reachable from the alert that fires on them.**
`ts2o-tls-cert-expiring` and `ts2o-tls-cert-reload-failing` carried **no `panel=` at all** — they
linked nowhere. They now resolve to "TLS certificate expiry countdown" and "TLS certificate reload
failures" on health. That criterion was nominally satisfiable without this; it isn't any more.

### A 7th leaf, "Exporter internals" — a deliberate deviation

The target structure lists 6 health tabs. Deleting `diagnostics.py` outright would have silently
dropped 14 panels no lane claimed: enrichment cache, rDNS resolver, per-tailnet API errors, tracing.
Each needs a judgement about which stage owns it (is reverse DNS *collection* or *ingestion*?), and
that is consolidation-pass work, not a wiring decision. They keep a leaf rather than being scattered
on the way past. Flagging rather than quietly shipping a 7-tab dashboard against a 6-tab spec.

### Two bugs the wiring found, both silent in the safe-looking direction

**1. The coverage gate was blind to the entire `process.*` family.** `metricRef` was anchored on the
tailscale prefixes, so `process_cpu_time_seconds_total` and `process_uptime_seconds` matched
nothing. This was undetectable while the only check ran panel→catalog — an unmatched name is simply
never asked about. It surfaced the moment the catalog→panel direction reported both as reaching no
panel *while two panels charted each of them*. **A gate that cannot see a family cannot report it
missing either**, so the hole hid in the direction that looks safe. Extractor widened.

**2. Six alert panel links were broken by the restructure** — four pointing at panels the
consolidation renamed, two (the TLS pair) pointing nowhere. `panel_ref` failing loudly on a moved
title is exactly why it resolves by title rather than by id, and it did its job.

### `test_selfobs_coverage.py` reduced, as the issue directs

It no longer asserts **presence** — that is the Go gate's job over both artifacts, and checking it
in both places makes every panel move fail two tests for one reason. It keeps **placement** (which
stage a family lands on), and its empty-state contract is now **derived** instead of a frozen title
list: every empty state that exists must be well-formed, with a floor so they cannot be quietly
deleted. A frozen list fails on rename for a reason unrelated to what it checks, and the reflex is
then to edit the list rather than look at the panel.

The polarity inventory gained two new booleans with **opposite** polarity (`Node-metrics discovery
OK` 1=good, `Annotation delivery degraded` 1=bad), kept adjacent on purpose — a "simplify these onto
one shared map" refactor is precisely what #385 was.

### Family panel count is UP, 437 → 466

Deliberate, and the point of the issue: 25 signals that previously reached no panel now do. The
query-budget ceilings moved with it, with the reason recorded next to them. Consolidation in Wave 4
will bring it back down.

### Gate evidence

```
go build ./... && go vet ./...          OK
go test -race ./...                     exit 0, 0 FAIL
golangci-lint run                       0 issues
scripts/verify-modules.sh               exit 0 — all 4 modules
python3 -m unittest deploy/grafana/gen  179 OK
python3 -m unittest deploy/alerts/gen   107 OK
regeneration idempotent                 yes
```

### Next

Wave 3, the product dashboard: Overview (≤30, absorbing the Tailnets panels + health strip),
Devices/Security/Policy sub-tab splits, Flows, Node Metrics — and the last 14 ledger signals,
5 of which are alertable-only. Then Wave 4: consolidation, the ≤15/≤6 variable budgets, live push,
and retiring `-overview` from both GitSync and the stack.

## Wave 3 landed — the product dashboard, and the ledger is empty (`b3572e8`)

`tailscale2otel-tailnet` is **298 panels over 15 leaves**, and **all 310 catalog signals now
reach a panel**. The pending ledger went 41 → 14 → **0**.

| | before | after | budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| panels | 308 | 298 | — |
| dashboard-level variables | 66 | **8** | ≤15 |
| visible controls | 16 | **6** | ≤6 |
| largest leaf | 59 | **33** | ≤35 |
| Overview | 34 | **30** | ≤30 |

```
Overview                                     30
Fleet & Network / Devices / Inventory & Hygiene       30
                          / Posture & Security        12
                          / Connectivity & Routing    20
                / Network & Flows                     33
                / Node Metrics                        32
Security & Policy / Security & Audit / Audit Trail    14
                                     / Risk & ACL      9
                                     / Posture & Compliance 16
                                     / Identity & Keys 18
                  / Policy & Config / Access & ACL      8
                                    / DNS & Settings   13
                                    / Identity & Credentials 16
                                    / Integrations     15
                  / Kubernetes Audit                   32
```

Built by five parallel lanes — three sub-tab splits, the Overview rebuild, and a health-side
consolidation lane — with `build.py`/`builder.py`/`variables.py`/`dashboards.py` touched only by
the wiring pass.

### The five alertable-only signals are now reachable *for real*

All five have panels, and all five alerts point at them. Worth recording **why the criterion was
not already met**: three of them *did* carry a `panel=` — each aimed at a panel charting a
**different metric**.

| alert | linked to | which charts | now links to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ts2o-key-broad-scope` | Credential scopes (top-N) | the scope **count** — the signal #415 replaced *because it inverted the answer* | Credential privilege class (blast radius) |
| `ts2o-key-unrestricted-tags` | Preauthorized auth keys | an unrelated field | OAuth client tag restriction class |
| `ts2o-posture-integration-error` | Integration sync detail | `last_sync` — the signal this alert exists **because it cannot detect** | Posture integration last-sync errors |
| `ts2o-device-attribute-expiring-14d` | *(nothing)* | — | Posture attribute expiry — time remaining |
| `ts2o-geoip-database-stale` | *(nothing)* | — | GeoIP database age since build |

A `panel=` that resolves is not the same as a panel that shows the condition that paged you.

### Three gates were blind, and each was hiding a real defect

1. **`test_empty_state_contract`'s row walker accepted only `GridLayout`.** Decision 6 converts
   uniform rows to `AutoGridLayout`; the walker returned an empty panel list for every converted
   row, so every per-panel assertion passed **vacuously** on them. No failure — just less
   coverage. It surfaced only because one test asserts its panel was *found* before checking it.
   Fixed, plus a floor: a row that reads as having zero panels is a bug in the reader, since the
   generator cannot build one.
2. **`test_sentinel_registry` only asked whether a name was declared *somewhere*.** After ~60
   sentinels moved onto tabs, that is too weak: a row gating on a **sibling tab's** variable
   passes and then renders permanently hidden — indistinguishable on screen from a row correctly
   hidden for want of data. It now checks resolution per scope, with a negative test, and caught
   `cardinality.py`'s "Ingest vs export cost" row in exactly that state.
3. **`test_unit_consistency` honoured `byName` overrides but not `byRegexp`.** The consolidation
   pass merges same-subject/different-unit panels whose extra series are templated
   (`p95 {{operation}}`) and so *cannot* be matched by exact name. Four correctly-rendering panels
   read as unit-family violations — and the reflex when a gate cries wolf is to exempt the panel,
   which is when it really would stop being checked.

### `tailscale.subnet_routes.advertised` was never on a panel

It satisfied the coverage gate solely through a hidden sentinel's `label_values()` query, and
looked covered right up until wave 3 deleted the row that sentinel gated. **A template-variable
reference is not a panel**, so a signal can clear the gate while being invisible to an operator.
It has a real panel now, but the gate's definition of "visualized" is looser than this issue's
stated bar and that gap is worth a follow-up.

### Four things the lanes found that the briefs got wrong

- My row split accounted for **17 of `security.py`'s 18 rows** — "Device share invites" (3 panels)
  was in no lane's brief and would have been dropped silently. Re-homed to Identity & Keys.
- My brief said "four alertable-only" on Security; the ledger says three. The lane checked the
  ledger rather than the prose, and was right.
- Three of five briefed row merges on Devices were **refused**, correctly: `fleet.py`'s
  single-panel rows are not sloppiness, they exist so a PII gate covers one table instead of nine
  aggregates. Merging would have either dropped the redaction or hidden non-PII content.
- Kubernetes Audit's five `— top users` rows look like prime merge candidates and are not, for the
  same reason. It stays at 32 panels, 15 rows.

`Exporter internals` (the 7th health leaf, flagged as a deviation in wave 2) is gone — its 14
panels distributed by stage: enrichment cache, rDNS and per-tailnet API errors to Collection,
tracing to Delivery, and its cardinality/dedup row dropped as an exact duplicate of what
Cost & Cardinality already carried. Health is 155 panels over the 6 stage tabs, none over 35.

### Gate evidence

```
go build ./... && go vet ./...          OK
go test -race ./...                     exit 0, 68 packages ok, 0 FAIL
golangci-lint run                       0 issues
scripts/verify-modules.sh               exit 0 — all 4 modules
python3 -m unittest deploy/grafana/gen  190 OK
python3 -m unittest deploy/alerts/gen   107 OK
regeneration idempotent                 yes (shasum before/after a second run)
```

### Next

Wave 4: delete `DispPendingPanel`, its now-empty ledger and `TestPendingPanelLedgerOnlyShrinks`
together; the consolidation pass; then live — push both dashboards, snapshot-render to prove
`conditionalRendering` hides what it should, push the rules, and retire `-overview` from **both**
the GitSync repo and the stack.

## Wave 4 landed — closed (`532ee16`)

All 14 acceptance criteria are ticked. Final shape:

| | tailnet | health |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| panels | 298 | 155 |
| leaves | 15 | 6 |
| dashboard-level variables | 8 (≤15) | 5 |
| visible controls | 6 (≤6) | 5 |
| largest leaf | 33 (≤35) | 35 |

**All 310 catalog signals reach a panel**, with three structural exemption classes (one member).
`verify_deployment.py`: 123 rules deployed, **0 missing, 0 orphaned, 0 drifted**. Both dashboards
are live and snapshot-rendered; `tailscale2otel-overview` is gone from the stack *and* from the
GitSync repo.

### `pending_panel` is deleted, as designed

The ledger went 41 → 14 → 0, so the disposition, its rows and `TestPendingPanelLedgerOnlyShrinks`
went together (`e726aad`). **Every disposition is now derived** — there is no value a human can
assign, so a signal on no surface cannot be settled by editing the manifest, only by giving it a
panel. That was the point of making it transitional and shrink-only: it could only ever be left
by gaining a panel, which is the only reason introducing it was safe. `raw_only`, `omitted` and
`pending_panel` are all gone; do not reintroduce one.

### Two bugs found by looking at the running system, not by a test

**1. `grafana-sync` had been green and publishing nothing (`f167a1c`).** Its commit step used
`git diff --quiet`, which sees only TRACKED files. Wave 1's rename made both new filenames
untracked, so the step printed *"dashboard already matches the stack source"* and exited 0 —
**three consecutive successful runs copied two files and published neither**, and `git commit -am`
would not have staged them anyway. The dashboards had not reached the stack at all since the split.
Found by querying the GitSync repo's tree rather than trusting the workflow's conclusion.

It now stages first and diffs the index, and publishes the current SET: any `tailscale2otel-*.json`
in the GitSync repo the generator no longer produces is removed. That made retiring `-overview`
automatic — GitSync deleted the live dashboard itself once its file went, which is the correct
mechanism, since an API delete alone is undone by the next sync from the file still sitting there.

**2. The degradation row rendered on a healthy exporter (`a273aa7`).** Seen on the pushed render,
not in any test. It gated on the *presence* of `tailscale2otel_scrape_errors_total`, and that
counter exists from the first scrape whether or not it has ever been incremented — so decision 2's
"renders only when a degradation sentinel fires" row was permanently visible, showing two "No data"
panels. Presence was the wrong question; it is a threshold. It now fires when a collector's last
scrape actually failed or an export failed within the hour, each side zero-filled independently so
a deployment emitting only one family cannot hide the row when the other is firing. Re-rendered
after the fix: **absent**. Verified in both directions.

### What the live renders confirmed

Beyond the two bugs: 6 visible controls on the product dashboard and 5 on health, the `(summary)`
suffix convention, the merged devices stat, and `conditionalRendering` correctly hiding the
multi-tailnet row on a single-tailnet stack. Live panel counts match the committed artifacts
exactly on both (298/298, 155/155).

Also worth recording against a note in this repo's own memory: **full-dashboard snapshots work
fine now**. The previous belief was that they render a blank rectangle and only `--panel` is
usable. Both dashboards rendered complete, with real data, at `--width 1400 --since 6h`.

### Docs

~29 runbook "First step" pointers named tabs that no longer exist, and eleven panel titles had
changed in the consolidation pass. Every reference was resolved against an index generated from
the committed artifacts, and every panel title left in the docs was checked to resolve to exactly
one panel. `docs/dashboards.md` is restructured around which dashboard answers which question; its
build and push commands still referenced the deleted single JSON file.

### Commits

```
372b169  split into a tailnet and a health artifact          (wave 1a)
4617b10  gate that every emitted signal reaches a panel      (wave 1b)
6a16821  rebuild the health dashboard around pipeline stages (wave 2)
b3572e8  rebuild the product dashboard around domains        (wave 3)
e726aad  delete pending_panel now that every signal has a panel
f167a1c  the dashboard sync reported success while publishing nothing
a273aa7  the degradation row rendered on a healthy exporter
af956f8  record the GitSync delivery path and two link contracts
532ee16  retarget the operator docs at the two-dashboard family
```

### One thing deliberately left open

The coverage gate credits a **template-variable** query as "visualized", so a signal can satisfy it
while appearing on no panel an operator can see. `tailscale.subnet_routes.advertised` was in exactly
that state — covered only by a hidden sentinel's `label_values()` call, and it stayed invisible right
up until wave 3 deleted the row that sentinel gated. It has a real panel now, but the gate's
definition is looser than this issue's stated bar. Narrowing it to panel queries only is a
self-contained follow-up, not something to fold in here.
Follow-up filed as #527 for the coverage gate's template-variable looseness described above.

## Correction: CI caught 65 failures the local gate could not see (`c300199`)

The closing comment above claimed a green gate. It was green **locally** and the closing commit
went red on CI. Recording the whole thing because the interesting part is not the bugs, it is that
nothing I ran locally could have found them.

### Why the local gate missed it

`promqlcheck` parses every dashboard and rule expression this repo ships and resolves each
`$variable`. It runs in ci.yml's *"generated dashboards and rules are in sync"* job. Everything
local — `go test -race ./...`, `golangci-lint`, `scripts/verify-modules.sh` — only ever **built and
unit-tested the tool**, which proves nothing whatever about the artifacts. The module-verify legs
look like they cover `tools/promqlcheck`, and in the sense that matters here they do not.

`scripts/verify-modules.sh` now runs it against the artifacts as an explicit "artifacts" leg,
verified by injecting a bad `$variable` reference into a committed dashboard and watching the
script exit 1.

### One tool bug, hiding three real ones

**The tool resolved every `$variable` against `spec.variables[]` at the DASHBOARD level.** #526
moved ~60 variables onto the tab that consumes them, so dashboard-level is now the minority case.
That is wrong in both directions: it reported correctly tab-scoped references as undeclared *and*
it would have accepted a panel borrowing a **sibling tab's** variable, which resolves to nothing at
render time — the same silent failure this whole issue is about. It now walks the layout and checks
each panel against what is in scope where it actually sits, with a negative test for the sibling-tab
case, since a walker that simply unioned every declaration in the document would pass the obvious
test and accept the bug.

The walk is generic rather than typed against the layout kinds. A typed reader meeting an unknown
kind deserialises it to an empty struct and drops every panel underneath from the check while still
reporting success — the fourth time in this issue that a checker went quietly blind rather than
failing.

Behind the false positives were three genuine ones, all the same shape: **a query keeps its
`$variable` reference when it moves between dashboards, and the variable does not follow it.** The
audit-pipeline panels that moved to health kept `$provider`, the SIEM delivery-error panel kept
`$log_filter`, and the top-N series tables kept `$topn`. None is declared on health. All three are
now scoped to the single tab that reads them, so health keeps its five controls.

### And decision 3 was only half done

`device_user`, `device_tag` and `posture_attr` folded into the `device_filters` adhoc variable — but
their selector fragments stayed in the queries, so those panels named variables that no longer
existed anywhere. An adhoc variable injects its own matchers, so naming them as well would have
filtered twice even if they had survived.

They were invisible because **promqlcheck stops at the first undeclared variable per expression**,
and every one of those selectors led with `$os_type`. Fixing the tool's scope-awareness is what
exposed them.

### State after the fix

CI green on every lane. `tailnet` 298 panels / 8 dashboard-level variables / 6 visible; `health`
155 / 5 / 5 — matching the live stack exactly. `verify_deployment.py` still 0 missing, 0 orphaned,
0 drifted. Regeneration idempotent.

title: Dashboard re-architecture: split product from self-observability, section-scoped variables, hard coverage gate

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #524 item 5. The `flows.capacity_profile` advisory landed in `6acd70f`; the sibling audit it asked for turned up three candidates. Two are real and are the subject of this issue. The third is explained below and is deliberately **not** being implemented.

This repo already treats "configured but not actually emitted" as a bug class — this is the exact pair that cost the <host-1> lab weeks.

## 1. `cardinality.flow.source_port` / `destination_port` under `metrics_mode: rollup` (the DEFAULT)

Both default `false`, so setting either is a deliberate act: the operator is asking for L4 ports on flow metrics. Under the default `rollup` mode they do **nothing**.

`internal/flowlog/processor.go` reads `p.srcPort` / `p.dstPort` only inside `if p.mode == flowModeAll || p.mode == flowModeBoth`. The rollup family carries no L4 ports at all — its own field doc says so ("Carries no L4 ports"), and the accumulator's key has no port dimension.

So the operator sets the knob, the config validates, the docs describe it, the status page reports it, and no port ever reaches a metric. Nothing says why.

- [ ] Advise when `source_port` or `destination_port` is true and `metrics_mode` is `rollup`

## 2. `cardinality.flow.rollup_top_n` under `metrics_mode: all`

`RollupTopN` is only consumed by `newRollupAccumulator`, which `internal/flowlog/processor.go` constructs only when `flowMode == flowModeRollup || flowMode == flowModeBoth`. Under `metrics_mode: all` there is no accumulator, so the value is read by nothing.

`Validate()` still range-checks it (`>= 0`), which makes it look meaningful. The field doc already says "only used when MetricsMode is rollup or both" — the docs are right and the runtime is silent.

- [ ] Advise when `rollup_top_n` is set to a non-default value and `metrics_mode` is `all`

## 3. NOT doing: `cardinality.per_entity.*` / `derp_region_rollup` / `subnet_route_rollup` with the owning collector disabled

Raised by the audit, checked, and rejected. Every one of these defaults to **`true`** (`internal/config/defaults.go:153-172`), so an advisory would fire for everyone who simply disables a collector, while the toggle sits at a value they never chose.

The distinguishing property of cases 1, 2 and the `capacity_profile` case is that the operator asked for **more** data and silently got none. Disabling a collector and thereby disabling its own cardinality knobs is the expected, requested outcome — no signal is lost and there is no surprise to surface. Warning about it would be noise in a startup path whose value depends on every line being worth reading.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Both advisories follow the existing `Warnings()` idiom: message opens with the dotted config key (so `advisoryKey` extracts it), states what is wrong, why it matters, and what to do instead
- [ ] Fire only on the inert combination — not when the mode does consume the key, and not when the key is at its default
- [ ] Table tests covering both the firing and the non-firing combinations, plus an `Advisories()` key-extraction assertion
- [ ] Full gate green

## Landed: `681fe1e`

Full gate green (`go build` / `go vet` / `go test -race ./...` / `golangci-lint` / `verify-modules.sh`), CI + CodeQL green on `main`. No generated-artifact drift.

### What shipped

One advisory **per key** rather than one combined message — `advisoryKey` takes the first whitespace-delimited token, so a combined message could only ever be attributed to one of the two ports on the status page. Rendered output:

```
[cardinality.flow.source_port] cardinality.flow.source_port=true has no effect under
cardinality.flow.metrics_mode=rollup (the default): L4 ports are carried only by the raw
per-connection metric family, and the bounded rollup family deliberately has no port
dimension, so no port will ever reach a metric. Flow LOGS still carry both ports. To get
ports on metrics set cardinality.flow.metrics_mode to "all" or "both" — note that raises
series cost sharply, which is why the rollup family excludes them — otherwise remove
cardinality.flow.source_port.

[cardinality.flow.rollup_top_n] cardinality.flow.rollup_top_n=1200 has no effect under
cardinality.flow.metrics_mode=all: it bounds the rollup accumulator, which is only built
in "rollup" or "both" mode, so nothing reads this value. Either switch metrics_mode to
"rollup" (bounded cardinality) or remove cardinality.flow.rollup_top_n.
```

### Non-firing cases are tested as carefully as the firing ones

An advisory that fires when the mode *does* consume the key, or when the key sits at its default, is noise in a startup path whose value depends on every line being worth reading. Covered: both ports under `all`/`both`; `rollup_top_n` under `rollup`/`both`; `rollup_top_n` at its default; and `rollup_top_n: 0`, which the field doc defines as "use the default" — warning there would be *wrong*, not merely noisy.

The test helper asserts **at most one** warning matches each key prefix. That caught a real collision while writing it: the pre-existing `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode=both` warning matched a looser `cardinality.flow.` prefix, which would have made the assertions pass for the wrong reason.

### Defaults and advisories now share named constants

`defaultFlowRollupTopN` and the `flowMetricsMode*` vocabulary were magic literals in `defaults.go`. The advisory has to distinguish "the operator tuned this" from "this is the value we picked", which only works while both read the same source — so they are now named constants used by both.

### Case 3 stays unimplemented, with the reasoning recorded in the code

`cardinality.per_entity.*` and the derp/subnet rollups with the owning collector disabled. All default to `true` (`internal/config/defaults.go:153-172`), so an advisory would fire for everyone who merely turns a collector off, about a value they never chose.

The asymmetry that justifies the other three: the operator asked for **more** data and silently got none. Disabling a collector and thereby disabling its own cardinality knobs is the requested outcome — no signal is lost and there is no surprise to surface. The reasoning is now a comment in `Warnings()` next to the two new advisories, so a future pass does not "complete the set" and add the noise back.
