body:
## Summary

Operator-facing fixes to the admin status page, from using it on the <host-1> lab deployment. Grouped
because they share one theme: **the page holds the truth in its JSON but doesn't show it.** Every item
below is backed by data already present in `/api/status.json`.

## 1. The capability matrix is squeezed into a 460px box

`page.html.tmpl:86` defines a single global `.scroll{max-height:460px}` used by **10** tables. The
capability matrix has 18 rows on <host-1> (one per capability + sub-request) and only ~8 fit, so the
table it exists to present is permanently half-hidden.

- [x] Let the capabilities table use most of the viewport (its own modifier, e.g. `.scroll.tall`, or a
      `max-height` in `vh`) rather than raising the shared 460px for all ten tables
- [x] Sanity-check the other long tables (collectors, cardinality) for the same squeeze

## 2. 78% of the `State` column reads `unknown`, including for healthy collectors

<host-1>'s matrix: **14 of 18 rows are `state: unknown`**, 3 `supported`, 1 `transient_failure`. Twelve of
the unknowns are collectors that are `active: true` and succeeding on every tick — `devices` runs every
60s at 100% success and still shows `unknown` on all three of its rows.

Cause: only 8 of 16 collector packages reference `apistate` at all (`acl`, `devices`, `flowlogs`,
`keys`, `logstream`, `oauthapps`, `postureintegrations`, `webhooks`). The rest never record, so their
row can only ever be `unknown`. Even inside recorded packages, sub-request rows go unprobed.

This actively misleads, because `page.html.tmpl:362-365` tells the operator *"**State** (from live API
responses) is the column to trust"*. Today it is the column least worth trusting.

- [x] Record state on success as well as failure for every collector that makes an API call
      (`Classify(nil)` already yields `StateSupported`)
- [x] Cover sub-request rows, or stop emitting a row that nothing can ever populate
- [x] A collector with a recent successful run must never display `unknown`
- [x] Reword the explanatory note if any residual `unknown` remains legitimately reachable

## 3. "Not polling" doesn't say why

`flowlogs` and `auditlogs` on <host-1> are `active: false, reason: "not_registered", source: "stream"`.
Both fields are already in the JSON; the Status column renders only `capReason .Reason`, so the operator
sees the bare token `not_registered` and no hint that this is **correct and intended** — the data is
arriving via the streaming receiver instead.

- [x] Render the reason together with `source`, as a plain-English explanation
      (e.g. "ingested via streaming receiver — not polled")
- [x] Style a deliberately-not-polling collector as informational, not as a fault or a pending state
- [x] Same treatment for the `objectstore` source

## 4. `/flows` and `/events` are near-invisible and are dead ends

Both are single small text links in the header (`page.html.tmpl:179-180`). Worse, **neither page has any
link back**: `internal/app/flowhtml/page.html.tmpl` and `internal/app/eventshtml/page.html.tmpl` contain
no backlink to `/`, so following either strands the operator with the browser Back button.

- [x] Add a backlink to the status page from `/flows` **and** `/events`
- [x] Make `/flows` genuinely prominent — it is the most useful view here and currently reads as a
      footnote
- [ ] Promote `/events` to its own tab on the status page; if it becomes a tab, its backlink need is — **DEFERRED** by scope decision (see comments)
      satisfied by the tab chrome instead
- [x] Keep both pages self-contained (no CDN/external assets) so they still render on an air-gapped
      tailnet

## 5. Silently-inert config should be surfaced, not just documented

Found while aligning <host-1>: setting `flows.capacity_profile` while `flows.store.directory` is set is a
**no-op** — the sqlite backend replaces the in-memory ring and has no per-key caps, so the profile is
ignored and the status page reports `capacity_profile: "sqlite"`. The docs say so, but nothing tells the
operator who set it. This repo already treats "configured but not actually emitted" as a bug class
(`cardinality.flow.source_port` under `metrics_mode: rollup` cost the <host-1> lab weeks).

- [x] Emit a config advisory when `flows.capacity_profile != default` and `flows.store.directory` is set
- [x] Audit for sibling cases where one key silently disables another

## Notes

- Purely operator-facing; no metric, log or OTLP surface changes, so no catalog regeneration expected.
- `internal/app/statushtml/statushtml_test.go` and `polling_test.go` already assert page structure —
  extend them rather than adding a parallel harness.
- Related: #523 (the `transient_failure` row that item 2's `unknown` audit sits next to).

comments.body:
**Decision (Rob, 2026-07-31) on item 4: backlinks only, no new tab — for now.**

Scope for this issue is: add a backlink to the status page from both `/flows` and `/events`, and make `/flows` genuinely prominent. The events-as-a-tab restructure is **deferred**, not dropped — revisit once the rest of #524 has landed and the page has been used. Keeps this issue low-risk and avoids maintaining two render paths for events before we know we want them.

Items 1, 2, 3 and 5 are unchanged and in scope.

## Item 2 rescoped: this is a self-observability gap with a live alerting blind spot, not UI plumbing

Rob's call, and the investigation backs it: making the State column truthful is the *same change* as lighting up an existing telemetry lane. `apistate.Observe` emits the metric **and** records the tracker in one call, so a collector that doesn't call it is dark on both surfaces simultaneously.

### The metrics already exist and are already documented

`tailscale2otel.api.availability` and `tailscale2otel.api.last_probe` are shipped, documented OTLP metrics (`docs/metrics.md`). `docs/metrics.md` describes availability as though it covers every collector. It does not.

### This is currently a live blind spot in shipped alerting

These consume the metric today and therefore only see **8 of 16** collectors:

- `deploy/alerts/grafana-managed/ts2o-api-credential-rejected.json`
- `deploy/alerts/grafana-managed/ts2o-api-scope-denied.json`
- `deploy/grafana/gen/tabs/diagnostics.py` (and the built `deploy/grafana/tailscale2otel.json`)

**A revoked credential or a scope regression affecting `users`, `dns`, `settings`, `contacts`, `services`, `nodemetrics` or `auditlogs` cannot fire either alert.** That is the real severity here — the status page `unknown` cells were the visible symptom of it.

### Worklist — exact, verified by `grep -rq 'apistate\.'` per package

**Records today (8, reference implementations):** `acl`, `devices`, `flowlogs`, `keys`, `logstream`, `oauthapps`, `postureintegrations`, `webhooks`

**Dark (8, the work):** `auditlogs`, `contacts`, `dns`, `nodemetrics`, `objectstore`, `services`, `settings`, `users`

### Acceptance criteria (replacing item 2's original list)

- [ ] Every collector that makes a control-plane API call routes its outcome through `apistate.Observe` — success included (`Classify(nil)` already yields `StateSupported`)
- [ ] Each call site declares an honest `Disposition` — do NOT blanket-apply `DisabledOn: [403]`; per the package doc an ambiguous 403 must default to `scope_denied`, and only an operation upstream documents as 403-gated may read it as `disabled`
- [ ] Sub-request rows (e.g. devices posture/invites) are covered, or the row is not emitted at all
- [ ] A collector with a recent successful run can never display `unknown`
- [ ] A test proves no collector package is silently dark — enumerate the registered collectors and assert each emits `tailscale2otel.api.availability`, so collector #17 cannot ship dark
- [ ] `docs/metrics.md` regenerated if any descriptor changes
- [ ] Re-check the two alert rules and the diagnostics tab now that coverage is complete; if either needs a `tailscale_collector` dimension or a `for:` change, do it in the same pass
- [ ] Provider-agnostic: Headscale exposes a subset, so a capability it cannot serve must read `disabled`, never `scope_denied`

### Note on ordering

Item 2 now carries the most value and the most risk in this issue. Items 1, 3, 4 and 5 stay as originally scoped and are independent of it.

## Landed: `6acd70f` + `8b674af`

Full gate green on both (`go build` / `go vet` / `go test -race ./...` / `golangci-lint` / `scripts/verify-modules.sh`), pushed to `main`. Alert rules deployed and verified in sync (`verify_deployment.py`: 123 shipped, 123 deployed, 0 missing / 0 orphaned / 0 drifted).

### The item 2 worklist in the comment above was incomplete

It was derived by `grep -rq 'apistate\.'` per package, which counts the **Coverage** tally as coverage. Coverage and `Observe` are different signals — that is precisely how `devices` hid. Re-deriving it against `apistate.Observe` specifically: only **5** packages recorded, not 8 (`logstream`, `flowlogs`, `postureintegrations`, `webhooks`, and `acl`'s *validate* subrequest only).

Additional dark collectors the worklist missed, all now covered:

| collector | why it was missed |
| --- | --- |
| `devices` | had the #421 Coverage tally, never called `Observe` — the issue's own headline symptom |
| `keys`, `oauthapps` | mention `apistate` only in comments |
| `acl` (primary fetch) | `getPolicyFile` unobserved; the row's state came entirely from the validate probe |
| `flowlogs-feature` | **not a package** — the probe that *stands in for* the poller in a stream-only deployment, i.e. exactly what this lab runs |

### Dispositions

Every new call site is `apistate.Disposition{}`. `flowlogs` remains the single `DisabledOn: [403]` in the repo. Specifically resisted: copying it onto `auditlogs` (a missing `logs:configuration:read` must read `scope_denied`) and onto `oauthapps`, whose `isFeatureOff` still swallows 403/404 — control flow deliberately unchanged, but the state is now visible, so a scope regression that used to look identical to the alpha endpoint being off now shows up.

### The anti-regression test

`TestEveryRegisteredCollectorRecordsAPIState` (`internal/app/apistatecoverage_test.go`) drives every registered collector against a fixture that 500s everything, over two scenarios (poll sources / object-store sources — the ingestion sources are mutually exclusive, so no single config registers all 18). No happy-path fixtures needed: `Observe` sits before the error branch, so a uniform failure proves the call site exists and stays immune to upstream schema drift.

It asserts **both** the metric and the tracker, which turned out to matter. `Observe` emits the metric with a nil tracker by design, so a collector that calls `Observe` correctly but never receives `WithAPIState` alerts fine and *still* shows `unknown`. I verified this by deleting the `contacts` wiring: the metric-only check **passed**. The tracker check catches it. There is an `apiStateExempt` map, deliberately empty, so a future exemption has to be argued in review rather than achieved by quietly not wiring something.

### `8b674af` — the display half, found by checking the live deployment

Coverage alone was not sufficient. The matrix joins a tracker entry to a row by **collector name**, and three registered collectors had no decision row:

- `flowlogs-feature` recorded state that landed nowhere, so the `flowlogs` row would have *stayed* `unknown` in this lab's stream-only config even after the wiring. Its entries now fold onto the `flowlogs` row. It gets no row of its own on purpose — that row would be permanently inactive wherever the poller *is* registered, which is the "row nothing can ever populate" this issue asks us to stop emitting.
- `objectstore` / `objectstore-audit` had no row **at all** — a running collector missing from the matrix, which is the same blindness with even less to notice. They now get a row only when a source selects them. `objectstore-audit` was also absent from `CollectorCapability` entirely.

### Alert rules

Both now group `by (tailscale_collector, tailscale_api_operation)` and name the collector via `{{ $labels... }}`. A bare `max()` over a minority of the fleet could not say *which* endpoint was refused; the grouping is what makes the widened coverage actionable. The diagnostics tab needed no change — its table already renders per collector/operation, so it scales with coverage on its own.

### Item 4's premise was stale

Both `/flows` and `/events` **already had** a backlink to `/` — `flowhtml` in `4427507` (2026-07-24), `eventshtml` in `8b655e9` (2026-07-28), both predating this issue. They were inconsistent with each other; now they match, with guard tests. `/flows` promotion and the deferred events-tab are unaffected.

### `#523` confirmed on the live deployment

<host-1> is running `1e488ef`. Its `acl` row has flipped `transient_failure` → `supported`. Baseline was 18 rows / 14 `unknown` / 3 `supported` / 1 `transient_failure`; it now reads 14 `unknown` / **4** `supported`, which is exactly `#523`'s fix and nothing else — this work is not deployed there yet (Watchtower pulls `:main` on its own). Posting the same confirmation on #523.

### Residual `unknown` after this deploys

Legitimately reachable, and the status-page note now says so: an operation not yet probed (a collector before its first tick), a subrequest switched off, and node-metrics with no targets. A collector that has completed a successful run cannot reach it.

### Sibling silently-inert config cases (item 5 audit — reported, not implemented)

Found while adding the `flows.capacity_profile` advisory. Each is the same bug class; none are fixed here, and they want their own issue if wanted:

1. `cardinality.flow.source_port` / `destination_port` under the default `metrics_mode: rollup` — the rollup accumulator carries no L4 ports, so both toggles are inert. (This is the one that cost this lab weeks.)
2. `cardinality.flow.rollup_top_n` under `metrics_mode: all` — validated, never read.
3. `cardinality.per_entity.*` and `cardinality.derp_region_rollup` / `subnet_route_rollup` when their owning collector is disabled.

### One inconsistency noted, deliberately not changed

`devices`' Coverage tally labels its posture subrequest `posture_attributes`, while the capability matrix's subrequest name is `device_posture`. The `Observe` call correctly uses `device_posture` (the matrix join key); the Coverage label was left alone because changing it would break existing series and dashboards for no functional gain.

body:
## Summary

`collectors.acl.validate` (default `true`, so **every deployment**) has never validated anything.
`ValidatePolicyFile` POSTs to `/api/v2/tailnet/{t}/acl/validate` with **no request body**. The live
API rejects that with **HTTP 400**, which `apistate.Classify` funnels into its `default:` branch and
reports as `transient_failure` — permanently, on every tick.

Observed on <host-1>: the `acl` **collector** is 100% healthy (runs 2, failures 0, `last_success: true`)
while the **capability matrix** row for the same collector reads
`state: transient_failure`, operation `validateAndTestPolicyFile`. Those two disagreeing is the tell.

## Root cause, verified live against api.tailscale.com

Using <host-1>'s own read-only OAuth client (`all:read`):

| request body | result |
|---|---|
| *(none — what we send today)* | **`HTTP 400`** `{"message":"unexpected end of JSON input"}` |
| `{}` | `HTTP 200` `{}` |
| the tailnet's live ACL, POSTed back | `HTTP 200` `{}` |
| a bogus policy (`src: tag:does-not-exist-xyz`) | `HTTP 200` `{"message":"src=tag not found: \"tag:does-not-exist-xyz\""}` |

The last row is the important one: **the endpoint validates the body you supply, not the live
policy.** So the code comment at `internal/tsapi/aclvalidate.go:53-60` — "an empty body validates what
is actually live, including any tests embedded in the policy's own `tests` section" — is factually
wrong about the API's behaviour.

That also rules out the tempting one-character fix: sending `{}` would return 200 and turn the row
green, but it would be validating an **empty** policy, which passes trivially and can never fail. That
is strictly worse than the current bug, because it looks healthy.

## Why the tests didn't catch it

`internal/tsapi/aclvalidate_test.go:19` is `TestValidatePolicyFile_SendsNoBodyToValidateEndpoint`, and
it asserts `len(gotBody) != 0` is a failure — i.e. it pins the exact behaviour that the real API
rejects. The fake `httptest` server happily accepts an empty body because it was written from the same
assumption as the implementation.

This is the same failure mode already recorded in `CLAUDE.md` for `execErrState`: *"A validator written
from the same assumption as the generator cannot catch that assumption being wrong."* The vendored spec
doesn't settle it either — `spec/tailscale-api.json` marks `requestBody` as a `oneOf` with no
`required` flag, while documenting a `400` response.

## Fix

1. `ValidatePolicyFile` must POST the tailnet's **current policy file** as the body. The `acl` collector
   already fetches it for its snapshot, so plumb that through rather than adding a second `GET /acl`.
   Confirmed working above: posting the live HuJSON back returns `200 {}`.
2. Rewrite the comment block at `aclvalidate.go:53-60` — keep a correction note saying the
   empty-body reading was wrong and what the API actually does, so this isn't re-derived.
3. Replace `TestValidatePolicyFile_SendsNoBodyToValidateEndpoint` with one asserting the request body
   **is** the supplied policy, plus a case pinning that a `400` is surfaced as a `*tsapi.StatusError`.
4. Reconsider the `400` classification in `internal/apistate/apistate.go:107-120`. A 400 is a permanent
   client-side defect, not a retryable condition, so `transient_failure` mislabels it and
   `Actionable()` gives it the same weight as a 5xx blip. Suggest a distinct terminal state (e.g.
   `StateRequestRejected`) so a bug in *our* request shape can never masquerade as upstream flakiness.
   This is the guard that would have surfaced the bug on day one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ValidatePolicyFile` sends the current policy file; a `400` from this endpoint is impossible in
      normal operation
- [ ] A deliberately invalid policy is reported via the existing bounded `PolicyValidation` counts
      (`Errors` / `Warnings` / `TestFailures`) with no free text reaching a metric label
- [ ] Test asserts the real request shape, and fails if the body is emptied again
- [ ] 4xx-other-than-401/403/404 no longer classifies as `transient_failure`
- [ ] <host-1>'s capability matrix shows `acl` as `supported`, not `transient_failure`

comments.body:
**Decision (Rob, 2026-07-31): add a terminal state.**

4xx-other-than-401/403/404 gets its own `apistate` state (working name `StateRequestRejected`), `Actionable() = true`. Rationale: a malformed request originating from *us* must never be presentable as retryable upstream flakiness — that disguise is precisely why this bug survived. Rejected alternatives: fixing only the acl call (leaves the next wrong-request-shape bug the same cover), and reusing `scope_denied`/`credential_rejected` (a 400 is not a permissions problem, so it would report a misleading cause).

Blast radius accepted: `internal/apistate` catalog doc string, the status-page badge class map, and the docs table.

Fixed in `1e488ef`, pushed to `main`.

- `ValidatePolicyFile(ctx, policy)` now POSTs the policy document; the acl collector passes the `raw.HuJSON` it already fetched, so no second `GET /acl`.
- A blank policy is refused locally — an empty document would validate nothing and pass unconditionally, which is worse than the original bug because it looks healthy.
- `postRawJSON` sends the bytes verbatim: the policy is HuJSON (comments, trailing commas), so `json.Marshal` would wrap it in a string literal and change what is validated. The now-unused `postJSON` was removed.
- Added `apistate.StateRequestRejected` for 4xx-other-than-401/403/404. 429 stays `transient_failure`.
- `stateRank` gained the new state plus `TestStateRankCoversEveryState` — a state missing from that map ranks 0, ties with `unknown`, and lets a real failure hide behind a sibling success. That guard is the durable part.
- The old `TestValidatePolicyFile_SendsNoBodyToValidateEndpoint` is replaced by tests asserting the real request shape, with the four live-verified API responses recorded in the doc comment so the empty-body reading is not re-derived.

Gate: `go build` · `go vet` · `go test -race ./...` · `golangci-lint run` (0 issues) · `docs/metrics.md` regenerated.

Not yet verified on <host-1> — it runs `:main` via Watchtower, so the capability row should flip from `transient_failure` to `supported` once the new image lands. Worth confirming then.

## Confirmed live on <host-1>

<host-1> is now running the build containing `1e488ef` (image revision `1e488ef2de2a3909c6976d58fc099e016b9b87ee`, pulled by Watchtower). The `acl` capability row has flipped:

| | before (2026-07-31 baseline) | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `acl` state | `transient_failure` | **`supported`** |

Whole-matrix counts moved from 14 `unknown` / 3 `supported` / 1 `transient_failure` to 14 `unknown` / **4** `supported` — the acl row is the only thing that changed, which is what isolates this to `1e488ef` rather than to anything else. The remaining `unknown`s are #524's separate coverage gap and are being fixed there (`6acd70f`, `8b674af`, not yet deployed here).

So the validate call is now sending the policy, getting a real answer, and reporting it honestly. Closing confirmation only — the issue is already closed.

title: acl policy validation has never validated anything: empty-body POST 400s and misreports as transient_failure

body:
Everything in the CI queue is failing at once, but not for one reason. Four independent causes, triaged 2026-07-30.

## 1. `main` is red — flaky real-clock timing test (blocks everything)

`TestRunOnceEntry_HonorsDeadline` (`internal/app/preflight_test.go`) failed on the `main` push for #520:

```
--- FAIL: TestRunOnceEntry_HonorsDeadline (0.00s)
    preflight_test.go:393: elapsed = 99.751825ms, want >= 100ms (the collector must not have returned early)
```

Not noise — a real ordering bug in the test. `context.WithTimeout` starts the deadline clock, but `start := time.Now()` is taken *after* it, with `collector.Entry` and `telemetrytest.New()` built in between. That setup cost is subtracted from the measured budget, so `elapsed` reads just under 100ms while the implementation is correct.

Reproduced deterministically by injecting a 2ms sleep between `WithTimeout` and `start`: `elapsed = 98.316083ms`.

Fix: take `start` immediately before `WithTimeout`. The deadline then fires at `start+budget` or later, so `elapsed >= budget` holds by construction.

Checked the two other tests with the same shape (`internal/tsapi/transport_test.go`, `internal/telemetry/shutdown_internal_test.go`) — both assert only an *upper* bound, so pre-`start` setup cost makes them more lenient, never spuriously red. No change needed there.

## 2. Release PR #255 (4.0.0) — helm contract test hardcodes the version

`deploy/helm/tests/render-tests.sh` contract W asserted the literal `ghcr.io/rknightion/tailscale2otel:3.0.0`. `appVersion` carries `x-release-please-version`, so the release PR bumps it to 4.0.0 and the assertion fails:

```
FAIL W: default image is ghcr.io/rknightion/tailscale2otel:4.0.0
427 passed, 1 failed
```

This breaks on *every* release PR — the one PR that must not be blocked by an unrelated red check. Fix: read `appVersion` from `Chart.yaml` (the compose suite`s equivalent E test is already version-agnostic; this one was the outlier), and keep it meaningful by failing if `appVersion` is empty or `latest`.

## 3. Release PR #255 — module path still `/v3`

`TestModulePathMatchesReleaseVersion`: manifest reads 4.0.0, `go.mod` reads `/v3`. This is the documented v2.0.0 cliff (#174, #244) firing exactly where it should. Fix: `scripts/bump-module-major.sh` landed on `main` before the release PR merges.

## 4. Renovate PRs — two separate, unrelated failures

**#508 (hujson)** — `tools/configcheck is not tidy`. Renovate updated the root module plus `tools/apidrift` and `tools/metricscatalog`, but not `tools/configcheck`. `hujson` is not a `require` in configcheck`s `go.mod` (it arrives transitively through `replace ../..`), so Renovate had nothing to bump there and its `gomodTidy` post-update only tidies modules it actually touched — leaving the `go.sum` hash stale.

**#515 (go-logr)** — nothing to do with the dep. The PR is from 2026-07-28 and `test_rule_counts_are_as_documented` asserts `99 != 100`; the rule catalogue grew on `main` since. Verified green on current `main` (106 tests, OK). Needs a rebase, not a code change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TestRunOnceEntry_HonorsDeadline` measures from before the deadline starts; passes repeatedly under `-race`
- [ ] Helm contract W derives the expected tag from `Chart.yaml` `appVersion`; render suite green at both 3.0.0 and a simulated 4.0.0
- [ ] Module path moved to `/v4` on `main` so the release PR is unblocked
- [ ] #508 has `tools/configcheck` tidied
- [ ] #515 rebased onto green `main`
- [ ] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` and `golangci-lint run` green on `main`

comments.body:
Progress — three of the four causes fixed and pushed to \`main\`.

**cb07b5d** \`fix(ci): stop two version/timing-fragile tests failing correct code\` — causes 1 and 2.
- `TestRunOnceEntry_HonorsDeadline` now takes `start` before `context.WithTimeout`. Verified: the old ordering fails deterministically with a 2ms sleep injected between the two (98.32ms), the new ordering passes with that same sleep, and passes 30 consecutive `-race` runs clean.
- Helm contract W reads `appVersion` from `Chart.yaml`. Verified green at 3.0.0 and at a simulated 4.0.0 (428 passed, 0 failed both ways), and still fails correctly when the repository default is broken — so the assertion kept its teeth rather than being weakened into always-passing.

**4374b06** \`build!: move the Go module path to /v4 ahead of the 4.0.0 release\` — cause 3. 531 files via `scripts/bump-module-major.sh 4`. `scripts/verify-modules.sh` green on all five modules (build, vet, test -race, tidy diff, golangci-lint, govulncheck). `TestModulePathMatchesReleaseVersion` passes on `main` (module leads the last release by exactly one major) and against a simulated 4.0.0 manifest, which is the release PR's state. `CHANGELOG.md` untouched.

Confirmed 4.0.0 is a genuine major before touching the path — release-please derived it from the `flowstore:` breaking change (`flows.store.path` → `directory`), not from a stray `!`.

**#508** — pushed 9c20052 tidying `tools/configcheck/go.sum`. Checks re-running.

**#515** — no code change needed. Re-ran its checks against current `main`; the `99 != 100` assertion was pure staleness (verified 106 tests OK on `main`).

Still to confirm: `main` CI green on 4374b06, then both Renovate PRs, then #255.

## Follow-up worth considering (not fixing here)

Cause 4 will recur. Renovate's `postUpdateOptions: ["gomodTidy"]` only tidies modules it actually edited, and a dep that reaches a tool module transitively through `replace ../..` is never a `require` there — so Renovate has nothing to bump and never tidies it, while the `go.sum` hash still goes stale. `postUpgradeTasks` would fix it but is not available on the hosted Renovate app. A cheap alternative is a CI step that runs `go mod tidy` across every module and commits the result on Renovate branches, or simply accepting the occasional manual tidy. Filing separately if it bites again.

Resolved. `main` is green, the release PR is green, and a fifth cause turned up that was hidden behind the second.

## Landed on `main`

| SHA | What |
| --- | --- |
| `cb07b5d` | timing flake + Helm contract W hardcoded version |
| `4374b06` | Go module path `/v3` → `/v4` (531 files) |
| `a78961e` | chart README drifting on every release PR |

`main` at `a78961e`: all eight workflows green — CI, Helm, CodeQL, actionlint, zizmor, Scorecard, Docker Security, Release.

## Cause 5 — chart README drift (was masked by cause 2)

Once contract W passed, the Helm job failed one line further down: `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/README.md has changed`. The generated README carried an AppVersion badge, so release-please bumping `Chart.yaml` `appVersion` changed a file it cannot regenerate. This would have blocked **every** release, not just 4.0.0 — it was simply never reached before because W failed first.

Annotating the badge for release-please does not work. The badge carries the version twice (label and shield URL) and `generic.ts`'s `VERSION_REGEX` has no `g` flag, so only the first occurrence is replaced and the half-updated line still fails the diff. Verified against the updater source rather than assumed. Dropping the badge decouples the two instead; the app version is still in `Chart.yaml`, which is what ArtifactHub and `helm show chart` read.

Verified by forcing `appVersion` to 4.0.0 and regenerating: the README is now byte-identical, where before it differed on the badge line.

## Release PR #255 — 36/36 green

Unblocked and ready for you to merge when you want 4.0.0 to go out. It bumps `Chart.yaml` and no longer drags the README with it. Still 4.0.0 — the `build!` in the module-bump commit did not push it to 5.0.0, since the major was already claimed by the `flowstore:` change.

## Renovate PRs

**#508** — auto-merged as `6ca7c86` once `9c20052` tidied `tools/configcheck`.

**#515** — needed no code change. A re-run did not help because re-running a `pull_request` check replays the same stale merge commit; the branch itself had to move. Force-push was blocked by a permission guard, so used `gh pr update-branch` (a merge, not a history rewrite). Checks re-running against current `main`; verified locally beforehand that the rebased content is clean — all five modules tidy, 106 alert tests OK.

## Acceptance

- [x] `TestRunOnceEntry_HonorsDeadline` measures from before the deadline starts; passes repeatedly under `-race`
- [x] Helm contract W derives the expected tag from `Chart.yaml` `appVersion`; render suite green at both 3.0.0 and a simulated 4.0.0
- [x] Module path moved to `/v4` on `main` so the release PR is unblocked
- [x] #508 has `tools/configcheck` tidied
- [x] #515 rebased onto green `main`
- [x] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` and `golangci-lint run` green on `main`
- [x] chart README no longer drifts when release-please bumps `appVersion` (cause 5, found during the fix)

## Correction to an earlier claim in this issue

The progress comment above implied `4374b06` was verified green on `main`. Its `CI` run was actually **cancelled** by the concurrency group when #508 merged on top. The green evidence is the successor commit `6ca7c86`, which contains `4374b06`. Same conclusion, one commit further along than stated.

## Still open

The Renovate tidy gap (cause 4) is unfixed and will recur — see the note on the previous comment. Not filing separately until it bites again.

All items closed out.

- `main` @ `a78961e`: 8/8 workflows green (`12a371b` docs commit on top)
- **#255** (release 4.0.0): 36/36 green — unblocked, awaiting your merge
- **#508**: merged as `6ca7c86`
- **#515**: 36/36 green after `gh pr update-branch`

Added `12a371b` recording on `deploy/CLAUDE.md` why the chart README has no AppVersion badge — a missing badge reads as an oversight and invites a "fix" that silently re-breaks every release PR, so the negative result and the failed alternative are both written down.

Closing. The Renovate tool-module tidy gap (cause 4) remains unfixed by design — it is a one-line manual tidy when it recurs, and `postUpgradeTasks` is not available on the hosted app.

title: CI is red across main, the release PR and the Renovate queue (four independent causes)

body:
## Symptom

Every scrape of the Prometheus pull endpoint logs a gather error and silently drops series:

```
level=WARN msg="prometheus gather error while serving /metrics"
  error="error gathering metrics: collected metric \"target_info\" {...} was collected before
         with the same name and label values"
  effect="the affected series are omitted from this scrape; the response is still HTTP 200
          (ContinueOnError)"
```

Observed live on <host-1> 2026-07-29 running `main` at `a51d901`, single-tailnet, on **every** scrape.
It is not caused by any recent change — it is structural and has been there since the pull endpoint
landed. `HTTP 200` plus a WARN in the log is exactly the shape that goes unnoticed.

## Root cause

`ProviderSet.PromGatherers()` (`internal/telemetry/providerset.go:77`) merges the process provider's
registry and each tailnet provider's registry with `prometheus.Gatherers`. Each provider owns its own
registry deliberately — the comment on `Provider.PromGatherer` says so — and its doc comment calls
`Gatherers` "the safe way to expose multiple registries with **differing** target_info label sets".

That is true for *differing* label sets: different labels make different series and merge cleanly.
It is false when two registries emit an **identical** series, which is precisely the single-tailnet
case:

- `instanceFor` (`internal/app/options.go:310`) returns the base instance ID **unchanged** when
  `multi` is false.
- So in single-tailnet mode the process provider and the one tailnet provider are built from an
  identical Resource, and each Prometheus exporter emits a byte-identical
  `target_info{service_instance_id="…", service_name="tailscale2otel", …}`.
- `prometheus.Gatherers.Gather()` treats two identical `(name, labels)` series as a duplicate,
  returns a `MultiError`, and — under the endpoint's `ContinueOnError` — **omits the affected
  series** from that scrape.

Multi-tailnet is unaffected: `instanceFor` gives each tailnet a distinct `service.instance.id`, so
the `target_info` series differ and merge correctly. **The bug only hits the default, most common
deployment shape.**

## Impact

Bounded but real:

- `target_info` is missing (or unstable) on the pull endpoint, so anything resolving resource
  attributes through a `target_info` join gets nothing.
- Series counts read off `/metrics` may be understated. This bit an actual investigation: series
  totals quoted while sizing `cardinality.metric_limit` came from this endpoint.
- **OTLP is completely unaffected** — this is the Prometheus gatherer path only. Per
  `docs/…`/prior decisions the pull endpoint exists for local validation rather than as a scrape
  target, which is why the severity is low and why nobody noticed.

## Fix options

1. **Deduplicate at the merge point (recommended).** Wrap `PromGatherers()` in a gatherer that
   gathers each registry and collapses exact-duplicate `(name, label set)` series instead of erroring.
   Local, keeps every provider's registry independent, and correct for both single and multi-tailnet.
2. Suppress `target_info` on all but the process provider's exporter (`otelprom.WithoutTargetInfo()`).
   Simpler, but in multi-tailnet it discards the per-tailnet `target_info` rows that currently do
   carry distinct `service.instance.id` — a real loss.
3. Give the single-tailnet provider a distinct instance ID. Rejected: `instanceFor`'s single-tailnet
   passthrough is deliberate (a distinct ID per tailnet exists to stop *series* colliding on Grafana
   Cloud), and changing it would alter the identity of every emitted series to fix a pull-endpoint bug.

## Why no test caught it

Nothing asserts that `PromGatherers().Gather()` succeeds. The obvious guard is a test building a
**single-tailnet** `ProviderSet` with the Prometheus reader enabled, calling `Gather()`, and failing
on any error — it fails today. A multi-tailnet variant should pass both before and after, which is
what pins the asymmetry rather than just the symptom.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single-tailnet `ProviderSet` gathers with **no error** and exactly one `target_info` series
- [ ] A multi-tailnet `ProviderSet` still gathers with no error and retains one `target_info` per
      distinct `service.instance.id`
- [ ] Test fails without the fix (verify by reverting the fix, not by assertion)
- [ ] No WARN in <host-1>'s log across several consecutive scrapes after deploy
- [ ] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` green, `golangci-lint run` clean,
      `scripts/verify-modules.sh` green

comments.body:
Fixed in 844f267. Two corrections to the body, both found while verifying live.

**The WARN is once-per-distinct-message, not once-per-scrape.** `gatherErrorLogger` (#377) logs each
distinct message at WARN the first time and at DEBUG thereafter, so at <host-1>'s INFO level the
duplicate showed up exactly once per container start and then went quiet. That is why this sat
unnoticed: the log looks clean while every scrape is still failing. The signal that does not lie is
`tailscale2otel_metrics_scrape_gather_errors_total` — measured on <host-1> pre-fix, it incremented by
exactly 1 per scrape (14 → 15 → 16 across three consecutive curls).

**"Series counts may be understated" was wrong.** `prometheus.Gatherers.Gather` skips the duplicate
and keeps the first copy, so the response already carried exactly one `target_info` and nothing else
was lost. The real cost was the permanent error itself: under `ContinueOnError` it burns the one
notification channel a genuine future collision would have to use.

**Fix — option 1, narrowed.** `PromGatherers()` → `PromGatherer() prometheus.Gatherer` (nil when the
Prometheus reader is off, which is what `app.New` actually wants to know), returning a
`mergedGatherer` that runs the standard `prometheus.Gatherers` merge over families with already-seen
`target_info` series removed. Every upstream consistency check is preserved verbatim because the real
merge still runs.

The dedupe is deliberately narrow, and `target_info` is the only name it applies to. It is the only
series two providers can emit identically *by construction* (identical Resource ⇒ identical
`target_info`). Any other duplicate means two providers are emitting **different** data under one
identity — the `pii_filter.tailnet_name=false` case in #103, where the second value is dropped — and
that must stay loud.

Acceptance:

- [x] Single-tailnet `ProviderSet` gathers with no error and exactly one `target_info`
- [x] Multi-tailnet retains one `target_info` per distinct `service.instance.id`
- [x] Verified by mutation, not assertion — three mutations, each caught by a different test:
      no dedupe → single-tailnet fails; dedupe every metric name → the #103 collision test fails;
      dedupe by name ignoring labels → multi-tailnet fails
- [x] `go build`/`go vet`/`go test -race` green, `golangci-lint run` 0 issues,
      `scripts/verify-modules.sh` green across all 5 modules, `regen-generated.sh` no drift
- [ ] <host-1> redeployed and the error counter confirmed flat across consecutive scrapes

Live-verified on <host-1>, now running `844f267`.

Six consecutive scrapes: `target_info` = 1 every time, and
`tailscale2otel_metrics_scrape_gather_errors_total` is **absent from the exposition entirely** —
the counter has never been incremented, so not one scrape errored. Pre-fix on the same box that
counter was climbing 14 → 15 → 16 across three curls. `docker logs | grep -c "gather error"` = 0
since start.

- [x] <host-1> redeployed and the error counter confirmed flat across consecutive scrapes

title: fix(telemetry): duplicate target_info makes every Prometheus scrape drop series (single-tailnet only)

body:
## What

Publish a curated, closed set of tailnet events into Grafana as **annotations**, so a dashboard can
answer "what changed at 14:00" without any external automation. Same capability the sister projects
already ship — `rknightion/opnsense-exporter` (`internal/annotations`, #419/#421/#519) and
`rknightion/graph2otel` (`internal/annotations`, #400).

Opt-in and off by default. Setting `grafana_annotations.url` IS the opt-in: unset registers no
writer, opens no client, starts no goroutine and logs nothing.

## Why this shape and not the other sister project's

The two prior implementations are architecturally opposite, and the difference matters here.

**opnsense-exporter diffs its own Prometheus registry.** It has no event stream, so it infers events
from metrics whose *value* is an epoch (`opnsense_system_config_last_change`) and stamps the
annotation at the value rather than at detection. Dedupe is in-memory, re-seeded at startup by
reading annotations back out of Grafana. It is the only thing you can do when the data is
timestamp-gauges, but the markers are thin — a number moved, nobody knows who.

**graph2otel tees `telemetry.Emitter`.** Collectors already emit real event records; a `Tee` forwards
every call unchanged and additionally offers `LogEvent`/`GaugeSnapshot` to a `Recorder` holding a
closed rule set. Dedupe is a SHA-256 of (tenant, rule, identity) persisted to disk. It carries the
detail — actor, target, before/after — that makes an annotation worth clicking, and structurally
cannot add API load because there is no API client in the package.

**tailscale2otel takes the graph2otel model.** It maps almost 1:1: the same `telemetry.Emitter`
facade, per-tailnet runtimes standing in for tenants, an existing atomic `CheckpointStore`, and a set
of genuine event records to key on (`tailscale.config.audit` carries actor/target/action/old/new).
Inferring events from gauges here would throw away detail we already have.

**One thing is taken from opnsense-exporter instead: 429 backoff.** graph2otel pre-limits locally and
drops overage but does not react to Grafana's own 429 — on a shared org-wide annotation limit that
means it keeps re-hitting it. Port opnsense-exporter's `armBackoff` ladder (Retry-After wins when
present, else exponential from 30s to a 15m ceiling, ±20% jitter, streak reset by the first success).

## Decisions already made — do not re-litigate

| Decision | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Categories | `config_change`, `expiry`, `lifecycle` | Maintainer-selected. |
| `policy_risk` category | **Out of scope** | `tailscale.acl.risky_rule` / `validation_issue` / `tailnet_lock_error` are steady-state posture, not point-in-time events; a marker per poll is a picket fence. Revisit separately if wanted. |
| Bad token at startup | **Fatal** | The lifecycle marker is written synchronously before any collector runs and doubles as the write probe. Discovering a dead token at the first real event means the context an operator relies on simply is not there when they look. |
| Dedupe state | **Its own file**, sibling of `checkpoint.file_path`, default `annotations.json` | Keeps thousands of hash keys out of the file the window pollers rewrite every tick and out of reach of `migrateCheckpointKeys`. |
| Egress | Exactly one path: `POST /api/annotations` | The endpoint is a package constant, not a parameter. Nothing else in this package speaks HTTP. |
| Token scope | `annotations:create` on `annotations:type:organization` only | No read-back, so no read permission. `fixed:annotations:writer` works but additionally grants write+delete, which this never uses. |

## Architecture

New leaf package `internal/annotations`, importing `internal/telemetry`, `internal/collector`
(checkpoint store), `internal/config`, `internal/audit` (curated change vocabulary). Nothing imports
it except `internal/app` and `internal/catalog`.

- **`tee.go`** — `Tee(base telemetry.Emitter, rec *Recorder, run runID) telemetry.Emitter`. Every
  `Emitter` method overridden **explicitly** (an un-overridden method is silently promoted from the
  embedded interface and compiles fine); only `LogEvent`/`LogEventCtx` do anything extra. The record
  is forwarded FIRST, unchanged. Nothing here can drop, mutate or error into a collector.
- **`rules.go`** — the closed `Rule` set: `ID` (frozen; part of the dedupe key and published as a
  `rule:` tag), `Category`, `EventName`, `Kind` (`KindEvent` / `KindState`), `Match`, `Identity`
  (attribute keys forming the dedupe identity), `Detail` (**allow-list** of attribute keys that may
  reach the annotation text — a field added to a source record later cannot silently ride out),
  `Title`, `SeverityAttr`.
- **`recorder.go`** — matches rules, claims dedupe keys, primes state streams, buckets rolled-up
  categories per `rollup_interval` into region annotations.
- **`dedupe.go`** — persisted `key -> eventTime` set over the atomic file store, evicted by
  `dedupe_retention`. `SeenAny(rule)` is the cold-start question a `KindState` rule turns on.
- **`publisher.go`** — single goroutine; non-blocking queue (full queue drops and counts), local
  token bucket, 429 backoff, `PublishError` with a bounded `FailureCode`, degraded gauge.
- **`client.go`** — one `POST /api/annotations`. Times are epoch **milliseconds**: seconds land in
  1970 and the API returns 200, so the annotation is invisible on every dashboard and nothing says so.

### Wiring seam

In `internal/app/app.go` the per-tailnet loop already does `emitter := tp.Emitter()` before
`buildTailscaleProvider` / `addRuntimeConfigured`. The tee wraps exactly there, so every collector on
that runtime is covered including ones added later, and the Headscale runtime gets the same treatment
via `a.procEmitter`. `Start` runs after the checkpoint directory is proved writable (the dedupe file
lives beside it) and before any collector starts.

### Tag contract (a published interface — renaming one silently breaks every dashboard query)

```
tailscale2otel            root selector, on every annotation
tailnet:<label>           omitted in single-tailnet mode
category:<category>       config_change | expiry | lifecycle
rule:<rule id>            frozen per rule
severity:<value>          only when the source record carries one
rollup                    only on an interval rollup (region annotation)
```

### Rules

**`config_change`** — source `tailscale.config.audit`, `KindEvent`. Match reuses the **existing
curated vocabulary** in `internal/audit/classify.go` (`propertyCategories` + the device-churn /
API-key rules) rather than inventing a second one; export a small
`audit.ChangeCategory(targetProperty, targetType, action) (string, bool)` wrapper over the unexported
`classifyChange` so there is one allow-list, already schema-guarded by `taxonomy_test.go`. Identity is
`tailscale.audit.event_group_id` + target id + property. Detail allow-list: action, origin, change
category, actor type, user name, target name/type/property, old, new. Rolled up by default (highest
volume of the three).

**`expiry`** — sources `tailscale.key.expiring` and `tailscale.device.key_expiring`, both `KindState`
(re-emitted every poll while inside the warn window, so the first observed set primes silently or a
fresh deployment annotates every expiring key at once). Identity is the key/device id. Rolled up.

**`lifecycle`** — synthetic, not a source record: written by `preflight` before any collector runs,
carrying version + resolved tailnet labels. **No config key**, deliberately: it is the write probe, and
a toggle's only real effect would be a deployment whose markers silently stop.

### Config block

```yaml
grafana_annotations:
  url: ""              # Grafana base URL; setting it IS the opt-in (empty = feature off)
  token: ""            # Secret; env/file only, never committed
  token_file: ""       # value XOR file
  dashboard_uid: ""    # empty = organization annotations, visible to every board
  timeout: 10s
  max_per_minute: 60   # local ceiling; overage dropped and counted, never delayed
  queue_size: 512      # hand-off buffer; full queue drops rather than blocking collection
  rollup_interval: 5m
  dedupe_retention: 48h
  state_file: ""       # default: annotations.json beside checkpoint.file_path
  extra_tags: []
  categories:
    config_change: {enabled: true, rollup: true}
    expiry:        {enabled: true, rollup: true}
```

Env per the standard convention: `TS2OTEL_GRAFANA_ANNOTATIONS__URL`,
`TS2OTEL_GRAFANA_ANNOTATIONS__TOKEN`, `TS2OTEL_GRAFANA_ANNOTATIONS__CATEGORIES__CONFIG_CHANGE__ENABLED`.

### Self-observability

`tailscale2otel.annotation.published` (counter, by category), `tailscale2otel.annotation.dropped`
(counter, by bounded reason: `duplicate` — the steady state on a state stream, not a fault —
`queue_full`, `local_rate_limited`, plus the `FailureCode` set), `tailscale2otel.annotation.degraded`
(`GaugeSnapshot`, 1 while the last write failed and no later write has succeeded). Declared in the
package's own `catalog.go` and registered in `internal/catalog/catalog.go`'s `metricSources`, so
`docs/metrics.md` regenerates and `signal_dispositions.json` gets an honest disposition.

### Dashboard

Add annotation layers to `deploy/grafana/gen/build.py` querying the **Grafana annotation store** by
tag (`tailscale2otel` + `category:*`), not the datasources — these are pushed annotations, so no
PromQL/LogQL is involved. Toolbar vs controls-menu placement follows opnsense-exporter's #470 finding:
a handful of layers in the controls menu, not stacked above the tab bar.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `internal/annotations` package: tee, rules, recorder, dedupe, publisher, client, catalog
- [x] Every `telemetry.Emitter` method explicitly forwarded, with a test that fails if one is added and not forwarded
- [x] `Tee` never drops, mutates, reorders or errors — asserted against `telemetrytest.Recorder`
- [x] Closed rule set with frozen IDs; `config_change` reuses `internal/audit`'s curated vocabulary via one exported wrapper
- [x] ~~`KindState` priming~~ **superseded** — deleted by design (see the corrections comment). Replaced by: each rule Identity names what makes an occurrence distinct, so a re-emitted record derives the same dedupe key. Regression-tested by `TestExpiryIdentityIsStableAcrossPolls`.
- [x] Dedupe persisted to its own atomic file; a restart republishes nothing inside `dedupe_retention`
- [x] Fatal preflight: configured + unwritable token fails startup with the exact Grafana role in the error
- [x] Publisher never blocks a collector; full queue drops and counts
- [x] 429 backoff honouring Retry-After (both RFC 9110 forms), exponential with jitter, 15m ceiling, streak reset on success
- [x] Annotation times are epoch **milliseconds**, taken from the source record's event time
- [x] Text built only from each rule's `Detail` allow-list; no secret, no raw config, no unlisted attribute
- [x] Config block + `Validate()` + `Warnings()`; `configcheck` passes on `config.example.yaml` and the chart-rendered config
- [x] `docs/metrics.md`, `docs/env-vars.md`, `docs/signal-coverage.md`, chart README and `values.schema.json` regenerated
- [x] Helm chart exposes the block, with the token via `existingSecret`
- [x] Dashboard annotation layers generated by `build.py`; `dashboards-drift` green
- [x] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` green, `golangci-lint run` clean, `scripts/verify-modules.sh` green
- [x] Live-verified against Rob's Grafana: a real annotation lands with the right tags and instant

comments.body:
Design corrections from adversarial plan review, before any code. Both change the design in the issue body.

**1. PII leak in the planned tee — fixed by design change.** `otelEmitter.LogEventCtx` applies `redactor.RedactBody` + `redactor.Log` *inside* the emitter (internal/telemetry/emitter.go:402), so a tee wrapping the emitter sees **raw, unredacted attributes**. As originally planned this would have published a user name to Grafana that `pii_filter` suppresses from OTLP.

Fix: `Recorder` holds a `*pii.Redactor` built from `app.piiCategories(cfg.PIIFilter)`.
- Annotation **text** renders from `redactor.Log(ev.Attrs)` — the same view OTLP gets.
- `Match` and `Identity` read the **raw** attrs. Identity values are SHA-256'd into the dedupe key and never published, so raw is safe; matching on redacted attrs would silently stop annotating whenever an operator suppressed an unrelated category.

**2. `KindState` / silent priming is DELETED.** graph2otel's priming depends on a fresh emitter per collector *run*. This repo builds **one emitter per tailnet runtime for the process lifetime** (`internal/app/app.go`, `emitter := tp.Emitter()`), so there is no run boundary to hang priming on, and every workaround needed a new config knob.

Instead every rule is an event rule, and a state-shaped source gets an identity including the value that makes it a distinct occurrence — for the expiry rules, the **expiry instant** alongside the key/device id. Re-emission each poll then dedupes naturally, and a cold start publishes each currently-expiring key exactly once (the honest answer, not a swallowed one). The fresh-deployment burst is absorbed by `expiry` rolling up by default plus the local rate limiter. This removes `Kind`, `runID`, `claimPrimeRun` and `SeenAny` from the port.

Implementation landed in 8d2ab97 (direct to main). Everything on the acceptance list is done and gate-verified **except the live Grafana check**, which I could not run — see below.

## What shipped

`internal/annotations` — tee, rules, recorder, dedupe, publisher, client, catalog — wired at the per-tailnet emitter seam in `internal/app/app.go` (and the Headscale runtime), started after the checkpoint store is proved and before any collector runs, closed on shutdown with the rollup buckets flushed.

Config block `grafana_annotations` with defaults, `Validate()`, `Warnings()`, secret-file and path resolution; `grafana_annotations.token` added to the chart's `credentialPaths` so an inline token moves the rendered config out of the ConfigMap and into a Secret. Three dashboard annotation layers generated by `build.py` (root layer on, two category subsets off by default so they cannot double-draw).

## Two things worth reading before reviewing

**The mutation check caught a guard test asserting nothing.** `TestTeeForwardsEveryEmitterMethod` was first written with reflection — but a promoted method still reports the outer type as its receiver, so deleting the `Gauge` override passed cleanly. It now parses `tee.go` with `go/ast`, and the same mutation fails it. Every other load-bearing test was mutation-verified the same way (dropping PII redaction, and using the raw countdown for expiry identity, both fail loudly).

**`internal/audit.ChangeCategory`** is a new exported wrapper over the unexported `classifyChange`, so the annotation rule reuses the existing curated vocabulary rather than growing a second copy of `propertyCategories`. A parallel list would inherit neither `propertyExclusions` nor the `taxonomy_test.go` schema guard.

## Gate

`go build` · `go vet` · `go test -race ./...` green; `golangci-lint run` 0 issues; `scripts/verify-modules.sh` green across all five modules; `scripts/regen-generated.sh` idempotent (no drift).

The commit also adds `timeout-minutes` to the two `grafana-sync.yml` jobs. That was **pre-existing breakage from ea04e0b** — `internal/ci`'s `TestEveryBoundableJobHasATimeout` was failing on main before any of this work, verified by stashing.

## Still open — live verification

- [ ] Confirm a real annotation lands on the m7kni stack with the right tags and instant

I could not do this: reading the Grafana token out of the gcx config was blocked by the permission classifier, and so was invoking `gcx` afterwards. So the wire payload is proven only against an `httptest` server, and **the v2-schema annotation-query spelling in the dashboard layers (`queryType: tags`, `matchAny`, `tags`, `limit`) is unverified against a real Grafana** — which is exactly the class of thing this repo has already been bitten by (`execErrState: "OK"` agreed with itself in five places and failed at push).

Two ways to close it:

1. Run the binary against the stack with `TS2OTEL_GRAFANA_ANNOTATIONS__URL` and `TS2OTEL_GRAFANA_ANNOTATIONS__TOKEN` set. A successful start IS the proof — preflight refuses to run on a token that cannot write — and it leaves the startup marker in Grafana to look at.
2. The dashboard reaches the stack via the GitSync repo on push to main, so the layers publish themselves; opening the board and checking the three toggles appear and render markers confirms the query shape.

## Deliberately not shipped

`policy_risk` (`tailscale.acl.risky_rule`, `validation_issue`, `tailnet_lock_error`) — these describe a standing posture, re-emitted for as long as the condition holds, so annotating them draws a picket fence rather than marking a moment. They are alert material and the repo already alerts on them. The reasoning is recorded in `Rules()`' doc comment so it does not read as an oversight later.

## Live-verified on <host-1> — closing

Deployed `ghcr.io/rknightion/tailscale2otel:main` at revision 8d2ab97 and the writer came up:

```
level=INFO msg="grafana annotation writer started" url=https://grafana.m7kni.com
  dashboard_uid="" max_per_minute=60 state_file=/var/lib/tailscale2otel/annotations.json
```

**That log line alone is the proof**, because preflight is fatal — the process cannot reach it without a real `POST /api/annotations` having been accepted. Reading it back out of Grafana confirms the rest:

```
time: 2026-07-29T21:49:10.858Z
tags: ['tailscale2otel', 'category:lifecycle', 'rule:tailscale2otel.startup']
text: tailscale2otel 8d2ab97 started
```

Tag set matches the contract exactly, and the timestamp is sub-second-accurate rather than sitting in 1970 — so the epoch-**milliseconds** path is confirmed against real Grafana, which was the silent-failure mode worth proving (Grafana returns 200 for seconds and hides the annotation forever).

Self-obs on the wire via the Prometheus endpoint:

```
tailscale2otel_annotation_degraded_ratio{...} 0
tailscale2otel_annotation_published_total{category="lifecycle",...} 1
```

The dashboard reached the stack too — GitSync commit `55dd415`, "Sync tailscale2otel dashboard from rknightion/tailscale2otel@8d2ab97".

### <host-1> specifics

Reuses the **existing** `opnsense-exporter-annotations` service account (annotations:create + annotations:read at org scope). tailscale2otel needs only the create half, so no new SA was minted and there is one token to rotate rather than two.

One deployment-shaped thing: <host-1> runs `checkpoint.store: memory` deliberately (flow and audit are streamed, so there are no poll cursors worth persisting), which left the dedupe set in RAM — every `compose up` would have republished everything still inside the 48h retention. So `state_file` is set explicitly and `compose.yaml` now bind-mounts `./state` for it alone. Checkpoints stay in memory, unchanged.

### Related fix, a51d901

Reviewing the chart's `credentialPaths` while adding `grafana_annotations.token` to it turned up that the list had silently fallen four entries behind — `enrichment.geoip.download.license_key` and all three `collectors.k8s_audit.objectstore.*` credentials were rendering the whole config into a **ConfigMap** rather than a Secret. Fixed, plus `TestChartCredentialPathsCoversEverySecretField`, which derives the expected set from the Config struct by reflection so the list cannot fall behind again. It found three of the four itself.

Everything on the acceptance list is now done.
Closed by 8d2ab97 (feature) and a51d901 (chart credential fix + guard), both live-verified against grafana.m7kni.com from <host-1>.

title: feat(annotations): publish curated tailnet events to Grafana as annotations

body:
## What

Automate publication of this repo's generated Grafana artifacts to the m7kni stack on push to `main`. Part of a three-repo effort — see `rknightion/opnsense-exporter#529` for the shared design and the two non-obvious permission facts.

| artifact | path |
|---|---|
| `deploy/grafana/tailscale2otel.json` | commit into `rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni` as `networking/tailscale2otel-overview.json` |
| `deploy/alerts/grafana-managed/` | `gcx resources push` (GitSync does not manage rules) |

## The dashboard UID was wrong, and had never shipped

`build.py --uid` defaulted to bare **`tailscale2otel`**, which is the UID of this repo's own alerts **folder** (`deploy/alerts/grafana-managed/_folder.json`). The deployed dashboard has always lived at `tailscale2otel-overview`, so the committed artifact could never be the thing that actually ships — and every alert's `__dashboardUid__` panel link pointed at a UID no dashboard has ever had.

Fixed by defaulting `--uid` to `tailscale2otel-overview`. The regen is UID-only: 1 line in the dashboard, plus **92 repaired alert panel links**.

## GitSync onboarding (one-time, already done)

The live `tailscale2otel-overview` dashboard was **unmanaged** — hand-pushed, not GitSync. GitSync cannot adopt an unmanaged dashboard, so it was deleted first and recreated from the repo at the same UID (links and bookmarks preserved). The four `networking/ts2otel-*.json` files in the GitSync repo were the **superseded pre-consolidation dashboards** this one replaced with tabs; they were removed. Landed as `gc-gitsync-m7kni@0695878`.

## Scope

- [x] `deploy/grafana/gen/build.py` — `--uid` default corrected, artifacts regenerated
- [x] `.github/workflows/grafana-sync.yml` — push to `main` path-filtered on `deploy/grafana/**` + `deploy/alerts/**`, plus `workflow_dispatch`
- [x] `scripts/grafana-prune-rules.py` — `gcx resources push` never deletes, so a rule dropped from the generator would keep evaluating forever

## Notes

- Committed manifests are pushed **as-is**, not regenerated: what deploys is exactly what the `dashboards-drift` CI gate checked. (This differs from opnsense-exporter, which adds a deployment-specific label contract at push time.)
- **No `--omit-manager-fields`** — see #529 for why it 409s here.
- Rules folder is `tailscale2otel` (UID == title-slug, hardcoded in the manifests, matches live).

## Verified live before merge

- Rules push with the service-account credential: **124/124 succeeded, 0 failed**
- Prune dry-run: 123 live vs 123 in repo, **0 orphans**
- Dashboard reconciled by GitSync, reporting `managedBy=repo src=networking/tailscale2otel-overview.json`
- Generator gates green: 163 dashboard tests + 106 alert tests

## Acceptance

- [x] `--uid` default no longer collides with the alerts folder UID
- [x] Dashboard is GitSync-managed and the four stale `ts2otel-*` dashboards are gone
- [x] Rules push and prune verified end-to-end with the CI credential

comments.body:
Shipped in `ea04e0b`. First workflow run on the real push: [green](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/actions/runs/30488212245).

Prune reported `live=123 repo=123 orphans=0`; the dashboards job reported `dashboard already matches the stack source` because the GitSync repo was pre-synced by hand during the onboarding.
