body:
Follow-up from #474 (`security:SEC-11`), found while fixing the tsapi side.

`internal/hsapi/limit.go:14,29-35` is a line-for-line copy of the pattern #474 replaced: a flat cap (32 MiB) wrapped in an `io.LimitedReader`, with `lr.N == 0` checked only **after** `encoding/json` has already materialized the value. `internal/hsapi/client.go:56` routes every Headscale endpoint through it.

Less severe than the tsapi case only because the cap is 32 MiB rather than 256 MiB, so the blast radius is roughly 100 MiB of live heap instead of ~900 MiB. That is still ~40% of the Helm chart's default 256Mi memory limit, for a body that is being rejected.

## Scope

- Lift `budgetReader` / `decodeBudget` / `BudgetError` out of `internal/tsapi/budget.go` into a shared internal package, or copy them. The tsapi implementation enforces the byte ceiling **and** structural budgets (nesting depth, single-string length, array elements per container) with a byte-level lexer on the read path, so nothing large is allocated before the limit trips.
- Expose `headscale.max_response_bytes` as the operator knob, following the `tailscale.max_response_bytes` precedent (fleet-wide, validated `> 0`, advisory warning above 64 MiB).
- Keep `errors.Is(err, ErrResponseTooLarge)` working for existing callers.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An oversized Headscale response is rejected with bounded measured heap growth, asserted in the test (the tsapi equivalent asserts a 32 MiB ceiling).
- [ ] Deep nesting, a huge single string, a huge array, and a missing `Content-Length` are all bounded.
- [ ] A representative valid Headscale response is still accepted, with measured headroom stated.
- [ ] The budget failure is observable and is not retried in a tight loop.

Note the tracker (#486) records "no further Headscale investment" among rejected directions. This is a memory-safety control on code that already exists and ships, not an expansion of Headscale feature coverage — but it is worth a conscious decision rather than an assumption.

comments.body:
Closed by `15b1038`.

**Measured, same harness as #474:**

| | totalAlloc | live heap at return |
|---|---|---|
| before (32 MiB `LimitedReader`) | 128.0 MiB | **96.6 MiB** |
| after (4 MiB streaming budget) | 16.0 MiB | **12.6 MiB** |

96.6 MiB is ~38% of the chart's 256Mi default, spent on a body being rejected — the estimate in this issue was accurate. The residual 16 MiB after is `encoding/json`'s own read buffer doubling toward the ceiling, not the body being buffered. The test asserts a 24 MiB ceiling rather than 16 MiB because one run measured 16,787,192 B — a 16 MiB assertion would have been flaky.

**Shared package `internal/jsonbudget`**, per the locked decision. Both clients keep their exported sentinels as **identity aliases** and `BudgetError`/`decodeBudget` as **type aliases**, so every existing `errors.Is` and `errors.As` call site is unaffected. Verified: every such call site lives inside `internal/tsapi` or `internal/hsapi` and all are in `_test.go` files — no collector, `internal/app`, `internal/provider` or `hsapi/adapt.go` code depends on them. **Zero tsapi test files were edited**, which is the strongest available evidence the sentinel identity and error shape survived.

Side effect, deliberate and documented: `errors.Is(hsapiErr, tsapi.ErrResponseTooLarge)` is now true, since the sentinel is one object. Harmless — a process runs one control plane — and it is exactly what stops the two guards drifting apart again.

**Headscale gets ONE 4 MiB budget, not tsapi's tiered pair.** All five endpoints (`/api/v1/node`, `/user`, `/preauthkey`, `/apikey`, `/policy`) are snapshot resources; Headscale has no bulk log-pull equivalent, so a 32 MiB log tier would cover nothing. Sized from a fully-populated node list measured at **~715 B/node**, so 4 MiB covers ~5,800 nodes with 3x headroom at 2,000 nodes. Net effect: the default is **tightened 8x** while still clearing every realistic response, and it is now raisable where the old constant was not.

**Bonus fix found while testing — an unbounded post-request drain.** `client.go` did `defer io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)` for connection reuse. Against an endless body that drained until the client timeout: rejecting an oversized response took **30.005 s** of wasted bandwidth per poll — the tight loop this issue's acceptance criteria forbid. Bounded to 64 KiB; the same test now completes in **22 ms**, and the hsapi suite went 30.5 s → 0.47 s. Memory was never at risk (`io.Discard`), only time and bandwidth.

Config: `headscale.max_response_bytes`, default `4194304`, env `TS2OTEL_HEADSCALE__MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`, validated `> 0` only under `provider: headscale`, advisory warning above 64 MiB.

On the #173 scope question raised when filing: this landed as a memory-safety control on shipping code. No Headscale feature coverage was added.

title: internal/hsapi has the same post-hoc JSON decode cap as tsapi did

body:
## Mission

Close the validated public hardening backlog across privacy controls, credential boundaries, redirect handling, Kubernetes secrets, local files, build context, checkpoints, and allocation limits.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P1

- [x] #464 — Reject future-dated object keys before advancing the durable cursor
- [x] #465 — Fail closed for unclassifiable semantic IP values and normalize IPv4-mapped addresses
- [x] #470 — Prevent inline Helm configuration credentials from landing in ConfigMaps
- [x] #472 — Make log-body PII redaction deterministic for overlapping sensitive values
- [x] #474 — Bound API JSON decoding memory below supported deployment limits
- [x] #475 — Git-ignore the documented Compose credential file
- [x] #476 — Exclude local secrets, captures, configs, and checkpoints from Docker build context

### Phase P2

- [x] #466 — Keep Tailscale API bearer credentials on the configured origin across redirects
- [x] #467 — Prevent workload-identity JWT replay across token-exchange redirects
- [x] #468 — Sanitize OAuth token error bodies before retry logging
- [x] #469 — Make `existingSecret` rotation restart or reload affected pods
- [x] #471 — Use randomized symlink-safe temporary files for checkpoint replacement
- [x] #473 — Apply the free-text PII policy to span status descriptions

## Dependencies and sequencing

- This tracker intentionally excludes private draft security advisories; never copy their details into public issues or comments.
- Treat PII-filter behavior and secret-safety promises as testable contracts across every signal and deployment surface.
- Coordinate Helm rotation/config work with EPIC-07 and telemetry credential reload with EPIC-04.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every child issue is closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed stale/unsupported decision.
- [x] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [x] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules, and deployment examples agree with the final contracts.
- [x] Full repository and affected tool-module gates are green at the final integration SHA.
- [x] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail, or follow-up exists only in an agent transcript.

## Audit epic identity

`EPIC-10`

comments.body:
## Execution plan and locked decisions

All 13 child findings were re-confirmed against `main` at `9401181` before any work started. Every premise holds; none were stale.

### Lane split (one owner per file, parallel build)

| Lane | Issues | Owned paths |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | #464 | `internal/collector/objectstore/**` |
| B | #465, #472, #473 | `internal/telemetry/pii/**`, `internal/telemetry/trace.go`, `internal/collector/scheduler.go`, `docs/security.md` |
| C | #466, #467, #468 | `internal/tsapi/{transport,auth,workloadidentity}.go` + new redirect helper |
| D | #474 | `internal/tsapi/{limit,logs}.go`, `internal/config/**`, `config.example.yaml` |
| E | #469, #470 | `deploy/helm/**` |
| F | #471 | `internal/collector/checkpoint.go` |
| G | #475, #476 | `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore`, `deploy/Dockerfile`, `deploy/docker-compose.yaml`, `docs/installation.md` |

Generated artifacts (`docs/metrics.md`, `docs/env-vars.md`, chart `README.md`, `values.schema.json`) have a single owner: a wiring pass after the lanes land, using the pinned tools per `scripts/regen-generated.sh`. No lane regenerates.

### Decisions

**#464 — clock-skew allowance is a fixed 5-minute constant**, not a config key. Keys timestamped later than `now + 5m` never advance the cursor, never enter the seen-set, and never influence the listing lower bound. Skipping is not permanent: the object is picked up on a later cycle once the clock catches up. Rejections are counted on the existing `docSkipped` counter under a new low-cardinality `reason`; object keys never enter a metric label.

**#465 — fail-closed rule.** For a semantic key in `ipValueKeys` with a non-empty but unclassifiable value and no `ipKeyFallback` entry, the value is dropped when any IP category is disabled. A fully-enabled deployment stays byte-identical (the `anyOff` fast path is untouched).

**#472 — deterministic longest-match-first** ordering, tie-broken lexicographically, so the result is independent of Go map iteration order.

**#470 — auto-route to Secret, fail only on genuinely unsafe combinations.** If any credential-bearing key is set inline in `.Values.config`, the whole rendered `config.yaml` moves to a Secret, reusing the existing multi-tailnet mechanism (`secret-config.yaml`) rather than a second one. The ConfigMap path is preserved for credential-free configs. Not a breaking change: an operator setting credentials inline keeps working, their config just stops landing in a ConfigMap.

**#474 — tiered, configurable decode budgets.** Bulk log endpoints default to 32 MiB of wire bytes, all other endpoints to 4 MiB, both settable through the normal `TS2OTEL_*` convention. Structural budgets (decode depth, maximum string length, maximum array element count) are enforced with a streaming token-counting decoder rather than materialising the object graph and checking afterwards. Defaults sized from real captures.

**#469 — documented `rolloutTrigger` value plus the Stakater Reloader annotation as the automated opt-in.**

The `prometheus-config-reloader` / `configmap-reload` sidecar family was evaluated and **rejected for now**. Recording why, because it is not obvious and will otherwise be re-proposed:

- Credentials are delivered by `envFrom: secretRef` (`deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/templates/deployment.yaml:51-53`). Kubernetes never refreshes environment variables in a running container, so a rotated Secret is invisible to the process and no watcher can change that.
- Those sidecars work by watching a mounted *volume* and then signalling the app. That needs two things this repo does not have: file-mounted rather than env-injected credentials, and an in-process reload trigger (SIGHUP handler or an HTTP reload route). `cmd/tailscale2otel/main.go:84` handles only SIGINT/SIGTERM, and the admin mux has no reload route.
- Building that trigger *is* configuration hot reload, which this tracker explicitly parks. So the sidecar path is gated on hot reload landing first; it is recorded as a follow-up, not adopted here.
- Stakater Reloader is different and does work today: it performs a rollout *restart*, so new pods pick up new env values. It is documented as the automated path.

Hard constraint carried from the acceptance criteria: no secret value and no reversible digest of secret content goes into a pod annotation. `rolloutTrigger` is an operator-chosen opaque value, never derived from secret content.

## Phase P1 + P2 completion receipt

Both phases landed together in a single integration commit. All 13 children closed by **`476f236`**, pushed to `main`.

### Receipts

| Phase | Issue | Audit id | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | #464 | SEC-01 | Fixed — 5-minute skew constant, future keys excluded at candidacy |
| P1 | #465 | SEC-02 | Fixed — fail-closed on unclassifiable IP-only keys, `Unmap` + whitespace trim |
| P1 | #470 | SEC-07 | Fixed — inline credentials auto-route to a Secret; chart 0.14.0 |
| P1 | #472 | SEC-09 | Fixed — deterministic longest-first single-pass body redaction |
| P1 | #474 | SEC-11 | Fixed — tiered configurable byte budgets + fixed structural budgets |
| P1 | #475 | SEC-12 | Fixed — `.env` family ignored, unanchored checkpoint/capture rules, hygiene gate |
| P1 | #476 | SEC-13 | Fixed — `.dockerignore` is now a default-deny allowlist |
| P2 | #466 | SEC-03 | Fixed — bearer bound to configured origin, cross-origin redirects refused |
| P2 | #467 | SEC-04 | Fixed — shared redirect policy on the token-fetch client |
| P2 | #468 | SEC-05 | Fixed — bounded error classification, one sanitizer for logs and telemetry |
| P2 | #469 | SEC-06 | Fixed — `rolloutTrigger` + Reloader annotation; sidecar deferred to #492 |
| P2 | #471 | SEC-08 | Fixed — randomized `O_EXCL` staging file in the destination directory |
| P2 | #473 | SEC-10 | Fixed — span status descriptions under the free-text policy, centrally |

No child was closed stale or unsupported. Every premise was re-confirmed against `9401181` before implementation and every one held.

### Scope expansions found during implementation

Four findings were **wider than the issue text**, and the fixes cover the larger surface:

- **#466** — Go forwards `Authorization` to a *subdomain* match, so `api.tailscale.com` → `evil.api.tailscale.com` would have carried the key even without the custom transport. Subdomains are now distinct origins.
- **#467** — the OAuth client-credentials path has the identical defect, replaying the client secret in the same form body. The issue named only workload identity. Also, 301/302/303 were not harmless: the exchange completed against the attacker-named origin and returned its `access_token`.
- **#468** — the token-URL userinfo leak was not confined to the DEBUG path. `sanitizeTransportError` interpolated `url.Error.URL` unmodified, so it also reached span statuses and the admin status page.
- **#473** — a second bypass exists at `internal/tsapi/transport.go:302`. Fixed centrally in the exporter rather than per call site, so it covers sites in files no lane owned.
- **#475** — the audit undercounted. Four further paths matched no rule (`deploy/checkpoints.json`, `checkpoints/state.json`, `deploy/checkpoints/state.json`, `deploy/.capture/devices.json`), because the anchored rules never matched one level down — including the `deploy/checkpoints/` bind-mount the compose file documents beside itself.

### Corrections to premises

- **#471** implied durability work was needed. It was already correct: the file and the parent directory were both already fsynced. What was actually missing was **cleanup** on error paths. Separately, this was also an *availability* bug — concurrent savers sharing one temp path lose a checkpoint outright.
- **#465** — only prefix-based ranges were affected by the missing `Unmap`; loopback and link-local already classified correctly via netip's own predicates.
- **#475** — this issue's own acceptance command, `git check-ignore -v --no-index -- deploy/.env`, is **not a sound test**: `-v` exits 0 even when the matching rule is a `!` negation. The check gates on `-q` instead.

### Deviations

- **#474** specified a `json.Decoder.Token()` loop. Rejected after checking `go doc`: `Token` materializes each string before it can be measured and `Decode` buffers the whole top-level value, so both allocate exactly what the fix prevents. A byte-level lexer on the read path was used instead — that is what produced 896 MiB → 12 MiB live heap.
- **#469** — the `prometheus-config-reloader` / `configmap-reload` sidecar family was evaluated at the maintainer's suggestion and rejected. It needs file-mounted credentials (the chart uses `envFrom`, and Kubernetes never refreshes env in a running container) and an in-process reload trigger, and building that trigger is configuration hot reload, which this tracker parks. Deferred to #492.

### Follow-ups filed

- #488 — `internal/hsapi/limit.go` has the identical post-hoc decode cap bug
- #489 — token-endpoint 401/403 still retried despite being classified non-retryable
- #490 — promote `error.type` to `internal/semconv`
- #491 — checkpoint staging file not swept after a hard process kill (deliberate gap in #471)
- #492 — config-reloader sidecar, gated on hot reload

### New guards, so a future red build is not misread

- `TestBoundedStatusDescriptionsCoverEveryLiteralSetStatus` walks the repo for literal `SetStatus(codes.Error, "…")` and fails if it is not in the admit-set. **Red means the guard worked**; the fix is one line in `internal/telemetry/pii/statusdesc.go`.
- `scripts/check-secret-hygiene.sh` — blocking, in the existing `docker-build` job.
- `deploy/helm/tests/render-tests.sh` — 101 assertions, in the existing helm lint job.

Both were added to **existing** jobs on purpose. Both are already in `ci-success`'s `needs`, so they become blocking without a branch-ruleset change — this repo has previously had every bot PR stall when a required check name changed.

### Gate at the integration SHA

Verified green after rebasing onto `5877cb8`, with the Go build and test caches cleared first (an earlier run reported three `gosec` hits that turned out to be stale cache entries from a deleted verification worktree, not repo code):

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...` — clean
- `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues, root + `tools/configcheck` + `tools/metricscatalog` + `tools/apidrift`
- `govulncheck ./...` — no vulnerabilities (no dependency changed)
- `helm lint` — 0 failed; `render-tests.sh` — 101/101
- `check-secret-hygiene.sh` with `HYGIENE_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1` — PASS, including a real image build
- `configcheck` on `config.example.yaml` and the chart-rendered config — OK
- `metricscatalog -check` — in sync

All four generated artifacts regenerated with the pinned tools (`helm-docs` 1.14.2, `helm-values-schema-json` v2.5.0).

### Incidental fix

The regeneration command in `internal/catalog/docs_test.go`'s failure message named `go run ./tools/metricscatalog -write`, which **fails** from the repo root because `metricscatalog` is a separate module — the exact gotcha `CLAUDE.md` documents. Anyone hitting that drift was being handed a broken command. Corrected in the same commit.
All 13 children closed by `476f236` and both phase receipts posted. Follow-ups tracked as #488, #489, #490, #491, #492. Definition of done met.

## Follow-up receipt

The five follow-ups this tracker filed are resolved. Four closed by `15b1038` (CI green); one stays open by design.

| Issue | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| #488 | Fixed — budget lexer lifted into `internal/jsonbudget`, shared by both clients; Headscale 96.6 MiB → 12.6 MiB live heap |
| #489 | Fixed — terminal token-endpoint failures no longer retried |
| #490 | Fixed — `error.type` promoted to `semconv.AttrErrorType` |
| #491 | Fixed — age-guarded startup sweep of orphaned checkpoint staging files |
| #492 | **Open and blocked**, correctly — needs configuration hot reload, which this tracker parks |

Two things found while doing them that were not in the original scope:

- **#488 turned up an unbounded post-request drain in hsapi.** `defer io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)` drained an endless body until the client timeout, so rejecting an oversized response cost **30 seconds** of wasted bandwidth per poll — the tight loop #474's acceptance criteria forbid, on the sibling client. Capped at 64 KiB; the same test now completes in 22 ms.
- **#490 was not just a rename.** The `error.type` key is shared between collector scrapes and OTLP export, but the value sets are different (`panic|timeout|error` vs `export|timeout`). The constant now documents both and says not to merge them — otherwise the natural next step is to "tidy" them into one enum, which would be wrong.

One claim I checked and rejected rather than acting on: an implementation note suggested `x/oauth2` flattens token-fetch transport errors with `%v` before this repo's `redactURL` can act, and proposed a sixth issue. It does not — `internal/token.go:261` returns the transport error unwrapped, and the `%v` at `:266` handles only the body-read error, which carries no URL. The existing #468 userinfo assertion already proves redaction works. No issue filed.

**#492 is the only outstanding work from EPIC-10.** It is gated on configuration hot reload getting its research/design issue first, per this tracker's binding decision on parked items. Nothing is broken meanwhile — `rolloutTrigger` and the Stakater Reloader annotation from #469 both handle rotation today; #492 is the nicer answer (no restart at all), not the only one.

## Mission

Time-box credible ecosystem additions, gather enough current evidence to accept or reject them, and only promote experiments that preserve privacy, bounded cardinality, supportability, and a clear operator use case.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P3

- [ ] #459 — docs(ecosystem): submit tailscale2otel to Tailscale Community Projects
- [ ] #460 — research(aperture): ingest privacy-safe usage aggregates from Tailscale Aperture S3 exports
- [ ] #461 — feat(flowlogs): add optional local GeoIP and ASN enrichment
- [ ] #462 — research(tsrecorder): determine whether safe session metadata can be exported

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Research issues may close with a documented no-go decision; implementation is not the required outcome.
- Do not resurrect Headscale expansion, native syslog ingestion, OTLP profiles, OpAMP, peer-relay control APIs, or other rejected #173 directions.
- Any adopted signal needs an explicit PII, cardinality, licensing, freshness, and failure-mode contract.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every child issue is closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed stale/unsupported decision.
- [ ] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [x] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules, and deployment examples agree with the final contracts.
- [x] Full repository and affected tool-module gates are green at the final integration SHA.
- [ ] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail, or follow-up exists only in an agent transcript.

## Audit epic identity

`EPIC-09`
