## Tracker started — prerequisite satisfied, P1 reconnaissance under way

#478 is closed: all 24 of its children are done, with the phase receipt and definition-of-done
evidence on that issue. The binding order's precondition for starting here is therefore met.

Baseline for this tracker: `639ca34`, all nine workflows green for that exact SHA, working tree clean,
`main == origin/main`. Release-please PR #255 remains open and unmerged — no release will be published
from this tracker unless a selected child explicitly requires it and Rob approves.

### First reconnaissance wave (read-only, three lanes)

Dispatched before writing any code, because several of these children were filed against
`9401181` and the audit's premises need re-confirming against current `main` — three of #478's
children turned out to rest on premises that had since changed, and one of its issues asserted the
exact opposite of a passing test.

| Lane | Children | Question it must answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | #431, #432 | What `internal/oas` parses and drops today; which 3.1/composition constructs actually OCCUR in the vendored spec (counts), so #431 is sized against reality rather than the standard; which of the four #432 drift dimensions are already partly covered |
| B | #436, #437, #438 | A 4×5 module-verification matrix (root + three tool modules × build/vet/race/lint/govulncheck) with workflow anchors; what is generated under `deploy/` and ungated; whether `deploy/grafana/gen/build.py` is even deterministic enough for a fail-on-diff gate; a TRUE/FALSE audit of every claim the README's API-drift section makes |
| C | #442, #443 | The real asset set per release and its publish ordering; the observed asset completeness of the last three releases from `gh release` data; whether a fixable high-severity image can be pushed and tagged today |

All three lanes are strictly read-only and are forbidden from touching #255 or dispatching any
workflow.

### What I have already established directly

Two P1 children not in the recon wave, scoped by direct inspection:

- **#434 (native fuzzing) is partly stale.** Go fuzz targets already exist and already run in CI —
  `ci.yml:226` runs a bounded 120s matrix over `FuzzExtractRecords`, `FuzzParseHECTime` and the two
  `FuzzProcessorProcessAll` targets in `internal/{stream,audit,flowlog}`. What is genuinely missing is
  what the issue names first: **no fuzz target covers webhook envelope/data decoding** (the
  `decodeAcceptedBatch`/`decodeEvent` path at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:703,891`) or **OAS 3.1
  schema parsing/classification**, and there is no longer scheduled run. Scope shrinks to adding those
  targets plus a scheduled lane, not building fuzzing from scratch.
- **#433 (boundary fixture matrix) is real and well-bounded.** The harness already exists
  (`contract.ByID` + `contract.Decode`), but `TestFuzz_EdgeVariants`
  (`internal/tsapi/contract/fuzz_test.go:86`) covers five edge shapes for exactly **one** operation,
  `listTailnetDevices`. There are **18 consumed operations** in `operation_dispositions.json`. The work
  is generalising that one case into a table over 18 ops × the boundary kinds the issue lists, failing
  per operation with a manifest entry — not new infrastructure.

### Ordering intent

Sequenced on the tracker's own dependency note. #436 and #437 come first: they establish what CI
actually verifies, and every later child's "add a gate" claim is only meaningful once that is written
down. #431 precedes #432, since detecting new drift dimensions is worth little if the parser still
drops the constructs those dimensions live in. #442/#443 are release-path work and stay last in P1,
because they are the only children whose verification could plausibly want a real release action —
which needs Rob's approval, not mine.

Receipts follow per child.

## Checkpoint — P1 half done, five children closed

Baseline: `607b32a` (CI in flight at the time of writing; every prior SHA below reached terminal
success on all applicable workflows before the next was pushed). Working tree clean,
`main == origin/main`. Release-please PR #255 still open, unmerged, no release published.

### Closed here

| Child | Commit | Substance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #436 | `54caa5e` | README claimed **weekly** for two lanes whose crons are **daily**. Guard test now reads the workflow files, so the prose is load-bearing. |
| #437 | `dad27b1` | `module-verify` matrix + local `scripts/verify-modules.sh`. Found `tools/configcheck/go.sum` **82 lines** short of tidy and three ROOT `go.mod` requirements marked `// indirect` while imported directly. |
| #438 | `8ee2ac5`, `a855dc7` | Drift gate for the two generated Grafana artifacts + `promtool check rules` + structural rule validation + counts pinned. Found the flagship dashboard grouping by `tailscale_user_invite_accepted`, **a label emitted nowhere**, and the README claiming 79 rules against a file holding 85. |
| #443 | — | Closed **out of scope** by maintainer decision: the gap is real and confirmed, but both the Trivy scan and the image push live in `rknightion/.github`. Full evidence and the shape of the eventual fix are on the issue. |
| #431 | `607b32a` | 3.1 type arrays were unparsed, and `Classify`'s guard meant a type change on any nullable field was **undetectable**. 22 fields and 8 typed maps now modeled; only 3 deliberately-loose `anyOf` nodes remain untyped. |

Every commit was gated in a throwaway worktree holding only its own diff, `cmp`-verified against the
staged tree.

### The pattern across all five

Four of the five turned up a **defect that no test, lint or gate could have caught**, because in each
case the only thing asserting the fact was English prose or an absent check: a cadence sentence, a
`// indirect` marker, a dashboard label, a rule count. That is why each fix ships an assertion rather
than just a correction — `internal/ci/workflowcontract_test.go` and
`internal/catalog/dashboardrefs_test.go` exist so these cannot silently drift back.

### Corrections to my own work, recorded rather than quietly fixed

- **I closed #438 early**, with three scope bullets outstanding. Reopened and finished.
- **I wrote an invented SHA256** into the first draft of the promtool install step. Replaced with
  verification against the release's own published `sha256sums.txt`, tested end to end.
- **Three of my own tests initially passed while proving nothing** — a `metricscatalog` drift test
  editing a hand-written region rather than a generated one; a `module-verify` step assertion satisfied
  by a command name inside an error message; a drift-gate negative control that tampered only the
  working tree, which regeneration undoes. Each is fixed with the escaped mutation named in the test
  comment.
- **My first Grafana structural test reported twelve false defects**, requiring a condition and summary
  of every rule; the twelve recording rules correctly have neither.

### Remaining P1 — state and sizing, so this needs no re-derivation

- **#432** (parameter / request-body / success-status / media-type drift) — **greenfield.** `oas.Operation`
  has no `Parameters` field; `parseResponseSchema` hardcodes `responses["200"]`; `extractJSONSchema`
  hardcodes `content["application/json"]`. Nothing partially covers any of the four. Anchors:
  `internal/oas/oas.go:37-42` (Operation), `:190-210`, `:214-244`; `classify.go:8-27` (ChangeKind, extend
  following the existing pattern). #431's parser work lands underneath it, which is why it was sequenced
  second.
- **#433** (boundary fixture matrix) — real but bounded, **not new infrastructure.** The harness exists
  (`contract.ByID` + `contract.Decode`); `TestFuzz_EdgeVariants`
  (`internal/tsapi/contract/fuzz_test.go:86`) covers five edge shapes for exactly **one** of the **18**
  consumed operations. The work is generalising that into a table over 18 ops × the boundary kinds,
  failing per operation.
- **#434** (native fuzzing) — **partly stale.** Fuzzing already exists and already runs in CI
  (`ci.yml:226`, bounded 120s matrix over 4 targets). Genuinely missing: no target covers **webhook
  envelope/data decoding** (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:703,891`) or **OAS 3.1 schema
  parsing/classification**, and there is no scheduled long run. Scope is adding those, not building
  fuzzing.
- **#442** (atomic release visibility) — real. Three job chains publish in parallel with no ordering and
  no completeness check, all uploads use `--clobber`, and nothing reads the release back. Confirmed from
  live data: **v2.0.1 is a second incomplete release** beyond the known v2.0.0 (#174) — missing
  `SHA256SUMS.intoto.jsonl`, which v2.0.2 and v3.0.0 both have, because the provenance step is fail-soft
  and skipped silently. Maintainer decision: **fix forward** (make the step fail loudly + add a
  post-release completeness gate); do not investigate the historical run, do not backfill v2.0.1. Note
  the fail-soft step itself is in `rknightion/.github`'s `binaries.yml`, so the local half is the
  read-back gate.

P2/P3 (#435, #439, #440, #441, #444, #445, #446) untouched.

### Standing constraints still in force

Work straight on `main`, one commit per child with `Closes #N`, push immediately, wait for every
workflow on the exact SHA before the next push (`ci.yml` uses `cancel-in-progress`, so a back-to-back
push cancels the previous SHA's CI — this bit earlier in the programme and needed serialised
`gh run rerun` to repair). Do not merge #255 or publish a release without Rob's approval.

CI confirmation: all seven applicable workflows green for `607b32a`, the checkpoint baseline above — actionlint, CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Release, Scorecard, zizmor. (Helm and docs-sync correctly did not trigger: no chart or docs path changed in #431.) Working tree clean, `main == origin/main`, no worktrees or stashes outstanding. Nothing is in flight.

## Checkpoint — P1 is one child from done, pausing here

Baseline: `6165a55`. Working tree clean, `main == origin/main`, no worktrees, no stashes, nothing in flight. **All seven applicable workflows green for that exact SHA** (actionlint, CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Release, Scorecard, zizmor — Helm and docs-sync correctly untriggered). Release-please PR #255 still open, unmerged, no release published.

### Closed since the last checkpoint

| Child | Commit | Substance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #432 | `ffb7a95` | Parameters, success statuses and media types were **entirely unmodeled**. 34 parameters on consumed operations — 30 of them `$ref`s, 30 declared at the path-item level, so a parser reading only inline `operation.parameters` sees four. 16 new change kinds on three severity axes. `parseResponseSchema` hardcoding `"200"` was not merely incomplete: a status moving emptied the response schema and reported every field as removed. |
| #433 | `f880ffe` | Boundary matrix over every consumed operation × 8 shapes, derived from each operation's own schema. **Found two real defects**: `listUsers` and `listWebhooks` decoded via tsclient's `map[string][]T`, so any additive top-level key failed the entire call and the collector would go dark on a benign upstream change. |
| #434 | `6165a55` | Five fuzz targets for the two uncovered untrusted-input paths (webhook batch decode + digest, OpenAPI parse/classify), a weekly 15-minute scheduled lane, and a guard that every target runs in both matrices. |

Each was gated in a throwaway worktree holding only its own diff, `cmp`-verified against the staged tree, and each SHA reached terminal success on every applicable workflow before the next push.

### The pattern, continued

The earlier checkpoint noted that four of five children turned up a defect no test or gate could have caught. That held again, and sharpened: **#432 and #433 each found a live defect that a *passing* test suite was actively concealing** — a drift dimension that could not be detected at all, and two decoders that fail on additive change. In both cases the fix ships the assertion, not just the correction.

Verification against reality rather than fixtures also earned its keep twice. #432's classifier was run against the **live** spec (no drift, no false positives) and then against a copy with five changes injected (all five classified at the intended severity). #433's must-error expectation was probed against all 18 operations before being asserted, rather than assumed.

### Corrections to my own work, recorded rather than quietly fixed

- **My pre-implementation measurement for #432 was wrong.** A probe that did not resolve `$ref`s reported 3 enum-carrying parameters; there are 4 (`logType` arrives via its `$ref`'d schema). The census test corrected it.
- **#432's first determinism test could not fail.** The sort-key mutation survived it. Fixed with a second test placed where instability actually bites — `Classify` appends in map-iteration order.
- **#433's first draft reported four decoder failures that were all my own bug.** Injecting the additive key into a *typed map*, where every key must carry the map's value type, builds a wrong-shape body and calls it additive. Isolating that is the only reason the two real findings were visible.
- **#434's first guard test reported eight fuzz targets where there are nine.** It keyed on the target NAME, and `FuzzProcessorProcessAll` exists in both `internal/flowlog` and `internal/audit`.

### Remaining P1: #442 only

**#442 (atomic release visibility)** — real, and Rob's decision is already recorded: **fix forward only**. Make the fail-soft provenance step loud and add a post-release completeness read-back gate. Do **not** investigate v2.0.1's historical Actions run and do **not** backfill the published release. Note the fail-soft step itself lives in `rknightion/.github`'s `binaries.yml`, so the half that belongs in this repo is the read-back gate.

After #442, P1 is complete and the tracker moves to P2/P3: #435, #439, #440, #441, #444, #445, #446 — all untouched.

### Standing constraints still in force

Work straight on `main`, one commit per child with `Closes #N`, push immediately, wait for every workflow on the exact SHA before the next push (`ci.yml` uses `cancel-in-progress`, so a back-to-back push cancels the previous SHA's CI). Do not merge #255 or publish a release without Rob's approval. Do not hand-edit generated files. Mutation-test every new guard — a guard that cannot fail is theatre, and three of mine this session initially passed while proving nothing.

## Resuming this tracker — P1's last child plus all of P2/P3

Baseline `5eead5b`, working tree clean, `main == origin/main`. EPIC-05 (#481) closed in the interim, so this tracker is the active one. Eight children remain: #442 (last of P1), then #435, #439, #440, #441, #444, #445, #446.

Release-please PR #255 remains open and unmerged. No release will be published from this tracker without Rob's approval, per the standing constraint on the previous checkpoint.

### Premise re-validation — all eight re-checked against current `main` before any code

Four read-only recon lanes ran first, because this tracker has already had children whose premises had moved since they were filed. Results:

| Child | Premise | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #439 | workflows lack timeouts/concurrency/retry | **CONFIRMED, worse than filed.** Of 15 workflows, exactly **one job** in the entire tree has a `timeout-minutes` (`live-contract.yml:27`). 4 have a `concurrency:` block. There is **no retry logic anywhere** — the `\|\| code=$?` patterns throughout are error-code capture for classification, not retries. |
| #440 | committed IANA data is stale | **CONFIRMED against the live registry.** The committed CSV was generated exactly once (`0835122`) and never regenerated. The live registry has `bencher,6610,tcp` + `bencher,6610,udp` (registered 2026-06-17) and `snif,7123,udp` (2026-07-22); all three are absent locally. `gen.go`'s filter is not a curated allowlist, so nothing excludes them by design — it is pure staleness. |
| #435 | matrix legs can race to create duplicate issues | **CONFIRMED.** `report-drift/action.yml:38-45` is a plain check-then-act on `gh issue list --label ... --state open` with no lock, and `clientlib-main.yml` is the only caller with a matrix (`ref: [main, latest]`, `fail-fast: false`) sharing one label. Two failing legs can both see `existing=""`. |
| #442 | releases are visible before assets are complete | **CONFIRMED, and the incomplete set is wider than filed.** `.goreleaser.yaml:110` sets `draft: false`; release-please creates the release visible immediately and three independent actors then attach assets in parallel with no ordering. Live asset audit: **v2.0.0** has no archives/checksums/signature/provenance at all (#174); **v2.0.1 and v1.0.0** are each missing only `SHA256SUMS.intoto.jsonl`. v2.0.2 and v3.0.0 are complete at 16 assets. |
| #441 | no performance regression gates | **CONFIRMED.** Nine `Benchmark*` funcs exist; `rg -- '-bench' .github/workflows/` returns nothing. None is gated. |
| #444 | free-form issue routing | **CONFIRMED.** Two legacy `.md` templates, no `config.yml`, no forms. (Also: `feature_request.md` has shipped a `[FEAUTRE]` title typo.) Nothing in the repo parses issue bodies, so a form change has no programmatic consumer to break. |
| #445 | no doc-command smoke tests; `secrets.*` typo live | **CONFIRMED and narrowed.** The typo is in exactly one place, `README.md:94-95` (`--set-string secrets.…` against a chart whose real key is `secret:`, `values.yaml:155`). `docs/installation.md` and `NOTES.txt` already use the correct singular. No workflow executes any command copied from README or docs. |
| #446 | no scheduled opportunity review | Deferred to last (P3); premise unexamined so far. |

### Corrections to the issues as filed

- **#440 understates the scope.** It names three missing entries; the real finding is that the artifact has never been regenerated since introduction, so the gap is whatever IANA has accumulated since. Also, contrary to the issue's framing, TCP 7123 *is* present (`snif`) — only the UDP half is missing.
- **#442's framing implies v2.0.1 is broken like v2.0.0.** It is not: v2.0.0 produced no binaries at all, v2.0.1 is missing one provenance file, and the same file is missing from v1.0.0 — so that gap belongs to a pipeline era, not a single release. Rob's fix-forward decision stands; no backfill.
- **#439 has an out-of-repo boundary that must be stated rather than worked around.** Ten jobs across seven workflows are `uses:` calls to reusable workflows, and GitHub does not permit `timeout-minutes` on a `uses:` job. Six of those target `rknightion/.github`. Those jobs will keep the implicit 6h default until that repo is changed; the local half can only cover the jobs that have real `steps:`.

### Why #439 goes first

Not hygiene. A job with no timeout that hangs holds a runner slot against the account-wide Free-plan concurrency cap, which is shared across every `rknightion` repo — a hung Renovate burst in a sibling repo has previously starved this repo's CI to a standstill with everything showing green-but-queued. Fourteen of fifteen workflows are currently in that state, including the ones that fetch untrusted upstream code (`clientlib-main.yml:45`, `go get ...@main`).

Order from here: #439, #440, #435, #442, #444, #445, #441, #446.

## Tracker complete — all children closed, P1 through P3

Final SHA `cfc60b9`. Working tree clean, `main == origin/main`. **All seven applicable workflows green for that exact SHA** — CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Release, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor. (Helm correctly did not trigger; no chart path changed.) Release-please PR #255 remains open and unmerged, and no release was published from this tracker.

### Closed in this phase

| Child | Commit | Substance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #439 | `d3cd115` | 21 job timeouts, 11 concurrency blocks, bounded retry on the two transient fetches. |
| #444 | `ea9f9bf` | Four issue forms with dropdowns derived from the real config surface, plus security routing. |
| #441 | `700e974` | Eight benchmarks over the flow/cardinality hot paths and an allocation budget gate. |
| #440 | `a0fdd75` | Regenerated the IANA table; monthly advisory freshness lane. |
| #435 | `b695f27` | Matrix verdicts aggregated before upsert, in **two** lanes. |
| #442 | `3c413e1` | Post-publish release completeness gate. |
| #445 | `123fe72` | Documented install commands validated against the generated schemas; README typo fixed. |
| #446 | `cfc60b9` | Changelog review lane with a decision baseline that records negative verdicts. |

### Findings beyond the filed scope

Four things turned up that no issue named:

- **A second instance of #435's race, in a lane scoping had explicitly cleared.** `fuzz-scheduled.yml` runs a **nine**-target matrix that also called report-drift per leg. One broken shared decode helper crashes several targets at once, which is exactly when it would have filed several issues for one defect. It was found by writing the guard against the *class* rather than the instance; reading had ruled it out.
- **The `area: api` label in the new API-drift form was unquoted**, so YAML parsed it as a mapping rather than a string. Every label in this repository's taxonomy contains a colon, and GitHub would simply never have applied it, with no error anywhere. A "does it parse" validator is happy with this.
- **`ts2o`-style measurement traps in #441.** `allocs/op` is not stable across benchtime — `BenchmarkProcess_RawMode` reports 227 at `-benchtime 200x` and 112 at the ~90000 iterations a default run reaches — so a gate wired to a short benchmark measures warm-up and "regresses" whenever the runner picks a different iteration count. The budgets use `testing.AllocsPerRun` instead and ride the existing `go test -race` leg.
- **`v1.0.0` is incomplete too.** #442 named v2.0.0 and v2.0.1; v1.0.0 is missing the same `.intoto.jsonl`, so that gap belongs to a pipeline era rather than to one release. Fix-forward stands; nothing backfilled.

### Corrections to my own work, recorded rather than quietly fixed

- **The retry helper shipped fail-OPEN in its first draft.** Written as `if "$@"; then ...; fi` followed by `status=$?`, the capture reads the status of the `if` construct, which is 0 whenever the else-branch runs — so every failure was reported as success. It reads correctly. Only the failing test case exposed it, which is the entire argument for negative-testing a gate.
- **Three separate guard tests initially passed while asserting nothing**, all the same way: a substring search over workflow text matching an unrelated line. `-raw` matched the filename `iana-raw.csv`; `scripts` matched `scripts/regen-generated.sh` on a different step; and the second attempt at fixing that one split on `- name:` in a string that contains only `run:` bodies. Each is now anchored to the invocation or scoped to the step, with the negative test shown to fire. Substring assertions over YAML are reliably weaker than they look.
- **My first negative test for the allocation budget did not fire, and the gate was right.** `_ = make([]byte, 64)` is eliminated by the compiler; it needed a package-level sink to escape. Once it did, 50 injected allocations took raw from 112 to 162 and failed the budget as intended.
- **#446 was largely already delivered.** `operation_dispositions.json` (#423) already classifies all 90 published operations with mandatory notes and a gate that rejects an empty disposition, and the operation-set classifier already runs daily — so the "record decisions, keep speculative APIs out of runtime" requirement was met. Only the changelog dimension was genuinely missing, and that is what shipped. The client-metric and log-destination doc dimensions are not implemented: they have no machine-readable form, and log-destination drift is already tracked as #354 under a different tracker.

### Deliberately not done

- **Ten jobs remain unbounded and cannot be fixed here.** They are `uses:` calls to reusable workflows, and GitHub rejects `timeout-minutes` on that job form outright — verified by actionlint, not assumed. Six target `rknightion/.github`. They keep the implicit 6-hour default until that repository is changed. The exemption set is frozen in the guard test and checked in both directions, so this is recorded rather than hidden.
- **#341 is not closed.** #445 fixed its typo half and gated it; its larger half — quick starts that put credentials inline on the command line, into shell history — is untouched and stays open under #483. Noted on that issue.
- **Two of the eight new benchmarks are measurement-only, not gated.** HEC decode round-trips an httptest server whose goroutine allocations are attributed unpredictably (265–383 allocs/op across benchtimes), and ProviderSet measures one-time startup cost rather than a per-event path. Stated rather than silently omitted.

### Standing constraints, unchanged

Work straight on `main`, one commit per child with `Closes #N`, push immediately. Do not merge #255 or publish a release without Rob's approval. Do not hand-edit generated files. Mutation-test every new guard — three of mine this session initially passed while proving nothing, which is the same count as the previous phase and suggests the rate is a property of the technique, not of a bad day.
All eight remaining children closed and verified green at `cfc60b9`. Receipts, findings beyond scope, corrections, and the explicit not-done list are in the phase-completion comment above.

title: Tracker: API drift, CI, generated artifacts, and release engineering

body:
## Mission

Provide secure, reproducible installation paths whose Compose, Helm, systemd, image, probe, credential, and shutdown behavior matches the binary’s runtime contract.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P1

- [x] #332 — Align Compose and Kubernetes shutdown budgets with staged draining
- [x] #333 — Fix the Compose optional config-file mount
- [x] #336 — Use platform-appropriate native checkpoint paths
- [x] #341 — Replace unsafe Helm credential quick starts and fix the `secrets.*` typo
- [x] #342 — Make Helm probes follow admin TLS

### Phase P2

- [x] #334 — Provide first-class Docker Compose secrets
- [x] #335 — Separate published-image Compose from developer builds
- [ ] #337 — Add a native healthcheck subcommand
- [ ] #338 — Document verified release-binary and image installation
- [ ] #339 — Ship a hardened systemd deployment
- [x] #343 — Add first-class projected Workload Identity Federation tokens
- [x] #344 — Add default-off, per-listener Kubernetes Services
- [x] #345 — Add an opt-in Prometheus Operator PodMonitor
- [ ] #346 — Add secure receiver Ingress/Gateway examples or blocks
- [x] #347 — Support externally managed application config resources
- [x] #348 — Add typed `extraEnv` and `extraEnvFrom`
- [x] #352 — Design HA semantics before adding shared checkpoint storage
- [x] #354 — Research log-stream destination drift before implementing a gauge
- [x] #458 — feat(helm): add an opt-in Prometheus ServiceMonitor

### Phase P3

- [ ] #340 — Publish a package-manager installation path
- [ ] #349 — Support immutable image digests
- [ ] #350 — Make probes configurable and add a startup probe
- [ ] #351 — Add an optional NetworkPolicy baseline
- [ ] #353 — Add a Prometheus HTTP service-discovery endpoint for tailnet nodes
- [ ] #355 — Exercise Workload Identity Federation in live-contract CI

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Fix secret handling, optional config mounting, TLS probes, and shutdown budgets before adding more deployment conveniences.
- Shared checkpoint/HA remains a design task until ownership, leases, fencing, and receiver semantics are explicit.
- Regenerate and verify Helm README/schema artifacts with the repository-pinned tool versions.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every child issue is closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed stale/unsupported decision.
- [ ] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [ ] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules, and deployment examples agree with the final contracts.
- [ ] Full repository and affected tool-module gates are green at the final integration SHA.
- [ ] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail, or follow-up exists only in an agent transcript.

## Audit epic identity

`EPIC-07`

comments.body:
## Phase P1 complete — all five children closed

Final SHA `3ce3461`. Working tree clean, `main == origin/main`. **All nine workflows green for that exact SHA** — CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Helm, Release, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, Trigger Documentation Sync. Release-please PR #255 remains open and unmerged; no release was published.

### Closed in this phase

| Child | Commit | Substance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #333 | `a9311a3` | Config mount moved to `docker-compose.config.yaml`; first CI gate that ever resolves the Compose assets |
| #342 | `82e43b5` | Probes render `scheme: HTTPS` under the same both-or-neither condition the runtime uses |
| #332 | `ac58014` | 45s budgets in Compose and the chart, **derived** from the stage constants, with a compile-time drift assertion |
| #341 | `7cd9a84` | Quick starts moved to `existingSecret`; inline-credential gate derived from the chart’s own credential list |
| #336 | `3ce3461` | Platform state path resolved at runtime when the default is unwritable, with no migration |

Why this tracker: #484’s closing comment left #341 explicitly open here, so this was the named continuation rather than a fresh pick.

### Premise corrections — validating first paid off on three of five

- **#333 understates nothing, but names the wrong failure mode.** Reproduced against Compose v5.1.2 before touching anything: uncommenting the second `volumes:` key is a **hard parse error** (`mapping key "volumes" already defined at line 77`), not a silent loss of persistence. The issue hedged this as "parser-dependent"; on current Compose the parser simply refuses. The documented path was dead, not lossy.
- **#342 acceptance item 3 was already done.** "Partial TLS configuration fails via OUX-03" is satisfied by `validateTLSFiles` (`validate.go:606-620`) under #170, with `TestValidate_AdminTLSBothOrNeither` pinning it. Verified, not reimplemented.
- **#336 acceptance item 3 was partly stale.** `#69` already made `checkpointStore` return the *effective* store kind and the status page already reported it. Only the effective **path** and the **reason** were missing.

### A design fork worth recording

**#336 cannot be fixed the obvious way.** Making `config.Default()` platform-aware was attempted and backed out: `TestExampleConfigMatchesDefaults` gates `config.example.yaml` to match `Default()` byte-for-byte, so a machine-dependent default cannot exist in a committed file. Resolution moved to runtime, which additionally left the image, compose file and chart needing **zero** changes, because `/var/lib` genuinely is writable in a container. `TestDefaultKeepsLegacyCheckpointPath` records the reasoning so the next reader does not retry it.

### Corrections to my own work, recorded rather than quietly fixed

- **A guard that asserted nothing, again.** Case L’s NOTES assertions used `helm template --notes`. **`helm template` does not render `NOTES.txt` at all** — it emits nothing, silently. The two positive assertions failed, which is the only reason it surfaced; the two negative-shaped ones passed happily against an empty string. Now uses `helm install --dry-run=client`, and the helper fails loudly if NOTES renders empty. That is the fourth such guard in this repository’s recent history, and the second caught only because a sibling assertion happened to be positive.
- **I shipped a chart guard I believed was doing work that the schema was doing.** After regeneration, `values.schema.json`’s `minimum: 45` rejects a low number during values validation, before templating — so case K’s assertion on the template’s message was wrong. The guard is **not** dead code: `null` bypasses JSON Schema `minimum` and rendered `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0` with the guard removed, which is worse than the 30s default #332 was filed about. Both layers now assert on their own input. Corrected on #332 rather than silently patched.
- **The new inline-credential gate flagged my own prose.** The anti-examples in the warnings parse as commands. I reworded them rather than adding a "this is only an example" escape hatch, which would be the first thing misused.

### Negative testing

Nineteen mutants across the five children; every gate was broken and confirmed to fail for the right reason before being restored. The ones worth naming:

- Raising `stream.ShutdownTimeout` **fails the build** (`constant -15000000000 overflows uint`), and raising `ingressWALFlushTimeout` fails all three budget tests with a recomputed requirement. The 45 is derived, not copied.
- `--set config.profiling.pyroscope.basic_auth_password=…` is flagged, proving the credential surface really is derived from `tailscale2otel.credentialPaths` and not just a hardcoded `secret.` prefix.
- Renaming the `credentialPaths` define makes `check_doc_commands.py` **exit 2** rather than check an empty set.
- Removing #336’s relocation, or applying it to an explicitly configured path, each fail a distinct test — the second is the boundary that keeps this from being a hidden migration.

### Deliberately not done

- **`ingress_wal.directory` keeps `/var/lib/tailscale2otel/ingress-wal`.** It has #336’s platform problem, but the WAL **fails closed** — a native operator who enables it gets a hard startup error naming the path, not a silent cold start. Extending the relocation would widen the blast radius to the chart and the receiver durability contract for no silent-failure gain.
- **`docker run --stop-timeout 45` is documentation only.** Nothing in the repository executes a bare `docker run`, so there is no artifact to gate it against.
- **No systemd unit was written.** The shutdown-budget table names `TimeoutStopSec` for operators writing their own, marked as such; shipping one is #339 under P2.

### New gates added

`deploy/tests/compose-tests.sh` (wired into `ci.yml`’s `docker-build` job, which already has Docker and a place in `ci-success.needs` — the same reasoning the secret-hygiene gate used, so no branch-ruleset edit). Render-tests cases J, K and L. `internal/app/shutdownbudget_test.go`. `check_doc_commands.py` gained inline-credential screening, `--set-file` extraction, `--from-literal` screening, `NOTES.txt` coverage, and a vacuity guard.

Chart 0.14.7 → 0.14.10.

### Next

P2 (15 children): #334, #335, #337, #338, #339, #343, #344, #345, #346, #347, #348, #352, #354, #458. Two of them — #352 (HA/shared checkpoint) and #354 (log-stream destination drift) — are parked design tasks and must start from their research/design acceptance criteria, not implementation.

## Phase P2 — 11 of 15 children closed

Final SHA `30589c4`. Working tree clean, `main == origin/main`, regeneration confirmed a fixed point (`scripts/regen-generated.sh` then a clean `git status`, not `git diff`).

**All nine workflows green for that exact SHA** — CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Helm, Release, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, and the scheduled Live API contract lane (advisory, deliberately not in `ci-success.needs`). Release-please PR #255 remains open and unmerged; no release was published.

**Four P2 children remain open** — see "Not done" at the end. This is a partial phase, recorded as such.

### Closed in this phase

| Child | Commit | Substance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #348 | `b188b9a` | Typed `extraEnv`/`extraEnvFrom` with a derived reserved-name policy |
| #354 | — | **Closed unsupported.** Research spike; negative result with evidence. Correction landed as `29f57c8` |
| #334 | `a544576` | Compose file-based secrets — **plus a real resolver bug found while validating** |
| #335 | `1faaa5e` | Published-image / dev-build split; both version pins now release-managed |
| #344 | `1e5d29a` | Four default-off per-listener Services, with credential guards |
| #345 | `e01d6c6` | Opt-in PodMonitor |
| #458 | `9ade22f` | Opt-in ServiceMonitor |
| #347 | `098dbb3` | `existingConfigMap` / `existingConfigSecret` for GitOps |
| #352 | — | **Closed as the design deliverable it asked for.** No implementation, scaling still locked |
| #343 | `30589c4` | Projected, audience-scoped WIF token |

### Bugs found that no issue named

**1. `auditlogs.objectstore.*_file` was never resolved (fixed in `a544576`).** `ObjectStoreConfig` is shared by flowlogs and auditlogs, so the audit object store has always *declared* `access_key_id_file`, `secret_access_key_file` and `session_token_file`, and `objectStoreAuditSpec` consumes the resolved values — but `resolveSecretFiles` only ever walked the **flow** ones, globally and per-tailnet. Setting one did nothing: no read, no error, an empty credential handed to the S3 client, surfacing later as a bucket auth failure pointing at the wrong thing. The Helm chart already listed those paths in `credentialPaths`, so the chart treated them as credentials while the app ignored their file form. For a `tailnets[]` entry it was the only way to supply the credential at all, since a list-of-structs key has no `TS2OTEL_*` env form (#79).

This was found *because* a recon lane reported the `_file` mechanism as complete. It was complete for the five categories #334 names, and I nearly recorded the whole runtime half as stale on that basis.

**2. Chart `appVersion` had rotted to `2.0.2` against a `3.0.0` release (fixed in `1faaa5e`).** That is the image tag the chart installs when `image.tag` is empty, so the default Helm install ran a major behind. A comment in `Chart.yaml` records this same pin being corrected once before from a long-stale `0.1.0` — so it has now rotted twice, which is why the fix is release-please `extra-files` plus a test, not a new number.

**3. The recorded reason for rejecting `getLogStreamingConfiguration` was wrong (fixed in `29f57c8`).** The disposition note said the endpoint returns "url, username and **token**". Per the vendored spec, `token` and `s3SecretAccessKey` are `writeOnly` and are **not** returned; `gcsCredentials` has no `writeOnly` flag and is live GCS credential material. Right verdict, wrong mechanism — and the next reader asking "can we just read the config endpoint?" would have weighed a token they were never going to receive and missed the field that actually leaks.

### Corrections to my own work

- **My gate ordering ran `check_doc_commands.py` before `regen-generated.sh`** on #347, so it flagged `--set existingConfigSecret` as an unknown chart value while the commit itself contained the regenerated schema and passes cleanly. A red gate printed next to a push, explained rather than left in the transcript.
- **`helm template` does not render `NOTES.txt` at all** (#341). My case-L helper produced an empty string, and the two negative-shaped assertions over it passed vacuously. Now uses `helm install --dry-run=client` and fails loudly on empty NOTES.
- **A `yq` length query over EMPTY input returns 1, not 0** (#344). "Exactly one Service" passed with zero rendered.
- **A guard that passed because a *different* guard fired** (#344). The disabled-listener case was caught by the credential check, so deleting the listener-enabled guard changed nothing and the test stayed green. It now sets a credential and matches the specific message.
- **The #341 inline-credential gate flagged my own anti-examples.** Correct behaviour — I reworded the warnings rather than adding an "it's only an example" escape hatch, which would be the first thing misused.

Four guards this session initially proved nothing. That is now consistent across three consecutive phases and is a property of the technique, not of a bad day: **every new guard gets a mutant, without exception.**

### Subagent lanes — and one wrong claim

Three read-only recon lanes ran (P2 premise sweep, #354 research, #338 release facts). They wrote nothing, so there was no file-ownership conflict with the chart work.

**One returned a confidently wrong claim**: that `collectors.auditlogs.objectstore.*` had `_file` resolution "for free". It does not — that is bug 1 above. The structs exist and are shared, which is exactly what makes the claim plausible from a struct-level read. Checking the resolver rather than the type is what found it.

The two lanes also **disagreed with each other** on SBOM naming (`.sbom` from the config's defaults vs `.tar.gz.sbom.json` observed on real release assets). Real assets win; this matters for #338 and is recorded there rather than acted on yet.

The #338 lane correctly flagged its own low-confidence items — the cosign `--certificate-identity` strings for both the checksum signature and the image — as needing a real `cosign verify` before publication. **Nothing unverified from that lane has been written into docs.**

### Deliberately not done

- **`ingress_wal.directory` keeps `/var/lib/tailscale2otel/ingress-wal`** (from #336). Same platform problem, but the WAL fails *closed* — a native operator gets a hard startup error naming the path, not a silent cold start — so it is not the silent-degradation defect #336 describes.
- **No implementation subtasks filed for #352**, per the tracker's rule for parked items. The design recommends *not* building leader election; that recommendation is an open decision for @rknightion with a stated default-if-unanswered.
- **#343 is render-level only.** It does not prove a real token exchange against Tailscale — that is #355, still open under P3.

### Still open in P2 — four children

| Child | Why it is not done |
| --- | --- |
| #337 | Native healthcheck subcommand — Go work in `cmd/`, plus Dockerfile and Compose wiring. Not started |
| #338 | Verified-install docs — **facts gathered but not written.** The cosign identity strings must be confirmed with a real `cosign verify` first; the lane explicitly flagged them, and publishing a verification command that does not work is worse than publishing none |
| #339 | Hardened systemd unit — not started |
| #346 | Receiver Ingress/Gateway examples — unblocked by #344's Services, but not started |

All of P3 (#340, #349, #350, #351, #353, #355) is likewise untouched.

### Chart

0.14.10 → **0.20.0** across this phase. Every bump regenerated `README.md` and `values.schema.json` with the pinned tools.

Decision resolved on #352: @rknightion approved **no leader election** (2026-07-28). Static sharding by tailnet is adopted; `replicaCount` stays locked at 1 per shard. Shared checkpoint storage, leader election and fencing are **not** to be built, and no implementation subtasks are to be filed for them — the prerequisite for reopening that door is recorded on #352. This clears the only open decision left by the P2 receipt above.

## Phase P2 complete — and a scope decision that retired two children

All four remaining P2 children are closed, plus one P3 that the same decision removed. Tracker is now **21 of 26 closed**, with four P3 children left.

| issue | outcome | commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #337 native healthcheck subcommand | shipped | `4cc1bb3` |
| #338 verified release-binary and image install docs | shipped | `36a6083` |
| #339 hardened systemd deployment | **won't do** — built, then reverted | `c8802cd` (the policy statement) |
| #340 package-manager installation path | **won't do** — same decision | `c8802cd` |
| #346 secure receiver Ingress/Gateway | shipped, chart 0.21.0 | `9993b50` |

### The scope decision

@rknightion, mid-phase: *"I dont think people will ever run this on a system the ONLY supported deployment model should be via docker container."*

**The container image is the only supported production deployment**, via Docker Compose or the Helm chart. A local binary remains supported for development, `-validate` runs and experiments — `docs/installation.md`'s Binary tab now says so explicitly, and says that no `systemd` unit or packaging is planned.

This landed *after* #339 was fully built: a hardened unit with `LoadCredential`, `StateDirectory`, `ExecStartPre=… -validate`, the full `Protect*`/`SystemCallFilter` block, and six mutation-tested guard tests. All reverted, none committed. The design is recorded on #339 so nobody re-derives it believing it was never tried.

Beyond preference, the decision holds up: the image already encodes the runtime contract a native install would have to reproduce and keep in step (non-root uid 65532, pre-seeded state directory, read-only rootfs, dropped capabilities, a stop grace period covering the staged drain), and **nothing in CI can boot a systemd unit** — a guard test there could only ever assert the file's text, never that it works.

### What #338 cost, and why it was worth it

#338 was blocked on verification, not writing. Four findings that a plausible doc would have got wrong, all established by running the commands against the real v3.0.0 release:

- The cosign identity is **`rknightion/.github`**, not this repo — signing happens inside the shared reusable workflows.
- That identity is **SHA-pinned and rotates on every Renovate bump** of the reusable pin. v3.0.0 signed under `d1c590b2…`; main now pins `a4182f2…`. A literal `--certificate-identity` is correct for exactly one release, so everything documented uses `--certificate-identity-regexp`.
- `gh attestation verify` subjects are the **archives**, not the checksums file — verifying `SHA256SUMS` returns HTTP 404.
- `--signer-repo rknightion/.github` is **required**; without it the command exits 1 with `verifying with issuer "sigstore.dev"`, naming neither cause nor fix.

`internal/ci/signingidentity_test.go` now derives each identity from the real `uses:` lines and fails if a documented regexp matches no signing workflow, if a signing workflow has no documented command, if an identity is SHA-pinned as a literal, or if a `gh attestation verify` loses `--signer-repo`.

### Guard discipline

Every new assertion this phase was mutation-tested — by the implementing lane and then independently by the dispatcher against the committed tree. Two findings worth recording:

- A lane caught a **vacuous assertion in its own test** before shipping: `yq 'has("tls")'` at the document root is unconditionally false, so the TLS check passed under a mutation that should have broken it. Fixed to `yq '.spec | has("tls")'`. Fifth instance of this class in this repo, first caught pre-merge.
- One dispatcher mutation appeared not to fire (#338's `--signer-repo` guard). It turned out to be a bad `sed`, not a vacuous guard — re-run with a verified mutation and it failed correctly. Worth stating: *"the mutation didn't fire"* and *"the mutation didn't apply"* look identical unless you check.

### State at `9993b50`

Full gate green: `go build` · `go vet` · `go test -race ./...` · `golangci-lint` (0 issues) · `verify-modules.sh` (all 5 modules) · `render-tests.sh` 317/317 · `compose-tests.sh` 40/40 · `helm lint` · three `python3 -m unittest` suites · `promqlcheck` (579 promql, 0 failures) · `actionlint` · `check_doc_commands.py` · `regen-generated.sh` a fixed point with a clean `git status`. Chart 0.21.0.

### Remaining (P3)

#349 immutable image digests · #350 configurable probes + startup probe · #351 NetworkPolicy baseline · #353 Prometheus HTTP-SD endpoint · #355 live WIF verification.

All four remain valid under the container-only decision. #355 is expected to need a decision from @rknightion — see the comment going on it.

## Tracker complete — all 26 children closed

Final SHA `2aa2e03`. Working tree clean, regeneration a fixed point, **all 7 workflows green at that exact SHA** (CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Release, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor); the path-filtered **Helm** lane is green at `9993b50` and `15cd177`, the two chart commits. Chart 0.22.0.

### P3 outcomes

| issue | outcome | commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #349 immutable image digests | shipped | `15cd177` |
| #350 configurable probes + startup probe | shipped | `15cd177` |
| #351 NetworkPolicy baseline | shipped | `15cd177` |
| #353 Prometheus HTTP-SD endpoint | **out of direction** | — |
| #355 live WIF verification | shipped + live-verified | `8de36d5`, `b75d3db`, `2aa2e03` |

Two closed by decision rather than code, both @rknightion's:

**#353** joins #352 and #486 as the third of #173's four explicitly-parked items to be settled the same way. Recorded on the issue: an HTTP-SD response must carry Tailscale IPs and hostnames, which `pii_filter` strips by default — so it would have needed an endpoint that fails closed on a listener whose `/metrics` is open by default. That tension is the thing to resolve first if it is ever revisited, not the caching.

**#339/#340** went earlier in the phase to the container-only deployment decision.

### #355 is the one worth reading

It was blocked on a tailnet mutation. Authorised, so two federated identities now exist — a read-only one for this lane pinned to `refs/heads/main`, and a `tag:ci` join identity for Actions joining the tailnet. Neither returns a secret; that is the point. `TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` are **deleted** from repo secrets, so no long-lived Tailscale credential is stored in GitHub at all.

Proven live by run [30351935446](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/actions/runs/30351935446), not asserted. The returned audience was exactly `api.tailscale.com/<client id>`, which incidentally **confirms the default the code and chart already computed** and had never been checked against a real identity.

It also produced a correction to my own earlier claim on that issue: I said every failure mode returns an identical opaque `400`, having probed with a *fake* client ID. With a real one, a wrong-audience token gives **403**. The conclusion survives — the response still cannot separate a wrong audience from a wrong issuer from an expired token, so it is one assertion, not four — but the stated fact was wrong and is corrected in place.

### Guard discipline, and a fifth vacuous assertion

Every new assertion across both phases was mutation-tested by its implementing lane and then **independently by the dispatcher** against the committed tree. Three things this caught that a green run would not have:

- The `id-token: write` guard in `internal/ci/liveauth_test.go` was **vacuous on first writing** — `strings.Contains(src, "id-token: write")` matches a commented-out line as happily as a live one. It now parses the permissions block. Fifth instance of this class here, and a security guard is the worst place for it.
- A lane caught its own vacuous `yq 'has("tls")'` (document-root, always false) before shipping.
- Twice a dispatcher mutation "didn't fire" and turned out not to have *applied*. Those two look identical unless checked — worth treating as a standing trap.

### A gate gap worth keeping

The final `actionlint` lane failed on **SC2015** in a workflow that was clean under local actionlint **1.7.7 and the CI-pinned 1.7.12**. Cause: actionlint shells out to whatever `shellcheck` is on PATH, and local shellcheck **0.11.0 does not emit SC2015 at all** while the runner's older one does. The version gap runs the wrong way — local is newer and reports *less* — so "my tooling is current" is not reassurance. Recorded in `CLAUDE.md`, because the natural conclusion from a green local run is exactly the wrong one.

### Left for @rknightion

The Tailscale-side OAuth client **`tailscale2otel-repo`** (`all:read`) still exists and is now unused, its GitHub-stored secret gone. Revoking it is yours — I was authorised to create, and deleting a credential I did not create is not something I will do unasked.

The `tag:ci` join identity is created and ready but wired to nothing. Per your call, no issue filed.

Closing this tracker. Remaining open trackers: #480 (telemetry/Prometheus/tracing/profiling), #482 (config/admin UI/operator experience), #485 (ecosystem/experimental research).

title: Tracker: deployment, packaging, and Kubernetes operations

body:
## Mission

Make configuration errors actionable, runtime state truthful, and the local admin/flow surfaces safe and useful enough to operate the exporter without reverse-engineering logs or source.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P0

- [x] #302 — fix(flows): version policy verdicts so retained traffic cannot join to the wrong current rules

### Phase P1

- [x] #294 — feat(flowstore): optional SQLite persistence for multi-day /flows history — unparked and SHIPPED 2026-07-29 (`4b25580`)
- [x] #295 — fix(flows): historical pinned windows must return matching recent rows
- [x] #301 — fix(flowstore): keep recent connections ordered by event time when late data arrives
- [x] #303 — Reject unknown YAML configuration keys
- [x] #304 — Make the Helm values schema reject unknown values
- [x] #305 — Validate complete, parseable TLS keypairs for every listener
- [x] #306 — Canonicalize listener addresses and fail startup on bind failure
- [x] #314 — Make the default admin landing page safely usable
- [x] #315 — Make Prometheus authentication fail closed
- [x] #317 — Report actual OTLP delivery state in the admin page
- [x] #318 — Unify component health, readiness, and status-page verdicts
- [x] #331 — Correct the operator documentation after recent security/UI changes

### Phase P2

- [x] #296 — feat(flows): server-side filtering and cursor pagination
- [x] #297 — feat(rdns): serve stale positive PTR values while refreshing
- [x] #298 — feat(flows): persist view state in shareable URLs
- [x] #299 — feat(flows): export filtered data as CSV and JSON
- [x] #300 — feat(admin): add a bounded audit and webhook event explorer
- [x] #307 — Report all configuration diagnostics in one pass
- [x] #308 — Publish a standalone application configuration JSON Schema
- [x] #309 — Add canonical redacted effective-config and provenance CLI output
- [x] #310 — Resolve file paths relative to their configuration source
- [x] #311 — Add safe preflight and single-cycle execution modes
- [x] #312 — Support structured JSON application logs
- [x] #316 — Reload listener certificates and expose expiry health
- [x] #319 — Surface active configuration advisories in the admin UI/API
- [x] #320 — Export the complete effective redacted configuration
- [x] #321 — Generate a privacy-safe support bundle
- [x] #322 — Add defensive HTTP headers to admin responses
- [x] #325 — Add a per-tailnet selector to the admin page
- [x] #327 — Complete accessibility and keyboard support for both embedded UIs

### Phase P3

- [x] #313 — Add transactional configuration and secret hot reload — CLOSED NOT_PLANNED (declined; containers restart, see the P3 wave-1 receipt)
- [x] #323 — Version and publish the admin status/flows API contract
- [x] #324 — Add explicit browser login/logout for the admin page — CLOSED by Rob as out of scope (tailnet-level network lockdown is sufficient)
- [x] #326 — Add authenticated per-collector “Run now” — CLOSED UNSUPPORTED (admin surface stays read-only)
- [x] #328 — Make UI polling single-flight, visibility-aware, and backoff-capable
- [x] #329 — Make flow-store capacity and memory policy configurable
- [x] #330 — Show update availability on the admin page

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Version the admin JSON contracts before adding controls or external consumers.
- Keep browser/admin actions authenticated, CSRF-safe, bounded, and separate from readiness semantics.
- Configuration hot reload is a design task first: preserve last-known-good state and define component ownership before implementation.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every child issue is closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed stale/unsupported decision. (#294 was parked, then unparked and shipped in `4b25580`; no exceptions remain.)
- [x] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [x] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules, and deployment examples agree with the final contracts.
- [x] Full repository and affected tool-module gates are green at the final integration SHA (`fde409f`).
- [x] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail, or follow-up exists only in an agent transcript.

## Audit epic identity

`EPIC-06`

comments.body:
## Phase P0 complete, P1 started (3 of 13)

| issue | commit | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #302 | `a6d14c9` | fixed — P0 done |
| #303 | `96c5e9b` | fixed |
| #304 | `69d7746` | fixed |

Full gate green at `69d7746`: `go build`/`vet`/`test -race`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues),
`verify-modules.sh` (all 5 modules), the three Python suites, `promqlcheck` (579 promql / 25 logql /
5 traceql / 217 server-side, 0 failures), `actionlint`, `render-tests.sh` (421 assertions),
`compose-tests.sh --self-test` (40), `regen-generated.sh` a fixed point, `check_doc_commands.py`,
clean `git status`. Chart `0.22.0` → `0.23.0`.

### Decisions taken

**These land WITHOUT a semver major, documented loudly instead.** #303 and #304 both turn a
previously-ignored input into a hard failure, so a config or values file that started before may now
refuse to start. Rob's call: no `!`, no v4, no Go module path move — a prominent BREAKING BEHAVIOUR
note in each commit body and in the docs. The same applies to the remaining behaviour changes in
this tracker (#314, #315). Do not re-litigate this per issue.

### Corrections and findings worth carrying

- **#302's rule identity is `(policy version, rule index)`, not the index.** The version hashes the
  compiled rule LIST (kind + source, in order), so it changes on an edit or a reorder but *not* on a
  reformat of the ACL document — churning it on whitespace would discard attributions that are still
  valid. `aclpolicy.Store` retains the last `MaxRetainedPolicies` (16) distinct rule lists; a
  recompile of unchanged rules does not consume a slot, or a busy user directory would evict the
  versions retained traffic still refers to. An unretained version reports
  `available:false` with no rule text — it is never backfilled from the current policy.
- **`/api/flows.json` gained `exercised[]`** (rule text resolved server-side per row) and
  `policy.version`. Consumers must stop joining `result.rules[].rule` to `policy.rules[]`; that join
  is correct only until the ACL is edited, which is exactly when someone is looking.
- **#303 immediately caught a dead key in this repo.** `internal/config/config_test.go`'s fixture set
  `cardinality.flow.destination_service`, removed in 0.13.0, and `internal/flowlog/catalog.go` still
  documented it as gating `tailscale.dst.service`. Both corrected — the attribute is unconditional,
  as its own tests already asserted.
- **Removed keys get their own error, not a spelling suggestion.** The nearest valid key to
  `cardinality.flow.destination_service` is `cardinality.flow.destination_port` — a *different*
  setting, and taking the suggestion would silently change an operator's cardinality. There is a
  `removedKeys` map in `internal/config/unknownkeys.go`; add to it whenever a key is removed.
- **CHANGELOG.md and the 0.13.0 chart notes explicitly promised** a leftover `destination_service:`
  would be "silently ignored". #303 breaks that promise on purpose. `-validate` is the pre-flight.
- **Helm root strictness has no values.yaml annotation.** A `# @schema` comment at the top of the
  file attaches to the first KEY, not the root mapping. `--set secrets.foo=bar` — the issue's own
  repro — is only rejected because `--schema-root.additional-properties=false` is in
  `scripts/regen-generated.sh` AND `additionalProperties: false` is in `.github/workflows/helm.yml`.
  **Those two must move together** or local regeneration silently drifts from CI; render-tests case
  Z is the guard, verified by removing the flag and regenerating.

### Trap hit again this phase

`scripts/regen-generated.sh` **silently no-ops on an unknown target** — I ran it as `schema` rather
than `helm-schema` while mutation-testing, the schema did not change, and it briefly looked like the
guard was vacuous. It was not; the command had simply done nothing. Same shape as the two "mutation
didn't fire / had not applied" incidents in the previous tracker. Always confirm the mutation
actually landed in the artifact, not just in the source.

## P1 progress: 8 of 13 done

| issue | commit | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #295 | `3de4fc7` | fixed |
| #301 | `3de4fc7` | fixed |
| #303 | `96c5e9b` | fixed |
| #304 | `69d7746` | fixed |
| #305 | `a3b96be` | fixed |
| #314 | `3584827` | fixed |
| #315 | `5a0be19` | fixed |

Plus #302 (`a6d14c9`), the P0. Remaining P1: **#294, #306, #317, #318, #331**.

All 9 workflows were green at `69d7746`, which is the SHA that matters most so far: it is the one
that proved the Helm `additionalProperties: false` action input generates the same schema as the
local `--schema-root.additional-properties=false` flag. That coupling could not be verified offline.

### Contract changes an operator can trip over

Four of these change behaviour that previously "worked". Per the decision recorded above, none is a
semver major; each carries a BREAKING BEHAVIOUR note in its commit and, where an operator has to act,
an upgrade admonition in `docs/configuration.md`.

- **#305** — TLS files were checked for READABILITY only, so `/dev/null` as both cert and key passed
  `-validate`, as did a cert paired with another listener's key. Both then failed inside
  `ListenAndServeTLS` — on a goroutine, after startup — leaving a healthy-looking process with a
  listener that never served. Now loaded with `tls.LoadX509KeyPair`. **Streaming had no TLS
  validation at all**, and is the worst place for it: `stream.Run` serves plain HTTP unless BOTH
  fields are set, so `cert_file` with no `key_file` silently downgraded a log receiver to plaintext.
- **#315** — `/metrics` is now refused (403) on a network-reachable bind with no token. Loopback stays
  open; `prometheus.auth.allow_unauthenticated` re-opens a network bind explicitly, because
  in-cluster scraping behind a NetworkPolicy is legitimate. A configured token is always enforced.
  The chart fails the render when a PodMonitor/ServiceMonitor points at an unauthenticated network
  bind — that scrape would return 403 forever and read as a broken exporter. Chart → `0.24.0`.
- **#314** — `admin.listen` now defaults to `127.0.0.1:9091`. The gate was NOT weakened: the landing
  page is on by default and fails closed on a network bind, so the old wildcard default served **403
  to its own UI on a first run**. Anyone relying on the wildcard to reach the page remotely was
  already being refused unless they had also set a token.
- **#303/#304** — covered in the previous receipt.

### Two findings worth keeping

- **A performance regression was introduced and caught inside #301.** Fixing the ordering bug replaced
  the O(1) ring write with a sorted insert that shifted the whole ring on every eviction. `Record`
  runs on the emit path under the store lock, once per connection, and one live capture carried
  **44,825 of them in a single poll** — measured at **12.6us/op**, roughly half a second of memcpy per
  poll cycle, which is exactly what this package's contract promises not to do. Eviction now advances
  a start offset with the dead prefix reclaimed once per `MaxRecent` inserts: **12622ns/op →
  248ns/op**, every ordering test unchanged. Benchmarks are committed as documentation, not gates —
  a timing assertion would be flaky.
- **#305 and #315 each had an existing test asserting the OLD, wrong contract.**
  `TestValidate_AdminTLSValidWithReadableFiles` asserted that two files containing the words "cert"
  and "key" were valid, and `TestRequireMetricsAuth`'s first subtest asserted `/metrics` was open with
  no token. Both encoded the bug. When a fix makes a test fail, check whether the test was the
  specification or the symptom.

### Vacuous-assertion count for this session: 2 caught, both mine

1. A `grep` on `$RENDER` for `allow_unauthenticated` passed while the guard it tested was absent —
   the string also appears in the rendered ConfigMap on a **successful** render. Now scoped to the
   guard's own wording.
2. `TestRecompilingTheSamePolicyDoesNotConsumeHistory` (#302) counted map entries, which a
   duplicate-filing bug leaves unchanged. Rewritten to drive the eviction boundary, where the bug is
   actually observable; the mutation then fired.

Also re-confirmed: adding the #315 guard broke **10 pre-existing render cases** that ran a monitor
with no token, and case P needed the acknowledgement so that ITS failure — not the new one — is what
it asserts. That is the "a guard passes because a different guard fires first" trap, arriving from
the other direction.

## #294 parked indefinitely — do not re-plan or close it

Rob, 2026-07-28: **park SQLite flow persistence (#294) indefinitely. The issue stays OPEN**, labelled
`status: blocked`, with the reasoning on the issue itself. It is not rejected and not stale; it is
just not being worked. A successor should skip it when working this tracker's P1 list and must not
re-litigate, re-scope, or close it.

It is the one P1 here that adds capability rather than fixing something already broken, and it carries
a cgo-vs-pure-Go dependency decision that would constrain the single-static-binary and distroless
packaging promises. Everything else in P1 remains in scope.

**Remaining P1 after this: #306, #317, #318, #331.**

All 9 workflows green at `3584827` (#314), the current head of this tracker's work.

## Phase P1 complete — 12 of 13, with #294 parked

| issue | commit | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #306 | `6a113d9` | fixed |
| #318 | `3aaab59` | fixed |
| #317 | `5c38fd2` | fixed |
| #331 | `c431611` | fixed |

Plus the eight closed in the previous receipts. **#294 stays open and parked** per the comment above.
P0 and P1 are otherwise done; P2 (18 items) is next.

Chart `0.24.0` → `0.24.1` (comment-only, but it regenerates the chart README).

### Contract changes

- **One readiness source, and it is no longer receiver-specific.** `recordReceiverStop` is
  `recordComponentStop`; `runAdmin` and `runMetrics` go through it instead of calling
  `componentError` directly, so a listener that never bound makes `/readyz` return 503 naming the
  component. The readiness reason says `component failure:` rather than `receiver failure:`, and the
  ingress WAL is spelled with its appcatalog name (`ingress_wal`) on the probe, the page and the
  metric attribute rather than a second human spelling.
- **Listener addresses are parsed, not compared.** `listenaddr.Canonical` / `Collides`. An enabled
  listener whose address cannot be bound now refuses to start, and `:9091` / `0.0.0.0:9091` /
  `[::]:9091` are one socket however they are spelled. A wildcard bind collides with **any** address
  on its port, so `admin.listen: ":9091"` with `prometheus.listen: "127.0.0.1:9091"` is rejected —
  only one of them ever bound. Port 0 never collides; a disabled listener is not checked.
- **`/api/status.json` gained `components[]` and `delivery[]`.** The health verdict now derives from
  the same component state `/readyz` reads. `delivery[]` is per signal (metrics, logs, traces) and
  reports what the exporters actually SHIPPED — `throughput` still counts what was handed to them.
  Keep the two distinct.
- **`last_error_class` is a closed set** (`timeout`, `canceled`, `unauthenticated`, `rate_limited`,
  `unavailable`, `invalid`, `other`). The backend's response text is never surfaced: an OTLP error
  can carry the response body, which is where an echoed credential or signed URL would be.

### Two deliberate asymmetries, both now tested as such

Neither is an oversight, and a future change that "fixes" either is a regression:

1. **A degraded collector shows on the page but does not gate readiness** (#57). Pulling a pod for
   one failed tick takes the whole exporter down for a partial fault.
2. **Sustained OTLP export failure degrades health but does NOT gate readiness** (#317). Three
   consecutive failures marks a signal `failing` and the page stops saying healthy, but `/readyz`
   stays 200 — otherwise a backend outage pulls every replica out of rotation at once and turns one
   vendor's bad afternoon into a cascading outage.

`/healthz` is unchanged and stays process-only, with its own guard test. A component failure means
stop sending traffic, not restart; conflating them turns a bad config into a crash loop.

### Findings worth carrying

- **The delivery tracker is populated with self-obs OFF.** The counting decorators used to be
  installed only under `self_observability.enabled`, so with it off nothing observed export outcomes
  at all. They are now always installed and only the data-point/record TALLY is still gated. The
  admin page is a local view and has to work on a deployment that exports no self-telemetry —
  particularly when the export path is the broken thing. The self-obs histogram that already existed
  is invisible in exactly that case, because it cannot be delivered either.
- **Traces had no export wrapper at all** and could fail every export silently. They now go through
  the same tracker, wrapped outside the PII span exporter so the measured duration is the real one.
- **#331's docs guard exists because nothing could have caught that class.**
  `check_doc_commands.py` checks that documented commands reference real keys; the completeness
  tests check every key is mentioned. Neither has an opinion on whether a sentence is TRUE. The six
  audited claims all told an operator to do the thing that now returns 403.
- **One #331 claim did not reproduce:** no "always-off" wording remains in `docs/configuration.md`.
  Fixed at some point between the audit commit and now.

### Vacuous assertions caught this phase: 3, all mine

1. `TestRender_ComponentFailureIsVisible` asserted `"componentsBody"` and `"metrics"`. Both match the
   JS updater and half the page besides, so they passed with the table deleted. Now
   `id="componentsBody"` and the failure reason.
2. `TestRender_DeliveryIsPerSignal...` asserted the bare phrase `"no exports yet"` — also built by
   the JS. Now the rendered badge markup.
3. The docs scanner matched one line at a time, so `values.yaml`'s `Empty leaves the / # status page
   open` went unflagged while the GENERATED chart README, which puts it on one line, was caught.
   Relying on a generated copy to catch its own source is not a check; it matches a two-line window
   now, with a test for the wrapped case.

Every mutation above was verified to actually land before being called a pass — the
`regen-generated.sh` silent-no-op trap from the P0 receipt.

### Tests that encoded the old contract

Two more, on top of the two in the previous receipt. `TestReadinessVerdict`'s receiver-failure
subtest asserted the narrower `receiver failure` wording, and the ingress-WAL readiness tests
asserted the old `ingress WAL:` spelling. Both were the old contract in test form, not failures.

## Phase P2 started — 3 of 18 | issue | commit | outcome | | --- | --- | --- | | #322 | `7d4aa8f` | fixed | | #319 | `8491a31` | fixed | | #312 | `c156ccd` | fixed | All 8 workflows green at `c156ccd` (Release is release-please's own, not a gate). Full gate green, regeneration a fixed point, clean tree. Chart `0.24.1` → `0.25.0` (#312 adds a key). **Remaining P2: #296, #297, #298, #299, #300, #307, #308, #309, #310, #311, #316, #320, #321, #325, #327.** P3 is untouched (7 items). ### Contract changes - **Every admin response carries defensive headers**, applied at the mux so a route added later cannot be born bare. The CSP is `default-src 'none'` with **no origin permitted in any directive**, which turns the documented "entirely self-contained, no CDN" property into something enforced — a test walks every directive and fails on any source token that is not `'none'`, `'self'`, `'unsafe-inline'` or `data:`, so adding a CDN means deliberately deleting that assertion. Scripts and styles are `'unsafe-inline'` deliberately: both pages are one inline bundle and use inline event handlers, which a nonce does **not** cover. `html/template` escaping is the XSS control; the CSP is the perimeter. HSTS only when `admin.tls` is set — on a plaintext listener a browser that saw it once would refuse `http://` to that host and port and lock the operator out. - **`/api/status.json` gained `advisories[]`** — `{key, message}` per active warning, recomputed every poll so a resolved advisory disappears without anyone clearing it.
