### Contract changes

- **`enrichment.reverse_dns.stale_ttl` (default `1h`, new).** A resolved PTR name is served for up
  to an hour past `cache_ttl` while one refresh runs, and a FAILED refresh leaves it in place rather
  than dropping it to a negative entry. Previously a transient resolver blip cost a full negative-TTL
  run of `external` labels — the flap the issue was about. Entries now occupy the cache for
  `cache_ttl + stale_ttl`, and a genuinely changed PTR is picked up up to `stale_ttl` later. New
  telemetry: `tailscale.rdns.refreshes{result}`, a `stale` result on the lookups counter, a
  `stale_expired` eviction reason.
- **`/api/flows.json` filters and paginates server-side.** Seven bounded dimensions across the whole
  retained ring, plus `recent_matched` / `recent_returned` / `recent_retained` / `recent_truncated`
  and an opaque cursor. The cursor is the ring's existing monotonic sequence, not an offset, so
  eviction between pages cannot skip or duplicate a row. A filter over 128 bytes is a 400 naming the
  parameter — truncating a filter matches MORE than was asked for, which reads as an answer. An
  unfiltered response is unchanged field for field.
- **`config.schema.json`** at the repo root (draft-07, 279 leaf keys, generated), advertised from
  `config.example.yaml` via the `yaml-language-server` directive. `TestConfigSchemaInSync` is the
  drift gate and rides `go test -race ./...` — no workflow change, no new tool module.
- **`-preflight` / `-once`.** One collection cycle, bounded by `-preflight-timeout`, `-json` for a
  machine-readable report. `-preflight` starts no listener, exports nothing without
  `-preflight-export`, persists no checkpoint, and runs no Pyroscope. Exit codes 1/2/3/4/5 name the
  class so the operator's next action is unambiguous; lowest non-zero wins.
- **`hsapi.StatusError`** now carries the Headscale status, mirroring `tsapi.StatusError`.

### Findings worth carrying

- **`-preflight` forces `collectors.acl.validate` off, and says so.** It is the one non-GET request
  the exporter makes (`POST /tailnet/{t}/acl/validate`). It mutates nothing, but "only reads, except
  for one POST you have to know about" is not the guarantee the mode is sold on. The report
  discloses the suppression rather than staying silent, so a green preflight is never read as proof
  the ACL policy validates. `-once` leaves it alone.
- **The Headscale exit-code split was silently wrong for every Headscale deployment.** `hsapi`'s
  `getJSON` wrapped each non-2xx in a bare `fmt.Errorf`, so a revoked API key had no status to
  type-assert and reported as a *collector* failure — sending an operator to debug a collector when
  the fix was to rotate the key. The whole point of 3-vs-4 is that the next action differs, so
  misclassifying is worse than not classifying. The lane found this, refused to paper over it with a
  string match (`tsapi.StatusCode`'s comment forbids exactly that), and flagged it instead of
  hiding it — the right call.
- **A defect the #297 lane shipped, caught in review.** It treated "a positive entry is present when
  this resolve lands" as "this is a refresh". `sweep()` runs only on the report interval, so an
  entry past `expires+stale_ttl` lingers in the map; a sighting in that gap is a plain miss, and a
  lookup that then failed took the keep-serving early return, so the dead entry was never replaced
  by a negative one and **every subsequent sighting re-queried the resolver** until the next sweep.
  Servability, not presence, is what makes a resolve a refresh. The window had three separate
  spellings (serve path, refresh test, eviction deadline), which is how they diverged; one
  `servableLocked` helper now defines it.
- **A new signal silently broke an existing panel.** The dashboard's rDNS hit-rate divided
  `result="hit"` by the total, and `stale` joins that total's denominator — so the panel would have
  shown the cache getting WORSE at the moment stale serving saved a lookup. Numerator now covers
  both, stale share plotted alongside. Nothing in the issue asked for this; it exists only because
  of the change.
- **The config-schema rule table matches by dotted-path SUFFIX**, so a bare leaf name (`source`,
  `port`, `layout`) would silently claim any future field with that name and give it an enum copied
  from an unrelated setting. A wrong enum is worse than none: an editor marks a valid value as an
  error and the operator believes it. All 29 current applications were checked by hand and are now
  pinned by a test, negative-tested by adding a `"timeout"` rule — it fired naming all six fields
  that would have inherited it.
- **A negative `stale_ttl` is rejected.** It is not a disable switch: it would make every entry
  unservable the instant it was written, quietly turning enrichment off while the config still read
  enabled. Zero is the documented disable.
- **`json:"...,omitempty"` is a silent no-op on a struct field**, so the new `filters` echo would
  have appeared as `"filters":{}` on every unfiltered response. `omitzero` (Go 1.24+) actually
  works.

  process-wide.
- **A per-tailnet selector on the status page**, filtering Collectors, API, Cardinality and
  Inventory, defaulting to the combined rollup. State persists in `?tailnet=`, the same convention as
  the `/flows` selector (#298) rather than a second scheme. An unknown or removed tailnet name
  degrades to combined rather than rendering empty. Single-tailnet pages are byte-identical.
- **Process-global data is LABELLED, not filtered.** Runtime, throughput and OTLP delivery describe
  one process serving every tailnet; narrowing them would be a lie, so each says so on the card.

### The dominant defect pattern, hit three more times — all the same shape as #320's

Every one is a component thoroughly tested in isolation with nothing asserting it is CONNECTED:

1. The `Full` projection could be unassigned from `/api/config.json` with the suite green (above).
2. **The event store could be disconnected from BOTH feeds with the suite green**, so the explorer
   could have shipped permanently empty. Every handler test assigned `a.eventStore` directly — and
   assigning a FRESH store *replaces* the one `buildProcessDeps` handed to `audit.NewProcessor`, so
   the processor kept feeding the original while the handler read the replacement. That is why the
   existing tests could not have caught it. Two tests now drive the real composition root end to
   end; each was verified by deleting its wiring line.
3. **The `/events` page had no link from anywhere.** Its routes register only when a store is fed, so
   the status page is the only way an operator would find it — and the two pages were built by
   different lanes, so neither package's tests would have noticed a page nobody can reach. The link
   is now gated on the store being fed and guarded in BOTH directions: linking unconditionally hands
   the operator a 404, which reads as a broken exporter rather than a disabled feature.

The lesson generalises past this tracker: **a lane split creates exactly this class of gap**, because
each lane tests what it owns and the seam belongs to neither. The wiring pass has to mutate every
seam it just connected, not merely confirm the tree builds.

### Findings worth carrying

- **`newApp` already runs the real composition root** (`buildProcessDeps` → `addRuntimeConfigured`),
  so an `internal/app` test does NOT need to hand-assemble dependencies — and hand-assigning one
  silently disconnects it, per (2) above. Prefer driving the seam.
- **Audit events carry no tailnet in the store.** `audit.Processor.Process(ev, emitter)` has no
  tailnet parameter, so audit rows have an empty `tailnet` while webhook rows are populated from the
  wire. A known asymmetry, flagged rather than papered over; threading a label through that signature
  is a separate change.
- **`docs/configuration.md` claims the flow view "obeys `pii_filter`", which the code contradicts** —
  `TestFlowsJSON_IdentityIsNotFilteredByPIIFilter` and the #241 comment both say identity is
  deliberately NOT filtered there. Pre-existing doc/code disagreement, found by the #300 lane, out of
  its scope, and still open.
- **`TestRender_PerTailnetSection`'s single-tailnet assertion was previously vacuous** — it checked
  for an `id="tailnets"` that existed nowhere in the template. It only became meaningful as a side
  effect of #325.
- **Stale editor diagnostics contradicted both lanes' reports and both lanes were right.** gopls
  reported a changed `tailnetStatuses` signature and an undefined `pathForError`; the compiler
  disagreed on both. CLAUDE.md already says to trust the compiler — worth restating, because the
  diagnostics arrived looking exactly like a lane having lied.

### Commit granularity

#300 and #325 both edit `status.go`, `statusdata.go`, `page.html.tmpl` and `statushtml_test.go`. The
#300 hunks were carved out, #325 committed and verified building and passing the full gate in
isolation, then #300 restored and committed — so each issue is one revertable commit. Every restored
file was `cmp`-verified byte-identical against the pre-carve backup before committing.

## P2 COMPLETE — wave 5 lands the last three, 18 of 18

| issue | commit | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #327 | `66ac88d` | fixed |
| #321 | `a7b49a6` | fixed |
| #309 | `355c8b1` | fixed |

Three parallel lanes on disjoint file sets, then a wiring pass. Full gate green at `355c8b1`,
regeneration a fixed point, clean tree. **All 9 workflows green at `355c8b1`**, Helm included. No
chart change this wave, so no version bump.

**Phase P2 is done except #294, which stays open and parked.** Remaining: P3 — #313 (now in scope),
#323, #324, #328, #329, #330. New follow-up filed: #512.

### Contract changes

- **`-print-effective-config`** (`json`|`yaml`) renders every key with its effective redacted value,
  sorted for byte-determinism. **`-print-effective-config-provenance`** adds which layer won each
  key: `default`, `file` or `env`. There is deliberately no flag that disables redaction, and
  provenance reports the SOURCE only — type-enforced, so it is safe on secrets.
- **`GET /api/support-bundle.zip`**, admin-gated: version, diagnostics, the complete redacted config,
  component/API/export state, the metric and log-event catalogs, and a manifest naming everything
  included AND everything excluded. Deterministic (fixed entry order, zeroed archive timestamps) and
  bounded, with truncation disclosed in the manifest. Flow records, device inventory and raw logs are
  excluded by default; device inventory has an opt-in that accepts only the literal `"1"`, and the
  other two have no opt-in path at all.
- **Both embedded UIs are keyboard-operable.** A real ARIA tablist with roving tabindex on the status
  page; focusable topology nodes, matrix cells and pickable rows on the flow view; `role="img"` plus
  live-recomputed textual summaries on all nine charts; focus-visible styles and live regions on the
  error, staleness and truncation banners.

### Two acceptance criteria NOT met, on the record

Recording these rather than letting a checked box imply coverage that does not exist:

1. **The flow timeline's drag-to-select-a-window has no keyboard equivalent.** The preset window
   buttons cover the common case; an arbitrary span cannot be chosen without a pointer.
2. **Browser-level accessibility testing was not done and is not deliverable here.** There is no JS
   test harness and adding one needs external assets, which the `default-src 'none'` CSP forbids. The
   new tests assert rendered markup and wiring only — the keyboard interactions themselves are
   implemented but **not behaviourally verified**, and no more than that is claimed.

### The wiring-pass finding: the same defect, a FOURTH time — and now closed as a class

#321's own tests build their own `http.ServeMux`, so deleting the route registration in `admin.go`
left the entire suite green while `/api/support-bundle.zip` would 404 in a running process. This is
the same shape as #320's unattached projection, #300's disconnected event store and #300's unlinked
page — four in two waves.

`TestAdminRoutes_AreActuallyRegistered` now drives the REAL `buildAdminServer` mux across every admin
route and fails loudly on a 404, with preconditions that `t.Fatal` rather than pass vacuously when a
store is absent. Verified by unregistering three different routes. **Every new admin route belongs in
that table** — the point is that a handler test which constructs its own mux, or calls the handler
directly, passes identically whether or not the route exists and whether or not it is wrapped in
`requireAdminAuth`.

### The other wiring-pass finding: provenance was a second spelling of the layering rule

`config.Provenance` necessarily replays `Load`'s three layers and diffs the tree after each, because
the merged tree has already destroyed the information — the same reason the existing secret `Source`
cannot tell YAML from env once loaded. That makes it a second spelling, which is this tracker's
dominant defect (#297's stale window had three, #320's URL redaction two, #316's reloader two whole
copies).

**Nothing tied the two together.** Proven by mutation: disabling `Load`'s environment layer entirely
left every provenance test green, so the CLI would have confidently reported `"provenance":"env"` for
keys whose effective value came from the file. A wrong provenance is worse than none — an operator
told "env" who edits an environment variable that is not in effect is worse off than one told nothing.
Same reasoning that pinned the schema rule table in #308.

`TestProvenance_AgreesWithWhatLoadActuallyDid` now asserts BOTH halves: that `Provenance` names a
source, and that the value `Load` actually produced is the one that source supplies. It uses a key set
in the file AND in the env, so it fails if env stops winning; a file-only key would pass even with the
env layer removed.

### Findings worth carrying

- **Two real provenance defects were found by running against `config.example.yaml` rather than
  synthetic fixtures.** A file writing the SAME value as the default was misreported as file-sourced,
  because the typed defaults snapshot (`config.Secret`, `config.Duration`) and koanf's untyped YAML
  parse compare unequal. And empty maps (`otlp.headers`, `profiling.pyroscope.tags`) got no
  provenance entry at all, because the flatten recursed into a zero-key map instead of treating it as
  a leaf, which is the convention the config-key surface already uses everywhere else.
- **`internal/app/eventshtml` is a third embedded page in the pre-#327 state** — it landed the same
  day as #327 and was outside its scope only because it did not exist when the issue was written.
  Filed as **#512**. This is what a lane split does: each lane covers what it owns and the seam
  belongs to neither.
- **A pre-existing accessibility bug turned up in passing**: a rule setting `outline:none` on
  `.collector-info` for hover AND focus, which killed the focus ring for keyboard users specifically.
- **`docs/configuration.md` still claims the flow view "obeys `pii_filter`"**, which
  `TestFlowsJSON_IdentityIsNotFilteredByPIIFilter` and the #241 comment both contradict. Reported in
  the wave-4 receipt, still open, still nobody's issue.
- **Stale gopls diagnostics contradicted three lanes' reports across this session and every lane was
  right** — a changed signature, an undefined method, a credential test "failing". The compiler
  disagreed every time. Trust the compiler, per CLAUDE.md.

### Commit granularity, and a near-miss worth recording

Each issue is one revertable commit; #321 and #309 both edit `docs/troubleshooting.md`, so #309's
section was stripped, #321 committed and verified building and passing the full gate in isolation,
then #309 restored and committed. Every restored file was `cmp`-verified byte-identical against the
pre-carve backup.

**The near-miss:** moving the untracked files aside by BASENAME collided —
`internal/config/provenance.go` and `internal/configexport/provenance.go` share a name, so the second
move silently overwrote the first and two files were momentarily lost. The full path-preserving
backup made immediately before the carve is what recovered them, and the `cmp` sweep afterwards is
what proved the recovery was complete. Preserve paths when staging files aside, and verify the
restore rather than assuming it.

## P3 wave 1 — 3 done, plus #313 DECLINED and its dependent closed

| issue | commit | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #512 | `25e5b2b` | fixed (follow-up filed by the P2 wave-5 receipt) |
| #330 | `e736ba2` | fixed |
| #329 | `ead2f47` | fixed |
| #313 | — | **CLOSED NOT_PLANNED — declined by Rob** |
| #492 | — | closed NOT_PLANNED, dependent on #313 |

Three parallel lanes on disjoint file sets, then a wiring pass. Full gate green at `ead2f47`
(`go build`/`vet`/`test -race`, `golangci-lint` 0 issues), regeneration a fixed point, clean tree.
Chart `0.27.0` → `0.28.0` (#329 adds a key).

**Remaining: #323 and #328, both in flight. #294 stays open and parked.** #324 was closed by Rob as
out of scope ("network lockdown is fine — tailnet after all"), so it needs no work.

### #313 declined — and this REVERSES the in-scope comment above

Rob, 2026-07-28: *"lets scrap hot reload entirely I decline it"* — the deployment model is
containers, where a restart is the reload mechanism. **The "#313 is IN SCOPE / the hot-reload
parking is REVERSED" comment earlier in this thread is superseded.** Its instruction to edit
`deploy/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/configuration.md` is now WRONG: both files still say there is no SIGHUP
and no reload route, and both are **correct as written**. Do not "fix" them. #316's certificate
reloader stays stat-on-handshake.

Full evidence and rejected alternatives are on #313. The one finding worth carrying here, because it
constrains anything that ever wants to re-read config at runtime:

- **Every credential in this codebase is captured at component-construction time. There is no
  per-use secret read anywhere.** All ~17 fields in `resolveSecretFiles`'s worklist end up frozen
  into a transport, an exporter header, a middleware closure, a server struct, an S3 provider or the
  GeoIP downloader. `admin.auth.token` and `prometheus.auth.token` are the easy ones to misjudge:
  `requireAdminAuth`/`requireMetricsAuth` read like per-request gates but are middleware
  **factories** called once at mux-build time, and the returned closure checks a captured string.
- **`App.cfg` is a plain unguarded `*config.Config`** read from ~109 non-test sites across at least
  14 files, several of them concurrently-invoked HTTP handlers. Any future swap needs an
  `atomic.Pointer` plus an accessor migration across all of them.

#492 (config-reloader sidecar) closed as a direct consequence — its own text sequences it after hot
reload, and its trigger prerequisite is now a decision taken against rather than unbuilt work.

### Contract changes

- **`/api/status.json` gained `update`** — a six-value closed state enum (`disabled`, `checking`,
  `error`, `unknown`, `current`, `available`) plus versions, `minors_behind`, `last_checked_at`,
  `last_error_class` and a static `release_url`. The enum exists because the acceptance bar is that
  a badge appears ONLY when the comparison is trustworthy: a `dev` build or an unparseable upstream
  value lands on `unknown` and can never render as `current`. `last_error_class` is surfaced even
  when the verdict came from an earlier successful fetch, so a fail-open answer says the most recent
  attempt failed rather than quietly aging. No new browser-side external request — the badge reads
  the `/api/status.json` the page already polls, and the release link is plain navigation.
- **`flows.capacity_profile`: `compact` | `default` | `expanded`** (new key, default `default`).
  Three fixed hard-coded presets scaling every per-bucket cap and the recent ring together — half,
  exactly today's values, double. Presets rather than per-dimension knobs is the point: the caps
  bound peak memory between evictions, and a number an operator could set to anything is exactly the
  unbounded raw limit the issue rules out. An unknown value, empty string included, fails validation
  naming the key. `flow_store` gained `capacity_profile`, `max_recent` and `estimated_bytes`, all
  read from the STORE rather than the config so the page reports what is in force, not what was
  asked for.
- **`estimated_bytes` is per tailnet, not summed**, and the card says it is a worst case with every
  dimension saturated at once. Summing worst cases across tailnets compounds an over-estimate into a
  number no deployment could reach.

### Findings worth carrying

- **#329 introduced a defect that the wiring pass caught and fixed in the same commit.**
  `maxExportRows` was `const = flowstore.MaxRecent`, the package constant. Under `expanded` the ring
  holds 4000 while the export stopped at 2000 — and the provenance line still said `truncated=true`,
  which reads as "the ring dropped them" rather than "the export refused to read them". Watched
  failing at exactly 2000-of-4000 before the fix. This is the class the tracker keeps hitting from a
  new angle: not a second spelling of a rule, but a constant that stopped being constant.
- **A lane rewrote its own test after finding it was not real coverage.** An earlier version drove
  the pairs cap by varying `DstNode`/`TrafficType` and survived deleting the pairs guard entirely,
  because those dimensions' own smaller caps tripped `Truncated` first and masked it. Isolated via a
  cross product now. Same shape as the P1 receipt's "a guard passes because a different guard fires
  first".
- **#512's acceptance criterion 1 was already met before the lane started**, and saying so was the
  right call rather than inventing work. The `/events` page's controls are all native `select`,
  `input`, `button` and labelled checkbox — no custom widget needs roving tabindex or `aria-pressed`.
  Verified independently against the template. A scope difference in the page, not an incomplete
  port of #327.
- **`internal/config` now imports `internal/flowstore`** for the profile constants. Accepted
  deliberately: the alternative is the profile names existing in two places, which is this tracker's
  dominant defect. No cycle — flowstore imports nothing from config.

### Vacuous assertions caught this wave: 0

Every guard in all three issues was negative-tested by deleting the exact construct it guards, with
the mutation confirmed present in the file before the run and the restore `diff`-verified after.
That includes both wiring guards added in the wiring pass — the status projection by deleting its
assignment, the page card by deleting the element.

### Not verified, and not claimed

- No live fetch against GitHub's release API for #330; no browser render for any of the three.
- #512's focus-ring contrast and actual assistive-tech announcement are markup-asserted only. There
  is no JS test harness and one must not be added — the CSP forbids the external assets it needs.

## P3 COMPLETE — wave 2 lands the last two. Tracker done except #294.

| issue | commit | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #328 | `1b3176a` | fixed |
| #323 | `fde409f` | fixed |

Two parallel lanes on disjoint file sets, then verification. Full gate green at `fde409f`:
`go build`/`vet`/`test -race`, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `verify-modules.sh` (all 5 modules incl.
`go mod tidy` diff and `govulncheck`), the Python rule suite (106 tests), `render-tests.sh` (428
assertions), regeneration a fixed point, clean tree. No chart change this wave.

**Every child of this tracker is now closed except #294, which stays open and parked indefinitely
per Rob's instruction — do not re-plan, re-scope or close it.**

### The build was red on arrival, and not from this tracker

`ci.yml`'s dashboards-drift job had failed on **every commit since `47d9e49`** (the GeoIP
enrichment commit, which predates this session's work). It added a 100th Grafana-managed alert rule
and updated the root README, but left three hand-maintained counts behind: the constant in
`deploy/alerts/gen/test_rules.py`, and two prose counts in `deploy/alerts/README.md` — one of which
("94 of the 99" carrying a panel link) was already stale before that commit. Corrected to the real
figures in `b27ed99`: **100 alert rules, 23 recording, 92 panel-linked**, cross-checked against both
the shipped manifests and the generator.

**The durable lesson:** a local `go test -race ./...` was green throughout. The count lives in a
Python suite CI runs separately, so the repo's primary gate cannot see this class at all. The root
README needed no change precisely because its counts are DERIVED by
`TestReadmeRuleCountsMatchTheShippedFiles`; the three that drifted are the three maintained by hand.
CLAUDE.md's "adding rules moves four prose counts" note covers the case where you add a rule — not
the case where someone else did and stopped after the derived one.

### Contract changes

- **Every admin JSON response carries a top-level `schema_version` integer**, starting at 1: status,
  config, cardinality, flows, events, and the flows JSON export. `ConfigSummary` and
  `CardinalityInfo` version INDEPENDENTLY of `Status` despite nesting inside it, because both are
  also served standalone and can change on their own schedule. Schemas published under
  `docs/api/schemas/`, policy in `docs/api/compatibility.md`.
- **All three embedded pages poll through one shared `createPoller`**: completion-scheduled ticks,
  an in-flight guard, a per-request `AbortController` timeout, capped exponential backoff,
  `visibilitychange` pause/resume, and a monotonic sequence number that discards a stale response.

### Decisions taken

- **The compatibility gate's two update paths are deliberately asymmetric.** `-update` regenerates
  the schemas and never touches a baseline; blessing a breaking change needs the separate
  `-update-baseline`, and the baseline pins the `SchemaVersion` constant so the acknowledgement and
  the version bump cannot drift apart. A gate that a routine regeneration silently satisfies is not
  a gate — the same reasoning that pinned #308's schema rule table.
- **#328 covers THREE pages, not the two the issue names.** `/events` landed after #328 was written.
  A rule holding for two pages out of three is worse than no rule; #316 shipped a reloader for three
  listeners out of four and that was recorded as failing its own acceptance.
- **Visibility resume does not restart a caller-paused or pinned view.** It only resumes polling
  that was already meant to be running. A paused status page staying paused across a tab switch is
  the point of having paused it.

### Findings worth carrying

- **Textual identity is the enforceable form of "one rule" when the rule cannot be a Go function.**
  The three pages are separate templates, so `createPoller` is byte-for-byte identical in all three
  and pinned by a test that extracts the block from RAW template source between sentinel comments
  and diffs it. It `t.Fatal`s on a missing marker, so it cannot pass by comparing three empty
  strings. This is the fourth appearance of the one-rule-many-spellings defect (#297's stale window
  had three, #316's reloader two whole copies, #309's provenance a second spelling of layering).
  The block sits flush-left in all three including inside eventshtml's indented IIFE — a deliberate
  style inconsistency traded for exact identity.
- **The `//` sentinel comments survive only because the test reads SOURCE.** `html/template` strips
  `//` comments out of `<script>` blocks entirely, so a rendered-output scan would never see them.
- **A lane caught two of its own guards being vacuous and fixed both.** The stale-discard gate is
  written twice (success and error paths) and a bare `Contains` passed with one copy deleted — it
  counts occurrences now; and a wiring test matched a call string anywhere on the page. Both were
  re-mutated afterwards and observed failing. Reporting them beats a clean-looking report.
- **The #323 reflector found a real bug in itself:** `flowstore.PairStat` embeds `PairKey`
  anonymously, which `encoding/json` promotes and the naive walker panicked on. Fixed and pinned.
- **The compat gate was mutation-tested against the REAL response types, not only synthetic
  fixtures**, and re-verified independently before commit: renaming `Status.Provider`'s JSON tag
  produced `provider: REMOVED (baseline promised type "string")` plus the remediation. A gate proven
  only on fixtures is a gate proven on fixtures.

### Vacuous assertions caught across both waves: 2, both self-caught by the lane that wrote them

Repo running count: 13.

### Not verified, and not claimed

- #328's runtime behaviour — that single-flight, backoff and stale-discard actually behave that way
  in a browser. Proving it needs executing the JS; there is no harness and one must not be added,
  since it would need external assets the `default-src 'none'` CSP forbids. The tests assert
  rendered script text only.
- The CSV export's `# schema_version=` comment line carries no automated assertion. CSV is not part
  of the JSON contract; its column order is its own de-facto one.

## P1 completion amended — #294 unparked and shipped (`4b25580`)

The last open child of this tracker is done, so the "#294 excepted" carve-out in the definition of done no longer applies. Body checkbox and DoD line updated.

#294 was parked on 2026-07-28 as a direction decision rather than a defect, with the instruction to start from the dependency question if it were ever picked up. That is how it was resumed: `modernc.org/sqlite` was verified empirically against the real release matrix (all five shipped targets build and run with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, +4.6 MB, BSD-3/MIT, `govulncheck` clean) before any schema work. The single-static-binary and distroless promises in `CLAUDE.md` are intact, and persistence is off by default.

Full receipts, the raw-rows-over-buckets design decision, the PII asymmetry against #241, and two integration defects the parallel build surfaced are on #294's closing comment.

Gate green at `4b25580` across all five modules; chart `0.30.0` → `0.31.0`.

title: Tracker: configuration, admin UI, and operator experience

body:
## Mission

Make the flagship and focused dashboards semantically correct, efficient, accessible, and installable, with recording and alert rules that cover both obtained Tailscale data and the exporter/poller’s own health.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P0 — dashboard-generator foundation

- [x] #495 — Make Grafana v2 dynamic-dashboard capabilities first-class before expanding coverage


### Phase P1

- [x] #385 — Correct semantic boolean maps and preserve unknown state
- [x] #386 — Rebuild the dedicated exporter-health dashboard from the current self-observability catalog
- [x] #387 — Add runbook and dashboard/panel links to every alert
- [x] #388 — Replace the global fail-open alert evaluation policy with per-rule semantics
- [x] #390 — Add a catalog-to-dashboard/rule disposition manifest
- [x] #391 — Modernize the legacy network dashboard for rollup-first operation
- [x] #399 — Add object-store ingestion health panels and alerts
- [x] #400 — Add cross-source ingestion freshness and delivery-delay views
- [x] #407 — Validate dashboard and rule queries with real parsers and synthetic fixtures

### Phase P2

- [x] #389 — Generate installable alert profiles and threshold overrides
- [x] #392 — Modernize fleet dashboards for authorization, external-device, and multi-tailnet state
- [x] #393 — Modernize audit/integration dashboards for multi-tailnet and optional-source semantics
- [x] #394 — Define and enforce the lifecycle of flagship versus legacy dashboards
- [x] #395 — Add prerequisite-aware empty states throughout the flagship
- [x] #396 — Add dashboard accessibility and visual-regression gates
- [x] #398 — Add exporter availability/freshness SLO recording and burn-rate rules
- [x] #401 — Add device connectivity and security-posture views
- [x] #402 — Add node packet-drop and peer-relay diagnostics
- [x] #403 — Add OAuth app, webhook subscription, and log-stream inventory views
- [x] #404 — Add API rate-limiter wait visibility
- [x] #405 — Cover receiver/rDNS loss and overflow signals
- [x] #406 — Expand and reuse canonical recording rules
- [x] #408 — Add post-deployment dashboard/rule smoke verification
- [x] #410 — Add approval-workflow alerts

### Phase P3

- [x] #397 — Benchmark and reduce the 298-panel flagship query load
- [x] #409 — Publish versioned dashboards to the Grafana dashboard catalog

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Complete #495 before adding dashboard panels, features, or coverage. Existing dashboard issues must consume its navigation, conditional-rendering, and generation contracts rather than inventing parallel patterns.
- Treat operational Tailscale views and exporter self-o11y as separate products with explicit navigation and signal ownership.
- Fix semantic boolean/unknown-state defects and rule evaluation policy before adding new panels.
- Consume stable recording rules and self-observation metrics from EPIC-04; do not hard-code provisional names.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every child issue is closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed stale/unsupported decision.
- [x] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [x] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules, and deployment examples agree with the final contracts.
- [x] Full repository and affected tool-module gates are green at the final integration SHA.
- [x] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail, or follow-up exists only in an agent transcript.

## Audit epic identity

`EPIC-05`

comments.body:
## Premise validation against `main` @ `6165a55` — read before starting any child

The execution contract requires validating each premise before implementation. Several numbers and
one core assumption in this tracker and its children are **stale or wrong**. Recording them here so
children inherit the corrected picture rather than re-deriving it.

### 1. The flagship is ALREADY Grafana v2 — #495's framing is wrong

#495 says the generator "must become a first-class Grafana v2 dynamic-dashboard system". It already
is one. `deploy/grafana/gen/build.py` emits `apiVersion: dashboard.grafana.app/v2`, `kind: Dashboard`,
with a real `TabsLayout` → `RowsLayout` → `GridLayout` nesting, panels in a flat `spec.elements` map
referenced by `ElementReference`, and working `ConditionalRenderingVariable` gating driven by 34
hidden `has_*` presence variables plus 10 `pii_*` redaction variables. There is no `schemaVersion`
key because that is a v1 concept. Current shape: **308 panels, 10 tabs, 101 rows, 73 variables**,
3 datasources (Prometheus/Loki/Tempo).

So #495 is not a v2 migration. The **real** gaps against the `../opnsense-exporter/grafana/`
reference are:

- **Monolith.** One 2536-line `build.py` vs the reference's `builder.py` + `tabs/*.py` + orchestrator
  split. This is what blocks parallel work — one file, one owner, so no two dashboard children can
  proceed concurrently.
- **No nested navigation.** 10 flat top-level tabs vs the reference's 7 domains × 41 leaves via a
  second `TabsLayout` nested inside each `TabsLayoutTab`.
- **No aggregation-identity chokepoint.** The reference routes every query through `sel()`/`grp()` so
  the instance label survives every aggregation, and has a test that scans ~970 targets for
  merge/drop/hide violations. tailscale2otel has no equivalent, which is the root risk behind the
  multi-tailnet asks in #392, #393 and #406.
- **Sentinels are raw query strings.** `presence_var(name, metric)` builds a query by string; the
  reference declares them structurally with validated scope modes and emits a diff-gated
  `sentinel-contract.json` + a generated table in `AUTHORING.md`.
- **Almost no tests.** See item 4.

### 2. Catalog counts are stale

| stated | actual on `main` |
| --- | --- |
| tracker: "191-signal catalog" | **270** — 255 metric descriptors + 15 log-event descriptors |
| #386: "11 of 51 current self-observability metrics" | self-obs is **67** metrics (`Group == "Self-observability"`), not 51 |
| tracker/children: "79 rules" / "68 live alert rules" | **85** — 73 alert rules + 12 recording rules, 55 paused |

Operational (tailnet) metrics: 188. Distinct label/attribute names across metrics and logs: 177.

### 3. #407's "four versus five groups" is real, but the defect is in the prose

`docs/alerts.md:35` says "Rules are organised into four groups:" and then lists **five** bullets
immediately below it. The generator and the shipped artifact both produce five
(`tailscale2otel-health` 26, `-security` 25, `-integrations` 10, `-network` 12, `-recording` 12).
`deploy/alerts/README.md:57` already says five correctly. So the file contradicts *itself*, not just
the code — which is a stronger argument for #407's "include documentation counts/group names in
generation" clause than the issue makes.

### 4. `deploy/grafana/gen/test_ingest_freshness.py` never runs

It is a real 4-test `unittest` suite that passes locally, and it is invoked by **nothing** — not CI,
not `scripts/regen-generated.sh`, not `.githooks/pre-commit`. Exhaustive grep for the filename across
workflows, scripts, hooks and Go sources returns no hits. The Python generators also have no linter
or formatter configured anywhere in the repo. Wiring a Python test job is a prerequisite for #407 and
#396, not an optional extra.

Related gap: `.githooks/pre-commit` has regeneration triggers for the helm, metrics and env-ref
artifacts but **none for the dashboard/alert generator inputs**, so editing `build.py` and committing
only that file does not regenerate the JSON locally. CI's `dashboards-drift` is the only backstop.

### 5. Confirmed as stated

- #385: `BOOL_MAP` (`build.py:457`) hardcodes 0→red/"off", 1→green/"on" regardless of the panel's own
  thresholds. Three inverse-risk panels render backwards — "SSH wildcard enabled" (`build.py:632`),
  "SSH wildcard" (`build.py:2167`, duplicate of the same metric), and "Exporter update available"
  (`build.py:873`). There are **64** `or vector(0)` zero-fills, four of them on update-availability.
- #388: all 73 alert rules use `execErrState: OK`; `ts-2o-exporter-down` is the only rule with
  `noDataState: Alerting`. Confirmed exactly.
- #387: no rule carries `runbook_url`, `__dashboardUid__` or `__panelId__` — all three substrings are
  absent from the serialized artifact. Annotations are `summary` + `description` only.
- #390: no disposition mechanism exists for catalog signals. The nearest prior art is
  `internal/tsapi/contract/dispositions.go` (#422) — closed disposition set + embedded JSON baseline +
  non-silencing `-update`. #390 should mirror that pattern one layer downstream.

### 6. Two constraints that change the design

**Conditional rendering is tab/row level only — never per-panel.** The reference states this as a hard
rule and has zero panel-level conditions. That means #495's "disabled, unsupported, absent, and
unhealthy states have deliberate, distinct rendering semantics" is **not fully achievable through
layout**. The reference renders two states honestly: *absent* (sentinel empty → tab/row hidden, and
disabled / unsupported / never-deployed are deliberately indistinguishable because all three produce
no series) and *configured-but-unhealthy* (series exists → row renders, and the value carries the
fault via mappings/thresholds). The remaining discrimination has to come from panel `noValue` text and
descriptions, not from hiding. Children #395 and #495 should adopt the honest two-state model plus
explicit empty-state text rather than claim four layout states.

Corollary the reference learned the hard way: gating a sentinel on `> 0` instead of existence
conflates "absent" with "present but zero" and hides the very health panel that answers "is it up?".
Presence must test existence, not value.

**#409 conflicts with #495.** Grafana's docs state plainly that "Exporting with the Classic model is
required for publishing to the Grafana community catalog" — a v2 dynamic dashboard cannot be published
there. #409 therefore needs either a second Classic-model rendering generated from the same source of
truth, or an evidence-backed close as unsupported. It is not a straightforward follow-on to #495 and
should not be planned as one.

### Sequencing consequence

#495 is being done as a staged refactor whose first two stages are provably safe: extract `builder.py`
and `tabs/*.py` as a **pure move** verified by the generated `tailscale2otel.json` remaining
byte-identical, then add the test suite and CI wiring, then the behavioural changes (structural
sentinels, nested navigation, empty-state semantics). One tab module per owner is what makes the P1
and P2 content children parallelisable at all.

## Phase receipt — P0 foundation, P1 correctness, and the P2 content wave

Commits, all on `main`: `8f36ffd` · `5841ebd` · `1d2203b` · `be4fc7d` · `e54a4cd` · `9a3674c`.

### Closed

| issue | commit | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #390 | `1d2203b` | disposition manifest + CI gate |
| #385 | `be4fc7d` | semantic boolean maps + build-time polarity guard |
| #409 | — | closed **unsupported**: the community catalog requires a Classic export |
| #394 | `9a3674c` | four legacy classic-schema dashboards deleted |
| #387 #388 #407 | `e54a4cd`, `9a3674c` | runbook/panel links, per-rule policy, real-parser gate |
| #386 #391 #392 #393 #399 #401 #402 #403 #404 #405 | `9a3674c` | dashboard halves complete — see the per-issue comments |

### The headline number

The #390 manifest measured coverage at **71 of 270 signals with no dashboard or alert surface at
all**. It is now **0**: 258 visualized, 11 recorded, 69 alertable, 6 `raw_only` and 2 `omitted`, each
of the last eight with a written reason. The dashboard went 308 → 404 panels; rules went 73 → 90.

### Deviations from the tracker, with reasons

**#495's premise was wrong and the issue was re-scoped.** The flagship was *already* Grafana v2 with
`TabsLayout`, `RowsLayout`, conditional rendering and 34 presence variables. The real gaps were a
2536-line monolith, no tests that CI ran, and sentinels declared in one shared function. All three
are fixed. **Nested sub-tab navigation is NOT done** and #495 stays open for it — see below.

**Three tracker/issue numbers were stale** and are corrected in the premise comment above: the
catalog is 270 signals not 191, self-obs is 67 metrics not 51, and the rule pack was 85 not 79.

**The alert format changed on the owner's direction.** Grafana-managed
`rules.alerting.grafana.app/v0alpha1` manifests pushed with `gcx resources push`, replacing both the
`apiVersion: 1` provisioning document and the hand-maintained Prometheus-ruler file. The project is
**Grafana 13+ / v2 only and will never ship a Classic export**, which is also what closed #409.

**#391 and #393 were re-scoped** from "modernize the legacy dashboard" to "fold the substance into
the flagship tab", because the legacy dashboards they named were deleted under #394.

### Two findings worth carrying forward

**Deleting the Prometheus rules file silently removed five alert behaviours that existed nowhere
else.** The #390 gate caught it; nothing else in the repo could have. All five are restored, and none
was redundant: the scrape error-rate rule catches a collector *flapping* between scrapes, which the
last-verdict `scrape_success_ratio` rule cannot see by construction. Restoring the node-metrics one
also fixed a latent bug — it templated `{{ $labels.instance }}`, a label that metric never emits, so
the page always rendered a blank hostname.

**`gcx resources validate` cannot validate these manifests.** It reports *"does not support
server-side dry-run … It did not validate the spec"*, and all 25 `noDataState` × `execErrState`
casing combinations pass through it. Since `noDataState` spells its OK value **`"Ok"`** while
`execErrState` spells its own **`"OK"`**, and the wrong casing makes a rule un-deployable while every
offline check passes, `deploy/alerts/gen/validate_manifests.py` is the only real gate.

### Gates green at `9a3674c`

`go build` · `go vet` · `go test -race ./...` · `golangci-lint` (0 issues) · `scripts/verify-modules.sh`
across all five modules including the new `tools/promqlcheck` · both Python suites (71 + 59) ·
`promqlcheck` 548 PromQL expressions, 0 failures · `promtool check` + `promtool test` ·
`scripts/regen-generated.sh` a verified fixed point.

Every new gate was **negative-tested** — broken deliberately to confirm it fails — rather than
assumed: the disposition gate, the CI-wiring assertions, the polarity guard, promqlcheck, and the
promtool fixtures.

### Still open

- [ ] #495 — **nested sub-tab navigation only.** Ten flat top-level tabs; the reference groups 41
      leaves under 7 domains. Everything else on the issue is done.
- [ ] #389 alert profiles · #396 a11y/visual-regression gates · #397 query-load benchmark (research)
      · #398 SLO burn-rate rules · #406 canonical recording rules · #408 post-deploy smoke · #410
      approval-workflow alerts
- [ ] **Alert halves** of #399, #401, #402, #404, #405 — the dashboard work landed; the panels those
      alerts should link to now exist. The four named on #399's own comment are the strongest
      candidates, `undecodable_object > 0` above all, since any non-zero means a broken feed.
- [ ] #395 prerequisite-aware empty states is **substantially satisfied** as a side effect — every
      new optional section names its config key and prerequisite, and a test forbids empty-state text
      from asserting a cause. It needs an audit pass over the pre-existing panels, not new work.

### One honest limitation, recorded rather than papered over

Presence gating **cannot** distinguish *disabled* from *unsupported* from *never-deployed* — all
three produce no series. The tracker and #495 ask for four distinct rendering states; the layout can
express two. So every empty state names the config key and the prerequisite and stops there, and a
test forbids text that asserts a specific cause. Claiming the fourth state would be a guess rendered
as fact.

## Phase receipt — alert halves closed (#399, #401, #402, #404, #405)

One commit: `99c1226`, pushed to `main`, CI green. **17 of 28 children now closed.** Tracker checkboxes were stale for every previously-closed child and have been reconciled in the body.

### What shipped

13 alert rules, **78 -> 91**. No new recording rules. These five issues all had their dashboard half delivered in `9a3674c`, which left the faults visible on a panel and reported by nothing — every one of them is silent by construction, so a panel nobody is looking at was the only surface.

| issue | rules | policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #399 object-store | 4 | all `optional`, one ships **enabled** |
| #405 receivers/rDNS/name-budget | 4 | all `optional` |
| #402 node drops + peer relay | 2 | `optional` |
| #401 device posture | 2 | `optional` |
| #404 rate-limiter wait | 1 | `advisory` |

Policy split is now coverage_critical **1**, core **7**, optional **64**, advisory **19**. `ExporterDown` remains the only coverage_critical rule — none of these 13 changed that allowlist, and none of them should: every one is keyed on a source that is legitimately absent when unconfigured.

Panel links: **90 of 91** rules now carry `__dashboardUid__`/`__panelId__`. All 13 new rules link, resolved by title at build time.

### Decisions worth not re-litigating

- **Two signals deliberately left unalerted**, with a test that keeps them out: `network.store.dropped` (only trims a local in-memory view — OTLP emission is unaffected, nothing is lost) and `webhook.duplicates` (a counted duplicate is the dedup failsafe working). Both stay `visualized` in the disposition manifest. Without the test, the next coverage pass reads them as a gap.
- **The unauthorized-device case stays with #410** so it and #401 do not double-page.
- **#404 ships with an admitted placeholder threshold** rather than being deferred. There is no honest way to pick a client-side rate-limiter wait threshold without a baseline; it ships paused with the tuning procedure in the description.
- **No recording rule for the rate-limiter quantile** — the panel aggregates `by (le, endpoint)` and the rule `by (le)`, so a shared series serves neither. Revisit under #406.

### Verification

Beyond the standard gate: **26 new promtool scenarios EXECUTE these rules against synthetic series.** Parsing proves an expression is well-formed; only execution proves it fires when it should. Every load-bearing behaviour was negative-tested — broken, confirmed to fail, restored:

- the `-1` no-discovery sentinel firing (#399) — a naive `> 3600` passes the two obvious cases and silently fails this one;
- the ACL exclusion holding under a fast ACL drop series (#402);
- `min_over_time` distinguishing a stuck backlog from fill-and-drain (#399);
- delta-not-level on key-expiry-disabled (#401).

Gate: `go build`/`vet`/`test -race`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), `verify-modules.sh` (all 5 modules), grafana gen 71 tests, alerts gen 68 tests, `promqlcheck` 561 PromQL expressions / 0 failures, `validate_manifests.py` 104 manifests, `promtool check rules` + `promtool test rules` across 4 fixture files, and `regen-generated.sh` verified idempotent by checksum.

The disposition gate did its job again: it flagged exactly the 13 signals moving to `alertable`, in both directions, before any of this could ship half-recorded.

### Remaining, in value order

1. **#406** canonical recording rules — #404 has already produced one candidate.
2. **#398** SLO burn-rate rules.
3. **#410** approval-workflow alerts — carries the unauthorized-device case held back from #401.

## EPIC-05 complete — all 28 children closed

Final session: **15 children closed across 5 commits**, `8f36ffd` -> `e0e20b9`, all pushed to `main`, CI green.

| commit | closes |
| --- | --- |
| `9a3674c` | dashboard halves (#385 #386 #387 #388 #390 #391 #392 #393 #394 #403 #407 #409 earlier) |
| `99c1226` | #399 #401 #402 #404 #405 — the alert halves |
| `623240e` | #406 #398 #410 — canonical recordings, SLO burn-rate, approval workflow |
| `db37106` | #395 #400 — false-healthy-zeros, cross-source ingestion |
| `ea53c30` | #389 #396 #397 #408 — profiles, a11y gates, budget, deployment verification |
| `e0e20b9` | #495 — two-level navigation |

## Where the artifacts ended up

**97 alert rules + 23 recording rules** (from 78 + 12), **405 panels** across **5 top-level tabs** (from 10 flat), **270 signals** every one carrying a declared disposition.

Evaluation policy: coverage_critical **1**, core **10**, optional **67**, advisory **19**. Panel links **92/97**. Runbook coverage **97/97** across 29 sections.

Test suites: **163** dashboard, **105** alert-generator, **5** promtool fixture files, **579** PromQL expressions parsed, **121** manifests schema-validated.

## The defects this actually found

Worth recording separately from the feature work, because these were live wrongness rather than gaps:

1. **Three security panels rendered a green `0` for checks that never ran** (#395). The Security scorecard row is gated on the ACL collector, but `Untagged devices`, `Unapproved subnet routes` and `Pending exit-node shares` are fed by the devices collector and zero-filled. "Untagged devices: 0" read as "every device is tagged".
2. **77 deployed rules still carry the pre-#388 fail-open `execErrState`** (#408). The per-rule policy fix has been in the repo since `e54a4cd` and was never pushed, so a query error still reads as OK on the live stack. Plus one orphaned rule, `ts2o-api-auth-failing`, still evaluating after deletion from the repo — `gcx resources push` is additive and never removes.
3. **An empty-state string asserted a cause it could not know** ("...or exporter self-observability is off"), found only once the text rules were made global rather than per-panel-list.
4. **Deleting the old Prometheus rules file had silently removed five alert behaviours** that existed nowhere else — caught by the #390 disposition manifest, which nothing else in the repo could have noticed.

## Decisions recorded, not to be re-litigated

- **Grafana v2 / 13+ only.** No Classic export ever — v1 cannot express `conditionalRendering`, so every feature-gated tab would render permanently EMPTY. This is why #394 deleted the legacy dashboards and #409 closed as unsupported.
- **Presence cannot distinguish disabled from unsupported from never-deployed.** Empty states name the config key and prerequisite and never assert a cause; a test forbids the phrasings that do.
- **Collector identity, not metric-name identity**, decides whether a zero-fill is honest.
- **The three SLIs stay separate.** A blended SLO reports a backend outage as an exporter failure.
- **#396 requirement 4 (render tabs in CI) declined** with evidence: the image renderer screenshots dense tabs before queries resolve. Manual `gcx dashboards snapshot` remains the visual-review path.
- **#397 optimisation deliberately not applied.** Whether hidden tabs issue queries is a live Grafana 13.2.0 question that changes real load ~5x and is not answerable offline; the issue says to optimise only where measurement justifies it.

## Open, and deliberately so

- **The live stack is out of sync** — 43 missing, 1 orphaned, 77 drifted. Nothing was pushed; deploying is yours to decide. `gcx resources push -p deploy/alerts/grafana-managed`, then delete `ts2o-api-auth-failing` by hand, then `python3 scripts/verify_deployment.py` to confirm (exit 0 = in sync).
- **Seven `policy=core` rules ship paused** (#389), which makes `baseline` not a subset of `recommended`. Right for the three SLO rules; `ts2o-config-invalid` looks like it should be enabled. Encoded as a reviewed known-deviation rather than silently changing your defaults.
- **The `--tab` preview sentinel gotcha** persists: previewing a tab that consumes a sentinel it does not own references an undeclared variable. Harmless for the full build.

Closing the tracker.

title: Tracker: Grafana dashboards, rules, and exporter self-observability

body:
## Mission

Make OTLP push, Prometheus pull, logs, traces, and Pyroscope predictable and diagnosable under failure while preserving the exporter’s resource, PII, cardinality, and multi-tailnet contracts.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P1

- [x] #375 — Add Pyroscope custom TLS and secret header controls
- [x] #457 — feat(otlp): make metric temporality selectable

### Phase P2

- [x] #356 — Pseudonymize per-tailnet `service.instance.id` when tailnet-name PII is disabled
- [x] #357 — Add a real OTLP HTTP/gRPC wire-contract integration suite
- [x] #358 — Configure log/trace batch queues and expose saturation/drop telemetry
- [x] #359 — Complete exporter self-observability for traces, partial success, and local status
- [x] #360 — Expose deterministic OTLP compression, timeout, retry, and request-size controls
- [x] #361 — Support independent signal destinations and enablement
- [x] #362 — Reload outbound telemetry credentials and TLS material without restarting
- [x] #363 — Ship production Alloy/Collector gateway recipes
- [x] #364 — Benchmark and reduce multi-tailnet exporter fan-out and synchronized bursts
- [x] #365 — Rate-limit OTLP outage diagnostics and emit recovery summaries
- [x] #366 — Bound individual OTLP log records and expose truncation
- [x] #367 — Preserve trace context on logs and receiver metrics
- [x] #368 — Negotiate OpenMetrics so pull-path exemplars survive
- [x] #369 — Add a scrape-duration histogram with trace exemplars
- [x] #370 — Add opt-in Pyroscope span-profile correlation
- [x] #371 — Trace currently dark outbound HTTP dependencies
- [x] #372 — Add workload-specific head-sampling controls
- [x] #373 — Add a trust policy for inbound `traceparent` sampling decisions
- [x] #374 — Expose Pyroscope upload health and complete profile identity
- [x] #376 — Add bounded collector labels to continuous profiles
- [x] #377 — Harden and instrument `/metrics` serving
- [x] #378 — Support client-certificate authentication on `/metrics`
- [x] #379 — Pin Prometheus translation semantics and test the complete name contract
- [x] #380 — Support controlled standard OTel Resource enrichment
- [x] #381 — Evaluate exponential/native histograms as a series-cost reduction
- [x] #382 — Evaluate OTel Go’s experimental SDK/exporter self-observation
- [x] #383 — Repair trace-era telemetry documentation and stale comments
- [x] #384 — Make `stdout` a genuinely immediate debugging exporter

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Freeze signal/exporter self-observation contracts before wiring dashboards and alerts in EPIC-05.
- Keep OTEL core and log SDK versions in lockstep and confirm current library behavior with upstream docs.
- Do not build embedded queueing, tail sampling, or backend fan-out that belongs in Alloy/Collector.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every child issue is closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed stale/unsupported decision.
- [x] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [x] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules, and deployment examples agree with the final contracts.
- [x] Full repository and affected tool-module gates are green at the final integration SHA.
- [x] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail, or follow-up exists only in an agent transcript.

## Audit epic identity

`EPIC-04`
