## Premise validation of all 29 open children (before any implementation)

132 commits have landed since the audit SHA `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`, none of them closing a child of this tracker. Every child's premise was therefore re-checked against current `main` before any code was written, per this tracker's execution contract. Three premises had moved:

**#360 — the headline fix already shipped.** The 2026-07-27 <host-1> 413 incident comment asks for export batching that keeps each request under the backend's ingest limit, and notes `OTEL_GO_X_METRIC_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE` was available but unexposed. It is now exposed: `otlp.metric_export_batch_size` (default 10000) is wired through `internal/telemetry/provider.go`'s `newPeriodicMetricReader`, and `internal/telemetry/provider_batching_test.go` decodes real protobuf off an httptest server to prove one cumulative collection is delivered as multiple OTLP requests. That is the acceptance criterion the incident comment added, already met. What remains under #360 is only compression, exporter/reader timeouts, retry policy, gRPC connection options, and the documented precedence between built-ins / YAML / `TS2OTEL_*` / standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_*` variables — no `OTEL_EXPORTER_*` handling exists at all today (`rg OTEL_EXPORTER` → zero hits), so that precedence is genuinely undefined.

**#359 is largely delivered.** `internal/telemetry/delivery.go` and `delivery_trace.go` did not exist at the audit SHA. Traces are no longer invisible — `observingSpanExporter` wraps the trace exporter into the same `deliveryTracker` as metrics and logs; `DeliveryState` carries exports/failures/consecutive-failures/last-success/last-failure/duration/error-class, populated unconditionally so the admin page works on a deployment that exports no self-telemetry; `classifyExportError` is a closed 7-value taxonomy that never forwards backend error text; and `ProviderSet.Delivery()` merges per-provider state worst-case-wins for multi-tailnet attribution. What actually remains: no span-count tally (`delivery_trace.go` says so in a comment and defers it explicitly), no OTLP `partial_success` handling anywhere (`rg artial` → zero hits), and `docExportFailures` still carries only `error.type` with no signal attribute.

**#372 / #373 — `internal/app/sampler.go` is a red herring.** It is new since the audit and its name suggests trace sampling, but it is entirely the admin status page's in-memory runtime/cardinality sparklines (`runtimeHistory`, `runSampler`, `samplerTick`). No `sdktrace.Sampler`, no per-class logic. The real sampler is still one global head sampler from `buildSampler` in `internal/telemetry/trace.go`, applied to scrape, receiver and background spans alike. Both issues are fully open.

Also worth recording: #371's baseline holds — the Tailscale API client **is** already traced (`internal/tsapi/transport.go`), and the three dark dependencies (`internal/hsapi/client.go`, `internal/collector/nodemetrics`, `internal/release`) are confirmed still dark. And every individual defect #383 lists is still present, at shifted line numbers, including a live self-contradiction inside `docs/configuration.md` (line ~418 calls `tailscale.tailnet` a resource attribute; line ~1549 correctly calls it signal-scoped).

## Frozen seams

`internal/config/config.go` and `internal/telemetry/provider.go` are contested by roughly fifteen children, so they are single-owner for this program and the config schema is frozen up front rather than negotiated per lane. Decisions taken, so they are not re-litigated later:

| child | frozen schema |
| --- | --- |
| #377 | `prometheus.max_requests_in_flight` (0 = unlimited), `prometheus.timeout` (0 = none), `prometheus.coalesce_gather` |
| #378 | `prometheus.tls.client_ca_file`, `prometheus.tls.client_auth` ∈ {`require_and_verify`, `verify_if_given`, `require`, `request`, `none`}; empty defaults to `require_and_verify` once a CA is set |
| #375 | `profiling.pyroscope.headers` (secret values), `profiling.pyroscope.tls.{insecure_skip_verify,ca_file,cert_file,key_file}` |
| #361 | `otlp.{metrics,logs,traces}` sub-blocks; nil inherits the common block |
| #380 | new top-level `resource:` block — `service_namespace`, `deployment_environment`, `attributes`, `from_env` (default false) |
| #372 | `tracing.samplers.{scrape,receiver,background}.{sampler,arg}`; unset falls back to the existing global sampler |
| #373 | `tracing.remote_parent` ∈ {`trust`, `ignore`, `link`}, default `trust` (current behaviour) |

#368 deliberately gets no config key: OpenMetrics is content negotiation, not a toggle.

Two validation helpers were added because "the file is readable" was already proven insufficient for keypairs (#305) and is equally insufficient for CA bundles: `validateCAFile` refuses a bundle that parses to an empty `x509.CertPool` (which would silently trust nothing and fail every handshake at request time), and `validateClientKeypair` applies the both-or-neither + actually-loadable rule to outbound client certificates. A client CA on a plaintext listener is also refused outright, since TLS only ever requests a client certificate during a handshake — configured-but-inert is the exact shape #305 stopped tolerating.

## Phase P1

- [x] #382 — closed as evaluated-and-deferred; see the decision record on that issue. It was gating, so recording the outcome here: `OTEL_GO_X_OBSERVABILITY` would be a **silent no-op** in this process (every instrument resolves through the global `MeterProvider`, which this app deliberately never sets), and making it non-no-op means giving one of N+1 providers the single global slot, which either erases per-tailnet attribution or mis-attributes every other tailnet's exporter activity to one tailnet. Pinned `sdk/log@v0.20.0` also only instruments `SimpleProcessor`, never the `BatchProcessor` this repo uses for logs, so there is no upstream answer to #358's log-queue ask at all. **Consequence for #358/#359: keep `tailscale2otel.*` naming.** Borrow the modelling — exported-vs-inflight split, `queue_full` as a first-class drop reason, partial-success-aware counting — not the names.

## Phase receipt — 16 of 29 children closed

| SHA | closes |
| --- | --- |
| `5c422ab` | #363 |
| `3858408` | #356, #366, #367, #369, #371, #374, #375, #376, #377, #378, #379 |
| — (decision records, no code) | #364, #381, #382 |
| `3858408`, closed by hand | #368 |

**#368 was closed manually.** `3858408` implements it but omitted the number from its `Closes` footer and the history is published, so per this repo's workflow the keyword was not retrofitted — a closing comment naming the SHA was posted instead.

`3858408` landed as one commit on purpose. `docs/metrics.md`, `config.schema.json`, `docs/env-vars.md`, `docs/signal-coverage.md`, `signal_dispositions.json` and the chart's schema/README are each derived from the whole catalog or the whole `Config` struct, so splitting per issue would have left intermediate commits failing their own `fail-on-diff` gates.

Verified at `3858408`, not asserted: `go build`, `go vet`, `go test -race ./...`, `golangci-lint run` (0 issues), `scripts/verify-modules.sh` green across all five modules, `helm lint`, `configcheck` on both `config.example.yaml` and the chart-rendered config, and every generated artifact regenerated and in sync. Chart bumped to `0.29.0`.

### Findings worth keeping

**#379 found a live bug, which is what that issue existed to catch.** `metricdoc.PromName()` reimplemented Prometheus normalization rather than delegating to it, and did not dedupe a unit-suffix token already present in the name. Three metrics were therefore documented — and queried by the flagship dashboard — under names that have **never existed on the wire**:

| documented and queried | actually served |
| --- | --- |
| `tailscale_logstream_bytes_sent_bytes_total` | `tailscale_logstream_bytes_sent_total` |
| `tailscale2otel_objectstore_bytes_bytes_total` | `tailscale2otel_objectstore_bytes_total` |
| `tailscale2otel_objectstore_decompressed_bytes_bytes_total` | `tailscale2otel_objectstore_decompressed_bytes_total` |

Those panels have been silently "No data" since they were written, on **both** transport paths, because Mimir's OTLP ingest applies the same library. `PromName()` now delegates to `prometheus/otlptranslator` — the library the exporter and Mimir both use — so the class of bug cannot recur. **No emitted metric name changed**, proven by a differential test across all 271 catalog metrics, so this was a docs/dashboard correction rather than a breaking change. The three generator sources were fixed and the dashboard regenerated.

**Two secret-leak holes in the upstream `pyroscope-go` SDK, closed while doing #374.** It formats a non-200 into `"failed to upload: (%d) '%s'"` with the response body **verbatim** and hands that to its logger, and its transport errors are `*url.Error` carrying the full URL. Both are now replaced with a closed error class before anything is logged. Worth knowing for any future use of that SDK.

**Header precedence in `pyroscope.Config` is the reverse of what you would want.** It applies `HTTPHeaders` with `Header.Set` *after* `SetBasicAuth` and the tenant header, so a user-supplied `Authorization` would win over the real credential. #375 therefore enforces reserved-header precedence by **removal** before the map reaches the SDK, not by ordering.

**`alloy validate` does not prove a config loads** (#363). It checks syntax and attribute names, not that the component graph builds. Two bugs got through it and appeared only on a real `alloy run`: `grafana.com/docs/alloy/latest` documents a `client_auth {}` block that **fails at startup on v1.18.0** (those docs are built from `main` and are ahead of the release; the flat `username`/`password` form is correct there and not deprecated), and the `grafana/alloy` image ships no HTTP client at all, so a `wget --spider` healthcheck fails on the missing executable rather than on Alloy.

`ContinueOnError` on `/metrics` still returns **500** when a Gather yields nothing at all — the registry must hold at least one healthy series for the partial-success path to run, so a test with only a broken collector tests the wrong branch.

### Dispositions

All thirteen new self-obs signals were given a `raw_only` disposition with a stated reason rather than left empty. Two are flagged in those notes as the strongest alert candidates once a baseline exists: `tailscale2otel.metrics.scrape.gather_errors` (a partial `/metrics` response returns 200 by design, so nothing else reveals it) and `tailscale2otel.log.record.truncated` (truncation is silent apart from the marker).

### Deliberately not done, so it does not read as an oversight

- **`tailscale2otel.scrape.duration.histogram` is not yet on a dashboard.** #369's acceptance mentions p50/p95/p99 panels; the flagship dashboard's scrape panels still read the retained gauge. Moving them is a visualization change that belongs with the panel edit, and the disposition note says so.
- **#376's optional pseudonymous tailnet profile label is not emitted.** A tailnet name is a customer identifier and the README claims profiles carry no Tailscale data. The config key it would need is `profiling.pyroscope.tailnet_label` (`off` default / `hashed` / `name`); landing it must update that README claim in the same commit.
- **#367 does not cover the streaming receivers' flow and audit logs.** `internal/stream`'s `flowProc.Process`/`auditProc.Process` and `internal/webhook`'s `emit()` still use the context-free variants, so a sampled flow or audit log arriving via HEC/webhook carries no trace context — only the poll path does. The `ProcessCtx`/`LogEventCtx` plumbing now exists, so this is a three-call-site follow-up.
- **#377's status DTO fields are not added.** The self-obs metrics carry the substance; the fields wanted are `ScrapesTotal`/`ScrapesShed`/`ScrapesFailed`, `InFlight`, `LastScrapeAt`/`LastScrapeDuration`, `GatherErrors`/`LastGatherError`/`LastGatherErrorAt`, `AuthRejected`, plus an effective-config echo.

### Remaining: 13 children

#357, #358, #359, #360, #361, #362, #365, #370, #372, #373, #380, #383, #384.

These are the `internal/telemetry/provider.go` exporter core plus the sampler work, and they contend for the same two files, so they are single-owner rather than parallelisable. Sequencing notes for whoever picks them up:

- **#358 and #359 must use `tailscale2otel.*` names**, per the #382 decision already recorded on this tracker. Concrete names are given there.
- **#360 is narrower than its body suggests** — the export-batching fix the <host-1> 413 comment asked for already shipped; only compression, timeouts, retry policy, gRPC options and the `OTEL_EXPORTER_*` precedence remain.
- **#359 is largely delivered** by `delivery.go`/`delivery_trace.go`; what is left is span counting, `partial_success`, and a signal attribute on `docExportFailures`.
- **#372 and #373 touch the same `tr.Start` call sites and the same sampler construction path**, so they want one owner and a layered sampler decorator, not two parallel edits to `buildSampler`. Frozen config schemas for both are in the seam-freeze comment above.
- **#383 should go last**, since its whole job is making the docs agree with the final contracts. Note it has already grown: `internal/telemetry/provider.go`'s `Options.TailnetName` and `Options.Provider` doc comments still describe both as *resource* attributes, which `constLabelAttrs` contradicts.

## Phase receipt — EPIC-04 complete, 29 of 29 children closed

| SHA | closes |
| --- | --- |
| `5c422ab` | #363 |
| `3858408` | #356, #366, #367, #369, #371, #374, #375, #377, #378, #379 |
| `0a3536e` | the streaming half of #367 (already closed; see below) |
| `0084290` | #357, #358, #359, #360, #361, #362, #365, #370, #372, #373, #380, #383, #384 |
| — (decision records, no code) | #364, #381, #382 |
| `3858408`, closed by hand | #368 |
| `18050d3`, `1e63883`, `8ed3cb0` | enabling refactors + one deps chore, close nothing |

Also closed earlier in this program: #375 and #457 (Phase P1).

### What made the remaining thirteen parallelisable

The previous receipt judged them single-owner because roughly fifteen contended for
`internal/telemetry/provider.go`, which had reached 798 lines. Two enabling commits changed that,
and they are the reusable part of this run:

- **`18050d3`** split `provider.go` along the axes the outstanding issues actually work on —
  `exporters.go`, `processors.go`, `resource.go`, `sampler.go` — as a pure mechanical move, plus
  four new seams (`newMetricReader`, `newLogProcessor`, `newSpanProcessor`, `newSampler`) so
  `NewProvider` stopped being the place processor and sampler policy is decided.
- **`1e63883`** added one nested `Options` block per issue, each **defined in the file that owns the
  behaviour it configures**. That is the trick worth remembering: a lane adds fields to its own
  struct in its own file instead of fifteen lanes editing one type.

Ten lanes then ran concurrently, each in its own git worktree so a lane could not break another's
compile — six of them were editing the same Go package. Config, docs, generated artifacts and all
wiring stayed with the integrator.

### Findings worth keeping

**A partial success was being counted as an outage.** The pinned exporters return a **non-nil error**
for an OTLP `partial_success` — the request arrives, decodes, the server answers 200, and
`Export`/`ForceFlush` still errors (`otlpmetrichttp`'s client joins `MetricPartialSuccessError` into
the return). `deliveryTracker.observe` had no carve-out, so a backend that accepted everything while
attaching an advisory message incremented `ConsecutiveFailures`; three in a row flipped
`DeliveryState.Failing()` on a perfectly healthy deployment. Now routed to `PartialSuccesses`, and
pinned on both transports by the #357 suite against a real receiver.

**#382's "upstream gives us nothing" finding extends to spans, not just logs.** That decision record
established that `sdk/log@v0.20.0` never instruments `BatchProcessor`. The same is true of the span
queue: `sdktrace`'s `dropped` counter and queue length are private fields on unexported types, and
its `internal/observ` instrumentation is reachable only through the process-global `MeterProvider`,
which #382 already ruled out. So #358's three queue metrics come from this repo's own queueing
wrapper and are emitted **only under self-observability**, where that wrapper is installed. That is
recorded in the signal dispositions rather than left for a reader to discover from a zero.

**`ShouldSample` really does receive Start-time attributes**, verified against
`sdk@v1.44.0/trace/tracer.go` rather than assumed — the whole per-class sampling design depends on
it. The corollary is that an attribute set via `span.SetAttributes` after `Start` is invisible to the
sampler, which has already run. And `link` mode for #373 cannot live in a `Sampler` at all, because
links are set at span start; it is a call-site helper.

**Grafana's `otel-profiling-go` v0.6.0 is much smaller than its docs imply.** Only
`NewTracerProvider` plus two scope options are live; `WithAppName`, `WithPyroscopeURL`, the
profile-URL builders and `WithRootSpanOnly` are all `DEPRECATED: Ignored by tracer` with literally
empty function bodies, while the Grafana docs page presents several of them as working. Same class of
gap as the `alloy` `client_auth {}` block from #363 — the docs run ahead of the released artifact.
Followed the module, not the page.

**Two real defects the parallel build exposed, same blind spot in both.**
`internal/ci/workflowcontract_test.go`'s two tree walks and `scripts/verify-modules.sh` all discover
`go.mod` files by walking the repo, and none of them skipped `.claude/worktrees` — where each agent
worktree is a full checkout of this same repository. The guard tests reported every module and fuzz
target twice as missing from the CI matrices, and `verify-modules.sh` went further: it ran the entire
gate, tidy diff and lint included, once per worktree, so another checkout's in-flight edits were
reported as this checkout's failures. Both fixed. Worth knowing before the next parallel run.

**The Grafana Cloud token file is the credential rotation that matters.** #362 would have been a
TLS-only curiosity if it watched only certificates: nearly every deployment authenticates with
`otlp.grafana_cloud.token_file`, and that is exactly what a secret rotation replaces. It cannot be
passed through as a header value (it is combined with the instance ID into a Basic credential), so it
is watched under an internal sentinel key and transformed on the way out — with a test proving the
sentinel never escapes as a real header.

### Deliberate calls, so they do not read as oversights

- **gRPC CA rotation is not immediate.** A rotated client certificate applies at the next handshake
  on both transports (`GetClientCertificate`), but on gRPC the root CAs are fixed when the connection
  is dialled, so a rotated bundle waits for a reconnect. `otlp.grpc_reconnection_period` bounds that.
  Documented rather than hidden.
- **`otlp.retry.*` and `otlp.stdout.metric_interval` now carry explicit defaults** instead of zeros.
  They are the values the pinned exporters already use, so nothing changed behaviourally — but the
  effective policy is now visible in `config.example.yaml`, in the generated schema, and in the
  status-page echo, which is what #360 means by deterministic.
- **`#376`'s tailnet profile label is deliberately outside the `pii_filter` categories.** Those
  govern the metric/log/span pipeline; profiles are a different destination with a different
  audience, so shipping a customer identifier there is a separately-stated choice. It is off by
  default, emitted only for a single configured tailnet (there is one profiler per process, so a
  per-tailnet value would be a lie), and `hashed` is described as pseudonymous rather than anonymous
  because a small name space is enumerable.
- **`#377`'s status page has the data but no dedicated HTML card.** Every field is live on
  `/api/status.json` and through `buildStatus()`; only a bespoke widget is missing, because
  `statushtml`'s suite enforces accessibility contracts on every card and adding one properly is a
  larger unit of work than this loose end warranted.
- **`#361`'s disabled-signal path uses a no-op exporter, not a no-op `LoggerProvider`.** Functionally
  identical — nothing is serialized or sent — and it keeps the change inside `exporters.go`. The more
  literal reading would save a little memory and nothing else.

### Verified at `8ed3cb0`, not asserted

`go build` · `go vet` · `go test -race ./...` · `golangci-lint run` (0 issues) ·
`scripts/verify-modules.sh` green across all five modules (`.`, `tools/apidrift`,
`tools/configcheck`, `tools/metricscatalog`, `tools/promqlcheck`) · `configcheck` on
`config.example.yaml` and the chart-rendered config · `helm lint` and `helm template` ·
`scripts/regen-generated.sh dashboards` clean · every generated artifact regenerated and in sync.
Chart `0.30.0`.

`0084290` landed as one commit for the same reason `3858408` did: `docs/metrics.md`,
`config.schema.json`, `docs/env-vars.md`, `docs/signal-coverage.md`, `signal_dispositions.json` and
the chart's schema/README are each derived from the whole catalog or the whole `Config` struct, so
splitting per issue would leave intermediate commits failing their own `fail-on-diff` gates.

### Nothing is parked

No open child, no blocked item, and no decision or security-sensitive detail living only in an agent
transcript. Every disposition, correction and deliberate omission above is on this issue or on the
child it belongs to.

All 29 children closed and the Definition of Done checklist is ticked. Final integration SHA `8ed3cb0`, full gate green across all five modules. See the phase receipt above for the findings, the enabling refactors that made the last thirteen parallelisable, and the deliberate calls.

title: Tracker: telemetry export, Prometheus, tracing, and profiling

body:
## Mission

Cover the useful read-only Tailscale control-plane surface, make collector capability and scope requirements explicit, and prove every consumed upstream field has an intentional telemetry or ignore disposition.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P0

- [x] #411 — Correct user-invite telemetry to match the open-invites endpoint
- [x] #429 — Preserve documented node-metric drop and peer-relay labels

### Phase P1

- [x] #414 — Export Tailscale SSH and key-expiry-disabled posture
- [x] #415 — Classify credential privilege by scope semantics
- [x] #416 — Expose top-level trust-credential allowed-tag blast radius
- [x] #420 — Distinguish intentionally unavailable optional APIs from broken authentication
- [x] #421 — Expose per-device subrequest coverage and partial failure
- [x] #422 — Add a consumed-field disposition contract
- [x] #423 — Detect newly added upstream read operations automatically
- [x] #424 — Exercise real path parameters in live contract CI
- [x] #425 — Preflight requested OAuth scopes against enabled collectors
- [x] #428 — Continuously validate the active ACL policy and embedded tests

### Phase P2

- [x] #412 — Expose user-invite age and delivery state
- [x] #413 — Expose device-share invite age and resend state
- [x] #417 — Report webhook event-level subscription coverage
- [x] #418 — Expose whether an external ACL policy link is configured
- [x] #419 — Improve OAuth Apps lifecycle and posture telemetry
- [x] #430 — Add explicit configuration-to-capability status

### Phase P3

- [x] #426 — Add bounded entity lifecycle/age signals
- [x] #427 — Add Linux distribution and codename inventory

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Use current official Tailscale documentation and `go doc` for every client shape; do not infer fields from stale editor diagnostics.
- Add capability/scope preflight before expanding dashboards or alerts that assume optional collectors work.
- Keep per-device subrequests bounded and expose partial coverage rather than hiding it.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every child issue is closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed stale/unsupported decision.
- [x] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [x] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules, and deployment examples agree with the final contracts.
- [x] Full repository and affected tool-module gates are green at the final integration SHA.
- [x] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail, or follow-up exists only in an agent transcript.

## Audit epic identity

`EPIC-03`

comments.body:
## Execution start — seams frozen, lanes dispatched

Commit `da772f5` lands the shared contract every child issue codes against. Recorded here because the
lanes were built in parallel and the reasoning is not recoverable from the diff alone.

### Decisions taken (Rob, 2026-07-25)

| Issue | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| #411 | Lands as `fix`, **no major bump**. The fabricated labels go, with an operator upgrade note. Not worth a v3→v4 module-path move for a correctness fix to invented data. |
| #428 | ACL validation is **on by default** when the acl collector is on. Added `collectors.acl.validate` (default `true`) as the off switch for anyone who wants a strictly GET-only client. |
| #425 | Scope preflight **warns and emits, never blocks**. No strict mode. A modelling bug in our own scope map must not be able to stop collection; the runtime 403 classification from #420 stays authoritative. |
| #426 / #427 | Implement both fully. |

### Premise verification against current code

Every child issue's premise was re-confirmed before any code was written. Three came back different
from the issue text:

- **#411 is right on two independent grounds, and worse than written.** `spec/tailscale-api.json`
  `components.schemas.UserInvite` has **no `accepted` and no `created` property at all**.
  `internal/tsapi/userinvites.go` decodes both, so `Accepted` is the Go zero value on every real
  invite — the `accepted=false` label was never sourced from the API. On top of that,
  `listUserInvites` is documented "List all open (not yet accepted) user invites", so an
  `accepted=true` series is unreachable. The real field `lastEmailSentAt` is dropped entirely, which
  is what #412 now picks up.
- **#418's premise needs reshaping.** `aclsExternalLink` is `type: string, format: uri`, not a
  boolean. It is emitted as a *derived presence* boolean; the URI itself is never emitted, since it
  can leak an internal repo path.
- **#416 has a bigger finding than stated.** The `Key` schema carries a **top-level `tags`** property
  — the trust credential's own tag restriction — which `wireKey` does not decode at all. It only
  decodes the nested `capabilities.devices.create.tags` (auto-applied device tags). Those are
  different things, and the top-level one is the actual blast radius.

Confirmed as written: #414 (`sshEnabled` is decoded, nothing emits it), #415 (`ts2o-key-broad-scope`
fires on `max(tailscale_key_scopes_ratio) > 10`, so a single `all` scores 1 and never fires while
eleven `*:read` scopes score 11 and do), #421 (`tallyDeviceInvites` and `emitPosture` both bare-`return`
on error — no log, no metric, invisible), #429 (only 2 of the 7 documented drop reasons are admitted;
all three peer-relay series use `noAttrs` and never read their labels).

#428 is safe: `validateAndTestPolicyFile` needs only `policy_file:read`, modifies nothing, and the
live lane's existing `all:read` token can already call it. The client is also **not** GET-only by
construction — `putJSON`/`ConfigureLogStream` is an existing PUT — so the only real guard to widen is
`manifest_test.go`'s `op.Method != "GET"` assertion, narrowly and by name.

### Stale repo facts corrected along the way

1. The OpenAPI spec is `spec/tailscale-api.json`, **not** `tailscale-api.yaml`/`.json` at repo root as
   the root `CLAUDE.md` says. Root has no such file.
2. The live-contract lane does **not** use a self-hosted `tailscale-api` runner. That runner was never
   provisioned and queued forever; `.github/workflows/live-contract.yml` now mints an OAuth
   client-credentials token on a standard hosted runner.
3. `deploy/grafana/tailscale2otel.json` and `deploy/alerts/tailscale2otel.grafana-rules.yaml` are
   generated but have **no CI fail-on-diff gate**, unlike the four artifacts the root `CLAUDE.md`
   tabulates. Forgetting to regenerate them is silent. Closing that gap is #438's job, not this
   tracker's, but nothing here should assume CI catches it.

Docs will be corrected as part of this epic.

### Frozen seams (commit `da772f5`)

Three new leaf packages, landed first so the parallel lanes could not drift:

- **`internal/apistate`** — bounded per-operation availability. Before this, six call sites hand-rolled
  their own predicate over `StatusError.Code` and disagreed: flowlogs read 403 as "premium off";
  oauthapps read 403 **or** 404 as "feature off"; logstream read **any** 4xx including a genuine 401 as
  "not configured"; devices' per-device subrequests dropped everything silently; postureintegrations
  and webhooks propagated everything as a hard failure. A tailnet merely lacking a premium feature was
  indistinguishable from one with a revoked credential. **An ambiguous 403 now defaults to
  `scope_denied`, not `disabled`** — only an operation that explicitly declares `DisabledOn{403}`,
  because upstream documents 403 as its feature gate, reads it as disabled. Defaulting the other way is
  precisely how a real permission regression becomes a healthy-looking zero.
- **`internal/tsscope`** — scope classification by privilege, not count. The rule is mechanical (last
  colon segment `read` ⇒ read-only) rather than a lookup table, because neither the vendored spec nor
  the published docs enumerate scopes as a closed set, and the docs state `all`/`all:read` cover APIs
  that do not exist yet. A hardcoded table would misclassify every scope Tailscale adds after today.
- **`internal/entityage`** — one shared age-bucket set so #426's distributions stay comparable across
  entity families.

**Emission is zero-seeded, not `GaugeSnapshot`.** This was a bug caught in plan review: a snapshot
replaces the entire series set for a metric *name*, and availability is emitted from many collectors,
so snapshots would have had each collector wipe the others' series every tick. Zero-seeding also stops
a plain cumulative gauge pinning a stale state at `1` forever.

Also in `da772f5`: the drop-reason admit-set widened to the seven reasons tailscaled documents (the
five that were being folded into `other` are long-standing upstream values, not unknown ones), the
peer-relay transport/state attribute keys, every new attribute key pre-registered in the PII registry
so no lane had to touch that shared file, and the two new config keys with their generated artifacts.

### Sequencing constraint on #422 / #423

Both are snapshots of *what the code decodes*, and several lanes are adding newly-decoded fields
(`lastEmailSentAt`, top-level `Key.tags`, `aclsExternalLink`, `redirectURIs`, `distro.name`/`codeName`).
So Lane G builds the mechanism and the drift check, and the **committed baselines are regenerated in
the wiring pass** once every other lane has landed. A baseline committed mid-wave would be stale on
arrival and would turn every other lane red.

### #425 uses requested scopes, not granted

Nothing in this repo captures the OAuth token's granted scope — the token is buried inside an
`oauth2.Transport` and `Token.Extra("scope")` is never read. The issue asks to preflight *requested*
scopes, and `tailscale.auth.oauth.scopes` already exists in config, so the preflight compares that
against each enabled collector's required scope. No token introspection and no new API call. Runtime
403 classification remains authoritative, which is exactly why warn-only is safe here.

## Phase receipt — 17 of 21 children closed at `7445cc6`

Seams `da772f5`, implementation `7445cc6`. Remaining: #422, #423, #424 (drift CI) land separately —
their baselines are snapshots of what the code decodes, so they had to be regenerated only after every
decode change was in.

### Closed

P0 #411 #429 · P1 #414 #415 #416 #420 #421 #425 #428 · P2 #412 #413 #417 #418 #419 #430 · P3 #426 #427

### What the premise checks changed

Three issues were not quite what their text said, and two of those changed the design:

- **#411 was wrong in a second way nobody had spotted.** Beyond the endpoint returning only open
  invites, the `UserInvite` schema has **no `accepted` and no `created` property at all**. The client
  decoded both, so `Accepted` was a Go zero value — the `accepted=false` label every deployment has
  been emitting was never sourced from the API. Both fields are gone, and a regression test now scans
  every emitted point for the fabricated key rather than trusting the grouping code. The real
  `lastEmailSentAt` field, previously dropped on the floor, is what #412's delivery state runs on.
- **#418 could not be built as written.** `aclsExternalLink` is `type: string, format: uri`, not a
  boolean. It is emitted as a derived presence flag and the URI is never emitted — it can carry an
  internal repo path. The field is decoded as a pointer so *absent*, *empty* and *set* stay three
  distinct states; absence emits nothing rather than a confident `false`.
- **#416 was bigger than described.** The `Key` schema carries a **top-level `tags`** — the trust
  credential's own tag restriction, i.e. which tags auth keys it mints may carry — that was not
  decoded at all. Only the nested `capabilities.devices.create.tags` (auto-applied device tags) was.
  Those are different things and the undecoded one is the actual blast radius. It is now decoded as
  `AllowedTags`, named so the two cannot be confused again.

### Corrections worth keeping

- **#415's alert was inverted, not merely coarse.** `max(tailscale_key_scopes_ratio) > 10` meant a
  single `all` scope — unrestricted read+write over the whole tailnet including APIs that do not exist
  yet — scored 1 and never fired, while eleven narrow `*:read` scopes scored 11 and did. The rule now
  keys off the privilege class. Scope classification is deliberately mechanical (last colon segment
  `read` ⇒ read-only) rather than a lookup table: nothing upstream enumerates scopes as a closed set,
  and the docs say `all`/`all:read` cover future APIs, so a table would misclassify every scope
  Tailscale adds after today.
- **#420's alert paged on expected conditions.** `ts2o-api-auth-failing` fired critical on any 401 *or*
  403 and declared "all polling fails" — but a legitimate 403 is how upstream reports an optional
  feature the tailnet does not have. It is now split: `ts2o-api-credential-rejected` (401, critical,
  tailnet-wide) and `ts2o-api-scope-denied` (403, warning, narrower). A feature the tailnet lacks
  reports as `disabled` and is not alertable at all.
- **#421 was invisible by construction.** Both per-device subrequests did a bare
  `if err != nil { return }` — no log, no metric, no effect on tick success. A missing
  `device_invites:read` scope 403'd every call while the collector reported a clean scrape and the
  absent invites read as "no invites exist".
- **#429** was discarding five of the seven documented drop reasons into `other`, and all three
  peer-relay series used an attribute deriver that never read its labels. Packets were visibly
  dropping with no way to distinguish a policy block from a malformed frame.

### Design notes that will not survive in the diff

**Availability is zero-seeded, not a `GaugeSnapshot`.** A snapshot replaces the entire series set for a
metric *name*, and this metric is emitted by many collectors — snapshots would have had each collector
wipe the others' series every tick. Zero-seeding also stops a cumulative gauge pinning a stale state at
`1` forever. Do not "simplify" this to a snapshot.

**An ambiguous 403 defaults to `scope_denied`, never `disabled`.** Only an operation that explicitly
declares `DisabledOn{403}`, because upstream documents 403 as its feature gate, reads it as disabled.
Defaulting the other way is exactly how a real permission regression becomes a healthy-looking zero.

**#428's POST is a read.** `validateAndTestPolicyFile` needs only `policy_file:read` and modifies
nothing; sending no body validates the *current* policy. Validation gauges emit only on a supported
state, so a permission denial surfaces as `scope_denied` and never as a passing validation. The
validator is an optional collector dependency rather than a `ControlPlane` method — that interface is
shared with the Headscale adapter, which has no such endpoint. On by default per the decision above,
with `collectors.acl.validate` as the off switch.

**#425 preflights REQUESTED scopes.** Nothing in this codebase captures the token's *granted* scope —
it is buried in an `oauth2.Transport` and `Token.Extra("scope")` is never read. So the preflight
compares configured scopes against each collector's documented requirement, warns, and never blocks.
Two capabilities (`services`, `user_invites`) are recorded as **undocumented on purpose**: neither
appears in upstream's scopes table, and inventing a plausible name would produce confident false
warnings on correctly-scoped deployments.

**A seam bug caught mid-build:** `apistate.Coverage.Reset()` cleared *every* collector's tallies, not
just the caller's. One `Coverage` is shared per runtime so the status page can read one object, so a
global reset would let collectors wipe each other mid-tick and emit each other's series. Fixed with
`ResetCollector`. Latent today — devices is the only N+1 collector — but it surfaces the moment a
second one grows a subrequest.

**Headscale absence handling.** `hsapi` hard-codes `sshEnabled` and `keyExpiryDisabled` false, so
without explicit suppression a Headscale build would have published a confident "SSH enabled nowhere".
Both are suppressed there, following the #64 precedent. The distro rollup needs no such flag — it
self-gates on wire presence.

### Stale repo facts corrected

1. The vendored OpenAPI spec is **`spec/tailscale-api.json`**, not a repo-root `.yaml`. Root has no
   such file. `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` fixed.
2. The live-contract lane runs on a **standard hosted runner**; the self-hosted `tailscale-api` runner
   the docs described was never provisioned (#160). Fixed, with the reason recorded so nobody
   "restores" it.
3. `deploy/grafana/tailscale2otel.json` and `deploy/alerts/tailscale2otel.grafana-rules.yaml` are
   generated but have **no CI fail-on-diff gate**, unlike the four artifacts the root `CLAUDE.md`
   tabulates. Forgetting to regenerate them is silent. That gap belongs to #438, not here.

## Final phase receipt — EPIC-03 complete at `fb4f877`

The final stack is pushed to `main` and all child issues listed in this tracker are closed.

### Commit stack

| Commit | Scope / issue linkage |
|---|---|
| `da772f5` | Frozen the shared availability-state, scope-class, and entity-age seams used by the parallel implementation. |
| `7445cc6` | Implemented and closes #411, #412, #413, #414, #415, #416, #417, #418, #419, #420, #421, #425, #426, #427, #428, #429, and #430. |
| `2b48098` | Corrected the alert rules to key off scope/auth semantics rather than raw counts; follow-up for #415/#420. |
| `fb4f877` | Completes the field-disposition baseline, closes the scheduled-operation-discovery gap, retains real live-contract path arguments, and closes #422, #423, and #424. |

### Final acceptance verification

- **#422:** all 214 rows are classified with no empty dispositions and no exclusion missing its required note. Totals: 174 `emitted`, 11 `enrichment`, 12 `excluded`, 17 `unhandled`. The detailed evidence-backed gap inventory is in [the #422 completion comment](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/issues/422#issuecomment-5083030999).
- **#423:** the existing baseline/unit contract passed, but independent verification found that scheduled CI only classified schema drift for already-consumed operations. A newly published unconsumed read operation would therefore remain invisible until the vendored spec changed. `fb4f877` adds a black-box regression test, a live-spec `-operations` classifier, a separate deduplicated `api-operation-drift` reporting lane, and the required repository label. The current official live specification reports no operation-set drift.
- **#424:** focused verification covers all three consumed parameterized operations (`listDeviceInvites`, `getDevicePostureAttributes`, `listServiceHosts`), proves deterministic IDs come from real list responses, proves the resolved values reach the request URL, and reports unavailable resources as explicit not-applicable results rather than skipped tests. No implementation gap was found.

### Gates

Local root-module gates at `fb4f877`:

- `go build ./...` — pass
- `go vet ./...` — pass
- `go test -race ./...` — pass
- `golangci-lint run` — pass, 0 issues
- `govulncheck ./...` — no vulnerabilities found
- generated metrics-catalogue sync, `actionlint`, and `git diff --check` — pass

Separate modules `tools/configcheck`, `tools/metricscatalog`, and `tools/apidrift` each passed `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run`. The first two have no test files; their build, vet, and lint gates still ran. `tools/apidrift` includes and passes the new operation-discovery CLI regression.

Post-push workflows are terminal green: [CI](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/actions/runs/30197740668), [Release](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/actions/runs/30197740917), CodeQL, actionlint, zizmor, Helm, Scorecard, Docker Security, and documentation sync all succeeded.

### Repository and tracker state

- All **20 distinct child issues actually enumerated in this tracker's Phase worklist** are closed.
- The handoff and the earlier phase receipt say 21 children, but the live tracker contains 20 issue checklist entries (`#411` through `#430` selectively, with no omitted fourth open child). The apparent fourth remaining item was epic completion itself; no missing child issue was invented.
- Every Phase and Definition of Done checkbox is checked.
- Local `main` and `origin/main` both resolve to `fb4f877a5c6b0a48f6cfc67eecf09342804e96fd`.
- The working tree is clean.

### Intermediate-red caveat

`7445cc6` alone fails `TestFieldDispositionsInSync` because the disposition baseline was intentionally left to the final single-writer integration lane while eight completed implementation lanes were preserved. History was not rewritten to conceal that. `fb4f877` completes #422 and restores a green branch tip, and the entire four-commit stack passed the full gate before its first push.

title: Tracker: Tailscale API and collector fidelity

body:
## Mission

Turn object-store and durable ingestion into a provider-neutral, restart-safe path whose key contract, ordering, retry, cursor, backfill, and acknowledgement claims match supported Tailscale exports.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P0

- [x] #283 — fix(config): reject object-store ingestion in multi-tailnet mode to prevent cross-tailnet attribution
- [x] #285 — fix(objectstore): resume listings beyond already-seen keys
- [x] #286 — fix(objectstore): persist failed-object gaps and correct the exactly-once contract
- [x] #447 — fix(objectstore): validate and support the official Tailscale object-key contract

### Phase P1

- [x] #279 — feat(receivers): optional ingress WAL for crash-safe acknowledgement
- [x] #284 — feat(objectstore): support per-tailnet storage destinations and credentials
- [x] #287 — declined: Grafana Cloud's 14-day retention makes a longer historical backfill unsupported (closed not planned)
- [x] #288 — feat(auditlogs): ingest configuration-log S3 and S3-compatible exports
- [x] #289 — security(s3): require explicit opt-in for plaintext remote endpoints
- [x] #292 — harden(objectstore): bound decompressed bytes and records per object
- [x] #448 — fix(objectstore): make object processing atomic across parser failures
- [x] #449 — fix(config): protect object-store static credentials with Secret and _file semantics
- [x] #450 — fix(selfobs): correct object-store ingest source and byte semantics
- [x] #496 — fix(objectstore): accept .json.zstd and .json.gzip export keys (found via #288 evidence work)
- [x] #497 — fix(objectstore): quarantine an object whose every row fails to decode (found via #288 evidence work)
- [x] #498 — fix(objectstore): a leading-slash prefix erases durable listing progress every cycle (found via #293)
- [x] #453 — refactor(objectstore): create a provider-neutral, multi-signal ingestion engine
- [x] #463 — docs: reconcile ingestion-source, backfill, and acknowledgement claims with runtime behavior

### Phase P2

- [x] #290 — fix(s3): preserve configured endpoint base paths
- [x] #291 — fix(s3): detect or stream oversized ListObjects responses
- [x] #293 — fix(objectstore): support flat copied-export layouts as the parser claims
- [x] #451 — feat(objectstore): expose provider request and cursor-health telemetry
- [x] #452 — feat(s3): support AWS container credential providers
- [x] #454 — feat(objectstore): add a native Google Cloud Storage backend
- [x] #455 — feat(objectstore): add an Azure Blob Storage backend

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Correct the official key/parser contract and loss semantics before adding providers.
- Freeze the provider-neutral listing/object/checkpoint interfaces before parallel S3, GCS, and Azure work.
- Do not claim exactly-once delivery; document the actual durable boundary and upstream guarantees.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every child issue is closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed stale/unsupported decision.
- [x] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [x] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules, and deployment examples agree with the final contracts.
- [x] Full repository and affected tool-module gates are green at the final integration SHA.
- [x] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail, or follow-up exists only in an agent transcript.

## Audit epic identity

`EPIC-02`

comments.body:
## Phase P0 complete

Closed children and completing commits:

- #283 — `c6f66b015013b9ad11e80b85d27dc0f2b22ef135`: rejects global object-store attribution across multiple tailnet runtimes.
- #447 — `9b9f7a3c24ba86fab75a182646ae9195f717f4e7`: accepts Tailscale's official `YYYY/MM/DD/HH:MM:SS.json[.zst|.gz]` keys and retains the supported legacy parser.
- #285 — `8c951e2c4c8d57ad22f83de9fb11db3f7f58c532`: explicit listing truncation plus restart-safe per-prefix scan positions, bounded backlog progression, and late-key wrap.
- #286 — `bf7e92def8c5729ac749a7f2f5169635928c34a2`: independent durable gaps, bounded indefinite retry, deterministic quarantine/manual acknowledgement, key-safe health telemetry, and the corrected at-least-once contract.

Evidence and deviations:

- #447 used the authoritative Tailscale object-key contract and a sanitized live network-flow payload shape. The lab tailnet was live-verified as Splunk-only for both network and configuration streaming; no external sink mutation was made just to manufacture an object key. That evidence and re-scope are recorded on the child.
- #285's adversarial pass found and covered the first-key failure case: scan state has an explicit prefix-start marker, so there is no missing predecessor key at which progress can be parked.
- #286 persists gap, seen, timestamp cursor, and scan changes through the same checkpoint batch. Metrics/logs have bounded fields and no raw object identity. Scanner partial-emission replay remains explicit follow-up #448 rather than a false exactly-once claim.
- No P0 blocker remains. No product/security decision was invented or left only in the session.

Integrated verification at `bf7e92def8c5729ac749a7f2f5169635928c34a2`:

- root build, vet, race, and golangci-lint
- build/vet/race/lint for all three tool modules
- all generated artifacts byte-stable
- Helm lint/template, 104 render-contract checks, example/rendered configcheck
- govulncheck, GoReleaser snapshot, Docker build, secret-hygiene, actionlint, and zizmor
- all eight exact-SHA workflows terminal success: CI, Release, CodeQL, Docker Security, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, and docs sync

Each earlier P0 SHA also reached terminal success on every workflow triggered for that commit; exact run links are recorded on the child receipts.

Next: reconcile P1 live state and freeze the provider-neutral/multi-signal seams before selecting parallel lanes. #453 remains the dependency boundary for provider fan-out; P0 behavior is now the regression contract that refactor must preserve.

## Clean pause checkpoint — P1 in progress

This is an intentional handoff boundary after the provider-neutral seam, not a phase-completion receipt. `main` and `origin/main` are identical at `d701ebe45ffabe34b5ccf1d3923372ff38270759`; the worktree is clean. No subagent remains active. The only open PR is release-please #255.

Completed since the P0 receipt:

- #289 — `1528787b27e517f800c3ec0c7b3c9cc2c2b39f8c`: remote object-store HTTP is rejected by default; loopback remains usable; explicit insecure opt-in warns.
- #449 — `32609631dd2d29bdce9a71a77097b0716e56fbab`: object-store credentials use `config.Secret`, support centralized `_file` resolution, and reveal only at provider construction.
- #453 — `d701ebe45ffabe34b5ccf1d3923372ff38270759`: provider-neutral object identity/list/get seam, signal processor seam, scoped tailnet/provider/signal/feed checkpoints, atomic migration of legacy cursor/seen/scan/gap state, and preserved S3 flow behavior.

Each child has a detailed closing receipt with local verification and exact-SHA workflow links. Every workflow triggered for all three SHAs reached terminal success. #453 also passed the complete local CI-equivalent gate (root and tool-module build/vet/race/lint, generated drift, Helm + 104 render contracts, configcheck, govulncheck, GoReleaser, Docker, secret hygiene, actionlint, zizmor).

Frozen seam now on `main`:

- `internal/objectstore.Backend`: bounded lexicographic `List`, opaque-identity `Get`, and `Object{Identity, Key, Size, LastModified}`.
- `internal/collector/objectstore.SignalProcessor`: signal name plus per-row decode/validate/process handoff; decode/validation sentinels remain row-local, other errors create object gaps.
- checkpoint namespace: `objectstore/v1/<base64url-tailnet>/<provider>/<signal>/<feed-digest>`, with inner `cursor`, `seen/`, `scan/`, and `gap/` state. The configured single-tailnet identity is stable even when `-` resolves to a display label.
- S3 remains behavior-compatible (`Identity == Key`) and flow records still enter the shared `flowlog.Processor`; no OTLP/provider details leaked into collectors.
- old bare and `<tailnet>/objectstore.flowlogs.*` state migrates atomically and idempotently; canonical state wins, malformed state stops rather than silently replaying.

Current open P1 work, live-reconciled at this checkpoint:

- #279 ingress WAL
- #284 per-tailnet storage destinations/credentials
- #287 historical backfill beyond fourteen days
- #288 configuration-log S3 ingestion
- #292 decompressed-byte/record bounds
- #448 atomic object processing across parser failures
- #450 object-store self-observability semantics
- #463 final ingestion/backfill/acknowledgement documentation reconciliation

All P2 children remain open: #290, #291, #293, #451, #452, #454, #455. No blocker or pending human decision is known. #454/#455 were deliberately not pulled into #453.

Recommended resume: re-read this tracker and all comments, then read every still-open P1 child and its comments in full and re-reconcile main/PR/issue state. Preserve the new #453 seam. Dependency-sort the phase before dispatch: #292 and #448 are correctness boundaries for large/backfill feeds; #288 consumes the signal seam; #284 precedes per-tailnet provider fan-out; #463 belongs at the end. #279 is an independent receiver durability lane and can proceed with disjoint ownership once its own seam is frozen. Do not start P2 or the next epic until every P1/P2 child is closed or evidence-backed unsupported and the phase receipts are posted.

P1 progress: #292 closed by `f969025543446239b0a59af80ce36ca8d394c5a0`. The exact staged tree passed the full local root/tool/generated/Helm/security/release/Docker gate; all nine exact-SHA workflows are terminal successful. The child receipt is https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/issues/292#issuecomment-5085103143. Next in the binding order is #448 atomic object preparation/commit; the independent seam review is complete and recorded locally for implementation.

### #448 completion receipt

- Closed by `f3e871e0a27c36e3b4fbf3febd5cb31aca431c64`.
- Whole-object preparation is now side-effect free; record effects commit only after every row prepares successfully.

Next active child remains #279. No later child has started.

## Clean pause checkpoint — P1 correctness and receiver durability complete

This is an intentional clean pause before #284. No later child has started.

Completed since the prior pause:

- #292 — `f969025543446239b0a59af80ce36ca8d394c5a0`: configurable decompressed-byte, record, per-cycle byte, and per-cycle object bounds with clear breach diagnostics.
- #448 — `f3e871e0a27c36e3b4fbf3febd5cb31aca431c64`: whole-object preparation and commit atomicity across parser/preparation failures.
