- All nine workflows succeeded: CI `30219480322`, Helm `30219480346`, Release `30219480603`, CodeQL `30219480502`, Docker Security `30219480478`, Scorecard `30219480500`, actionlint `30219480505`, zizmor `30219480493`, docs sync `30219480326`.
- Child receipt: https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/issues/279#issuecomment-5085323569

Current continuation state:

- Next binding child is #284. Its public YAML, no-inheritance, duplicate-feed, fail-fast policy is maintainer-approved but implementation has not started.
- #288 remains evidence-blocked on a sanitized real Tailscale configuration-log S3 object. Owner/unblock condition: an existing destination holder or Rob-authorized capture must provide a sanitized object that proves framing and field shapes; do not invent a decoder from synthetic guesses.
- Later P1 children #450 and #463 remain unstarted; P2 remains unstarted.
- Release-please PR #255 remains the only open PR and was not merged. No release was published.

Pause invariant: `main == origin/main == 04384a20e6ae47f2ab08425907f729f4e026979b`, all applicable exact-SHA workflows are green, and the worktree is clean. Resume by reconciling live state and reading #284 plus all comments in full; do not begin #484 until every actionable #478 child is closed or evidence-backed unsupported.

## P1 resume reconciliation — baseline correction and wave dispatch

Live state at resume differs from the last pause receipt; recording the correction before continuing.

**Reconciled facts**

- `main == origin/main == 6b1093a89fd60f959d35989abc80a9e2b66722f6`, worktree clean, non-fork, owner `rknightion`.
- All nine workflows for that exact SHA are terminal success: CI, Helm, Release, CodeQL, Docker Security, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, docs sync.
- Only open PR remains release-please #255. Not merged; no release published.
- The prior pause receipt named `04384a2` as the pause invariant. `main` is one commit further along at `6b1093a`.

**Out-of-band commit since the pause**

`6b1093a` closed #494 — cumulative OTLP metric payloads exceeding Mimir's 20,000,000-byte uncompressed request limit, which had stopped all metric delivery from a live deployment. That is a production incident fix, not tracker scope, and it is the concrete incident slice of #480's #360. It is recorded here because it lands between two #478 receipts and would otherwise look unaccounted for. #360 keeps ownership of the remaining compression/timeout/retry/serialized-guard surface.

**Tracker body vs live children: agreed, no correction needed**

P1 `[x]` marks for #279, #287, #292 and #448 match live state. #287 remains closed `not planned` (Grafana Cloud's fourteen-day retention makes longer backfill unsupported).

**Actionable remainder**

- P1: #284, #288 (evidence-gated), #450, #463.
- P2: #290, #291, #293, #451, #452. #454/#455 stay closed under the binding S3-only decision and are not being reopened.

**Guardrails re-read in full before dispatch:** #477 (closed, contracts intact), #173 (rejected directions), this tracker and every comment, and every remaining child body and comment.

**Wave 1 — dispatched now, one owner per file**

| Child | Owned surface |
| --- | --- |
| #284 | `internal/config/{config,validate,defaults}.go` + tests, `internal/app/{objectstore,collectors}.go` + tests, `config.example.yaml`, `docs/configuration.md`, chart `values.yaml` + config template |
| #290 | `internal/s3/{s3,sign}.go` + their tests |
| #452 | `internal/s3/credentials.go` + test, new `containercreds*.go` |
| #450 | `internal/appcatalog/catalog.go`, `internal/app/ingest.go`, `internal/collector/objectstore/objectstore.go` + tests |
| #288 | read-only evidence hunt, no file ownership |

Generated artifacts (`docs/metrics.md`, `docs/env-vars.md`, chart README, `values.schema.json`), dashboards, rules and every commit stay serial with the primary.

**Seams frozen before dispatch**

- #284 implements the maintainer-approved contract in https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/issues/284#issuecomment-5084586339 verbatim, with one deliberate narrowing: only `tailnets[].objectstore.flow` ships. An `audit` sibling key is not exposed while #288 is evidence-blocked, because a documented key that ingests nothing is worse than an absent one. The type is shaped so `audit` is a purely additive later change. The #453 checkpoint namespace and the configured-name-is-checkpoint-identity rule are unchanged.
- #450 resolves its documented either/or explicitly: `tailscale2otel.ingest.size` becomes **uniformly decompressed/decoded payload bytes** for every source that emits it, so cross-source ingestion volume is comparable. Object-store currently passes compressed wire bytes into the same metric that `stream`/`webhook` populate with decompressed bytes. `tailscale2otel.objectstore.bytes` (compressed, including failed attempts) and `objectstore.decompressed.bytes` are unchanged and keep the transport/expansion view. Both descriptor vocabularies gain `objectstore`, guarded by a new catalog/emit-site parity test.

**Deferred to wave 2 purely on file contention, not dependency:** #291 (shares `internal/s3/credentials.go` with #452 and `s3.go` with #290), #293 and #451 (share `internal/collector/objectstore/objectstore.go` with #450, and #293 also needs config after #284). #463 stays last by design — it documents whatever #284/#288/#290/#293 actually conclude.

**Awaiting decision:** #288 only. The prior owner/unblock condition stands (one sanitized real S3 configuration-log object proving object framing). An independent adversarial evidence hunt is running to confirm or overturn that block before it is accepted a second time; its verdict and a concrete yes/no recommendation will be posted on #288.

## Clean pause checkpoint — P1 and P2 implementation complete, three children open

Intentional handoff boundary, not a phase-completion receipt. No subagent is active, the worktree is clean, and no scratch worktree or stash remains.

**Pause invariant:** `main == origin/main == 6709c54d65968eb22dadec220cdde7e39ef3f97a`. Every workflow applicable to every SHA landed this session reached terminal success. Release-please PR #255 remains the only open PR; it is mergeable with all checks passing and was **not** merged, and no release was published.

### Landed this session, one commit per child

| Child | Commit | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #290 | `1e716e11fa2d0aa23e22f4845b7073619cc99cda` | single request-path composition; signed path cannot diverge from sent path |
| #450 | `cc6e4985af4fd4665cfeff8fcd51ac68fe54618d` | `ingest.size` uniformly decoded bytes; catalog/emit-site parity guard |
| #284 | `ddef9181e92240a2e2fa783c9e89f1cb79dcd4e2` | per-tailnet destinations, no inheritance, duplicate-feed rejection |
| #452 | `26bb03ceaaf321e837b5753a0de6fd8e854200be` | ECS/EKS container credentials with a hardened SSRF boundary |
| #496 | `3df1b32634a32d6116679db63f191f4c5ec6bd3f` | `.json.zstd` / `.json.gzip` keys were silently never fetched |
| #497 | `4f670abb636afeed079195b9a2634b0477476269` | an all-rows-fail object no longer completes silently |
| #291 | `7ebdb9c4f4408d096f05468c60e3b11f213af515` | streaming list decode; truncation refused explicitly |
| #293 | `0794f61a1658776888120d36a806200117aa5792` | opt-in flat layout; chart 0.14.6 |
| #451 | `6709c54d65968eb22dadec220cdde7e39ef3f97a` | provider request and cursor-health telemetry |

Each child has a detailed closing receipt with RED evidence, local gate output and exact-SHA workflow run IDs. Every commit was verified in a throwaway worktree containing **only** that child's diff, because concurrent lanes kept the main tree dirty — so the gate that ran is the tree that was pushed, not a union of half-finished work.

### Three children remain open, with precise state

- **#288** — evidence-blocked, and the block was independently re-audited rather than accepted twice. Verdict: the S3 object *framing* for configuration logs is genuinely undocumented everywhere (docs, vendored spec, changelog, blog posts, upstream issues, four code searches), and our own flow-log framing has never been validated against a real Tailscale object either. The maintainer **authorised** a short lab capture, but it cannot be executed as things stand: there are no object-store credentials in `.secrets/`, and Tailscale's publisher runs in Tailscale's infrastructure so the destination must be reachable from the public internet — a local MinIO cannot receive the upload. **Unblock condition:** a publicly reachable S3-compatible bucket plus write credentials, and confirmation the lab's configuration-log destination may be repointed for a few minutes. Owner: maintainer. Full evidence table and the shippable-subset plan are on the issue.
- **#498** — filed this session from a defect found while implementing #293, verified independently. A configured prefix with a *leading* slash makes the loader disown the prefix enumeration builds, so every scan row is deleted each cycle, which defeats #285's backlog progression rather than merely wasting requests. **The fix recommendation in the issue body is superseded by a correction comment**: normalising the prefix would change the `FeedID` digest and orphan the cursor and seen set, re-emitting up to `initial_lookback` of data. Correct the predicate instead. Not started.
- **#463** — the terminal documentation reconciliation, deliberately last because it documents what the other children concluded. Not started. Its factual base has been verified against the committed tree and is recorded below so it needs no rediscovery.

### #463 groundwork already verified (do not re-derive)

- **Source matrix, from `validate.go`:** `flowlogs` accepts `poll`, `stream`, `both`, `objectstore`; `auditlogs` accepts `poll`, `stream`, `both` only. `README.md` says auditlogs "takes the first three of those", which simultaneously implies `objectstore` (rejected) and omits `both` (accepted). `docs/streaming-webhooks.md` already states this correctly, so the two documents currently contradict each other.
- **Two durability claims went stale under this session's work.** `README.md` still says "a scanner error after partial emission can replay already-emitted rows" and `docs/streaming-webhooks.md` still says retry "may duplicate those rows after restart **until object processing is atomic**" — #448 made it atomic. The record-level-failure description in both also predates #497's all-rows-fail case and the new `undecodable_object` reason.
- **The backfill ceiling has three distinct causes** and the README's "the only practical way to backfill a long history" is wrong on all of them: partitioned enumeration is capped at `maxDayPrefixes = 14` day partitions per cycle, walking backwards from newest so older days are never reached; flat mode (#293) has one prefix and no such cap, so its ceiling is `initial_lookback` (default 6h); and above both sits #287's real ceiling, Grafana Cloud's 14-day retention.
- **A false premise in the code itself:** the comment beside the source validation says "audit logs are not exported to object storage". They are — S3 configuration-log streaming went GA in January 2025. The value is rejected because the object framing is unproven (#288), which is a different reason and should say so.

### Corrections recorded this session — do not re-litigate

- **My own frozen #293 design was wrong** and would have double-emitted. Specifying "the same stale filter" for flat mode meant the `progress.active` exemption, bounded to one day for a partition, spanned the whole export for a single flat prefix; combined with seen-set pruning at `cursor - 2*Lookback` this re-fetched and re-emitted old objects on every wrap and silently defeated `initial_lookback`. The lower bound is absolute in flat mode; partitioned is byte-identical. Failed objects are retried from durable gap rows, so nothing depended on that exemption.
- **My own #497 brief was wrong** in claiming bounded retry escalates to quarantine. It does not: `Quarantined` is set only from error classification, and `Attempts` feeds backoff delay alone. Retry-forever is deliberate and correct here, because a framing mismatch is fixed by a code change and pending gaps recover automatically once it ships, whereas quarantine is terminal and would need manual row deletion per object.
- **#451 dropped two of its own acceptance bullets with evidence:** scan truncation was already delivered by #285, and there is no transport retry layer in `internal/s3` at all, so a provider retry counter would be permanently zero.
- **#454 / #455 stay closed** under the binding S3-only decision and were not reopened.

### Process trap worth knowing

`ci.yml` and CodeQL use `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` keyed on the ref, so **each push to `main` cancels the previous SHA's still-running run.** Landing #496, #497 and #291 in quick succession left #496's CI and #497's CodeQL at conclusion `cancelled`, which does not satisfy the exact-SHA requirement even though each commit was green locally. Both were repaired by `gh run rerun` against the same SHAs and are now green, but re-runs share that concurrency group so they must be serialised one SHA at a time. Subsequent children waited for terminal CI before the next push. Note also that path-filtered workflows legitimately do not trigger for some commits (Helm and documentation sync do not run for a commit touching only `internal/s3/**`) — that is not a cancellation and needs no repair.

### Resume instructions

Reconcile live state, then read this tracker and every comment in full, plus #288, #463 and #498 and their comments. Do **not** start #484 until these three are closed or evidence-backed blocked. Suggested order: #498 (small, self-contained, correct the predicate per the correction comment), then #463 as the terminal documentation commit using the verified groundwork above, leaving #288 open on the capture prerequisite. The ignored local plan under `docs/superpowers/` was never committed and `git ls-files docs/superpowers` is empty.

**Awaiting maintainer decision:** #288's bucket prerequisite only. Two optional judgement calls from #284 also remain open on that issue with working defaults already shipped (whether a leftover global object-store block alongside a `tailnets:` list should be a hard error rather than a warning, and whether an explicit `0` budget on a list entry should be rejected rather than read as unset).

## Phases P1 and P2 complete — every child closed

All 24 children across P0, P1 and P2 are closed. This comment is the phase receipt for P1 and P2 and
the tracker's own completion record.

### This session's commits

| Child | Commit | What it changed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #290 | `1e716e1` | S3 endpoint base paths preserved through one join point, so signed and sent paths cannot diverge |
| #450 | `cc6e498` | object-store ingest source/byte semantics corrected to mean decoded, not wire, bytes |
| #284 | `ddef918` | per-tailnet destinations and credentials, dispatching on config shape |
| #452 | `26bb03c` | ECS/EKS container credential provider, SSRF-hardened beyond what the AWS SDKs allow |
| #496 | `3df1b32` | `.json.zstd`/`.json.gzip` export keys accepted; stem × codec cross-product now guards the table |
| #497 | `4f670ab` | an object whose every row fails to decode is quarantined instead of silently skipped |
| #291 | `7ebdb9c` | ListObjects responses bounded and streamed; size verdict checked before the decoder error |
| #293 | `0794f61` | flat copied-export layout, with an absolute lower bound so a wrap cannot re-emit |
| #451 | `6709c54` | provider request and cursor-health telemetry |
| #288 | `2018f07` | configuration-log S3 export ingestion, on live-captured evidence |
| #498 | `2fb0c45` | leading-slash prefix no longer erases durable listing progress every cycle |
| #463 | `639ca34` | ingestion-source, backfill and acknowledgement claims reconciled with runtime behavior |

Each commit was gated in a throwaway `git worktree` holding **only that child's diff**, `cmp`-verified
file-by-file against the staged tree, so the gate that ran is the tree that was pushed rather than a
union of concurrent lanes' half-finished work. Every commit's exact SHA reached terminal success on all
applicable workflows before the next was pushed.

Three issues were **filed** during the work rather than found by the audit — #496, #497 and #498 — all
discovered while producing evidence for another child, and all closed here.

### Corrections recorded, including mine

- **My frozen #293 design would have double-emitted.** Specifying "the same `stale` filter" for flat
  mode made the `progress.active` exemption span the whole export instead of one day; combined with
  seen-set pruning it re-fetched and re-emitted old objects on every wrap and silently defeated
  `initial_lookback`. The lane's absolute-lower-bound fix was accepted instead.
- **My frozen #497 brief was factually wrong.** I claimed the existing bounded retry escalates an
  undecodable object to quarantine. `gap.Quarantined` is set only from error classification or an
  unparseable gap key; `Attempts` only feeds `gapRetryDelay` and no threshold exists. The acceptance
  bullet was dropped; retry-forever is correct on the merits.
- **My #498 fix recommendation was wrong** and would have converted a wasted-requests bug into a
  data-duplication bug. `FeedID` applies no normalisation, so trimming the prefix at the config
  boundary moves the checkpoint namespace of an existing `/flow` deployment and re-emits its history.
  Corrected on the issue before implementation; the shipped fix corrects the predicate instead.
- **`key.go`'s layout names were backwards.** It called the live export's self-dated basename "legacy"
  and the never-observed time-only form "official". Behaviour was always right; the names and comments
  lied. Corrected under #288 with live evidence.
- **The documented atomicity guarantee was inverted.** The docs said a scanner failure could replay
  already-emitted rows — contradicting a *passing committed test*. Corrected under #463.

### Process trap worth keeping

`ci.yml` uses `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` keyed on the ref, so pushing to `main` cancels
the **previous** commit's in-flight CI and CodeQL. Three back-to-back pushes earlier in this programme
left two SHAs with cancelled runs; repairing it needs serialised `gh run rerun` because re-runs share
the group. Every child since has waited for terminal CI before the next push.

### Definition of done

- [x] Every child issue closed with a verified commit or an evidence-backed decision. #287, #454 and
      #455 closed as unsupported with the reason recorded (Grafana Cloud retention; S3 is Tailscale's
      only supported export path).
- [x] Every phase has a tracker completion comment with receipts and deviations.
- [x] Generated artifacts, documentation, dashboards/rules and deployment examples agree with the final
      contracts. Verified rather than assumed: `scripts/regen-generated.sh` is drift-free at
      `639ca34`; the shipped alert rules aggregate `sum by (tailscale_collector)` with no hardcoded
      collector list, so the new `objectstore-audit` collector is covered automatically; and the
      flagship dashboard's ingest panels use `sum by (source, signal)`, so object-store audit
      ingestion appears as `objectstore/audit` with no generator change.
- [x] Full repository and affected tool-module gates green at the final integration SHA. `639ca34`:
      root + `tools/{configcheck,metricscatalog,apidrift}` build/vet/race/lint, govulncheck, helm
      lint + 141 render tests, configcheck on example and rendered config, GoReleaser snapshot, Docker
      build, actionlint, zizmor — all green locally, and all workflows green for the exact SHA.
- [x] No unresolved decision, security-sensitive detail or follow-up exists only in an agent
      transcript. Everything is on the child issues; the capture recipe and its four API traps are in
      #288's evidence comment.

### Handoffs, not gaps in this tracker

- **The `tailscale2otel.objectstore.*` metrics added by #451 have no dashboard panels and no alert
  rules.** Ingest volume is covered by the generic `source`/`signal` panels, but the object-store
  specific gauges — backlog, gap health, cursor age, discovered/pending ages, request outcomes — are
  emitted and undisplayed. That belongs to **#481** (Grafana dashboards, rules and self-observability),
  not here.
- **Two #284 judgement calls remain open on that issue with working defaults shipped**: whether a
  leftover global object-store block in multi-tailnet mode should warn (current) or hard-error, and
  whether an explicit `0` budget on a list entry should default (current) or be rejected. Neither
  blocks anything.
- **Normalising a leading-slash prefix** would need an atomic idempotent state migration in the shape
  #453 established. Deliberately not done and deliberately not filed — the shipped `Warnings()`
  advisory makes it a non-issue for new deployments, and #498's receipt records the reasoning.

## Tracker closed

Every child across P0, P1 and P2 is closed — 24 issues, including the three (#496, #497, #498) filed during the work itself. The definition of done is ticked with the evidence for each item in the [phase-completion receipt](#issuecomment-5091803176) above.

Final integration SHA: `639ca34`. All applicable workflows green for that exact SHA, and the full local gate (root + three tool modules, govulncheck, helm lint + 141 render tests, configcheck on example and rendered config, generated-artifact drift, GoReleaser snapshot, Docker build, actionlint, zizmor) was run in an isolated worktree matching it.

Two things deliberately leave this tracker as handoffs rather than gaps, both recorded in the receipt: the `tailscale2otel.objectstore.*` gauges from #451 have no dashboard panels or alert rules yet, which belongs to #481; and two #284 configuration judgement calls stay open on that issue with working defaults shipped.

title: Tracker: durable object-store ingestion, backfill, and cloud providers

body:
## Mission

Make every real-time and polled event path preserve the upstream record, apply explicit trust semantics, avoid silent loss or misattribution, and expose enough bounded diagnostics to prove what happened.

This tracker is the launch prompt for the theme identified by the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. Read this issue and every selected child issue in full, including all comments, before changing code.

## Binding decisions

- GitHub is the source of truth. Keep each child checklist current, close it from its completing commit, and post a tracker phase receipt with issue numbers, commit SHAs, re-scopes, stale closures, and anything parked.
- Do not reopen the rejected directions recorded in #173: further Headscale investment, a Prometheus mixin, an OpenTelemetry Collector receiver donation, native OTLP profiles, OpAMP, unsupported control-plane peer-relay APIs, federated-identity key coverage, per-device route N+1 polling, services address/comment telemetry, or a bespoke Kubernetes operator.
- Parked items—configuration hot reload, shared checkpoint/replica semantics, HTTP service discovery, and log-stream destination drift—must begin with the research/design acceptance criteria in their child issue. Do not jump directly to implementation.
- Research issues may close as unsupported when evidence does not justify adoption; record the decision and rejected alternatives.

## Execution contract

- Validate the premise against current code and current upstream contracts before implementation.
- Use strict TDD: observe the focused test fail for the expected reason, implement the smallest complete change, then refactor green.
- Assert emitted telemetry through `internal/telemetrytest.Recorder`; keep collectors behind their narrow interfaces and `telemetry.Emitter` facade.
- Freeze shared seams before parallel work and assign one owner per file. Integration and generated registries have one owner.
- Preserve bounded cardinality, the PII policy, secret redaction, multi-tailnet identity, and poll-versus-stream exclusivity.
- Regenerate every affected committed artifact with the pinned repository tools.
- Run the full affected-module gate and the root `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` gates before closing work.
- Work directly on `main`; the completing commit must use `Closes #N` for every child it finishes and be pushed immediately under the repository issue workflow.

## Phase worklist

### Phase P0

- [x] #257 — fix(flowlogs): preserve embedded node identity through poll boundary dedup

### Phase P1

- [x] #258 — fix(flowlog): include traffic type in connection dedup identities
- [x] #259 — feat(flowlog): detect conflicting duplicate records instead of silently taking the first
- [x] #260 — feat(flowlogs): replay a bounded overlap for late-arriving API records
- [x] #261 — fix(flowlogs): expose feature-probe failures in stream and object-store modes
- [x] #264 — feat(flowlog): add shared semantic validation and data-quality telemetry

- [x] #268 — feat(audit): preserve deferred timing, event type, actor tags, and ephemeral targets
- [x] #269 — feat(audit): expand the security and lifecycle change taxonomy from the current schema
- [x] #272 — feat(webhook): emit typed structured event data with PII controls
- [x] #273 — security(webhook): fail closed on network-reachable binds with no secret
- [x] #274 — feat(webhook): suppress upstream retry duplicates for all event types
- [x] #278 — fix(stream): stop all side effects after the request deadline returns 503
- [x] #280 — feat(receivers): route HEC and webhook traffic in multi-tailnet mode
- [x] #282 — feat(ingest): expose per-source event age and accepted-data freshness
- [x] #456 — research(webhook): verify timestamp tolerance against 24-hour retries, then correct replay handling

### Phase P2

- [x] #262 — fix(flowlog): omit network.type when neither endpoint is valid
- [x] #263 — fix(flowlog): canonicalize tag-set dimensions before emission and storage
- [x] #265 — feat(flowlog): expose reporter provenance and trust diagnostics
- [x] #266 — feat(flowlog): distinguish Destination Logging privacy gaps from malformed records
- [x] #270 — feat(audit): emit bounded schema-drift signals for unknown values
- [x] #271 — fix(stream): classify explicit CONFIG audit records even when actor is absent
- [x] #275 — feat(webhook): add native TLS listener support
- [x] #276 — research(webhook): verify secret-rotation signature overlap and correct local guidance
- [x] #277 — research(webhook): validate and instrument webhook-to-audit cross-source dedup
- [x] #281 — fix(config): preflight streaming.public_url against Tailscale endpoint rules

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Land record-identity and trust-boundary fixes before building richer derived views.
- Coordinate durable receiver acknowledgement with EPIC-02 rather than inventing a second persistence contract.
- Feed new health/freshness signals into EPIC-05 only after their telemetry contracts are stable.

## Definition of done

title: Tracker: trustworthy flow, audit, webhook, and receiver semantics

body:
## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The security audit validated each control failure end to end and routed these items to the public tracker because they are operator hardening, privacy-contract, or resilience work rather than private vulnerability disclosures.

## Finding and proposed scope

Problem: Compose selects the repository root as build context at `deploy/docker-compose.yaml:19-21`; `.dockerignore:1-8` does not exclude the documented local secret/config/capture paths; and `deploy/Dockerfile:8` runs `COPY . .`. Those files are therefore transferred to the builder and recorded in a build-stage cache even though the final distroless image does not copy the source tree.

Scope:

- Deny every documented local-sensitive path in `.dockerignore`, including `.env` variants, `.secrets/`, local YAML, `.capture/`, and checkpoints.
- Prefer an allowlisted build context or narrower `COPY` instructions where maintainable.
- Add a disposable sentinel-based context test; never inspect or send real local secret/capture content.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Fake sentinel files in every sensitive path are absent from the builder context and all resulting layers/cache records.
- [ ] Required source, generated files, licenses, and module downloads still build reproducibly.
- [ ] Compose, direct Docker, BuildKit, and release build contexts follow the same policy.
- [ ] Documentation warns that `.gitignore` is not a Docker context boundary.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

`security:SEC-13`

comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

`.dockerignore` is now a **default-deny allowlist** rather than a deny-list. Chosen over narrower `COPY` instructions deliberately: `.dockerignore` is the only thing governing what is transferred to the daemon and recorded in the build cache, which is what this issue actually describes — a narrower `COPY` fixes the layer but not the context.

Sixteen leaks confirmed from *inside the builder* before the fix, including `.env`, `.secrets`, `.capture`, `checkpoints`, and the local config YAMLs.

**The sentinel probe never touches real secrets.** `.secrets/` and `.capture/` already exist in this tree with real content, so the probe backs off on any path that already exists and relies on a path-prefix assertion instead — it never overwrites and never reads. **Non-obvious behaviour verified rather than assumed:** BuildKit *does* descend into a directory excluded by `**` when `!` exceptions exist, which is what makes `!cmd/**` and `!internal/**` work. Both `//go:embed` assets are asserted present, so a tightened context cannot silently break the build.

Image still builds, verified twice for real (direct `docker build` and `docker compose build`), binary runs, and all 1400 paths across the final image layers were scanned: everything the Dockerfile promises is present, nothing sensitive is.

`security:SEC-12`

comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

**The acceptance criterion in this issue's own body is an unsound test.** It says `git check-ignore -v --no-index -- deploy/.env` should succeed. It does — but `-v` **exits 0 when the matching rule is a `!` negation too**, so it cannot serve as the ignored/not-ignored verdict:

```
.env.example    quiet:not-ignored(1)    -v: .gitignore:44:!.env.example    (-v exit=0)
.env            quiet:IGNORED(0)        -v: .gitignore:27:*.env           (-v exit=0)
```

The first version of the new check used `-v` and consequently reported `.env.example` as wrongly ignored. The script now gates on `git check-ignore -q` and uses `-v` only to fetch the rule text for its report.

## Audit identity

`security:SEC-11`

comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

**Measured, which is the headline for this issue.** Same input both runs (an unterminated JSON string literal, the body the pre-existing oversized test used):

| | totalAlloc | live heap at return |
|---|---|---|
| before | 1024 MiB | **896 MiB** |
| after | 16 MiB | **12 MiB** |

896 MiB live heap against the chart's 256Mi default limit means the guard was OOM-killing the process it existed to protect. The after figure is ~4.5% of that limit, and a test asserts a 32 MiB ceiling so it cannot regress.

Worst *survivable* case — an endless stream of legal ~250 B records, where nothing structural trips and the byte ceiling is the only control — measures 127 MiB totalAlloc / 96 MiB live. Under half the limit, and the honest cost of a 32 MiB log budget.

**Design deviation, justified:** the plan called for a `json.Decoder.Token()` loop. That was rejected after checking `go doc` — `Token` materializes each string before it can be measured, and `Decode` buffers the whole top-level value first. Both allocate exactly what we are preventing. The implementation instead puts a byte-level JSON lexer on the *read* path, tracking depth, string length and array elements as bytes flow past and failing the `Read` the instant a budget trips. That is what produces 896 MiB → 12 MiB; a `Token()` loop would still have allocated the multi-MB string.

**Sizing, and the tuning constraint operators need:** the snapshot default (4 MiB) comes from a real capture at ~1.8 KiB/device, i.e. ~2,400 devices. These endpoints are **not paginated**, so a bigger tailnet is a bigger single body — a tailnet past ~2,000 devices must raise `tailscale.max_response_bytes`, and the error message names the key. The log default (32 MiB) covers ~13,600 flow records at ~2.4 KiB each; `.capture/` holds no flow or audit captures, so that tier was sized from synthetic envelopes built off the record types, stated here so it is not mistaken for a live measurement.

Budget failures cannot drive the retry loop — the limit trips while decoding a 200 after `RoundTrip` has returned. Verified empirically: 4 max attempts against an endless-body server produces exactly 1 request.

`internal/hsapi/limit.go` has the identical bug and is tracked as #488.

title: Bound API JSON decoding memory below supported deployment limits

`security:SEC-09`

comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

All three failure modes reproduced before the fix:

- **Remnant:** body `rotated deploy-key-primary-2026 for tailnet` with candidates `deploy-key` and `deploy-key-primary-2026` → `rotated [redacted]-primary-2026 for tailnet`.
- **Nondeterminism:** identical input produced `tcp [redacted]-[redacted] …` on one iteration and `tcp [redacted]-[redacted]-[redacted] …` on the next.
- **Marker re-match:** candidates `supersecret` + `red` on body `supersecret` → `[[[redacted]ed]acted]`.

Implementation is dedupe → sort longest-first with a lexicographic tie-break → single left-to-right pass with a first-byte gate and a lazily allocated builder, so a no-match body is returned identically rather than copied.

Measured bounds for a 1 MiB body (the acceptance criterion): ~1.6 ms and one body-sized allocation; a no-match 1 MiB body allocates 1136 B total. 64 candidates costs no more than 10, because the first-byte gate dominates.

Determinism is asserted by running the redaction 200–500 times per test and requiring identical output, rather than by reasoning about map ordering.

- [ ] A pre-existing symlink at the historical predictable path is never followed or modified.
- [ ] Concurrent saves cannot share or clobber temporary files.
- [ ] Crash/restart behavior leaves either the old or complete new checkpoint, not a partial file.

`security:SEC-08`

comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

**Two corrections to the premise, both worth recording.**

First, the durability work the issue implies was already done: the file *and* the parent directory were both already fsynced (`checkpoint.go:146` and `:157-160`). Those were preserved unchanged, not reinvented. What was genuinely missing was **cleanup** — no error path removed the temp file, so every failed save leaked a stale `.tmp` permanently.

Second, this was also an **availability** bug, not only a security one. Under the old fixed `.tmp` name two concurrent savers race, and one's `rename` fires after the other has consumed the file — `Set` returns a hard error and that checkpoint is silently lost.

The symlink test caught the exploit landing in full against unmodified code: the checkpoint JSON was written *into the attacker's sentinel file outside the checkpoint directory*, and the symlink was then renamed onto the checkpoint path, so every later save kept writing through it.

The tests were verified to be real regression tests by temporarily reverting the helper to the legacy scheme and confirming they fail.

**Known remaining gap, deliberate:** a SIGKILL between `CreateTemp` and `rename` still leaves a staging file, and randomized names mean they now accumulate one per hard kill rather than reusing one. comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

**The issue named only workload identity, but the OAuth client-credentials path had the identical defect** — it posts the client secret in the same replayable form body through the same unbounded-redirect token-fetch client. Both are fixed by the one shared policy.

**Also worth recording: 301/302/303 were not harmless.** Go rewrites them to a bodyless GET, so no JWT appeared in the body — but the exchange still *completed* against the attacker-named origin and returned its `access_token` (`Token() err = nil`). All five statuses are now covered by explicit tests.

The policy is built once in `buildHTTPClient` and installed on both the API client and the token-fetch client, so the API-key, OAuth and workload-identity paths cannot drift apart. `newBoundedTokenFetchClient` now *requires* it as a parameter rather than accepting a nil default.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The security audit validated each control failure end to end and routed these items to the public tracker because they are operator hardening, privacy-contract, or resilience work rather than private vulnerability disclosures.

## Finding and proposed scope

Problem: `internal/tsapi/transport.go:28-31` unconditionally attaches the API-key bearer credential in `RoundTrip`. Go correctly strips an original cross-origin `Authorization` header during redirect handling, but the custom transport adds it back to the redirected request.

Production uses a fixed TLS-validated Tailscale origin and no in-scope actor controls its redirects, so this is defense in depth rather than a private vulnerability.

Scope:

- Bind credential attachment to the configured Tailscale scheme and authority.
- Reject cross-origin redirects for authenticated API requests, or require an explicit safe allowlist if an upstream same-origin redirect is needed.
- Define redirect behavior once so OAuth, API-key, and future authentication methods cannot drift.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Same-origin redirects retain the required authentication behavior.
- [ ] Cross-origin redirects never receive the bearer credential.
- [ ] Scheme downgrade and userinfo/alternate-port cases are covered.
- [ ] The redirect failure is observable without logging credentials or full destinations.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`security:SEC-03`

comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

**The hole was wider than the issue states.** Go forwards `Authorization` to a *subdomain* match, not only to an exact-origin match — so `api.tailscale.com` → `evil.api.tailscale.com` would have carried the key even without the custom transport re-adding it. The fix treats a subdomain as a distinct origin.

Origin comparison is against `via[0]` (the request the credential was issued for), not the previous hop, so a redirect chain cannot walk the credential away one step at a time. Scheme downgrade, alternate port, subdomain and any userinfo difference are all distinct origins.

Two layers, deliberately: `redirectPolicy` refuses the redirect outright, and `authKeyTransport` independently attaches the bearer only on the configured origin. The transport's `origin` field is required — the zero value matches nothing, so a mis-wired transport fails closed with 401s rather than reverting to unconditional attachment.

Note that installing a custom `CheckRedirect` removes net/http's default redirect cap, so the policy re-implements the 10-redirect limit.

title: Keep Tailscale API bearer credentials on the configured origin across redirects

- For IP-only semantic keys, remove or replace non-empty values that cannot be classified when their permitted category is unknown.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Canonical IPv4, mapped IPv4, IPv6, address-port, bracketed, whitespace, and malformed cases have table-driven coverage.
- [ ] Disabled IP categories cannot be bypassed by changing textual representation.
- [ ] Redaction remains deterministic and never logs the rejected value.
- [ ] Documentation states how unclassifiable semantic values are handled.

`security:SEC-02`

comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

**Correction to the premise, worth recording:** only the *prefix-based* ranges were affected by the missing `Unmap`. `::ffff:127.0.0.1` and `::ffff:169.254.1.1` already classified correctly, because netip's `IsLoopback`/`IsLinkLocalUnicast` handle 4-in-6 themselves. It was `Prefix.Contains` that refused to match a mapped address against an IPv4 prefix, which is why CGNAT and RFC1918 were the ones that leaked.

A second representation bypass turned up that the issue did not name: whitespace-padded addresses returned `ipNotIP` entirely. Trimming is now part of the same normalisation.

Fail-closed rule as implemented: for an IP-only semantic key (`source.address`, `destination.address`, `tailscale.dns.resolver.address` — the three with no `ipKeyFallback`) carrying a non-empty unclassifiable value, the value is dropped when any IP category is disabled. With every IP category enabled the value is kept and behaviour is byte-identical, so the fast path is untouched. The rejected value is never logged.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The security audit validated each control failure end to end and routed these items to the public tracker because they are operator hardening, privacy-contract, or resilience work rather than private vulnerability disclosures.

## Finding and proposed scope

Problem: object-store enumeration parses the basename timestamp at `internal/collector/objectstore/key.go:51-68` and rejects old or malformed keys at `internal/collector/objectstore/objectstore.go:262-273`, but never rejects a timestamp later than the current collection cycle. A valid object with a future basename can therefore be processed and persisted as the cursor at `objectstore.go:204-205,231-234`. The next cycle derives no day prefixes until wall clock catches up.

This was reproduced with two collection cycles. It is public hardening because the supported bucket is a trusted Tailscale export and no lower-privileged key-creation path exists in the repository.

Scope:

- Reject or quarantine timestamps later than the collection time plus an explicit, documented clock-skew allowance.
- Never let a future key influence the durable cursor, recent-key window, or listing lower bound.
- Surface a bounded rejection counter and stable error class without putting object names into metric labels.

Acceptance:

- [ ] A future basename under a currently listed prefix cannot advance the cursor.
- [ ] A current object remains discoverable on the next cycle.
- [ ] The skew policy covers S3, GCS, and Azure implementations consistently.
- [ ] Tests cover the exact boundary, restart persistence, and a legitimate near-future timestamp within allowance.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.

## Audit identity

`security:SEC-01`

comments.body:
Closed by `476f236`.

Fixed 5-minute constant (not a config key). Keys later than `now + 5m` are excluded at candidacy, so they cannot reach the cursor, the seen-set, the backlog gauge or the per-cycle budget. Rejections are counted on the existing `objectstore.skipped` counter under a new `future_timestamp` reason — no object name in any label.

**Worth knowing for anyone touching this again:** a future-dated key does not need a future day-partition directory to cause the failure. `parseKey` deliberately reads the basename only, so `flow/2026/07/24/2027-01-01-00-00-00.ndjson` sits under today's listed prefix and parses as 2027.

The failing test before the fix showed the exact symptom the issue describes — `records after a restart = 0`, i.e. a second process over the same checkpoint store enumerated nothing at all.

The 'covers S3, GCS and Azure consistently' criterion is satisfied by construction: `objectAPI` (objectstore.go:89) is the only backend interface, GCS and Azure are reached through their S3-compatible endpoints, and the filter sits in `enumerate` above that interface, so a future backend inherits it with no per-backend code.

## Closed by `639ca34`

`docs: reconcile ingestion-source, backfill and acknowledgement claims with runtime behavior` — pushed
direct to `main`.

Each of the three claims was re-confirmed against the code before being changed, and each correction
now has a test that fails if the documentation drifts back. Two of them turned out to be worse than
"imprecise wording".

### 1. Maximum effective backfill — measured, and much smaller than documented

README and `docs/configuration.md` called the object store "the only practical way to backfill a long
history". Under the default `layout: partitioned` it **cannot reach further back than 14 day
partitions** — today plus the previous 13 — whatever `initial_lookback` says.

The ceiling is **permanent, not per-cycle**, which is the part that makes it a data-loss issue rather
than a throughput one: `dayPrefixes` walks backwards from the newest day so a capped span keeps the
recent days, and the cursor only ever moves forward, so the older days are not enumerated on any later
cycle either.

Measured rather than reasoned about. With `initial_lookback: 720h` against 30 days of one-object days,
twelve consecutive cycles ingest day offsets **1–13 and never more**:

```
cycle  1: records= 13 fetched=13
...
cycle 12: records= 13 fetched=13
distinct day-offsets ingested: 13 of 30
oldest day-offset reached: 13
```

Sixteen days are silently lost — **no gap, no `skipped` count, no metric**, because those objects are
never listed at all. Every health signal stays green. The same probe under `layout: flat` reaches all
30 days.

`TestCollect_PartitionedBackfillIsCappedAtFourteenDayPartitions` pins this from both sides (offsets
1–13 present, 14–30 absent) across twelve cycles, so it fails if the reach ever grows; the flat
counterpart pins that flat is not capped.

Since the engine cannot report the loss, `Warnings()` now does. That needed the bound in
`internal/config`, which cannot import the engine, so `objectstore.MaxDayPrefixes` is exported and
`TestObjectStoreBackfillCeilingMatchesTheEngine` — in the external `config_test` package, the one place
both are importable — asserts the two copies still agree. Mutation-proven in **both** directions:
moving `maxDayPrefixes` to 20 fails it ("config's ceiling is SHORTER … the advice is needless"), and
moving the config ceiling to 30 days fails it ("config's ceiling is LONGER … an operator is told
nothing while objects are silently skipped").

### 2. Object-level atomicity was documented backwards

`docs/streaming-webhooks.md` said "a scanner can fail after it emitted valid rows, so retry may
duplicate those rows after restart until object processing is atomic", and README said the same. That
predates the two-phase prepare/commit engine (#453): every row is decoded and validated before any is
committed, so a mid-object failure emits **nothing** rather than a partial prefix.

The documentation was contradicting a **passing committed test** —
`TestCollect_LateScannerErrorEntersDurableGapPath` asserts 0 records on the failing cycle and exactly
1 on the retry after restart. Corrected in both places, with the correction and its cause stated
inline so the old claim is not reinstated by someone reading only the prose. What genuinely *is*
at-least-once — the object as a unit, replayed if the process dies between emission and the checkpoint
write — is now said explicitly instead of being implied by a false statement about rows.

### 3. One authoritative source/signal matrix

`docs/streaming-webhooks.md` now opens with a single table covering poll / stream / objectstore /
webhook / both against `flowlogs`, `auditlogs` and Tailscale events, each with its delivery guarantee,
durability boundary and maximum backfill. The flow-vs-audit asymmetry the old text implied is gone
(#288 made object-store audit real). The table also states plainly what no page said before: **
acknowledgement stops at this process** — an advanced checkpoint means "handed to the emitter", never
"stored by the backend".

`initial_lookback` gains the ceiling caveat in `docs/configuration.md`, `config.example.yaml` and the
chart's `values.yaml`, so an operator meets it where they set the value rather than only in prose.

### Local verification

Isolated `git worktree` at `HEAD` holding exactly this diff, `cmp`-verified file-by-file against the
staged tree: root + all three tool modules `go build`/`go vet`/`go test -race`/`golangci-lint` clean;
`govulncheck`; `helm lint` + 141 render tests; `configcheck` on the example and chart-rendered config;
`scripts/regen-generated.sh` drift-free; GoReleaser snapshot; Docker build; `actionlint`; `zizmor`.

### Deviations

- **A `Warnings()` addition and an exported constant are not purely documentation.** The issue's
  acceptance asked to "update … validation text", and a silent 16-day data loss that no metric reports
  cannot be fixed by prose alone — an operator who never reads the docs still needs to be told. Flagged
  here rather than filed separately because it is the same finding.
- **No `Chart.yaml` bump.** The chart change is comment-only; no values keys added or altered.
- **#287's declined long-history backfill is referenced, not reopened.** Grafana Cloud's retention
  makes a longer load unsupported regardless of what this reader can reach, and the new section says so
  rather than implying `flat` solves it.

title: docs: reconcile ingestion-source, backfill, and acknowledgement claims with runtime behavior

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit checked current official Tailscale and ecosystem capabilities against the implementation and retained only a concrete, independently reviewable addition or research question.

## Finding and proposed scope

P3 · low/medium confidence · research first

- Restrict investigation to Kubernetes API/session metadata such as verb, resource, namespace, status, recorder, and source identity.
- Explicitly prohibit command text, stdout/stderr, request bodies, query strings, terminal recordings, and arbitrary event payload.
- Acceptance:
  - Establish a stable documented object/event contract.
  - Produce sanitized fixtures and privacy threat model.
  - Close as unsupported if safe metadata cannot be separated reliably.
- Sources: [Tailscale session recording](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/tsrecorder), [Kubernetes recorder](https://tailscale.com/docs/kubernetes-operator/recorder), [upstream event type](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/main/sessionrecording/event.go).

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Record the evidence, decision, rejected alternatives, and follow-up implementation slices; closing as unsupported is valid when the evidence does not justify a feature.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`ecosystem:F3`

comments.body:
## Research findings — scoped to Kubernetes audit data. Verdict: SUPPORTED, proceeding to implementation.

Evidence base: 807 real `.event` objects + 5 `.cast` objects captured from a live tsrecorder S3 bucket on 2026-07-29, cross-checked against upstream source (`sessionrecording/event.go`, `k8s-operator/api-proxy/proxy.go`, `k8s-operator/sessionrecording/hijacker.go`).

### Scope decision

Scoped to **Kubernetes audit data only**. The owner has **explicitly overridden** this issue's "prohibit command text" acceptance criterion: aggregates of command text carry real SIEM value, and the design bounds them rather than banning them. Recorded here as a decision, not left as a silent gap.

Locked scope: `.event` objects in full, plus the **first line only** of `.cast` objects. Terminal output frames are recognised and deliberately ignored — never inspected for meaning, never emitted.

### The finding that shapes everything

**There is no response side in this data.** No status code, no latency, no byte count, no error field anywhere in the schema. This is a request-side proxy log, not a Kubernetes audit log. Allowed-vs-denied, error rates and latency histograms are all impossible. This gets documented rather than approximated.

### Ingestion surface

S3 polling is the **only** consumption surface that exists:

- No control-plane API for listing or fetching recordings (`api.tailscale.com` has nothing).
- tsrecorder's HTTP surface (`/record`, `/v2/record`, `/v2/event`) is **write-only, receiver-side** — how the API-server proxy pushes data in, not something a third party reads out.
- No webhook, syslog or OTLP push capability anywhere.
- The tsrecorder server is **closed source** — the OSS repo has no `cmd/tsrecorder`, and the binary's build path is `tailscale.io/...`, not `tailscale.com/...`. Only the client-side packages that talk to it are public.

The feed is gated by `enableEvents` in the `tailscale.com/cap/kubernetes` ACL grant and is **beta upstream**.

### The object is not the upstream type

The S3 object is `{stableID, event, timestamp}` — a server-side wrapper around upstream `sessionrecording.Event`. Proof it is a wrapper: the OSS proxy never populates `Destination`, yet all 807 captured objects carry it. The wrapper is unversioned, undocumented and closed-source, so we decode our own type defensively rather than importing upstream's.

Two decode traps, both silent if missed:

- `event.kubernetes.*` serializes **PascalCase** (`Verb`, `Namespace`, `Resource`) because upstream pasted k8s' `request.RequestInfo` without json tags, while every sibling is camelCase. Same again for the `.cast` header's nested `Kubernetes` block.
- There is **no schema version field and no stability guarantee**. Schema-drift counter is mandatory, mirroring `internal/audit`.

### Privacy threat model

| Vector | Handling |
|---|---|
| `request.path` carries the **full query string including URL-encoded exec command text** (`.../exec?command=sh&command=-c&command=clear%3B+%28bash...`) | Never emitted. `kubernetes.Path` is the query-free equivalent and is the only path field exported. Redacting `queryParameters.command` while emitting `request.path` would leak exactly what was redacted. |
| `request.body` is read with `io.ReadAll` and has **no size cap upstream** | Never emitted raw; inspected only under our own limit. |
| `.cast` frames are raw terminal output — arbitrary secrets in plain text | Never read for meaning, never emitted. |
| Exec command text | Bounded `command_class` label on metrics (interactive_shell / recon / package_mgmt / net_tool / file_transfer / credential_read / other). Raw text is a **log attribute only**, on by default under a new `command_text` PII category, redactable independently. The class survives redaction — it is not PII. |
| Object names, paths, selectors, pod/container | Log attributes only, never metric labels. |

Cardinality measured on the real corpus: `verb + api_group + resource + subresource + namespace + user + user_agent` = **67 series**; adding object `Name` = 107. Unbounded fields are `Name` (55), `Path` (142), `LabelSelector` (6) — all log-only. Every client-controlled string is normalised to a closed admit-set, unknown → `other`.

### Two traps found in the data

1. **Object keys are not safely sortable.** Keys are `<RFC3339Nano>.event`, and Go's RFC3339Nano **trims trailing zeros** — the corpus holds 7-, 8- and 9-digit fractional seconds (10 / 83 / 714 files). So `…11.9115044Z` sorts *after* `…11.91150441Z` despite being 10ns earlier. The engine's `sortCandidates` is safe (it orders by parsed time), but `enumerate` passes a raw key as S3 `StartAfter`, which **is** lexicographic — so a naive checkpoint silently skips objects, permanently, with no error and no metric. Fixed-width Tailscale export keys are immune; these are not. Mitigation: truncate the scan position to a second boundary and let the durable seen-set absorb the overlap.
2. **`.cast` completeness is undetectable.** No `.tmp` marker, no documented signal, server closed-source. Reading the header line only is what makes an in-progress recording safe to ingest.

Also: `event.id` is byte-identical to the S3 object key — a free, self-describing dedup token. And every `.event` file is a single compact JSON object with zero newlines, so it is already NDJSON-compatible and the engine's line scanner works unmodified.

### Rejected alternatives

- **Close as unsupported.** Rejected: safe metadata separates cleanly, and the highest-value signals are all low-risk. One hour of capture already showed 7 `get secrets` reads, `pods/exec` into `kube-system/aws-node`, `pods/log` reads against the recorder's own pod (an audit-tampering signal), 43 deletes, and a 60-request `SelfSubjectRulesReview` sweep across every namespace whose bodies decode to exactly which namespace was probed.
- **A new S3 subsystem.** Rejected: `internal/objectstore` + `internal/s3` + `internal/collector/objectstore` already provide listing, durable checkpointing, gap/quarantine retry, decompression and byte limits behind a `SignalProcessor` seam. This is a third signal on that engine.
- **`aws-sdk-go-v2`.** Rejected: `internal/s3` is hand-rolled precisely to avoid +8.3 MiB and +18 modules for what is two HTTP calls. No new dependency is needed.
- **A `poll` / `stream` source toggle** like flowlogs and auditlogs have. Rejected: S3 is the only surface that exists, so the toggle would offer a choice that cannot be honoured.
- **Discriminating `.event` from `.cast` by object key.** Not possible — `SignalProcessor.PrepareRecord` receives only the bytes, never the key. Discriminated by content instead; asciinema frames become accepted no-op records so a long session cannot mint thousands of bogus decode-failure observations.

### Accepted trade-off

Ingesting `.cast` means downloading the whole object to read its first line. The engine streams line-by-line so memory stays bounded, but a very large session could exceed `MaxObjectDecompressedBytes` and be quarantined into the gap table. Documented; operators recording long sessions should raise that limit for this feed. Stopping the read after line 1 needs an early-terminating record source in the engine — out of scope for this slice.

### Acceptance

- [x] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract
- [x] Establish a documented object/event contract
- [x] Produce a privacy threat model
- [ ] Sanitized fixtures
- [ ] Implementation: `internal/k8saudit` record/processor/catalog, recorder object-key layout, signal adapter, config, PII category, app wiring
- [ ] Generated artifacts regenerated and dispositions filled in
- [ ] Full gate green including tool modules

## Correction to the research comment above

One claim in my findings comment was **overstated** and is corrected here rather than left to mislead a future reader.

**What I wrote:** that the PascalCase json tags on `event.kubernetes.*` are load-bearing, and that dropping one makes the field silently decode as its zero value.

**What is actually true** (verified empirically 2026-07-29 with a standalone program, after a subagent's negative-test surfaced it): Go's `encoding/json` falls back to a **case-insensitive** field match. So all three of these decode `"APIGroup": "batch"` correctly:

| declaration | result |
|---|---|
| untagged field `APIGroup string` | `"batch"` ✅ |
| `json:"APIGroup"` | `"batch"` ✅ |
| `json:"apiGroup"` | `"batch"` ✅ |
| `json:"api_group"` | `""` ❌ **silent zero value** |

So the hazard is real but is about **letters, not case**. A tag whose letters differ from the wire name — `api_group` for `APIGroup` — breaks silently with no error. That is worth guarding against precisely because snake_case is the spelling a Go developer reaches for by reflex, and is what the rest of this repo's config types use.

**No code changes.** The PascalCase tags as implemented are correct and work; only the rationale comment was wrong. The doc comments in `internal/k8saudit/record.go` and `cast.go` have been rewritten to state the accurate version, since a re-learn-proof note that is subtly wrong is worse than no note at all.

Nothing else in the findings comment is affected.

## Shipped in `b61fe7a`

Implemented as a **third signal on the existing object-store engine** (`internal/objectstore` + `internal/s3` + `internal/collector/objectstore`), not a new subsystem. No new module dependency — the hand-rolled SigV4 client already there was sufficient.

### What landed

`internal/k8saudit` — wrapper/event/cast record types, bounded vocabularies + exec command classification, and the processor that is the single emission path. Plus the recorder object-key layout, the signal adapter, config plumbing, the `command_text` PII category, app wiring, docs and every regenerated artifact.

7 metrics, 2 log events, all `raw_only` in `signal_dispositions.json` with notes — no dashboard or rule ships for this feed, because useful thresholds for the sensitive-read and RBAC-probe counters depend on a cluster's own baseline and an arbitrary one would page on ordinary operator traffic.

### Two engine bugs the design had to solve

**Checkpoints could silently skip objects.** S3's `StartAfter` is a lexicographic comparison, and tsrecorder basenames are RFC3339Nano, which Go trims trailing zeros from — the live corpus held 7-, 8- and 9-digit fractional seconds. So `…11.9115044Z` sorts *after* `…11.91150441Z` while being 10ns earlier, and a naive checkpoint drops the earlier object permanently, with no error and no metric. Scan positions are now truncated to a second boundary for this layout only; the durable seen set absorbs the overlap. Fixed-width export layouts were never affected.

**`.event` and `.cast` cannot be told apart by filename.** They share a prefix, and `PrepareRecord` receives only the record bytes, never the object key. They are discriminated by content instead, and asciinema frames are accepted as no-op records rather than decode failures — otherwise one long session mints thousands of bogus data-quality observations and the object-level guard fails an otherwise healthy recording whose header is its only non-frame line.

### Two latent bugs found on the way, both fixed

- `piiCategories` mapped `PIIFilterConfig` field-by-field, and a category missing from that map is simply **absent** from the returned set — which the redactor treats as **enabled**. Any future category added without updating it would have had a silently dead config toggle. The comment claimed this couldn't happen; nothing enforced it. Now guarded by `TestPIICategoriesMapsEveryCategory`, negative-tested.
- The generated JSON schema derived `collectors.k8s_audit.objectstore.layout`'s enum from the shared type, giving it `[partitioned, flat]` — excluding `recorder`, the only valid value, while admitting the two that are refused. It would have rejected our own `config.example.yaml`.

### Corrections to my earlier comments

- The PascalCase-tag claim, already corrected above.
- **The plan's own checkpoint test was vacuous.** `TestRecorderCheckpointDoesNotSkipShorterKey` asserted `skipped > truncatedStartAfter(pos)`, which for that key pair already holds on the untruncated string — it passed identically against a no-op implementation. Caught by negative-testing, verified by neutering the function and watching it stay green. Deleted rather than kept as a weak pin, and replaced with two tests that pin the exact truncated output and the real skip direction. A comment in the file explains why, so it does not get reinstated.

### Verification

```
go build ./...        OK
go vet ./...          OK
go test -race ./...   67 packages ok
golangci-lint run     0 issues
govulncheck ./...     No vulnerabilities found
scripts/verify-modules.sh   all 5 modules verified
tools/configcheck config.example.yaml   OK
helm lint + helm template (k8s_audit enabled)   OK
```

All seven generated artifacts regenerated. A 57-record fixture sanitized from the live bucket (covering all 5 verbs, 4 subresources, 9 API groups, 3 user agents, request bodies, secrets reads and exec argv) is driven end-to-end through the decode path by `TestK8sAuditSignal_RealCorpusIsLeakFree` and `TestProcess_RealCorpusStaysBoundedAndLeakFree`.

### Not done, deliberately

- **No dashboard or alert rules.** See above; a follow-up once there is a baseline to threshold against.
- **`.cast` objects are streamed whole to read one line.** Memory stays bounded, but a very large session can exceed `max_object_decompressed_bytes` and be quarantined. Documented, with the knob called out in `docs/kubernetes-audit.md` and both config references. A clean fix needs an early-terminating record source in the engine.
- **Session duration.** `.cast` completeness is not observable from the bucket, so sessions are counted at start only.

## Dashboard follow-up: `0e02a05`

This issue's delivery requirements included updating affected **dashboards**, and the first commit did not. That was an under-delivery on my part, not a scope decision — collecting signals nobody can visualize is half a feature. Now done.

### What landed

A **Kubernetes Audit** leaf tab under the *Security & Policy* domain — 14 rows, 32 panels, generated by `deploy/grafana/gen/tabs/k8saudit.py`:

| Row group | Content |
|---|---|
| Request volume | rate by verb, namespace, resource (top N), user agent (top N) |
| Sensitive reads | by resource, namespace, user agent, + top readers |
| Exec / attach / portforward | by `command_class`, namespace, session type, + top users |
| Mutations | by verb, resource, namespace, + top users |
| RBAC probes | by resource, namespace, + top users |
| Terminal sessions | by session type, namespace, command class, + top users |
| Schema drift | rate by field/status + range stat, any drift red |
| Log detail & investigations | Loki drill-down: secrets reads, exec detail, enumeration probes, anti-forensics recorder-log reads |

### Gating

Uses the existing `conditionalRendering` presence-sentinel mechanism, so **the whole tab disappears on a tailnet with no recorder** (`has_k8s_audit`), and each row hides when its own signal has no data. Identity rows hide under `pii_filter.emails`; command-bearing panels hide under `pii_filter.command_text`, while `command_class` stays visible — which is the entire reason the bounded class exists.

### One defect I found and fixed in review

The tab initially gated the whole *investigations* row on `pii_command_text`. Three of its four panels — permission enumeration, secrets reads, and the anti-forensics "reads of the recorder's own logs" query — carry no command text at all. An operator making the conservative choice to redact command text would have lost the most valuable SIEM panels on the tab, for a reason that did not apply to them. The exec panel is now its own row, so only it carries that gate.

### Corrections to my earlier comment

- Dispositions moved `raw_only` → **`visualized`**, derived from the artifacts by `TestSignalDispositionsInSync -update`, not asserted by hand.
- Four disposition notes and one paragraph in `docs/kubernetes-audit.md` still said no dashboard shipped. All corrected — a doc that contradicts the artifact is worse than no doc.

### Verification

```
python3 -m unittest discover  (grafana/gen, alerts/gen, scripts)   163 tests, OK
scripts/regen-generated.sh                                          idempotent
go build ./... && go vet ./...                                      OK
go test -race ./...                                                 67 packages ok
golangci-lint run                                                   0 issues
govulncheck ./...                                                   No vulnerabilities found
TestFlagshipDashboardQueriesOnlyCatalogMetrics                      PASS
```

Panel count 405 → 437, inside the query-budget ceiling (460/560), so no budget constant needed raising.

**Alert manifests changed but no alert behavior did.** `__panelId__` annotations are resolved *by panel title* (`build_rules.py:361`), so inserting a tab renumbers them; spot-checked that they still resolve to the same panels.

### Still deliberately absent

**No alert rules for this feed.** The sensitive-read and RBAC-probe counters are the obvious candidates, but a `selfsubjectrulesreview` sweep across every namespace is routine for UI clients like Freelens — a threshold picked without a baseline would page on ordinary operator traffic. Worth revisiting once the tab has a week of real data behind it.
