## Closed by `607b32a`

`fix(oas): parse OpenAPI 3.1 type arrays and typed maps in drift analysis`.

### The premise, and why it was worse than "a missing feature"

The vendored spec is OpenAPI **3.1.0**, where nullability is a type ARRAY —
`"type": ["boolean","null"]`. The parser was written against 3.0's `nullable: true`, which **does not
appear in this spec at all** (0 occurrences). 16 type arrays do, every one inside a schema reached by
a consumed GET.

`json.Unmarshal(rawType, &s.Type)` into a string silently fails on an array, leaving `Type == ""`. And
`Classify`'s type-change check is guarded on **both** sides being non-empty — so with the empty type on
old *and* new, a field flipping `["boolean","null"]` → `["string","null"]` upstream was
**undetectable**. Not "reported vaguely": invisible. On exactly the optional fields most likely to be
retyped.

### Measured on the real spec

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nullable fields modeled (consumed GET responses) | 0 | **22** |
| typed maps with a value schema | 0 | **8** |
| fields left with an empty type | 25 | **3** |

The 3 remaining are the deliberately loose `anyOf` nodes — audit `old`/`new` and the posture attribute
map — which our decoders read as `json.RawMessage`/`map[string]any` on purpose.

### `additionalProperties` now modeled

The spec uses it for real typed maps that consumed GETs return: `SplitDns`,
`DnsConfiguration.splitDNS`, `DevicePostureAttributes.attributes`. Without it those nodes were
indistinguishable from an object with no properties, so a change to the map's **value** type looked
like nothing at all. The boolean forms (`additionalProperties: true|false`) carry no value type and
correctly leave it nil; neither appears in the spec.

### Composition stays unmodeled — now with evidence instead of assertion

This resolves the open question from the recon: **is `VIPServiceInfoPut`'s `allOf` reachable?** No.

- `oneOf` — 1 occurrence, in a POST request body.
- `allOf` — 1 occurrence, `VIPServiceInfoPut`, `$ref`'d only from
  `PUT /tailnet/{tailnet}/services/{serviceName}` (verified by walking every `$ref` in the spec).

`ParseSpec` keeps GET operations only, so **neither is reachable at all**. The doc comment now records
that rather than claiming composition is unmodeled by preference, and preserves the existing (correct)
rationale for `anyOf` rather than deleting it.

One limitation is stated in the code so it is not mistaken for completeness: a union of two
**concrete** types is still not representable. None appears in the spec, and taking the first non-null
type is strictly better than taking none, because it keeps the type-change check alive on the common
nullable case.

### Why the test is through `Classify`, not just the parser

A parser-level assertion would have proved the field parses. The failure that mattered was
*downstream* — the guard silently swallowing the comparison — so
`TestClassify_DetectsTypeChangeInsideATypeArray` drives a real boolean→string flip through
`Classify` and requires a `TypeChanged`. That is the test that would have stayed green while real
drift went unnoticed.

### Verification

`scripts/verify-modules.sh` green over all four modules — **including `tools/apidrift`'s own tests,
which no CI job ran before #437**, so this is the first change to that module verified by them.
`apidrift` self-compare against the vendored spec reports no drift. Whole root suite green under
`-race`, with no fallout in the schema-synthesis fuzz tests that now synthesize values for the 22
newly-typed fields. actionlint, zizmor, helm lint + 141 render tests, configcheck, generated artifacts
drift-free, GoReleaser snapshot, Docker build — in an isolated worktree holding exactly this diff.

### Note for #432

The recon also found that `tools/apidrift/main_test.go` was never executed by any workflow. That is
now fixed by #437's `module-verify` job, so CLI-level tests added to that module for #432 will actually
be enforced.

comments.body:
Done in `623240e`. Closed by that commit.

Two alerts plus a new `## Device and user approval {#device-and-user-approval}` runbook section.

| rule | expression | for | severity | page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ts2o-devices-unauthorized` | `sum(tailscale:devices_unauthorized:count) > 0` | 2h | warning | **false** |
| `ts2o-user-invites-stale` | p90 pending invite age > 7d | 1h | warning | **false** |

## Avoid a default page-level severity

Both carry an explicit `page=false` label, and a test asserts it. An unapproved device is a **queue to work through, not an incident** — paging on it at 3am is how a channel gets muted, and a muted channel is worse than no alert. Negative-tested by flipping one to `page=True`.

## External/shared-in kept distinct from unauthorized internal

Enforced by construction rather than by convention. The alert reads the `tailscale:devices_unauthorized:count` recording rule (#406), whose expression filters **both** `tailscale_authorized="false"` **and** `tailscale_external="false"`. A device shared in from another tailnet is not yours to approve, so counting it would produce an alert nobody can action.

Enforced twice over:

- a unit test asserts both filters survive in the recorded expression (negative-tested by removing `tailscale_external="false"`);
- a **promtool scenario feeds an external unauthorized device sustained for 150 minutes and asserts the alert never fires**, alongside an internal one that does. That is the one that proves the exclusion under execution rather than in the source text. Negative-tested by flipping the expectation.

The dashboard keeps them as two separate panels — `Unauthorized (internal)` and `External (shared-in)` — and the alert links to the first.

## Sustained, not on arrival

The 2h `for` is deliberate: firing the moment a device joins would page during the normal minutes before an admin approves it, which is the behaviour that makes approval alerts get disabled. This reports a device that has been *waiting*.

7 days on `ts2o-user-invites-stale` is a "nobody is going to accept this" horizon, not an SLA. The runbook says what to actually do with it: a long-stale invite is usually an access-review and offboarding problem — an invite sent to someone who has since left, or to the wrong address — and should normally be **revoked rather than chased**, because every outstanding invite is a standing grant waiting to be claimed.

## Coordination with #401

As agreed on that issue, the unauthorized-device case was held back from #401 and landed here instead, so the posture rules and the approval rules cannot double-page on the same condition. #401 shipped `ts2o-device-key-expiry-disabled-new` and `ts2o-device-multiple-connections`; neither overlaps with these two.

comments.body:
## Closing as unsupported — the catalog cannot take what this project produces

Per the tracker's rule that a research issue may close as unsupported when the evidence does not justify adoption, with the rejected alternatives recorded.

**The blocker.** Grafana's own documentation states plainly that **"Exporting with the Classic model is required for publishing to the Grafana community catalog."** (grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/dashboards/share-dashboards-panels, checked 2026-07-27). V2 Resource export supports JSON or YAML; the catalog will not accept either.

`deploy/grafana/tailscale2otel.json` is a v2 resource — `apiVersion: dashboard.grafana.app/v2`, a real `TabsLayout` → `RowsLayout` → `GridLayout` nesting, panels in `spec.elements` referenced by `ElementReference`, and `ConditionalRenderingVariable` gating driven by 34 presence variables. So it is not publishable as it stands.

**Rejected alternative — generate a Classic rendering alongside the v2 one.** Technically possible, and it was the obvious escape hatch. Rejected on two grounds:

1. **Project direction.** The repo owner has confirmed the project targets **Grafana 13+ and the v2 schema only**, and that no Classic export and no sub-13 support is required, ever. That decision also removed the four legacy classic-schema dashboards outright (see #394).
2. **A Classic copy would be actively misleading.** The v1 schema cannot express `conditionalRendering`. Every feature-gated tab and row — object store, node metrics, posture, webhooks, log streaming, traces, profiling, and the multi-tailnet scorecard — would render **permanently empty** instead of hiding itself. A published dashboard whose feature areas are blank on most tailnets is worse for a first-time user than no published dashboard, and it would generate exactly the "your dashboard is broken" reports the conditional rendering exists to prevent. The reference implementation in `rknightion/opnsense-exporter` reached the same conclusion and deliberately ships no v1 build.

**What replaces the distribution goal.** `deploy/grafana/tailscale2otel.json` stays the single source of truth in-repo, and `docs/dashboards.md` now documents the three import paths that do work for a v2 resource — `gcx resources push` (recommended), the Grafana UI importer, and file provisioning. It also warns about the two misleading version failures, because neither says "your Grafana is too old": **12.4 returns 200 and renders a blank dashboard**, and **11.5 rejects it with `Dashboard title cannot be empty`**.

**Reopen condition.** If Grafana adds v2 support to the community catalog, this becomes viable unchanged — the artifact is already versioned, has a stable UID, and resolves datasources through template variables rather than pinned UIDs, which were the other publication prerequisites.

`scripts/verify_deployment.py` — read-only, run against the current gcx context.

## Why this exists

**`gcx resources push` is additive.** It creates and updates; it never deletes. So a rule removed from this repo keeps evaluating on the stack indefinitely, firing against an expression nobody maintains, and nothing in the normal workflow ever tells you. That is the failure this catches.

## What it reports

| finding | meaning | fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **missing** | in the repo, not on the stack | `gcx resources push -p deploy/alerts/grafana-managed` |
| **orphaned** | on the stack, deleted from the repo | delete by hand — push will not remove it |
| **drifted** | same name, different behaviour | push re-applies the repo definition |

Drift compares only behaviour-bearing fields — `title`, `noDataState`, `execErrState`, `for`, `paused`, `labels`. Grafana adds server-side fields (uid, version, timestamps, provenance) that differ on every pull; comparing those would report everything as permanently drifted, which is the same as reporting nothing.

Exit `0` match / `1` drift / `2` cannot reach Grafana.

## Read-only, and sanitized

It never pushes and never mutates — deployment stays an explicit operator action. Only rule **names, counts and field names** reach stdout; expressions, annotations, datasource UIDs and folder UIDs never do, so the output is safe to paste into an issue. The pulled resources go to a temp dir that is deleted unless `--keep` is passed, and `--keep` writes the sanitized comparison, not the raw pull.

## It found real drift on its first live run

Against the `m7kni` stack (Grafana 13.2.0):

```
shipped      : 120 rules (81 paused)
deployed     : 78 rules (43 paused)
missing      : 43
orphaned     : 1   - ts2o-api-auth-failing
drifted      : 77
```

Two things worth acting on:

1. **`ts2o-api-auth-failing` is orphaned** — a rule from an earlier release, still evaluating, no longer in this repo. Exactly the case above: push will never remove it.
2. **77 rules differ on `execErrState`.** The deployed copies still carry the old global fail-open value, so **a query error is still being read as OK on the live stack** — long after #388 replaced that with per-rule policy in `e54a4cd`. The fix shipped to the repo months of commits ago and was never deployed, and nothing would have surfaced that.

That second one is the argument for this issue existing: a correctness fix that lands in git but never reaches the stack is indistinguishable, from the repo side, from one that is working.

**Nothing was pushed.** Deploying is the operator call.

## Not implemented

Canary panel/rule queries over a bounded live window, and sanitized snapshot rendering, are not included. Both need a live datasource query path and, for snapshots, the image renderer — which `deploy/grafana/README.md` already records cannot reliably screenshot the dense tabs (see #396, where requirement 4 was declined for the same reason). Rule-definition drift is the part that is both reliable and where the real silent failure lives; adding a flaky live-query step would undermine the check that works.

title: Add post-deployment dashboard/rule smoke verification

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-23`

comments.body:
Closed by `e54a4cd` and `9a3674c`.

The issue's framing was right but its example was sharper than stated: `docs/alerts.md:35` said *"organised into four groups"* **directly above a list of five**. The file contradicted itself, not just the code — a stronger argument for generating the counts than the issue makes.

What landed:

- **`tools/promqlcheck`** (new module) parses every expression in the dashboard and every rule manifest with the real `prometheus/promql/parser`, after substituting Grafana templating tokens **by position** (a variable inside a string literal becomes `.*`, one alone in a range selector becomes a duration, one used as a number becomes `1`). It also fails on a reference to a template variable the dashboard does not declare — a typo class no name-existence or regex check can see. Currently 548 PromQL expressions, 0 failures. Mutation-tested against the real artifact.
- **LogQL and TraceQL are not parsed, loudly.** Importing Loki's parser resolves **583 modules** and then does not compile — its `go.mod` carries `replace` directives that do not apply to consumers, so `dskit/kv/memberlist` fails against the memberlist version a downstream module resolves. Verified, not assumed. Those 26 expressions are counted and reported in a dedicated `NOT PARSED` block on every run, and still get the variable check. A silent skip would let a green run read as full coverage.
- **Execution against synthetic fixtures.** `promtool test rules` over fixtures covering `absent()` coverage, a counter reset across a restart, multi-tailnet label preservation, per-target and per-collector isolation, and healthy-zero versus absent on a feature probe. Since the shipped rules are Grafana-managed manifests promtool cannot read, the generator re-renders the catalogue as a **test-only** Prometheus file, never committed.
- **The Python generator suites ran nowhere.** `test_ingest_freshness.py` passed locally and was referenced by nothing — not CI, not the regen script, not the pre-commit hook. Now wired, with a guards-the-guard test because `unittest discover` over a directory with no test module exits 0.

These fixtures immediately earned their keep: removing the `> 0` lower bound from the key-expiry rule makes every long-dead device alert forever as "expiring soon", and the fixture catches it. Parsing proves an expression is well-formed; only execution proves it fires.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-22`

comments.body:
Done in `623240e`. Closed by that commit.

Five canonical recording rules, **12 -> 20** total.

| metric | dimension kept | ships |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tailscale:devices_unauthorized:count` | `tailscale_tailnet` | **enabled** |
| `tailscale2otel:export:success_ratio` | `signal` | paused |
| `tailscale2otel:scrape_freshness:seconds` | `tailscale_collector` | paused |
| `tailscale2otel:objectstore_backlog:max` | none (aggregated) | paused |
| `tailscale:direct_path:byte_fraction` | none (aggregated) | paused |

(#398 added three more — the SLI recordings — in the same commit.)

## On "preserve tailnet, provider and instance dimensions deliberately"

Taken as an instruction to make each choice explicitly and write down the reason, so every one of the five carries its rationale in the rule description:

- **`devices_unauthorized` keeps `tailscale_tailnet`.** On a multi-tailnet/MSP deployment a summed count hides *which* tailnet holds the unapproved device, which is the only actionable part of the number.
- **`export:success_ratio` keeps `signal`.** A backend can accept metrics while rejecting logs; one blended number averages that away. This is the per-signal diagnostic view, and #398 deliberately added a *separate* aggregate delivery SLI rather than reusing it — different questions.
- **`scrape_freshness` keeps `tailscale_collector`.** Bounded (~15) and useless aggregated: "something is stale" is only actionable once it names the collector.
- The other two are fully aggregated because no label is meaningful, and the descriptions say that rather than leaving it looking like an oversight.

No `instance` dimension anywhere — it would resolve empty under OTLP push, per the standing decision.

## The raw+rollup double-count test

Added, and it is more specific than "does not double-count". `ts2o-rec-flow-throughput` is `sum(rate(rollup)) or sum(rate(raw))` — `or` is a **fall back to raw when rollup is absent**, whereas `+` would double-count wherever both exist. The test asserts any recording rule referencing both metrics splits on exactly one ` or `, with rollup on the left and raw on the right. Negative-tested by swapping `or` for `+`.

## Refactor rather than a second copy

`_derp_byte_fraction` was generalised to `_path_byte_fraction(path)`, so the new direct-path fraction is the **same construction** instead of a second hand-written expression that could drift. That construction matters: it unions the two directions with `label_replace(...) or label_replace(...)` rather than `rate(in) + rate(out)`, because the latter is a one-to-one join that silently drops any node present in only one direction. A test asserts both the delegation and the union survive; the shipped DERP expression came out **byte-identical**, verified against the committed manifest before anything else was changed.

## New gate this issue made necessary

`record()` defaults to `paused=True`. Once an alert *consumes* a recorded metric — `ts2o-devices-unauthorized` reads `tailscale:devices_unauthorized:count` — a paused recording means the alert has no series at all, and under `optional` policy (`noDataState: Ok`) it is silently dead forever while every offline check passes. There is now a test asserting **every recording rule whose metric name appears in any alert expression is not paused**, derived from the catalogue rather than a hard-coded list. Negative-tested by pausing `ts2o-rec-sli-delivery`.

title: Expand and reuse canonical recording rules

comments.body:
### Dashboard half done in `9a3674c` — alert half still open

New **Receiver loss & rejections** row on Exporter Diagnostics, plus additions to the gated rDNS row and a node-metrics name-budget row on Cardinality & Cost. Covers `rdns.cache.overflows`, `stream.skipped`, `webhook.request.duration`, `webhook.duplicates`, `webhook.schema_drift`, `network.store.dropped` and `nodemetrics.metric_names.dropped`.

**The issue's "pair counters with accepted volume so rates have context" is enforced by test** — each loss counter must share a panel with its accepted-volume series. A bare "12 dropped" is unreadable without "of how many", and this is the assertion that keeps it that way.

One case where the pairing needed a judgement call: **there is no accepted-sample counter for forwarded node metrics** — the scraper forwards verbatim and counts nothing. The denominator used is `series_by_group{metric_group="other"}`, where uncataloged passthrough names bucket, and the panel description says exactly that rather than implying a true accepted count exists.

`webhook.schema_drift` was the last signal in the whole catalog still awaiting a curation decision; it now has a by-field/by-status panel whose description makes the failure mode explicit — a field moving to unknown status means Tailscale changed the payload shape, the receiver keeps accepting, nothing else goes red, and whatever that field feeds is quietly no longer populated.

**Remaining: the alerts**, with configuration-aware absence semantics — the receivers are off by default, so every one of these belongs on the `optional` evaluation policy (`noDataState: Ok`, `execErrState: Error`) rather than `core`.

Alert half done in `99c1226`. Closed by that commit.

Four rules, **all `optional`** — exactly as you called it on the dashboard half. The receivers, the rDNS cache and the node-metrics scraper are each off by default, so `noDataState: Ok` / `execErrState: Error` is the correct pair: absence means not configured, a datasource error is still a fault. That is the issue configuration-aware absence semantics.

| rule | signal | for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ts2o-rdns-cache-overflowing` | `rdns.cache.overflows` | 30m |
| `ts2o-stream-records-skipped` | `stream.skipped` by reason | 15m |
| `ts2o-webhook-schema-drift` | `webhook.schema_drift{status="unknown"}` by field | 15m |
| `ts2o-nodemetrics-name-budget` | `nodemetrics.metric_names.dropped` | 30m |

`ts2o-webhook-schema-drift` is the one worth the attention. It fires per field, and the description carries the failure mode you identified verbatim: a field moving to `unknown` means Tailscale changed the payload shape, the receiver keeps accepting, nothing else goes red, and whatever that field feeds is quietly no longer populated. That silence is the entire reason the rule exists.

Each description names the config key or the fix rather than asserting a cause — `enrichment.reverse_dns.max_entries`, `node_metrics.max_distinct_metrics`, the two documented stream skip reasons (`unclassified`, `unwrap_drop`).

## Two candidates deliberately NOT alerted

The issue says *add only actionable alerts*, and two of the signals covered by the dashboard half do not clear that bar:

- **`tailscale.network.store.dropped`** — it only trims the local in-memory flow view. OTLP emission is unaffected, so nothing is actually lost and there is no operator action. It stays a panel.
- **`tailscale.webhook.duplicates`** — a counted duplicate is the dedup failsafe doing its job.

There is now a **test asserting no rule queries either metric**, with the reasoning in its docstring. Without it, a future coverage pass reads two visualized-but-unalerted signals as a gap and adds two unactionable rules. The signal-disposition manifest agrees: both stay `visualized` only, and that is a decision rather than an omission.

`webhook.request.duration` is likewise left to the existing `ts2o-receiver-latency-high` rather than duplicated.

comments.body:
### Dashboard half done in `9a3674c` — alert half still open

New **API rate-limiter wait & probe freshness** row on Exporter Diagnostics, placed deliberately *after* the existing API-latency row and **not merged into it**:

- p50/p95/p99 wait by endpoint
- time waiting vs time on the wire (`rate_limit_wait_seconds_sum` vs `api_duration_seconds_sum` — disjoint budgets)
- share of requests actually delayed (`_count` over total requests; a request that waits zero is never recorded, so `_count` *is* the delayed population)
- API operation last-probe age

The issue's "keep rate-limiter wait separate from upstream API latency" is enforced by test, not just convention: one assertion checks the latency panel contains no `rate_limit_wait`, another that the wait panel contains no `api_duration_seconds`. They are different faults — wait means the poller is throttling *itself*, latency means the tailnet or network is slow — and charting them as one series makes the first look like the second.

**No recording rule added.** The issue says add one "if the histogram query is reused"; the quantile expression appears once, so a recording rule would add indirection for nothing. Revisit if #406 pulls it into more panels.

**Remaining: the tuned saturation alert/advisory** on sustained wait relative to collector intervals. It needs a baseline from real traffic to pick a threshold that is not arbitrary — the panels now exist to take that baseline from.

Alert half done in `99c1226`. Closed by that commit.

One rule: **`ts2o-api-rate-limit-wait-high`**, `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(tailscale2otel_api_rate_limit_wait_seconds_bucket[10m])))` > 5s for 30m, policy `advisory`, ships paused.

`advisory` rather than `optional` is the deliberate choice: the histogram only observes requests that actually waited — a request delayed zero seconds is never recorded — so absence is the healthy state, and a transient datasource error is not actionable at this severity either.

**The threshold is an explicit placeholder, and the description says so in those terms.** The issue is right that this needs a real baseline, and there is no honest way to pick 5s from first principles — a busy tailnet legitimately waits. Rather than defer the rule until a baseline exists, it ships paused with the tuning instruction attached: take a week from `Rate-limiter wait p50/p95/p99 by endpoint`, set the threshold above your own normal, then enable. The fix is also named: lengthen the intervals of the endpoints at the top of that panel, or raise the limit if the tailnet quota allows.

**Kept separate from upstream API latency**, per the issue, and now enforced by test in both directions:

- `ts2o-api-rate-limit-wait-high` must query `..._rate_limit_wait_seconds_bucket` and must contain no `api_duration_seconds`;
- `ts2o-api-rate-limited` (server-side HTTP 429) must still contain no `rate_limit_wait`.

Those are three distinct faults that look identical on a naive latency chart and have completely different fixes — client-side self-throttling, a server-side 429, and genuine upstream slowness. The `tailscale-api-health` runbook section gained that three-way distinction.

**Still no recording rule**, for the reason recorded on the dashboard half: the quantile expression appears in the panel and now in this rule, but with different aggregation (`by (le, endpoint)` vs `by (le)`), so a shared recorded series would serve neither well. Revisit if #406 pulls it into more places.

A promtool scenario executes the histogram with an explicit two-bucket layout so the quantile lands on an exact hand-verifiable value rather than an approximated one.

comments.body:
### Dashboard half done in `9a3674c` — alert half still open

Two new rows on **Node Metrics**: *Packet drops (raw tailscaled)* gated on `has_dropped`, and *Packet drops & peer relay (curated)* gated on `has_node_curated`. Covers `node.packets`, `node.peer_relay.packets`, `node.derp.home_region`, and drop-reason / transport / peer-relay-state breakdowns.

**The issue's "do not alert on ACL drops merely because they occur" is honoured in the rendering, not just deferred to the alert.** `Policy drops (ACL)` filters `tailscale_drop_reason="acl"` and carries **no thresholds and no red anywhere in its field config** — an ACL drop is the filter doing its job, and colouring it as a fault teaches operators to ignore the panel. `Error & malformed drops by reason` filters `!="acl"` and is the only one with an escalation threshold. `Drop share by reason` is a deliberately unthresholded ratio over offered packets that includes ACL purely as context. There is a test asserting the ACL panel is not red.

`has_dropped` was a **dead sentinel** — registered and querying Prometheus on every dashboard load while gating nothing. It now gates the raw drops row, which is exactly what it was named for.

Also fixed here: the same missing-`xField` bug as #391 on two path-mix barcharts.

**Remaining: the alerts** — sustained error/unknown drop states after baseline validation, and peer-relay state transitions. The issue is right that this needs a baseline first; the panels now exist to take one from, and the ACL/error separation means an alert can be written against the error population without a further query change.

Alert half done in `99c1226`. Closed by that commit.

Two rules, both `optional` (both need the node-metrics scraper, so both are absent and inert without it).

**`ts2o-node-error-drops`** selects `tailscale_drop_reason=~"error|unknown_protocol|other"` and **excludes `acl` by construction**. That is the issue requirement, and it is now enforced two ways rather than left to convention:

- a unit test asserts `"acl"` does not appear in the expression at all;
- a promtool scenario feeds a fast-incrementing `tailscale_drop_reason="acl"` series and asserts the alert does **not** fire, alongside a concurrent `error` series that does.

The second one is the real gate — it proves the exclusion under execution, not just in the source text. Negative-tested by relabelling the ACL series to `error` and confirming the "does not fire" case then fails.

`other` is included deliberately as the "unknown" arm the issue asks for: it is the fold bucket in `internal/semconv/attrs.go` for a reason tailscaled emits that this exporter does not recognise, so a tailscaled upgrade introducing a new reason surfaces here rather than vanishing.

**`ts2o-peer-relay-stuck`** covers the peer-relay side: `tailscale_peer_relay_state="connecting"` sustained for an hour. `connecting` is a transient state, so an endpoint that has not reached `open` after an hour is not going to, and traffic that expected that relay is falling back to DERP or not flowing. The third bounded state, `other`, is **not** alerted — that is version drift rather than a fault, so it stays visible on the panel only. Recorded in the rule description so it does not read as an oversight.

On the issue baseline point: both thresholds are `> 0` sustained rather than a rate threshold, which needs no baseline to be meaningful — a non-zero error/malformed drop rate held for 30m is a fault at any volume. The panels from the dashboard half are what a rate-based refinement would be tuned from if one is ever wanted.

Both link to `Error & malformed drops by reason` and `Peer-relay endpoints by state`, and the `node-client-health` runbook section gained the ACL-exclusion rationale and the bounded reason set.

Fleet aggregates plus bounded per-device drill-down for block-incoming, direct capability, endpoints, IPv6, UDP, multiple-connections, posture-identity, enabled routes and key-owner signals. New *Device security flags* row (7 stats) and *Connectivity detail (per device)* table, plus four connectivity coverage panels.

**Bounded, as the issue requires**: per-device panels sit in rows gated on presence and behind the existing `pii_perdevice` sentinel, and are bounded by the existing `$host_name` selector rather than `topk` — `topk` across a merged table would pick a different device set per column.

**Absence for unsupported providers is defined correctly.** No new query zero-fills. The five signals a control plane without the concept simply does not emit each carry a `novalue` naming the prerequisite or config key (`cardinality.per_entity.device`, `collect_connectivity`), and the per-device flags table states that a blank column means *not reported* — which is not the same as *reported off*. A test asserts no `vector(0)` and that each empty state names a config key or prerequisite.

Boolean polarity is explicit per flag: blocks-incoming / IPv6 / UDP / direct-capable are healthy-on, key-expiry-disabled / multiple-connections / posture-identity-disabled are healthy-off, SSH-enabled is neutral. Since #385, a value map disagreeing with its panel's thresholds **fails the build**.

Tightened during the wiring pass: the *Device security flags* row was ungated and so rendered seven empty-state panels wherever `cardinality.per_entity.device` is off — reading as "nothing to report" rather than "not collected". Now gated on a new `has_device_flags` sentinel.

**Remaining: alerts for actionable sustained posture states only** — not raw existence, per the issue. The three panels whose thresholds already encode an alertable sustained state are *Unauthorized (internal)*, *Key expiry disabled (fleet)* and *Multiple simultaneous connections*. Related: #410 (approval-workflow alerts) covers the unauthorized-device case and should be written together with this one so they do not double-page.

Alert half done in `99c1226`. Closed by that commit.

Two rules, both `optional`, both keyed on a **sustained** state rather than raw existence — which is what the issue asks for and is the whole design constraint here.

**`ts2o-device-key-expiry-disabled-new`** alerts on `max(delta(tailscale_devices_key_expiry_disabled_ratio[1h])) > 0`, not on the level. Alerting on the level would fire permanently on any tailnet with tag-owned servers, since disabling key expiry on a server is normal and correct. What is actionable is a *new* one appearing: that key has just become invisible to `ts2o-device-keys-expiring-7d` and `ts2o-device-key-expiring-critical`, and someone chose that. A unit test asserts the expression still uses `delta(`, and a promtool scenario proves a flat high count (40, held) does not fire while a step (40 -> 41) does. Negative-tested by swapping the flat series for a stepped one and confirming the healthy case then fails.

**`ts2o-device-multiple-connections`** alerts on `count(max by (host_id) (...) == 1) > 0` with `for: 1h`. The one-hour `for` is what makes this sustained rather than a transient re-auth overlap. The framing in the description is credential-sharing, not connectivity: the second client inherits the first tags and ACL grants, and the fix is to remove and re-authenticate the device.

**The unauthorized-device case is deliberately left to #410**, per your note that the two should be written together so they do not double-page. Nothing here touches it.

On the third candidate panel you listed, *Unauthorized (internal)* — same reasoning, it belongs to #410.

Both rules link to their canonical panels (`Key expiry disabled (fleet)`, `Multiple simultaneous connections`) and to the `credential-expiry` / `device-posture-coverage` runbook sections, which gained the delta-not-level and shared-node-key rationale respectively.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit compared the generated artifacts with the live Grafana deployment, rendered all five dashboards, inspected all 79 rules, and reconciled them with the 191-signal catalog.

## Finding and proposed scope

Priority: P1

- Compare poll, HEC, webhook, and object-store accepted rate, rejection rate, event delay, and durable backlog.
- Add source/signal recording rules that preserve tailnet identity.
- Make silence alertable only when a source is configured and expected to be active.
- Treat event-driven webhook silence as informational by default.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-16`

comments.body:
Done in `db37106`. Closed by that commit.

## Source/signal recording rules that preserve tailnet identity

Three new recordings (**20 -> 23**):

| metric | grouping |
| --- | --- |
| `tailscale2otel:ingest_records:rate5m` | `source, signal, tailscale_tailnet` |
| `tailscale2otel:ingest_rejected:rate5m` | `source, tailscale_tailnet` |
| `tailscale2otel:ingest_freshness:by_tailnet` | `source, signal, tailscale_tailnet` |

`tailscale.tailnet` is a **provider-scoped const attribute appended to every emitted metric** (`internal/telemetry/emitter.go`), so it was available all along — the flagship ingest panels simply aggregated it away. On a multi-tailnet/MSP deployment that aggregation is the bug: "ingest is healthy" across five tailnets hides the one that has gone silent. Grouping by an absent label is harmless, so these still work when an operator has disabled the tailnet attribute category.

The existing `tailscale2otel:ingest_event_freshness_seconds` is kept as the **fleet-wide** view rather than modified — the aggregate is what an SLO should burn against, and the per-tailnet split answers a different question. Same reasoning as #406 keeping a per-signal export ratio alongside #398 aggregate delivery SLI.

## The cross-source comparison that was actually missing

Most of what this issue asks for already existed: `Ingest records/s by source+signal`, `Ingest decoded bytes/s by source`, `Accepted event freshness`, `Accepted event age p95`, `Capture delay p95`. Accepted rate and event delay were already comparable across poll, HEC, webhook and object store.

**Rejection rate was not.** The three paths count rejections under three differently-named metrics (`tailscale_stream_rejected_total`, `tailscale_webhook_rejected_total`, `tailscale2otel_objectstore_skipped_total`) and could not be read on one axis. New panel **`Rejected/s by ingestion source`** on the Ingestion volume row unifies them:

```promql
sum by (source) (
  label_replace(rate(tailscale_stream_rejected_total[$__rate_interval]), "source", "stream", "", "") or
  label_replace(rate(tailscale_webhook_rejected_total[$__rate_interval]), "source", "webhook", "", "") or
  label_replace(rate(tailscale2otel_objectstore_skipped_total[$__rate_interval]), "source", "objectstore", "", "")
)
```

`label_replace` + `or`, **not** `+`. Addition is a one-to-one join that silently drops any source present in only one operand, which is the *normal* case here because each receiver is independently optional. Same construction as the path-fraction helper, for the same reason.

The panel description records that object-store contributes skipped-object counts including per-cycle budget skips, so it should be read alongside the by-reason breakdown rather than as pure loss.

**Durable backlog** is deliberately not duplicated into this row: object store is the only source that has one, so a cross-source comparison of it would be degenerate. It stays on its own Exporter Diagnostics row (`Backlog & oldest pending object age`, `Unresolved gaps & oldest gap age`), added under #399.

## The two alerting requirements were already satisfied

Validated rather than re-implemented:

- **"Make silence alertable only when a source is configured and expected to be active."** `ts2o-ingest-data-stale` ships **paused**, on `optional` policy, and its description already says to enable it only for source/signal pairs expected to deliver continuously, with label filters or a tuned threshold for that workload. Firing it on everything produces noise, not coverage.
- **"Treat event-driven webhook silence as informational by default."** Nothing alerts on webhook silence by default — the only rule that could is the paused one above, and the webhook receiver is off by default so its series are absent anyway.

Recording this as verified so a future pass does not "fix" it by enabling a rule that should stay paused.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit compared the generated artifacts with the live Grafana deployment, rendered all five dashboards, inspected all 79 rules, and reconciled them with the 191-signal catalog.

## Finding and proposed scope

Priority: P1

- Cover listing truncation, cursor age, newest discovered age, pending/failed objects, oldest gap, backfill progress, request/decode failures, and resource budgets.
- Alert on growing/stuck backlog and failed objects aging toward permanent loss.
- Keep object keys, locations, and credentials out of labels/annotations.
- Depend on corrected cursor/failure telemetry rather than building rules on misleading current gauges.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-15`

comments.body:
## Incoming dependency from #478: two corrected signals and one new reason

Recording this here so this child inherits the corrected object-store telemetry rather than encoding the older, misleading shape. All three items are already on `main`.

**1. New closed reason `undecodable_object` on `tailscale2otel.objectstore.skipped`** — delivered by #497 (`4f670ab`). It counts whole objects that decoded no record at all while at least one row failed, which is the signature of an export whose framing is not newline-delimited records. This is the single most valuable object-store alert available: before #497 such an object was recorded as successfully ingested with `gap.healthy=1`, so an entire feed could be discarded silently. **Any non-zero value means a broken feed, not corrupt data**, so it warrants an alert rather than only a panel, and the alert text should say to treat it as a feed-level fault.

Note a reading subtlety when designing panels: for a failed object the row-local `decode_error` / `semantic_invalid` reasons are deliberately *not* emitted, so the all-rows-fail case shows as one `undecodable_object` rather than N `decode_error`.

**2. `tailscale2otel.ingest.size` changed meaning for `source="objectstore"`** — delivered by #450 (`cc6e498`). It is now decompressed/decoded payload bytes for every source that emits it, so a cross-source sum is finally meaningful. Previously object-store fed compressed wire bytes into the same metric that stream and webhook fed decompressed bytes into. The flagship panel was retitled "Ingest decoded bytes/s by source" accordingly. `tailscale2otel.objectstore.bytes` remains compressed bytes read (including failed attempts) and `objectstore.decompressed.bytes` remains the expansion view — use those two for transfer cost and expansion, not `ingest.size`.

**3. `objectstore` is now a documented value of the `source` attribute** on both `ingest.records` and `ingest.size`, guarded by a catalog/emit-site parity test.

**Still to come before this child should finalise its panels:** #451 adds provider request count/duration/outcome, object-level retry count, cursor age, newest-discovered-object age and oldest-pending-object age. Its frozen descriptor table is on that issue. Two corrections recorded there are relevant to panel design: `objectstore.scan.truncated` already exists (delivered by #285) so it needs no new metric, and there is no transport-level retry in `internal/s3` at all — the retry concept is object-level via the durable gap mechanism from #286.

Per the tracker sequencing, this child should consume #450 at minimum and preferably #451, and must not encode the pre-#450 byte semantics.

### Dashboard half done in `9a3674c` — alert half still open

All 17 object-store signals are now visualized; this was the single largest blind spot the #390 disposition manifest found (the entire S3 ingestion path had zero surface). Two new rows on **Exporter Diagnostics**:

**Ingestion freshness** — cursor age, newest-exported-object age, gaps-clear, listing-complete, backlog + oldest *pending* age, unresolved gaps + oldest *gap* age.
**Throughput & faults** — objects/records per second, bytes read vs decompressed, retries, skipped-by-reason, undecodable objects, expansion limit failures, provider requests and latency by operation and outcome.

The corrections from your earlier comment are all encoded, not just noted:

- **`undecodable_object`** has its own panel with green/red at 1 and text saying **any non-zero is a feed-level fault, not corrupt data** — plus the reading subtlety that a wholly-failed object emits *one* `undecodable_object` rather than N `decode_error`.
- **`-1` on `discovered.newest.age` is value-mapped** to "no timestamped object listed", so the sentinel never renders as a negative age. There is a test for that mapping specifically.
- **`ingest.size` is not used for transfer cost.** The bytes panel uses `objectstore.bytes` (compressed, including failed attempts) and `objectstore.decompressed.bytes`, with the post-#450 meaning of `ingest.size` recorded in the description.
- **`gap.oldest.age` vs `pending.oldest.age`** are on separate panels, each stating that one ages *failed* objects and the other objects merely *not yet ingested* — and that a gap aging while the count holds means repeated failure, not recovery.
- **`objectstore.retries` is described as object-level via the durable gap mechanism**, with no transport-level retry in `internal/s3`.
- `scan.truncated` gets an inverse-risk map, and the backlog/pending panels state both are lower bounds while listing is truncated.

A test asserts every `by (...)` on an object-store series groups only by `{reason, limit, operation, outcome, le}` — nothing derived from an object key, bucket, prefix, endpoint or credential can reach a label.

**Remaining: the alerts.** Four candidates, in priority order:
1. `increase(objectstore_skipped_total{reason="undecodable_object"}) > 0` — the strongest alert available here, since any non-zero means a broken feed.
2. `gap.oldest.age` aging toward permanent loss.
3. `discovered.newest.age` above threshold **or `== -1`** — the `-1` disjunct is mandatory or the no-discovery case is silently excluded.
4. Growing/stuck backlog.

Every one of them now has a canonical panel to link to via `__dashboardUid__`/`__panelId__`.

Alert half done in `99c1226`. Closed by that commit.

Four rules, all `optional` — the object-store path is off by default, so every series is legitimately absent and absence is not a fault.

| rule | expression shape | for | ships |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ts2o-objectstore-undecodable` | `increase(objectstore_skipped_total{reason="undecodable_object"}[15m]) > 0` | 5m | **enabled** |
| `ts2o-objectstore-gap-aging` | `gap.oldest.age > 24h` | 30m | paused |
| `ts2o-objectstore-export-stale` | `discovered.newest.age > 1h` **or `== -1`** | 30m | paused |
| `ts2o-objectstore-backlog-stuck` | `min_over_time(backlog[1h]) > 0` | 30m | paused |

Your priority order from the dashboard comment is exactly the order these were written in, and the three corrections you recorded are encoded rather than noted:

- **`undecodable_object` ships ENABLED.** It is the only one of the four that does. The reasoning is the one you gave: any non-zero means a broken feed, and the whole path is absent unless configured, so an enabled rule is inert for everyone not using it. The description carries the reading subtlety too — a wholly-failed object emits *one* `undecodable_object`, not N `decode_error`, so the count understates the volume lost.
- **The `-1` disjunct is mandatory and is now enforced by two independent tests.** The expression folds the sentinel to +86400 so one threshold covers both arms:
  ```
  max(clamp_min(last_over_time(...[10m]), 0)
      + 86400 * (last_over_time(...[10m]) == bool -1))
  ```
  A unit test asserts both the `clamp_min(` arm and the `== bool -1` arm survive — a test that only checked the metric name would not catch someone "simplifying" this. A promtool scenario then *executes* a series pinned at `-1` and asserts it fires. That scenario was negative-tested: flipping it to `exp_alerts: []` fails with the alert firing at 35m.
- **`gap.oldest.age` and `pending.oldest.age` are kept distinct** in both the rule descriptions and the new runbook section, including the point that a gap aging while the count holds means repeated failure, not recovery.

`ts2o-objectstore-backlog-stuck` uses `min_over_time` rather than a level or a derivative: if the backlog ever reached zero in the window the minimum is zero and it cannot fire, so a busy bucket that keeps catching up stays quiet. Negative-tested by removing the drain-to-zero segment from the healthy fixture and confirming it then fires.

New runbook section `## Object-store ingestion {#object-store-ingestion}` backs all four, and all four carry `__dashboardUid__`/`__panelId__` links to the panels from the dashboard half.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit compared the generated artifacts with the live Grafana deployment, rendered all five dashboards, inspected all 79 rules, and reconciled them with the 191-signal catalog.

## Finding and proposed scope

Priority: P2

- Define exporter availability separately from collector freshness and backend delivery.
- Add canonical recording rules for successful collection, freshness, and export outcomes.
- Provide optional multi-window burn-rate alerts with no-data semantics.
- Keep backend outage from being mislabeled as tailnet operational failure.
- Document when the SLO is meaningful for pull, push, and mixed export modes.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-14`

comments.body:
Done in `623240e`. Closed by that commit.

Three SLI recording rules + four multi-window burn-rate alerts, plus a new `## SLO burn rate {#slo-burn-rate}` runbook section.

## The three SLIs are separate, and that is the deliverable

| SLI | metric | target | means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| availability | `tailscale2otel:sli_availability:ratio` | 99.9% | the exporter is running |
| freshness | `tailscale2otel:sli_freshness:ratio` | 99% | collection is current |
| delivery | `tailscale2otel:sli_delivery:ratio` | 99% | the **backend** is accepting |

> Keep backend outage from being mislabeled as tailnet operational failure.

This is the requirement everything else hangs off. A Grafana Cloud outage drives delivery to zero while the exporter is healthy and the tailnet is untouched — a single blended SLO reports that as "the exporter is failing" and pages the wrong people. So `ts2o-slo-delivery-fast-burn` states in its description, in those words, that it is a **backend fault, not a tailnet fault, and must not be routed to tailnet owners**. A test asserts the three SLIs have three distinct expressions and that the delivery alert references only the delivery SLI — negative-tested by blending availability into it.

## The four alerts

| rule | windows | burn | severity | policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ts2o-slo-availability-fast-burn` | 5m + 1h | 14.4x | critical | `core` |
| `ts2o-slo-availability-slow-burn` | 30m + 6h | 6x | warning | `core` |
| `ts2o-slo-freshness-fast-burn` | 5m + 1h | 14.4x | warning | `core` |
| `ts2o-slo-delivery-fast-burn` | 5m + 1h | 14.4x | warning | `optional` |

**No-data semantics** are the policy split, not an afterthought. Availability and freshness are `core` because their SLIs are emitted by any running exporter and ship enabled — absence is genuinely abnormal and must surface as NoData rather than silence. Delivery is `optional` because `export.duration` is legitimately absent under the stdout exporter or an idle pipeline.

## One implementation detail that would silently rot

The burn expression is a **product of two `> bool` comparisons**, not `and`:

```
(1 - avg_over_time(SLI[5m]) > bool 0.0144) * (1 - avg_over_time(SLI[1h]) > bool 0.0144)
```

`a and b` returns **a value**, so a rule written that way would have its threshold depend on the magnitude of the short-window error rate rather than on the two windows agreeing — which is the entire point of a multi-window alert. A test asserts each rule has exactly two `> bool`, no ` and `, one SLI, and two distinct window durations. Negative-tested by rewriting `_burn` with `and`.

The strongest fixture proves the multi-window requirement under execution: a **brief blip that breaches the 5m window but not the 1h window does NOT fire** (avg 0.9 over 5m -> 0.10 error, vs avg 0.99167 over 1h -> 0.008 error), while a sustained outage breaching both does. If a window were ever dropped, that scenario is what catches it. Negative-tested.

## Correction to my own working assumption

I had assumed one of ten collectors failing (10% error) would breach the 14.4x freshness threshold. **It does not** — 0.10 < 0.144. The fixture uses two of ten. Worth recording because the arithmetic is not intuitive: a 14.4x burn on a 99% target needs a 14.4% error rate, not "any meaningful degradation".

## Meaningful for pull, push and mixed export modes

Documented in the runbook section rather than only here: availability and freshness are export-mode-independent, delivery only exists on the push path — under `otlp.protocol: stdout` or a pull-only deployment the delivery SLI is legitimately absent, which is why it is `optional` rather than `core`.

## Operational trap, recorded in the runbook

All four alerts query recorded metrics, so the three SLI recordings **ship enabled**. If someone pauses them the burn-rate alerts get no series and go silently dead. That is now enforced by the paused-recording gate added under #406.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit compared the generated artifacts with the live Grafana deployment, rendered all five dashboards, inspected all 79 rules, and reconciled them with the 191-signal catalog.

## Finding and proposed scope

Priority: P3 research

- Measure datasource requests, query duration, browser memory, and render time per tab.
- Verify whether hidden tabs issue queries in the target Grafana version.
- Introduce recording rules, query sharing, or lazy tab loading only where measurement justifies it.
- Set an explicit performance budget and retain visual/function coverage.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Record the evidence, decision, rejected alternatives, and follow-up implementation slices; closing as unsupported is valid when the evidence does not justify a feature.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-13`

comments.body:
Done in `ea53c30`. Closed by that commit — with an explicit boundary between what was measured and what was not.

## Premise correction

The title says **298 panels**. It is **405**, across **484 queries**, with **58 presence variables**.

| tab | panels | queries |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exporter Diagnostics | 83 | 108 |
| Fleet & Devices | 59 | 73 |
| Security & Audit | 49 | 57 |
| Policy & Config | 47 | 56 |
| Events & Logs | 43 | 54 |
| Node Metrics | 35 | 35 |
| Overview | 34 | 37 |
| Network & Flows | 32 | 33 |
| Cardinality & Cost | 20 | 26 |
| Tailnets | 3 | 5 |

## The finding that matters

**58 presence variables are query variables, so they run on EVERY dashboard load regardless of which tab is open.** No amount of tab lazy-loading amortises them away — they are the dashboard fixed admission cost, and they are the number to watch, not the 484.

Put concretely: opening the default Overview tab costs roughly 58 variable queries + 37 panel queries. The 484 figure is only reachable if hidden tabs also query, which is the open question below.

## Explicit performance budget

`deploy/grafana/gen/test_query_budget.py` gates panels/queries in total and per tab, and the sentinel count separately. Budgets are set with headroom on purpose — a gate that fails on the next single panel is a gate people delete. Exceeding one requires raising the number **in a commit that says why**, which is the record this issue asks for. Negative-tested: dropping the sentinel budget below the real count makes it fail, naming the count and the budget.

The suite also guards itself — a walker that silently returned nothing would make every budget pass vacuously, so there is an assertion that the measurement found a real dashboard.

## What is NOT claimed

This is a static measurement. It does **not** measure datasource request duration, browser memory or render time, and I am not going to imply otherwise.

**The "do hidden tabs issue queries" question is unresolved and is the single most consequential unknown** — the answer changes real load roughly fivefold. It is a live Grafana behaviour question (target confirmed as **13.2.0** on the `m7kni` stack) that cannot be answered offline. I checked current Grafana documentation for it rather than guessing; the docs do not state the lazy-loading behaviour for v2 `TabsLayout`. Answering it needs browser devtools against a real stack: open the dashboard, count `/api/ds/query` requests before and after switching tabs.

## No optimisation applied, deliberately

The issue says to introduce recording rules, query sharing or lazy loading **only where measurement justifies it**. No offline measurement justifies any of them yet. The obvious lever if the live measurement shows the sentinels dominate is reducing the 58 — several gate rows that could share one variable — but that is a change with real behavioural risk (a shared sentinel hides a row for the wrong reason) and it should not be made on speculation.

23 recording rules already exist to precompute the heaviest expressions (#406, #398), so the "add recording rules" lever has partly been pulled already, for correctness reasons rather than performance ones.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit compared the generated artifacts with the live Grafana deployment, rendered all five dashboards, inspected all 79 rules, and reconciled them with the 191-signal catalog.

## Finding and proposed scope

Priority: P2

- Audit color meaning for color-vision deficiency and dark/light themes.
- Standardize units, decimal precision, thresholds, legends, and table density.
- Ensure panel descriptions communicate metric caveats and missing-state behavior.
- Render representative tabs at desktop and narrow widths in CI.
- Add screenshot/structural regression checks for high-risk panels without freezing every pixel.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-12`

comments.body:
Done in `ea53c30`. Closed by that commit. Four of the five requirements are implemented; the fifth is deliberately not, with evidence.

Four new gate modules, **149 tests** in the dashboard suite (was 94).

## 1. Colour meaning, CVD and themes — `test_cvd_and_palette.py`

Colour is never the sole carrier of meaning: every boolean 0/1 value map must carry **non-empty, mutually distinct text for both states**, so a red/green distinction survives greyscale and deuteranopia. The palette in use is derived from the generator, frozen to the named Grafana set (`red`/`green`/`yellow`/`orange`/`text`) and asserted — **no raw hex anywhere**, which is what keeps it theme-adaptive, since named colours resolve per theme while a hex value does not.

This complements the existing `check_bool_polarity` build failure from #385 rather than duplicating it: that one asserts polarity is *correct*, this one asserts the state is *readable without colour*.

## 2. Units, precision, legends, density — `test_unit_consistency.py`

Expected units are **derived, not listed**, from two sources: the OTLP→Prometheus suffix contract in the root `CLAUDE.md` (`_seconds`→`s`, `_bytes`→byte units, `_days`→`d`) and `docs/metrics.md` own descriptions, which distinguish a genuine `[0,1]` fraction from a plain integer count that merely gained `_ratio` under the unit-`"1"` rule. That distinction is the subtle one — `tailscale_devices_count_ratio` is a **count**, and rendering it `percentunit` would be nonsense.

The check accounts for per-series `fieldConfig.overrides`, `count()`-wrapped and boolean-selection queries, and division-derived ratios, so genuinely multi-unit panels are not false-flagged. Three near-misses (`Goroutines & stack`, the two object-store age/count pairs) turned out to already be correct via `byName` overrides once those were accounted for — reported as correct rather than "fixed".

No unit or polarity defects found. The gates were negative-tested to prove that is a real result and not a vacuous pass.

## 3. Descriptions communicate caveats and missing-state behaviour — `test_panel_descriptions.py`

Population derived structurally: every panel inside a row gated by `present=`/`hide_when=`, or by its enclosing tab gate. Requires a **real** description (>=20 chars), not merely non-empty — a "non-empty" assertion passes vacuously on a single character.

**Found 69 panels inside gated rows with no description at all**, across fleet, network, events, security, policy, nodemetrics and diagnostics. All fixed.

## 5. Structural regression without freezing pixels — `test_panel_fingerprints.py`

A golden fingerprint per high-risk panel: viz type, unit, threshold steps, boolean mapping polarity, and queried metric names. **Explicitly excludes panel ids and grid positions**, so it survives the renumbering that inserting any panel causes — which matters here, since ids shift constantly and a fingerprint including them would be pure noise.

13 panels chosen deliberately, justified in the module docstring:
- inverse-risk pairs (SSH wildcard x2, update-available, delivery-error, the object-store gap/truncation pair) — where a polarity flip renders danger as safe
- the flagship security-scorecard counts
- healthy-polarity liveness flags (`Config valid`, `Exporter up`, `Discovery OK`) — included specifically so a systematic "flip every boolean" bug cannot hide by breaking only the inverse-risk half
- two compliance tables (PII filter status, OAuth scope preflight), which colour table cells through a different code path than stats

Negative-tested against the **real** generator, not just synthetically: moving `Auto-approved exit nodes` threshold from 3 to 10 makes the fingerprint fail, then reverted.

## 4. Render tabs in CI — deliberately NOT implemented

`deploy/grafana/README.md` already records the blocker, and it predates this issue:

> static PNG rendering of dense, variable-heavy tabs (Fleet, Policy, Node Metrics) can show "No data" because the renderer screenshots before all queries resolve — this is a renderer limitation, not a dashboard defect.

Rendering needs a live Grafana 13+ instance plus the image-renderer plugin. In CI that means either secrets and a live stack (against this repo posture of keeping live-tenant access out of PR-time CI) or a job that silently no-ops. Worse, on exactly the dense tabs most worth checking it produces **false failures** — a gate that cries wolf on the tabs you care about gets disabled, and then requirements 1/2/3/5 lose their home too.

Recommendation: keep `gcx dashboards snapshot --tab "..."` as a manual visual-review step for PRs that materially change layout, not a CI gate. Recorded here so it is not re-attempted without new information.

Every gate negative-tested — 15 cases in total, each broken, confirmed to fail for the right reason, and restored.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit compared the generated artifacts with the live Grafana deployment, rendered all five dashboards, inspected all 79 rules, and reconciled them with the 191-signal catalog.

## Finding and proposed scope

Priority: P2

- For optional collectors/features, state the exact config key and required source/scope.
- Distinguish disabled, unsupported, permission-denied, idle, and genuinely empty where the signals permit it.
- Avoid presenting an absent check as a healthy zero.
- Add generator-level empty-state text tests.
- Cover object store, node metrics, posture, webhooks, log streaming, traces, and profiling.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-11`

comments.body:
Done in `db37106`. Closed by that commit.

## The defect this found

Three panels on the flagship **Security scorecard** rendered a green `0` when their data was never collected.

The row is gated on `has_acl_risk`, which proves the **acl** collector is running. But these three are fed by the **devices** collector, and all three zero-filled with `or vector(0)`:

| panel | metric | collector |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Untagged devices` | `tailscale_devices_untagged_ratio` | devices |
| `Unapproved subnet routes` | `tailscale_subnet_routes_unapproved` | devices |
| `Pending exit-node shares` | `tailscale_device_invites_count_ratio` | devices |

Run the ACL collector without devices and the scorecard says **"Untagged devices: 0"** — which reads as "every device is tagged" when the truth is "nothing was ever checked". That is precisely the issue bullet *avoid presenting an absent check as a healthy zero*, and because these are security checks a false pass is the worst available failure mode.

Fixed by dropping the zero-fill and adding an empty state naming the prerequisite collector and its config key (`collectors.devices`, `collectors.devices.collect_device_invites`), verified against `config.example.yaml` rather than guessed.

## The contract: collector identity, not metric-name identity

My first pass flagged 23 panels, then 12. **Both were wrong**, and the reason matters: two metrics emitted by the *same* collector always co-exist, so a differing metric name is not by itself a problem. Checking each candidate against `internal/collector/` narrowed it to the three genuine cross-collector cases above.

Four superficially identical cases were checked and **deliberately left alone** — changing them would be a regression:

- `Exit nodes` row: `has_exit` is a devices metric and `Unapproved subnet routes` is a devices metric. Same collector, honest zero.
- `Service health` / `App health`: gated on `has_selfobs`; `Scrape budget (max)` and `Config warnings` are self-observability too, always emitted together.
- `Key-expiry distribution` / `Keys already expired`: both devices.
- `Security scorecard`s own acl-fed panels (`Unrestricted ACL rules`, `Auto-approved exit nodes`, `SSH wildcard enabled`): same collector as the sentinel.
- Every **label-filtered subset** query (`{tailscale_exit_node_state="advertised"}`): when the collector runs and there are none of that kind, the series genuinely does not exist and `0` is the correct answer.

## Generator-level empty-state tests

New `deploy/grafana/gen/test_empty_state_contract.py`, 23 tests, **94 total in the suite**.

Collector ownership is **derived, not hand-listed**, from two things already in the tree: the dotted OTEL name literals in `internal/collector/<dir>/*.go`, and the dotted/Prometheus name pairing in the generated `docs/metrics.md` tables (with histogram `_bucket`/`_count`/`_sum` suffix handling). A metric emitted by zero or several collectors buckets as `shared` and never gates a check — which is *why* the self-obs rows stay silent, rather than an exception list. A new panel dropped into a mismatched row is caught with nobody maintaining anything.

The gate was verified against the pre-fix tree and named exactly the three offenders, with the owning and gating collectors attributed:
```
(Unapproved subnet routes, Security scorecard, [has_acl_risk], tailscale_subnet_routes_unapproved, devices, [acl])
(Untagged devices,         Security scorecard, [has_acl_risk], tailscale_devices_untagged_ratio,   devices, [acl])
(Pending exit-node shares, Security scorecard, [has_acl_risk], tailscale_device_invites_count_ratio, devices, [acl])
```

## A pre-existing defect the global check exposed

Making the empty-state text rules **global** rather than scoped to hand-listed panels found one no existing test could see: the Cardinality tab `Series limit` panel said *"...or exporter self-observability is off"* — asserting a cause that presence cannot distinguish from *unsupported* or *never-deployed*. Reworded to name the prerequisite without claiming why it is missing. Enforcement is now unconditional, with no carve-outs.

## Coverage of the listed feature areas

Object store, posture, webhooks and log streaming already had empty states. **`nodemetrics` and `tailnets` were checked and have no violations** — every nodemetrics row is gated by a nodemetrics-collector sentinel (same collector throughout), and the tailnets tab gates at *tab* level with no row-level sentinels and no zero-fills at all. Recorded as a verified negative rather than left ambiguous.

Traces and profiling have no dashboard panels to gate.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-10`

comments.body:
Closed by `9a3674c`.

**Decision: the flagship is the only supported dashboard. The four legacy classic-schema dashboards are deleted.**

`tailscale-fleet.json`, `tailscale-network.json`, `tailscale-audit-events.json` and `tailscale-exporter-health.json` are gone. They were hand-maintained `schemaVersion: 39` JSON, duplicated content the flagship already covers, and were **excluded from `scripts/regen-generated.sh` and the `dashboards-drift` gate** — which is precisely why they rotted unnoticed. Nothing regenerated them, nothing tested them, and nothing noticed when they drifted.

The issue's acceptance criteria are met by removal rather than by lifecycle management, because the underlying question was settled by a product decision from the repo owner: **tailscale2otel targets Grafana 13+ and the v2 schema only, and will never ship a Classic export.** Given that, maintaining four Classic dashboards was maintaining artifacts for a configuration that is explicitly not supported.

On the *"add deprecation banners and migration links before removal of any UID"* criterion — **deliberately not done**, and this is a conscious deviation. A deprecation release costs a cycle of maintaining artifacts already known to be stale, for UIDs on dashboards that were never generated or tested. The migration guidance instead lives where someone hitting a dead UID will actually look: `docs/dashboards.md` and `deploy/grafana/README.md` both now name the replacement tab for each removed UID (fleet → **Fleet & Devices**, network → **Network & Flows**, audit events → **Events & Logs** plus **Security & Audit**, exporter health → **Exporter Diagnostics** plus **Cardinality & Cost**).

The deeper reason a Classic copy could not have been kept honestly: **v1 cannot express `conditionalRendering`.** Every feature-gated tab and row — object store, node metrics, posture, webhooks, log streaming, traces, profiling, the multi-tailnet scorecard — would render **permanently empty** instead of hiding itself. That is worse than not shipping it, and it is the same constraint that closed #409.

*"Test that a release cannot ship silently divergent copies of the same view"* is now structurally satisfied: there is exactly one dashboard, it is generated, and it is drift-gated. `deploy/CLAUDE.md` and the root `CLAUDE.md` both record why a v1 path must not be reintroduced, since "ship a classic version too" is the obvious wrong instinct for a future session.

`grafana:GRAF-09`

comments.body:
Closed by `9a3674c`, **re-scoped**.

The issue targets the audit/integration *dashboards*; `tailscale-audit-events.json` was deleted under #394 (Grafana v2 / 13+ only, no Classic export ever). Its substance moved to the flagship's **Events & Logs** and **Policy & Config** tabs.

**The four-state distinction is the core of this issue, and the honest answer is that the signals separate three of them.** Rendered as a shared state key on every panel in the new *Audit pipeline state* row:

| state | how it reads |
| --- | --- |
| **idle tailnet** | scrape gauge 1, accepted counter has series, both range counters 0 |
| **absent Loki data** | the Prometheus counter moved over `$__range` but the Loki counter over the *same* range is 0 — accepted, but not in the queried Loki datasource |
| **ingestion failure** | scrape gauge 0, or a non-zero series on *Audit ingestion failures/s*; any non-zero here rules out idle |
| **audit collection not enabled** | **not separable** from *unsupported by the provider* or *never deployed* — all three produce no series at all |

The fourth is stated as not-separable rather than faked. The panel names the prerequisites (`collectors.auditlogs.enabled`, `collectors.auditlogs.source`) and stops. Worth knowing *why* the usual escape hatch is unavailable: the `auditlogs` collector emits no `tailscale2otel.api.availability`, so the `disabled` vs `scope_denied` split that exists for acl/webhooks/flowlogs/logstream/postureintegrations cannot be used here.

Also landed: tailnet/provider/source filters; an *Audit events by ingestion path* panel so poll vs stream vs webhook vs object-store is visible; audit pipeline latency (deferred and local processing delay); log-stream delivery requests and failure ratio; and Loki panels sharing the same `$__range` as their metric siblings, since a window mismatch is a classic false "the data is missing" report.

PII controls preserved — identity-dense audit panels stay inside rows gated by the existing `pii_actor`/`pii_usernames` sentinels; exposure was not widened.

## Audit identity

`grafana:GRAF-07`

comments.body:
Closed by `9a3674c`, **re-scoped**.

The issue targets "the legacy network dashboard". That dashboard no longer exists — `tailscale-network.json` was deleted under #394, because the project is Grafana v2 / Grafana 13+ only and will never ship a Classic export. Its substance was folded into the flagship's **Network & Flows** tab instead. Every ask still applies, just to that tab.

- **Rollup-first with a safe raw fallback, never summing both.** This is now structurally impossible rather than merely avoided: `rollup_first()` takes *one* query template with a single placeholder, renders it against both metric names, and joins with PromQL `or`. There is no code path through it that emits `+`, and it is the only place in the module where a raw and a rollup name may co-occur in one expression. A test drives the detector with fabricated `+` and mismatched-half shapes to prove it is not vacuous.
- **Top-talker fix — root cause identified.** The live symptom ("no device labels, a time-like category") was a missing `xField`: a barchart with none takes the **first string field** as its category axis, so an un-excluded `Time`/`instance` column silently became the axis. Excluding the noise is not sufficient on its own — the category is now *pinned* to the renamed device column, so it is stated rather than inferred from column order. Applied to all six talkers plus two path-mix charts.
- **Tailnet and provider selectors** on every Prometheus flow panel. Deliberately **not** applied to the two Loki panels: there they are record attributes, and a label filter would drop lines carrying none.
- **Raw-only panels** name `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` in their description and sit in rows gated on `has_raw_flow`.
- **Route, path, service and peer-relay context** added without duplicating the flagship.

Bonus: `has_unique` was a **dead sentinel** — registered, querying Prometheus on every dashboard load, gating nothing. It now gates the peer/port topology row, whose panels query exactly the two `unique_*` gauges that need `cardinality.flow.node_dims` on top of the rollup mode.
