**Priority/theme:** P1 / Helm correctness  
**Evidence:** `deployment.yaml:68-85` renders HTTP probes with no scheme. `values.yaml:759-766` admits enabling admin TLS breaks them. Runtime correctly switches to TLS at `internal/app/admin.go:166-180`.  
**Why:** A supported chart setting makes the pod permanently unready and repeatedly restarted.  
**Scope/out:** Conditional `scheme: HTTPS` on both probes, with render tests. No Service/Ingress requirement.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] TLS-enabled admin renders HTTPS liveness/readiness probes.
- [ ] Plain HTTP remains default when TLS is absent.
- [ ] Partial TLS configuration fails via OUX-03.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-46`

comments.body:
Closed by `82e43b5`.

## Premise — CONFIRMED as filed, with one acceptance item already satisfied

- `deployment.yaml` rendered both probes with no `httpGet.scheme`. Kubernetes treats that as HTTP.
- The runtime does switch: `internal/app/admin.go:265-267` picks `ListenAndServeTLS` iff `certFile != "" && keyFile != ""`.
- `values.yaml` carried the admission verbatim: *"this chart's liveness/readiness probes set no httpGet.scheme, so they speak HTTP — serving the admin server over HTTPS breaks them until you patch the probes to scheme: HTTPS."*

**Acceptance item 3 ("Partial TLS configuration fails via OUX-03") was already done** and needed no work here. `validateTLSFiles` (`internal/config/validate.go:606-620`, called for admin/prometheus/webhook at 780-786) already rejects a half-set pair, under #170, with `TestValidate_AdminTLSBothOrNeither` pinning it.

## What shipped

Both probes render `scheme: HTTPS` under `and .Values.config.admin.tls.cert_file .Values.config.admin.tls.key_file` — the same both-or-neither condition the runtime uses.

`and`, not `or`, deliberately. One file alone is not a TLS server; it is a startup error the app already rejects. Flipping the probes there would break a pod that was going to fail loudly for a better reason, and would replace a clear config error with a probe-handshake failure.

## Stated limitation, not worked around

Admin TLS set through `TS2OTEL_ADMIN__TLS__CERT_FILE`/`__KEY_FILE` (via `secret:`/`existingSecret`) is invisible at render time — Helm cannot see an env var's effect on runtime behaviour. Those pods keep HTTP probes and will break the same way. This is recorded in the template comment and in the `values.yaml` annotation, with the remedy: use the `config.admin.tls` keys. Deriving it from the env layer would mean the chart parsing its own Secret, which it should not do.

## Negative test — all four assertions, three mutants

`render-tests.sh` case J covers neither / both / cert-only / key-only, plus a check that the workaround text is gone. Each was broken and confirmed to fire:

| Mutant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `or` instead of `and` | 2 failures — both single-file cases |
| unconditional `{{- if true }}` | 3 failures — the plain-HTTP case and both single-file cases |
| workaround warning restored to `values.yaml` | 1 failure |

Restored: 151 passed, 0 failed. Worth noting the cert-only/key-only cases passed *vacuously* before the fix, when every scheme was `null` — mutant 1 is what proves they mean something now.

## Acceptance

- [x] TLS-enabled admin renders HTTPS liveness/readiness probes
- [x] Plain HTTP remains default when TLS is absent (asserted as "not HTTPS", so an explicit `scheme: HTTP` would also pass)
- [x] Partial TLS configuration fails via OUX-03 — pre-existing, verified not re-implemented
- [x] Workaround warning removed, and its absence gated

Chart bumped 0.14.7 → 0.14.8; `README.md` and `values.schema.json` regenerated with the pinned tools. Full gate green at `82e43b5`.

- [ ] NOTES output is mode-aware.
- [ ] CI smoke-tests documented Helm commands.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-45`

comments.body:
Partial fix landed as a side effect of #445 (`123fe72`): the `secrets.*` → `secret.*` typo in the README quick start (README.md:94-95) is corrected, and `scripts/check_doc_commands.py` now validates every documented `--set`/`--set-string` key against the generated `values.schema.json` in CI, so that specific class cannot come back silently.

**This issue stays open.** Its other half is untouched and is the more important one: `docs/installation.md` and `templates/NOTES.txt` still teach `--set secret.KEY=<value>` with the credential inline on the command line, where it lands in shell history and the process table. That needs a different quick start (`--set-file`, a values file with restrictive permissions, or `existingSecret`), not a spelling fix.

Closed by `7cd9a84`.

## Premise — CONFIRMED, and this is the half #445 could not reach

The typo half was fixed by `123fe72` under #445. The remaining half was live in all three places the issue names, and the gate added by #445 was structurally incapable of catching it: **the commands were correct**. Every key resolved against `values.schema.json`. A schema check looks for keys that do not exist; this is a key that exists being used in a way that leaks its value.

10 inline-credential occurrences across `README.md` and `docs/installation.md`, plus `NOTES.txt`, which was not even in the scanned file set.

## What shipped

**Quick starts, in preference order.** `existingSecret` leads: `kubectl create secret generic --from-env-file`, then `--set-string existingSecret=<name>`. Helm never sees the credential, so it is not in the release values either.

Documented alternatives with their weaker property stated rather than glossed: a mode-0600 values file (`-f`) and `--set-file`. Both store the value in the Helm release — a Secret in the release namespace, so under Secret RBAC, but readable by anyone who can run `helm get values`. `existingSecret` avoids that; those do not. Inline is described as development-only and **deliberately not written as a copy-pasteable command**.

**The gate.** `check_doc_commands.py` grew the check that would have caught the original:

- Credential prefixes are **derived** from `tailscale2otel.credentialPaths` in `_helpers.tpl` — the list `deploy/CLAUDE.md` names authoritative and every template routes through — plus `secret.`. Adding a credential field to the chart extends this check with no edit to the script.
- If that block stops parsing, the script **dies** rather than checking an empty set.
- `kubectl --from-literal=TS2OTEL_*` is screened too: identical exposure, and the obvious way to write the new `existingSecret` quick start wrongly.
- `--set-file` keys are now extracted and schema-validated. They were previously invisible to the extractor entirely.
- `NOTES.txt` joined the scanned file set. It is the most-copied text the chart emits and it taught the bad pattern for just as long.
- A new vacuity guard: zero `--set` keys screened is a failure, not a pass.

## Negative tests — four branches, all fire

| Mutant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Reintroduce inline `--set secret.*` in README | flagged as CREDENTIAL inline |
| `--set config.profiling.pyroscope.basic_auth_password=hunter2` | flagged — proves the **derivation** works, not just the `secret.` prefix |
| `--from-literal=TS2OTEL_..._TOKEN=<token-1>` | flagged with the `--from-file` remedy |
| Rename the `credentialPaths` define | script exits 2: "an empty credential set would make the inline-credential check pass vacuously" |
| Revert NOTES.txt to an inline `--set secret` | render-tests case L fails **and** the doc gate flags it |

## A guard of mine that initially asserted nothing

Case L's NOTES assertions used `helm template --notes`. **`helm template` does not render NOTES.txt at all** — it emits nothing silently. The two positive assertions failed, which is what exposed it, but the two *negative*-shaped ones ("no chart-Secret text", "no inline credential command") passed against an empty string. Fixed to use `helm install --dry-run=client`, and `notes_of` now fails loudly if the rendered NOTES is empty rather than letting anything assert over nothing.

That is the fourth guard in this repository's recent history to pass while proving nothing, and the second caught only because a sibling assertion happened to be positive.

## Acceptance

- [x] README command uses real keys and successfully renders credentials — case L asserts `envFrom` references the pre-created Secret **and** that no chart Secret is rendered alongside it
- [x] Preferred quick start keeps secrets out of command history/release values — `existingSecret` achieves both; the two alternatives achieve the first only, and say so
- [x] NOTES output is mode-aware — asserted in both directions: the `existingSecret` mode names the Secret and does **not** print the chart-managed-Secret text
- [x] CI smoke-tests documented Helm commands — the #445 script, extended, plus case L rendering the documented command shapes

## Correction carried into this commit

Case K (from #332, `ac58014`) went red once `values.schema.json` was regenerated: the generated `minimum: 45` rejects any number *before* templating, so the template `fail` guard never sees one and my case-K assertion on its message was wrong.

The guard is **not** dead code, though — removing it and rendering `--set terminationGracePeriodSeconds=null` produces `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0`, an immediate SIGKILL. JSON Schema `minimum` does not reject null. Two layers, different inputs, both now asserted on their own input. Recorded on #332 as well.

Chart bumped 0.14.9 → 0.14.10. Full gate green at `7cd9a84`.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P3 / Native QoL  
**Evidence:** GoReleaser produces archives only (`.goreleaser.yaml:27-71`); no Homebrew/Scoop/Nix packaging exists.  
**Why:** Native users have no straightforward install/upgrade/uninstall workflow.  
**Scope/out:** Start with Homebrew tap; file separate follow-ups for Scoop/Nix if desired. Preserve signed upstream artifacts.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] Package installs the correct architecture and reports version.
- [ ] Upgrade/uninstall are documented and tested.
- [ ] Packaging consumes verified release assets.
- [ ] Config/state are not removed on upgrade.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Record the evidence, decision, rejected alternatives, and follow-up implementation slices; closing as unsupported is valid when the evidence does not justify a feature.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-44`

comments.body:
Closing as **won't do**, for the same reason as #339 — scope decision by @rknightion, 2026-07-28: the container image is the only supported production deployment model, via Docker Compose or the Helm chart.

A Homebrew tap (or Scoop, or Nix) exists to make a *native install* convenient. Native install is no longer a supported deployment surface, so packaging it would advertise a path the project does not stand behind, and every one of this issue's own acceptance criteria — upgrade, uninstall, config/state preserved across upgrade — is a promise about a lifecycle nothing in CI can exercise.

The premise itself is unchanged and correct: `.goreleaser.yaml` produces archives, checksums, per-archive SBOMs and a cosign signature over the checksums, and no `brews:`/`scoops:`/`nix:` block exists. Those archives keep being published and signed — they are the right thing for development, for `-validate`, and for anyone knowingly going off the supported path. What they verifiably are is documented under [Verifying a release](https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/installation/#verifying-a-release) (#338), which is the closest thing to "packaging consumes verified release assets" that this decision leaves room for.

Reopen only if the deployment policy changes.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit exercised configuration validation and reviewed the CLI, admin/status/flow UIs, Compose assets, Helm chart, installation paths, and operational documentation.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P2 / Native production use  
**Evidence:** Binary docs stop at foreground execution (`docs/installation.md:125-154`); no unit files exist.  
**Why:** Users must invent service ownership, directories, secret handling, restart, shutdown, and hardening.  
**Scope/out:** Example/installable unit with non-root user, `StateDirectory`, `ConfigurationDirectory`, `LoadCredential` plus `_file`, `ExecStartPre -validate`, restart policy, and adequate `TimeoutStopSec`. No distro package daemon.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] Fresh installation starts without root-owned-state fallback.
- [ ] Secrets do not appear in the environment.
- [ ] Validation prevents starting a bad config.
- [ ] Upgrade, rollback, logs, and uninstall are documented.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-43`

comments.body:
Closing as **won't do** — scope decision by @rknightion, 2026-07-28: *"I dont think people will ever run this on a system the ONLY supported deployment model should be via docker container."*

The container image is the only supported production deployment, via Docker Compose or the Helm chart. A local binary stays supported for development, `-validate` runs and experiments, but not as a service.

**This was built before the decision landed, and then reverted.** A full hardened unit existed and passed its gate: `Type=exec`, static `User=`/`Group=` with `DynamicUser=no` (a transient UID breaks checkpoint ownership across restarts), `StateDirectory=`/`ConfigurationDirectory=`, `LoadCredential=` paired with the `TS2OTEL_*_FILE` keys, `ExecStartPre=… -validate`, `TimeoutStopSec=45s` covering the staged drain, and the full `Protect*`/`Restrict*`/`SystemCallFilter` block. It came with six guard tests in `internal/config` that derived the credential list from `secretfile.go` rather than duplicating it, and all of them were mutation-tested. None of it is committed. Recording that here so nobody re-derives the design believing it was never attempted.

**Why the decision is right, beyond the preference.** The image already encodes the runtime contract a native install would have to reproduce and then keep in step by hand: non-root uid 65532, the pre-seeded `/var/lib/tailscale2otel` with correct ownership, a read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, and a `stop_grace_period` covering the staged shutdown drain. Shipping a second deployment surface means two places to get all of that right, and the second one has no CI that can exercise it — nothing in this repo can boot a systemd unit, so the guard tests could only ever assert the file's *text*, never that it works.

**Consequences, so they are not rediscovered later:**

- `docs/installation.md`'s Binary tab now carries an explicit warning that running the binary directly is not a supported deployment and that no `systemd` unit or packaging is planned. Landed in `c8802cd`.
- #340 (package-manager installation path) closes for the same reason — it is the same native-install surface a level further out.
- Release binaries keep being published and signed. They are useful for `-validate`, for local development, and for anyone who chooses to go off the supported path knowingly. Verifying them is documented under [Verifying a release](https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/installation/#verifying-a-release) (#338).
- `-healthcheck` (#337) is unaffected: it exists for the container path, which is where it is wired.

Reopen this only if the deployment policy changes; the design above is the starting point if it does.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit exercised configuration validation and reviewed the CLI, admin/status/flow UIs, Compose assets, Helm chart, installation paths, and operational documentation.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P2 / Supply-chain UX  
**Evidence:** `docs/installation.md:125-154` primarily teaches building from source. `.goreleaser.yaml:52-96` already publishes checksums, SBOMs, and Sigstore bundles.  
**Why:** Users are told artifacts are signed but not how to verify them.  
**Scope/out:** Exact download, SHA, cosign/GitHub attestation, container verification, SBOM discovery, upgrade/rollback commands.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] Commands work against a real current release in CI.
- [ ] Binary and image verification paths are both covered.
- [ ] Platform archive naming is documented.
- [ ] Verification failure is explained clearly.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-42`

comments.body:
## Verification evidence — every command below was actually run against the published v3.0.0 release

This issue was blocked on verification, not on writing. Publishing a `cosign` invocation that
does not work is worse than publishing none, so nothing gets documented that was not executed
here, including the failure cases.

Tooling: `cosign v3.0.6` built locally from source (`go install github.com/sigstore/cosign/v3/cmd/cosign@v3.0.6`)
and `gh attestation verify`. Target: release `v3.0.0` and `ghcr.io/rknightion/tailscale2otel:3.0.0`.

### The signing identity is the SHARED repo, not this one

Signing happens inside `rknightion/.github`'s reusable workflows, so the Fulcio certificate's SAN
names `rknightion/.github` — **not** `rknightion/tailscale2otel`. Read straight off the v3.0.0
signing certificate:

```
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: critical
    URI:https://github.com/rknightion/.github/.github/workflows/binaries.yml@d1c590b295b9d7f2535fadc7bc5e74f2eddbd512
1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.1: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.5: rknightion/tailscale2otel      <- the *caller* repo, not the identity
```

A doc that guessed `--certificate-identity ...rknightion/tailscale2otel...` would fail for every
user, every time. Verified by negative test below.

### The identity is SHA-pinned, so it rotates on every Renovate bump

The SAN ends `@d1c590b2…`, the reusable-workflow SHA that was pinned in `release-please.yml` **at
the time v3.0.0 was built**. `main` now pins `a4182f2…` (v1.5.0). A hardcoded
`--certificate-identity` is therefore correct for exactly one release and then rots silently.

**Everything documented uses `--certificate-identity-regexp` anchored on the workflow path**, which
survives the bump while still pinning the workflow that is allowed to sign.

### 1. Release binaries — `cosign verify-blob` on the checksums file

```
cosign verify-blob \
  --bundle tailscale2otel_3.0.0_SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/rknightion/\.github/\.github/workflows/binaries\.yml@' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  tailscale2otel_3.0.0_SHA256SUMS
```
→ `Verified OK`, exit 0.

Negative tests, all failing for the right reason:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| identity regexp `^https://github\.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/` | `expected SAN value to match regex …, got "https://github.com/rknightion/.github/…"` |
| one byte appended to `SHA256SUMS` | `failed to verify signature: could not verify message: invalid signature` |
| issuer `https://accounts.google.com` | `expected issuer value "https://accounts.google.com", got "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"` |

### 2. SLSA provenance — `gh attestation verify`, and two traps

Provenance comes from `actions/attest-build-provenance` (**not** slsa-github-generator), so
`gh attestation verify` is the tool and `slsa-verifier` is not.

**Trap 1 — the subject is each ARCHIVE, not the checksums file.** The workflow passes
`subject-checksums:`, which attests every artifact *listed in* `SHA256SUMS`. Decoding the DSSE
payload of `tailscale2otel_3.0.0_SHA256SUMS.intoto.jsonl` confirms it: 10 subjects, the 5 archives
plus their 5 `.sbom.json` files, and `SHA256SUMS` itself is **not among them**. Verifying the
checksums file therefore 404s:
```
Error: HTTP 404: Not Found (…/attestations/sha256:5978bd2c…)
```

**Trap 2 — `--signer-repo` is required,** for the same shared-repo reason as above. Without it:
```
Error: verifying with issuer "sigstore.dev"     # exit 1, and the message says nothing useful
```

The command that works:
```
gh attestation verify tailscale2otel_3.0.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz \
  -R rknightion/tailscale2otel \
  --signer-repo rknightion/.github
```
→ exit 0.

Negatives: `--signer-repo rknightion/tailscale2otel` → exit 1; one byte appended to the archive →
exit 1 with a 404 on the mutated digest.

### 3. Container image — `cosign verify`

```
cosign verify ghcr.io/rknightion/tailscale2otel:3.0.0 \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/rknightion/\.github/\.github/workflows/container-publish\.yml@' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
```
→ verified, digest `sha256:9a5a18117890cc2c42d4ec285e58c42b4d197bd1cd0d992dffd8eb49690b6374`.
Note the identity is `container-publish.yml`, a **different** workflow from the binaries path, so
the two commands do not share an identity string.

Negative: identity regexp `^https://github\.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/` → exit 1, `got
"https://github.com/rknightion/.github/.github/workflows/container-publish.yml@f3169068…"`.

Image provenance also verifies:
```
gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/rknightion/tailscale2otel:3.0.0 \
  -R rknightion/tailscale2otel --signer-repo rknightion/.github
```
→ exit 0. Image signing is on by default (`container-publish.yml`'s `sign` input defaults `true`
and `publish.yml` does not override it).

### 4. Asset naming, confirmed against the real release

`v3.0.0` assets: archives `tailscale2otel_3.0.0_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` (`.zip` for `windows_amd64`
only), per-archive SBOMs `<archive>.sbom.json` (**not** `.sbom`), `tailscale2otel_3.0.0_SHA256SUMS`,
`…_SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json`, `…_SHA256SUMS.intoto.jsonl`, plus `tailscale2otel.{spdx,cdx}.json`,
`tailscale2otel-3.0.0.tgz` (Helm chart) and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

**Older releases are not uniform and the docs must not pretend otherwise:** `v2.0.0` has no
archives at all, and `v2.0.1` and `v1.0.0` are missing `SHA256SUMS.intoto.jsonl`. Any provenance
step is written as version-gated / "if present".

Docs to follow in the closing commit.

body:
## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit exercised configuration validation and reviewed the CLI, admin/status/flow UIs, Compose assets, Helm chart, installation paths, and operational documentation.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P2 / Container/service integration  
**Evidence:** Distroless image has no curl (`deploy/Dockerfile:35-58`) and no HEALTHCHECK; Compose has none.  
**Why:** Operators cannot declare health without adding tooling or using platform-specific workarounds.  
**Scope/out:** Small built-in readiness probe command with timeout/TLS options, wired into Compose. Avoid an unconditional Dockerfile healthcheck because admin may be disabled.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] Healthcheck returns distinct success/unready/transport exit codes.
- [ ] HTTP and HTTPS admin listeners are supported.
- [ ] Compose enables it only when admin is enabled.
- [ ] No shell or extra runtime binary is required.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-41`

comments.body:
Closed by `4cc1bb3`.

**Premise re-confirmed before implementing.** `deploy/Dockerfile` is `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot` with no shell and no `HEALTHCHECK`; `deploy/docker-compose.yaml` had no `healthcheck:` block; `cmd/tailscale2otel/main.go` was a flat `flag.FlagSet` with `-config`, `-version`, `-validate`. All as described.

**What shipped**

`tailscale2otel -healthcheck` (plus `-healthcheck-timeout`, default 5s) probes this process's own admin `/readyz` over loopback. It is a fourth dispatch mode in `run()`, ordered `-version` → `-healthcheck` → `-validate` → server.

| exit | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | `/readyz` returned 2xx |
| 1 | reached the listener, it reported not-ready |
| 2 | could not probe at all — config invalid, `admin.enabled: false`, dial refused, TLS failure, timeout |

Acceptance, item by item:

- **Distinct success/unready/transport exit codes** — the three above, pinned by `TestProbeReady`.
- **HTTP and HTTPS admin listeners** — scheme is `https` iff `admin.tls.cert_file` *and* `admin.tls.key_file` are both set. Only one set stays `http`, because that combination is already a `Validate()` error and the URL builder must not invent a scheme to paper over it.
- **Compose enables it only when admin is enabled** — the base file now pins `TS2OTEL_ADMIN__ENABLED: ${TS2OTEL_ADMIN__ENABLED:-true}` next to the healthcheck block, with a comment stating that the two move together and what to do if you disable admin.
- **No shell or extra runtime binary** — `["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/tailscale2otel", "-healthcheck"]`. Exec form, not `CMD-SHELL`, which would fail 100% of the time on a shell-less image.

**Two judgement calls, stated so they can be vetoed**

*No `HEALTHCHECK` in the Dockerfile*, per the issue's own scoping. `admin.enabled` is a runtime choice an image-level instruction cannot see, so it would be wrong whichever way it guessed. The Dockerfile carries a comment saying so and pointing at the Compose block.

*TLS verification is skipped on the probe*, and no flag is offered to change it. The destination is the trust boundary — a loopback address in the same network namespace as the process being probed — not the certificate. There is no third party to impersonate on loopback, and a kubelet `httpGet` probe with `scheme: HTTPS` makes exactly the same call for exactly the same reason. A test against `httptest.NewTLSServer` proves it is actually wired rather than accidentally working.

**Negative-testing.** Every new assertion was mutated and observed to fail, by the implementing lane and then independently by the dispatcher:

| mutation | assertion that fired |
| --- | --- |
| ready range widened to `< 600` | `503 -> hcUnready`: `probeReady() = 0, want hcUnready (1)` |
| wildcard-rewrite `case` made unmatchable | 5 `TestHealthcheckURL` subtests, incl. both wildcard cases |
| TLS condition `&&` → `\|\|` | `only_cert_set` / `only_key_set` |
| `admin.enabled` check inverted | all 10 `TestHealthcheckURL` subtests |
| `InsecureSkipVerify` dropped | the TLS-server subtest, with an `x509` error |
| `healthcheck.test` → `CMD-SHELL` form | compose-tests case F exec-form assertion |
| `TS2OTEL_ADMIN__ENABLED=false` | compose-tests case F admin-default assertion |

The last two are wired into `deploy/tests/compose-tests.sh --self-test`, so they stay proven rather than being a one-off check.

**Gate:** `go build` · `go vet` · `go test -race ./...` · `golangci-lint run` (0 issues) · `compose-tests.sh --self-test` (40 passed, 0 failed) · `check_doc_commands.py`. Docs: a new "Health checks" section in `docs/installation.md` covering the flag, the exit codes, the Compose block and the `docker run --health-cmd` equivalent.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit exercised configuration validation and reviewed the CLI, admin/status/flow UIs, Compose assets, Helm chart, installation paths, and operational documentation.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P1 / Binary lifecycle  
**Evidence:** Default is `/var/lib/tailscale2otel/checkpoints.json` at `internal/config/defaults.go:184-187`; binary instructions at `docs/installation.md:125-154` neither create nor chown it. Releases include macOS and Windows.  
**Why:** Non-root native runs silently fall back to memory; the Linux-centric path is unsuitable on other platforms.  
**Scope/out:** Platform-aware state directory or a required explicit path in native quick starts; container/chart explicitly retain `/var/lib`. No hidden migration that risks losing an existing checkpoint.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] Native defaults are writable on Linux/macOS/Windows.
- [ ] Existing path migration/precedence is documented.
- [ ] Effective store/path/fallback reason appear in validation/status.
- [ ] Container and Helm behavior remains stable.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-40`

comments.body:
Closed by `3ce3461`.

## Premise — CONFIRMED, but acceptance item 3 was largely already built

The path was live as filed (`internal/config/defaults.go:224`) and the silent degrade was real (`app.go` `checkpointStore` → WARN → memory store).

**Correction:** acceptance item 3, "effective store/path/fallback reason appear in validation/status", was **partly stale**. `#69` already made `checkpointStore` return the *effective* store kind and the status page already reported that rather than the raw config value. Only the effective **path** and the **reason** were missing, and that is what was added — the store half needed no work.

## The design decision, and why not the obvious one

The obvious fix — make `config.Default()` platform-aware — is **not possible here**, and I tried it first and backed it out:

1. `TestExampleConfigMatchesDefaults` gates `config.example.yaml` to match `Default()` byte-for-byte. A machine-dependent default cannot be written into a committed file, so that gate would have to be weakened.
2. The container image and the chart both depend on `/var/lib` being the default. Changing it silently moves every container's checkpoint unless every image and compose file also sets it explicitly.

So resolution happens **at runtime**, in `checkpointStore`. The committed default stays deterministic, and container behavior is untouched because `/var/lib` genuinely *is* writable there — zero config changes to the image, compose or chart. `TestDefaultKeepsLegacyCheckpointPath` records this reasoning against a future "fix".

## Not a hidden migration

The issue's constraint was the binding one. Two boundaries:

- **Nothing is ever moved or copied.** A usable configured path always wins, so relocation can only happen where there was no readable checkpoint to begin with. An existing checkpoint cannot be stranded by this.
- **An explicitly configured `file_path` is never relocated.** Naming a path is a decision — usually a mounted volume that is briefly absent. Relocating would hide that misconfiguration and split state across two locations. Those keep the existing WARN-and-degrade.

## Negative tests — four mutants

| Mutant | Caught by |
| --- | --- |
| Relocation disabled | `RelocatesUnwritableDefaultToPlatformPath` — "degrading to memory means the relocation did not happen" |
| Relocate an **explicit** path too | `ExplicitPathIsNeverRelocated` — "must WARN and degrade, never relocate" |
| `Reason` left empty on relocation | `RelocatesUnwritableDefault...` — "the status page would show no explanation" |
| macOS branch of the path helper returns "" | `DefaultCheckpointPath_PlatformAppropriate` — "returned the legacy root-only path" |

The relocation test injects what counts as "the default" rather than depending on whether the test process can write `/var/lib`, which would otherwise pass or fail based on whether CI runs as root.

## Acceptance

- [x] Native defaults are writable on Linux/macOS/Windows — `$XDG_STATE_HOME`/`~/.local/state`, `~/Library/Application Support`, `%LocalAppData%`, each pinned per-`GOOS`. `LocalAppData` not `AppData` on Windows: checkpoints are machine-local state and must not follow a roaming profile.
- [x] Existing path migration/precedence is documented — new "Where checkpoints go on a native run" section in `docs/installation.md` states the precedence, that nothing is moved, that an explicit path is never relocated, and that migrating an existing root install is manual and optional (doing nothing is safe).
- [x] Effective store/path/fallback reason appear in validation/status — `checkpoint_store` (pre-existing), plus new `checkpoint_path` and `checkpoint_reason` in `/api/status.json` and on the status page.
- [x] Container and Helm behavior remains stable — no image, compose or chart change was needed at all, and `WritableDefaultIsNotRelocated` asserts a writable default is used as-is with an empty reason.

## Deliberately not done

**`ingress_wal.directory` still defaults to `/var/lib/tailscale2otel/ingress-wal` and was left alone.** It has the same platform problem, but the WAL **fails closed** rather than degrading silently — an operator who enables it natively gets a hard startup error naming the path, not a silent cold-start — so it is not the defect this issue describes. Extending the relocation to it would widen the blast radius to the chart and the receiver durability contract for no silent-failure gain. Stated rather than quietly included.

Full gate green at `3ce3461`.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit exercised configuration validation and reviewed the CLI, admin/status/flow UIs, Compose assets, Helm chart, installation paths, and operational documentation.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P2 / Deployment predictability  
**Evidence:** Compose contains both `build:` and `image: ...:latest` at `deploy/docker-compose.yaml:19-24`; its header says `up --build`, while `docs/installation.md:57-74` says plain `up`.  
**Why:** Users may unexpectedly build/tag a checkout as `latest`, while others think they are running the published image.  
**Scope/out:** Stable published-image base plus development override/profile; explicit version/pull policy.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] Default Compose uses a released image predictably.
- [ ] Development build is an explicit command/profile.
- [ ] Image version is configurable and reported.
- [ ] Both configurations are CI-rendered.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-39`

comments.body:
Closed by `1faaa5e`.

## Premise — CONFIRMED, contradiction still live

`deploy/docker-compose.yaml` had both `build:` and `image: ghcr.io/rknightion/tailscale2otel:latest` in one service block, its header said `up --build`, and `docs/installation.md` said plain `up`. So which thing you ran depended on which instruction you had read — and `up --build` tagged a working tree with the **published** image name, making a local build indistinguishable from a release in `docker images`.

## What shipped

- **Base file: published image only**, pinned to a real release. `latest` is not a predictable default — it moves under a running deployment — so the pin is a version, overridable with `TS2OTEL_VERSION`.
- **`deploy/docker-compose.dev.yaml`** carries `build:` and tags `tailscale2otel:dev`, deliberately *not* the published repository, so a dev image can never be mistaken for a release.
- Docs and the compose header now agree, both saying plain `up` for the published image and naming the override for a build.

## Beyond the filed scope — the chart had the same rot, worse

While wiring the version pin I checked the chart: **`appVersion` was `2.0.2` against a `3.0.0` release.** `appVersion` is the image tag the chart installs when `image.tag` is empty, so the default Helm install was silently running a major behind.

A comment already in `Chart.yaml` records this same pin being corrected once before, from a long-stale `0.1.0` that "tracked nothing". Fixing the value again would just queue up a third occurrence, so both pins are now **maintained by release-please `extra-files`** and gated:

- `TestComposeImageTagMatchesRelease`
- `TestChartAppVersionMatchesRelease`

Both compare against `.release-please-manifest.json`. The timing is what makes this catchable, and it is the same property `TestModulePathMatchesReleaseVersion` relies on: the manifest is bumped **by the release PR**, so if `extra-files` ever stops updating a pin, the mismatch shows up there — on the one PR that must not merge unnoticed — rather than after the tag is cut.

## Acceptance

- [x] Default Compose uses a released image predictably — a pinned version, asserted **not** to be `:latest`
- [x] Development build is an explicit command/profile — a separate `-f` override, tagged distinctly
- [x] Image version is configurable and reported — `TS2OTEL_VERSION` override asserted to take effect; the running version is already reported via `-version`, the startup log and `/api/status.json`
- [x] Both configurations are CI-rendered — `compose-tests.sh` case E resolves base and base+dev, in the CI job added under #333

## Negative tests

| Mutant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Revert the pin to `:latest` | Go test fails to find the pinned form; case E fails twice (`:latest` + override no longer applies) |
| Reintroduce `build:` in the base | Go test and case E both fail |
| Stale pin (simulate a missed release bump) | `compose default image tag is "2.0.2", but the current release is "3.0.0"` |

## ⚠️ Note on release-please PR #255

This adds `extra-files` to `release-please-config.json`. #255 was opened **before** that config existed, so its current diff will not contain the two new pin updates. release-please regenerates and force-pushes its branch on each push to `main`, so it should pick them up on the next run.

If it does not, the two new tests will fail **on #255**, which is the intended signal rather than a surprise — but it is worth knowing before you look at it. **#255 remains unmerged and no release was published**, per the standing constraint.

Full gate green at `1faaa5e`; chart bumped 0.15.0 → 0.15.1.

## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit exercised configuration validation and reviewed the CLI, admin/status/flow UIs, Compose assets, Helm chart, installation paths, and operational documentation.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P2 / Container security  
**Evidence:** Compose teaches `.env` secrets at `deploy/docker-compose.yaml:3-16,35-45`; runtime supports `_file` secrets at `internal/config/secretfile.go:19-47`.  
**Why:** Environment credentials are visible through container inspection and process tooling.  
**Scope/out:** Compose `secrets:` files mapped to supported `*_file` variables, with env mode retained for development.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] OAuth, OTLP, receiver, admin, and profiling secrets have file-based examples.
- [ ] Secrets are absent from rendered environment.
- [ ] `docker compose config` and startup smoke tests cover the mode.
- [ ] Documentation explains rotation behavior.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-38`

comments.body:
Closed by `a544576`.

## Premise — CONFIRMED for Compose, but the runtime half was **not** as complete as it looked

The Compose side was exactly as filed: `deploy/docker-compose.yaml` teaches `.env` env-var credentials and nothing else.

The runtime side needed checking, because the issue says the app "supports `_file` secrets". It mostly did — and I nearly recorded that as fully stale. Then I checked the actual resolver rather than the struct definitions, and found a real gap.

## Bug found while validating the premise

`ObjectStoreConfig` is **shared** by flowlogs and auditlogs, so the audit object store has always *declared* `access_key_id_file`, `secret_access_key_file` and `session_token_file`, and `objectStoreAuditSpec` consumes the resolved values at runtime. But `resolveSecretFiles` only ever walked the **flow** ones:

- `collectors.auditlogs.objectstore.*_file` — never resolved
- `tailnets[].objectstore.audit.*_file` — never resolved (the loop did `t.ObjectStore.Flow` only)

Setting either did **nothing**: no file read, no error, and an empty credential handed to the S3 client. That surfaces much later as a bucket authentication failure pointing at the wrong thing entirely.

Two aggravating details:

- The Helm chart already listed `collectors.auditlogs.objectstore.*` in `tailscale2otel.credentialPaths`, and render-tests case B covers them — so the chart correctly treated these as credentials while the app ignored their file form.
- For a `tailnets[]` entry this was the **only** way to supply the credential without writing it into YAML, because a list-of-structs key has no `TS2OTEL_*` env form (#79). There was no workaround.

Three tests pin it, and all three failed first with empty values.

## What shipped for Compose

`deploy/docker-compose.secrets.yaml`, applied as a second `-f`, covering all five categories the acceptance names — OAuth, OTLP, receiver (streaming + webhook), admin, profiling. It explicitly **clears** the plain-valued variables the base file passes through, because value+file on one key is a hard startup error, not a precedence rule; without that, anyone with credentials in `deploy/.env` would hit a confusing conflict.

## Acceptance

- [x] OAuth, OTLP, receiver, admin, and profiling secrets have file-based examples — all six variables, count-asserted so dropping one fails
- [x] Secrets are absent from rendered environment — a sentinel value is written into the secret files and the resolved config is grepped for it; only `/run/secrets/...` paths appear
- [x] `docker compose config` **and startup smoke tests** cover the mode — see below
- [x] Documentation explains rotation behavior — files are read **once** at config load, so a bind-mounted edit does not reach the running process; `up -d --force-recreate` is required. Framed against the chart’s `rolloutTrigger`, which has the same underlying constraint.

## The startup smoke test, and why it has teeth

`compose-tests.sh` case D can only prove the resolved config carries *paths*. Proving the binary **reads** them needs a real start, so `ci.yml`’s `docker-build` job (which already builds the image) now runs it with `-validate` — no tailnet, no OTLP backend needed, and `-validate` is exactly where `*_file` resolution happens. It also runs in the distroless runtime as uid 65532, so it proves the mount is readable by the real user.

The load-bearing part is the **negative half**: the same config with a non-existent path must FAIL. Without it, the positive check would pass just as happily against a file that was never opened — which is precisely the bug fixed above.

Both halves were run against a locally built image before being wired into CI:

```
positive: rc=0, "config OK", value not echoed
negative: config invalid: tailscale.auth.oauth.client_secret_file "/run/secrets/absent": open ...: no such file or directory
```

## Negative tests

| Mutant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Drop the profiling credential from the override | 2 failures (missing var + count 5≠6) |
| Leave a plain variable set alongside its `_FILE` sibling | value-XOR-file assertion fires |
| Revert the auditlogs resolver fix | all three config tests fail with empty credentials |

`deploy/secrets/` is git-ignored; `check-secret-hygiene.sh` passes. Full gate green at `a544576`.

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit exercised configuration validation and reviewed the CLI, admin/status/flow UIs, Compose assets, Helm chart, installation paths, and operational documentation.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P1 / Compose correctness  
**Evidence:** `deploy/docker-compose.yaml:57-62` tells users to uncomment a second `volumes:` key, overriding or duplicating the checkpoint block.  
**Why:** Following the shipped comment can discard persistence or produce parser-dependent behavior.  
**Scope/out:** Put the mount in the existing list or ship a clean override file.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] Documented config-file mode preserves checkpoint volume.
- [ ] `docker compose config` validates both default and file-backed modes in CI.
- [ ] Commands match installation docs.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-37`

comments.body:
Closed by `a9311a3`.

## Premise — CONFIRMED, with one correction to the severity

The commented-out second `volumes:` key at `deploy/docker-compose.yaml:79-82` was live exactly as filed.

**Correction:** the issue says following it can "discard persistence or produce parser-dependent behavior". On Compose v5.1.2 it is neither silent nor parser-dependent in practice — it is a hard parse error, reproduced before any change:

```
failed to parse .../docker-compose.yaml: yaml: construct errors:
  line 28: line 80: mapping key "volumes" already defined at line 77
```

So the documented file-backed path did not lose checkpoints quietly; it did not work at all. The fix is unchanged, but the failure mode on record should be "the documented path is dead" rather than "persistence is silently discarded".

## What shipped

`deploy/docker-compose.config.yaml` — an override applied as a second `-f`. Across two files Compose **merges** the volume lists by mount target, so the base checkpoint volume survives and the config mount is added beside it. That merge is the contract, and it is why this cannot be a comment in the base file.

`deploy/tests/compose-tests.sh` — resolves both modes with `docker compose config` and asserts against the resolved document with `yq`:

- default mode: checkpoint mount present, no config mount, no `command` override
- file-backed mode: checkpoint mount **still** present, config mount present and `read_only: true`, `command` is `-config /etc/tailscale2otel/config.yaml`, and exactly 2 mounts — a count check, because a *replaced* list naming both volumes would satisfy the two presence assertions on its own
- the base file carries no duplicate service keys and no commented `volumes:`

Wired into `ci.yml`'s `docker-build` job. That job already has a checkout, Docker, and a place in `ci-success.needs`, so the gate is blocking without touching the branch ruleset — the same reasoning the secret-hygiene gate in that job used.

## Negative test

`--self-test` runs in CI and does two things:

1. Strips the checkpoint mount from a resolved document and asserts `assert_checkpoint_mount` **fails**. If it does not fire, the script exits 1 with "it asserts nothing".
2. Re-synthesises the duplicate-`volumes:` form and asserts Compose still rejects it — case C's premise, checked rather than assumed.

Both were observed firing before the implementation landed; the pre-implementation run was 5 passed / 7 failed for the right reasons (no override file, base file still carrying the comment).

## Acceptance

- [x] Documented config-file mode preserves checkpoint volume — asserted directly, and negative-tested
- [x] `docker compose config` validates both default and file-backed modes in CI
- [x] Commands match installation docs — `docs/installation.md` gained a "Running from a config file" section carrying the same two-`-f` command, plus a warning recording why the mount cannot go in the base file

## Also done

`deploy/config.yaml` (the operator-supplied file the override mounts) added to `.gitignore`. `.dockerignore` needs no change: it is an allowlist and `deploy/` was never in it. `scripts/check-secret-hygiene.sh` passes.

Full gate green at `a9311a3`.

body:
## Audit context

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit exercised configuration validation and reviewed the CLI, admin/status/flow UIs, Compose assets, Helm chart, installation paths, and operational documentation.

## Finding and proposed scope

**Priority/theme:** P1 / Data durability  
**Evidence:** Compose has no `stop_grace_period` (`deploy/docker-compose.yaml:17-68`); Docker Compose defaults to 10 seconds. The app waits for receiver drains then gives telemetry another 10 seconds at `internal/app/app.go:569-585`; receivers can each spend 10 seconds shutting down. Deployment has no explicit `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.  
**Why:** Compose can SIGKILL the process before final flow flush/export completes.  
**Scope/out:** Compose ≥30s, Helm configurable ≥30s default, `docker run --stop-timeout` docs. No indefinite shutdown.

**Acceptance:**

- [ ] Deployment budgets exceed the worst supported staged drain.
- [ ] Graceful-stop integration test proves final flush opportunity.
- [ ] Operator docs explain the budget.
- [ ] Excessively low chart values warn or fail.

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
- [ ] Update affected catalog, generated artifacts, configuration references, operator documentation, dashboards, and rules as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve bounded-cardinality and PII/secret-handling contracts.
- [ ] Run the full repository gate, including all affected tool modules and generated-artifact drift checks.

## Audit identity

`operator:OUX-36`

comments.body:
Closed by `ac58014`.

## Premise — CONFIRMED, and the drain is exactly as tight as filed

- `deploy/docker-compose.yaml` had no `stop_grace_period`; Compose defaults to **10s**.
- The chart had no `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` anywhere (`grep -rn terminationGracePeriod deploy/ docs/` → nothing); Kubernetes defaults to **30s**.

Worst-case staged drain, read off the code rather than estimated:

| Stage | Bound | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Receivers drain (stream + webhook, **parallel**, one `receiverWG.Wait`) | 10s | `stream.go:528`, `stream.go:1908`, `webhook.go:392`, `webhook.go:565` |
| Ingress WAL final drain | 10s | `ingressWALFlushTimeout`, `app.go:747` |
| OTLP flush + shutdown | 10s | `app.go:762` |
| **Total** | **30s** | |

Schedulers are not budgeted: `runTick` takes the same canceled context, so `Scheduler.Run`'s `wg.Wait()` returns promptly.

So Compose was killed partway through stage one, and **the Kubernetes default equals the drain exactly, with zero margin** — the value most likely to be chosen by someone "restoring the default", and not a safe one.

## What shipped

Both paths budget **45s** (drain + 15s headroom — the stages are bounds, not durations, and process teardown lands after them). `docker run --stop-timeout 45` is documented for the one path the repo does not control.

**The number is derived, not restated.** `internal/app/shutdownbudget.go` names each stage and proves the receivers' bound with a compile-time assertion against `stream.ShutdownTimeout` / `webhook.ShutdownTimeout` (both newly exported, replacing four scattered `10 * time.Second` literals). `shutdownbudget_test.go` parses `docker-compose.yaml` and `values.yaml` and fails if either stops covering the sum, naming the file to change.

The chart **fails to render** below 45 rather than truncating a drain, with a message stating the arithmetic. `@schema minimum:45` covers `--set`; the `fail` guard covers a values file and explains *why* 45.

## Negative tests — six mutants, all caught

| Mutant | Caught by |
| --- | --- |
| `stop_grace_period: 10s` | `TestComposeStopGracePeriodCoversDrain` |
| `stop_grace_period` deleted | same, distinct "sets no stop_grace_period" branch |
| `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30` | `TestChartTerminationGracePeriodCoversDrain` |
| Template floor changed to 20 without the code | `TestChartMinimumMatchesDrain` **and** render-tests case K (2 failures) |
| `stream.ShutdownTimeout` raised to 25s | **build failure**: `constant -15000000000 overflows uint` |
| `ingressWALFlushTimeout` raised to 40s | all three tests, recomputed to a 1m15s requirement |

That last pair is the point of the design: raising a stage timeout cannot leave a stale floor behind.

## Acceptance

- [x] Deployment budgets exceed the worst supported staged drain — 45 > 30, derived and gated in both directions
- [x] Graceful-stop integration test proves final flush opportunity — **already existed**: `TestApp_RunFlushesRollupOnShutdown` (`tick_emission_test.go:84`) accumulates a rollup, runs with a 100ms context, and asserts the counter was emitted, which only the final `FlushRollup` can do. Verified still passing; no duplicate written.
- [x] Operator docs explain the budget — new "Shutdown budgets" section in `docs/installation.md` with the per-stage table, the four deployment paths and their (inadequate) defaults, and a `--stop-timeout` warning on the `docker run` path
- [x] Excessively low chart values warn or fail — they **fail**, at render time, and both 20 and 30 are covered in render-tests case K

## Deviation

`--stop-timeout` is documentation only. Nothing in the repository executes a bare `docker run`, so there is no artifact to gate it against — stated rather than left implied.

Chart bumped 0.14.8 → 0.14.9; `README.md` and `values.schema.json` regenerated. Full gate green at `ac58014`.

Follow-up correction, landed in `7cd9a84` (#341).

**My case-K render assertion was wrong, and the regenerated schema exposed it.** After `scripts/regen-generated.sh helm` produced `"terminationGracePeriodSeconds": {"minimum": 45}`, Helm rejects a low number during *values validation*, before templating:

```
Error: values do not meet the specifications of the schema(s) ...
- at /terminationGracePeriodSeconds: minimum: got 20, want 45
```

So the template `fail` guard never sees a numeric value, and case K's grep for its message failed. I had committed a guard I believed was doing the work when the schema was doing it.

**The guard is still load-bearing, for a different input.** JSON Schema `minimum` does not reject `null`. With the guard removed:

```
$ helm template t . --set terminationGracePeriodSeconds=null | grep terminationGrace
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0
```

A zero budget — SIGKILL with no drain at all, the worst possible outcome, and worse than the 30s default this issue was filed about. So the two layers cover disjoint inputs and both are needed:

| Input | Caught by |
| --- | --- |
| any number < 45 | `values.schema.json` `minimum` (fires first) |
| `null` / absent | the template `fail`, which also explains the drain arithmetic |

Case K now asserts each against its own input, and `TestChartMinimumMatchesDrain` checks **both** the template string and the schema's `minimum` against the derived requirement — so dropping the `@schema minimum:45` annotation, or removing the template guard, each fail independently. Both were negative-tested: dropping the annotation trips the Go test and case K; removing the guard trips the Go test and two case-K assertions.

Nothing about the shipped budgets changed — 45s in both paths, as committed in `ac58014`.

comments.body:
## Closing unsupported — the admin surface stays read-only

Rob's decision, 2026-07-28. Premise re-confirmed against current `main`, not the audit commit: the
scheduler still executes by cadence only (`internal/collector/scheduler.go`), so the finding is
accurate. It is being declined on posture, not because it is wrong.

**Why.** Every admin route is a GET today, and several other decisions in this tracker lean on that:

- `#322`'s CSP is `default-src 'none'` with no origin permitted in any directive, and both pages are
  inline-only. A POST control needs same-origin/CSRF handling that the current perimeter does not
  have to think about.
- `#311`'s `-preflight` is sold as "makes no non-GET request", and goes as far as forcing
  `collectors.acl.validate` off — the single POST the exporter otherwise makes — and *disclosing*
  the suppression. Adding an operator-triggered mutation to the admin surface makes that guarantee a
  per-surface caveat instead of a property of the binary.
- `#314`/`#315` fail closed on a network bind. A mutating endpoint raises the cost of any future
  mistake there from "read local status" to "trigger work on the control-plane API".

**What already covers the need.** The stated motivation is "verification and incident response
otherwise wait up to the configured interval". `-once` runs exactly one collection cycle and exits,
and `-preflight` does the same without exporting or persisting anything (#311, `ee7e206`). Both are
available in the container. That covers verification without making the long-running process mutable.

**Rejected alternatives.**

- *Default-disabled, admin-authenticated POST.* The most defensible version, and still declined: a
  config flag that turns a read-only surface mutable means the surface's security properties can no
  longer be stated without qualification, which is the actual cost.
- *Unconditionally enabled when an admin token is set.* Worse — makes every authenticated deployment
  mutable with no opt-in.
- *GET-triggered run.* Not considered seriously; a side-effecting GET is worse than the POST.

**If this is ever reversed**, the acceptance criteria on this issue stand as written (overlap
rejection, bounded timeout, unchanged cadence, same-origin/auth/rate-limit tests) and should be the
starting point. Nothing here says the design was wrong.

No code changes. Closing as unsupported per the tracker's "research issues may close as unsupported
when evidence does not justify adoption" rule and this issue's own delivery requirements.

session will read the old prohibition and undo the work.

Scope stays as the issue writes it: a reloadability matrix, SIGHUP (plus an optional watcher),
transactional validation with last-known-good retention, precise restart-required diagnostics, and no
duplicate schedulers or listeners. `#316`'s certificate reloader is NOT to be reworked onto the new
mechanism — stat-on-handshake is correct for a file a browser handshake already forces a check on,
and it keeps working with no reload signal at all.

This is the largest remaining item in the tracker and is not an ordinary parallel lane.

## #326 closed unsupported

See the closing comment on #326. The admin surface stays read-only; `-once`/`-preflight` cover the
stated need. `#322`'s CSP, `#311`'s "no non-GET request" guarantee and `#314`/`#315`'s fail-closed
binds all currently hold without qualification, and that is the property being protected.

**Remaining after this comment — P2: #300, #309, #321, #325, #327. P3: #313, #323, #324, #328,
#329, #330.**

## Closed — declined. Hot reload is not going to be built.

Rob's decision, 2026-07-28, reversing the 2026-07-28 reversal recorded on #482. The deployment
model is containers; a restart is the reload mechanism, and it is a better one than anything this
issue would have built.

**This supersedes the "#313 is IN SCOPE" comment above.** The original parking decision (#173,
`#486`) stands, and so do the two prohibitions written under it — `deploy/CLAUDE.md`'s "do not add
a SIGHUP handler or a reload route" and `docs/configuration.md`'s statement that there is no SIGHUP
and no reload endpoint. **Neither file needs editing**, which is the opposite of what the in-scope
comment instructed. #316's certificate reloader stays as it is: stat-on-handshake, correct for a
file a TLS handshake already forces a check on, and working with no reload signal at all.

## Evidence gathered before closing, worth keeping

A full read-only trace of every secret in `internal/config/secretfile.go`'s `resolveSecretFiles`
worklist — the ~17 `Secret`-bearing fields and their `*_file` siblings — found that **every single
one is captured at component-construction time. There is no per-use credential read anywhere in
the codebase.**

| consumer | mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| `tailscale.auth.apikey` | closed into `authKeyTransport{key:}` at `tsapi.NewClient` |
| `tailscale.auth.oauth.client_secret` | frozen into `clientcredentials.Config` inside the `oauth2.Transport`; the library refreshes the token, never re-reads the secret |
| `headscale.api_key` | copied into `Client.apiKey` at `hsapi.NewClient` |
| `otlp.grafana_cloud.token` | base64'd into a fixed `Authorization` header string passed to `WithHeaders` at exporter build |
| `admin.auth.token`, `prometheus.auth.token` | **not per-request.** `requireAdminAuth`/`requireMetricsAuth` are middleware *factories* called once at mux-build time; the returned closure checks a captured string |
| `streaming.token`, `webhook.secret` | copied onto `Server.token` / `Server.opts` at construction |
| `profiling.pyroscope.basic_auth_password` | frozen into `pyroscope.Config` at `Start` |
| object-store credentials (flow + audit, incl. per-tailnet) | frozen into `s3.StaticProvider` at collector build |
| `enrichment.geoip.download.license_key` | frozen into the one `*geoip.Downloader`; its periodic loop reuses that struct |

The admin/metrics tokens are the easy thing to misjudge here — the names read like per-request
gates, and only the call site shows the wrapper is built once.

Two consequences, which together are why this closed rather than shrank:

1. **"Reloadable secrets are reread safely" could not have been met by mutating config in place.**
   There is no live secret-holder to swap a value into. Honouring it means rebuilding the owning
   component — client, exporter set, mux, stream/webhook server, profiler, S3 client, GeoIP
   downloader — which runs straight at this issue's own "no duplicate schedulers or listeners"
   constraint.
2. **`App.cfg` is a plain unguarded `*config.Config`** read from ~109 non-test sites across at
   least 14 files, several of them concurrently-invoked HTTP handlers. Swapping it safely needs an
   `atomic.Pointer` plus an accessor migration across every one of those sites — mechanical, but
   wide, and touching every subsystem for a capability the deployment model does not need.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Log level + collector intervals only** (the genuinely reloadable pair: `slog.LevelVar`, no
  `LevelVar` exists in the repo today; `ticker.Reset`, since `Entry.Interval` is frozen at
  registration and `time.NewTicker` is called once per entry). Real, but it delivers a SIGHUP
  handler, a reloadability matrix and a transactional-validation path to change two values a
  container restart already changes.
- **Also making the two auth tokens live** by having the middlewares read a holder per request.
  Bounded and safe, but it does not change the verdict above.
- **Rebuilding every owning component.** Maximum capability, likeliest to ship a subtly broken
  reload, and explicitly against the issue's own constraint.

No code was written for this issue. Nothing to revert.

comments.body:
## Parked (2026-07-28)

Rob's call: **park for now. The issue stays OPEN** — it is not rejected, not stale, and not
superseded. It is simply not being worked, and no successor should re-plan it, re-scope it, or close
it as won't-do.

Why it is separable from the rest of #482: every other P1 in that tracker fixes something that is
already wrong. This one adds a storage engine to a project that has been deliberately in-memory since
`internal/flowstore` was written, which is a direction decision rather than a defect, and it carries a
dependency choice (cgo SQLite vs a pure-Go driver) that would constrain the single-static-binary
packaging promise in `CLAUDE.md` and the distroless container image.

Nothing about the current flow store blocks it. The #295/#301 work (`3de4fc7`) tightened the in-memory
path — recent rows are now ordered by event time and scoped to the query window, and `RecentRange` is
the bounded time-range read a persistent backend would also have to implement — so that seam is in
better shape for this than it was, not worse.

**If it is ever picked up, start from the dependency question, not the schema.**

## Shipped — `4b25580`

Picked up from the parked state. Per the park note, this started from the dependency question rather than the schema.

### The dependency question, answered empirically

`modernc.org/sqlite` v1.55.0, per #237's frozen decision. Not taken on trust — measured against the actual release matrix:

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `CGO_ENABLED=0` build + real SQL execution | pass |
| linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64 | **all pass** (the real binary, not a probe module) |
| binary size delta | **+4.6 MB** stripped |
| licences | BSD-3 / MIT throughout — no copyleft, SBOM-safe |
| `govulncheck` | clean |
| maintenance | releases every 1–3 weeks |

One SBOM-review trap worth recording: `go list -m all` shows a C transpiler toolchain (`modernc.org/ccgo`, `cc/v4`, `x/tools`) in the module **graph**. None of it is compiled into the binary — verified against the actual `go list -deps` import graph. It is build-time tooling for the dependency's own regeneration.

The +4.6 MB is paid by every operator, including those who never enable this. Accepted rather than hidden behind a build tag, which would mean two release artifacts and break the single-binary promise for a 4.6 MB saving.

### Design decision: raw rows, not persisted buckets

The acceptance criteria implied mirroring the memory store. I did not. It keeps fifteen capped aggregate maps per one-minute bucket; at 30-day retention that is up to 43,200 buckets × ~10k keys, and it would inherit `__other__` cap-folding that exists only because RAM is scarce.

This stores one row per connection and derives every aggregate with `GROUP BY`. Consequences, all improvements:
- Aggregates are **exact**; `Truncated` is 0 unless the write queue actually dropped, so "partial coverage" means something again.
- `RecentPage` pages the whole retained window rather than a 2,000-row ring.
- Bounding is retention sweep + hard row cap, not per-key caps.

### Acceptance

- [x] Narrow store interface implemented by memory and `modernc.org/sqlite` — `flowstore.Store`; only three call sites pinned the concrete type, and the full `internal/app` suite passed with zero handler changes.
- [x] Opt-in path, retention sweep, schema migrations, per-tailnet namespace, health — forward-only migrations refusing a newer schema; one `flows-<tailnet>.db` per tailnet; health via `Stats().Backend`.
- [x] Writes bounded/non-blocking — write-behind queue, batched transactions, drop-and-count on overflow.
- [x] Default remains stateless memory.
- [x] Container/Helm volume and backup guidance — the chart's existing `persistence:` PVC at `/var/lib/tailscale2otel` already covers it, so this is config-only; no new template.

### Two integration defects, both invisible to per-file tests

Worth recording because both came from parallelising the build, not from the design:

1. **The window clamp read `flows.retention`** (capped 24h), so a 30-day disk retention was **unreachable through the only UI that reads it**. Every query and export would have come back silently trimmed to a day. Fixed via `flowRetention()`, with a regression test.
2. **Nothing exercised `Record` → `Query`/`RecentPage` together.** Each lane's unit tests used raw SQL on the *other* side of the seam — the writer read back with SQL, the readers seeded with SQL. Added integration tests for the round trip, per-tailnet isolation, redaction, and an actual restart.

### PII — a decision, not a mechanical port

`internal/flowlog/processor.go:595` deliberately feeds the store **unfiltered** identity (#241), justified explicitly by *"the store is in memory, never leaves the process."* A file outlives the process and lands in backups, so that premise does not survive persistence.

Behaviour is therefore asymmetric: **the memory ring stays unfiltered (#241 intact); the disk path applies `pii_filter`**, reusing `internal/telemetry/pii`'s own redactor so disk classification cannot drift from OTLP's. This matches this issue's parent decision on #237's open question 2.

### Other decisions

- **Open failure switches the view OFF**, it does not fall back to memory — an operator who configured persistence and sees a working `/flows` would reasonably conclude they had history. It is **not** fatal to the process: OTLP export is the job, and an auxiliary view's unwritable directory must not take the pipeline down (`/flows` 404s, ERROR logged).
- **No new OTLP metrics.** `flowstore` is contractually "not a second telemetry pipeline", so queue depth, drops, DB size and health surface only on the admin API. Keeps `docs/metrics.md` and `docs/signal-coverage.md` out of the diff.
- **`flows.retention` and `flows.store.retention` are alternatives, not tiers.** A store is one or the other, chosen at startup. Two doc passages initially claimed they ran alongside each other with the ring serving live data — false, and corrected.
- **`flows.store.path` requires an absolute path** rather than joining #310's config-relative resolution: the tag does not match `isPathTag()`'s auto-detection, and renaming it to `directory` would break the name frozen in #237. Flagging as a deliberate, reversible deviation.

### Gate at `4b25580`

`go build` / `vet` / `test -race` (root), `golangci-lint` **0 issues**, `verify-modules.sh` all 5 modules, `regen-generated.sh` a verified fixed point, `helm lint`, `configcheck`, compose tests 40/40, `promqlcheck` (586 promql / 25 logql / 5 traceql / 223 server-side, 0 failures), `check_doc_commands.py`, python suites 38 passed, cross-compile all 5 release targets. Chart `0.30.0` → `0.31.0`.

Generated artifacts refreshed: `docs/env-vars.md`, `config.schema.json`, `docs/api/schemas/flows.schema.json` (additive, +29/−0, so no contract version bump), chart README + `values.schema.json`.

## Follow-up shipped — `5b25a5e`

Two things after `4b25580`: the config-key convention question, and a completeness audit of every surface this feature touches. The audit found the "health" acceptance criterion was met on paper but not in practice.

### Config key renamed: `flows.store.path` → `flows.store.directory`

The closing comment flagged the deviation from #310's path convention as deliberate-but-reversible. On a proper look it was simply wrong: `internal/config/paths_test.go`'s `isPathTag` states that a bare `path` is **reserved for HTTP route paths** (`webhook.path`, `streaming.path`, the node-metrics scrape path). So `path` both collided with an existing meaning and silently opted the field out of relative-path resolution.

It is now registered in `pathFields()` next to `ingress_wal.directory` — its exact precedent — so a relative value resolves against the config file rather than the process working directory. The absolute-path requirement is **gone**; it only ever existed to compensate for not being registered.

No released config is affected: `v3.0.0` predates the feature entirely, so the old key never shipped. #237's `flows.store.path` sketch is recorded in `config.go` as deliberately superseded.

### "Health" was not actually wired

`flowstore.Backend` was populated but consumed by **nothing** except the export provenance line. Concretely, a healthy persistent store rendered on the status page as:

- `Retained: 0 of 0 one-minute buckets per tailnet`
- `Estimated memory: 0 B`
- `Capacity profile: sqlite`

— all reading as *broken* rather than *not applicable*, because those fields describe the in-memory ring. Fixed:

- `statusdata.FlowStoreInfo` gains `Backend`; the status page and `/api/status.json` now report backend kind, health, **queue drops**, retained rows and on-disk size. Queue drops matter most: they mean the view is missing traffic OTLP still carried, and they are **not** `Truncated`, which counts per-minute cap folding this backend does not do.
- The status page renders backend-appropriate cards instead of the ring's numbers.
- The support bundle now carries `flow_store.json`. A stuck store was otherwise undiagnosable after the fact. Counts and health only — flow records stay unconditionally excluded, and the manifest comment claiming this sizing already travelled via `Collectors`/`Components` was inaccurate and is corrected.

**Deliberately not gating `/readyz` on it.** `componentFailureReasons()` unifies the probe and the page (#318), so adding it there would pull the pod out of service for an auxiliary admin view while OTLP export — the actual job — is fine. Same proportionality call as the open-failure behaviour. The state is loud where an operator looks instead.

### Documentation that was actively wrong

- **`docs/security.md`** asserted *"the flow store never leaves the process"* as the reason `/flows` is exempt from `pii_filter`. True only of the in-memory default — a database on disk lands in backups. Now states both, and that the persistent path **does** apply `pii_filter`.
- **`docs/flow-view.md`**'s worked YAML example still used the old key, so a copy-paste would fail startup on an unknown key (#303).
- **`tailscale.network.store.dropped`** described itself as rejections from "the local in-memory flow view". It fires for whichever backend is wired in.
- **`decodeFlowsCursor`**'s comment claimed a cursor goes stale across a restart because the seq counter resets. True of the ring; the persistent backend's `AUTOINCREMENT` rowid survives, so a shared `/flows` URL keeps its place.

Also: `flows.store` bounds now stated in the configuration reference (matching the other flows keys), compose and `deploy/CLAUDE.md` document pointing the directory at the existing state volume, `.gitignore` covers a stray `flows-*.db` and its WAL sidecars.

### Verified NOT needed

The chart requires no template change. `templates/deployment.yaml` already mounts the `persistence` PVC at `/var/lib/tailscale2otel`, and `fsGroup: 65532` / `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` already make a fresh PVC writable by the container — built for checkpoints, applies identically here.

### Gate at `5b25a5e`

`build`/`vet`/`test -race`, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, all 5 modules, regen a verified fixed point, `helm lint`, `configcheck`, compose 40/40, doc-command + python suites, cross-compile across the release matrix.

Identified during the comprehensive audit of `9401181b163417e517eb69f112fc79b78534e77e`. The audit traced poll, HEC, webhook, object-store, processor, enrichment, checkpoint, and built-in flow-view behavior end to end and checked the current Tailscale logging contracts.

## Finding and proposed scope

Problem: `parseKey` deliberately accepts timestamps from basenames and says partition directories are redundant (`internal/collector/objectstore/key.go:42-70`), but enumeration only lists `YYYY/MM/DD` prefixes (`objectstore.go:248-287`). Flat copied/recompressed objects can parse but are never discovered.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Add bounded `partitioned`, `flat`, or proven-safe `auto` layout support.
- [ ] Flat listing uses resumable pagination and cannot scan an entire unbounded bucket per cycle.
- [ ] Tests cover mixed layouts and copied extensions.
- [ ] If support is intentionally rejected, remove the misleading code/comments and document the limitation.

# Proposed epic E: Durable and trustworthy local exploration

## Delivery requirements

- [ ] Re-confirm the premise against the current implementation and upstream contract before changing behavior.
- [ ] Add a failing regression or telemetry-level test first, then implement the smallest complete change.
