## Problem

The streaming receiver caps each decompressed request body, but it has no server-wide concurrency or weighted-byte budget. A valid token holder can hold enough in-limit requests open at once to drive aggregate buffering beyond the process memory budget.

## Evidence

- `internal/stream/stream.go:268-280` defaults `maxBody` to `defaultMaxBodyBytes` (64 MiB).
- `internal/stream/stream.go:527-581` reads each request into a byte slice with `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(...))`.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:895-903` configures HTTP timeouts, but no request concurrency or aggregate buffered-byte control.
- The existing per-request decompression limit prevents one oversized body; it does not limit the sum of simultaneous valid bodies.

## Failure scenario / impact

A holder of a valid streaming token submits many concurrent, in-limit requests. Each handler buffers and parses its body independently. The process can hit memory pressure or be OOM-killed, taking the receiver down for normal senders.

## Suggested direction

Add server-wide admission control before body buffering. A weighted semaphore based on the body limit, a bounded worker pool, or a global byte budget would work. Keep the existing per-request decompression limit as a separate control.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Concurrent streaming requests are subject to a server-wide admission or aggregate-byte limit
- [ ] Rejected or timed-out requests return a clear bounded-resource response
- [ ] The existing per-request compressed and decompressed body limits remain in place
- [ ] Focused tests cover concurrent requests at and beyond the new limit
- [ ] Normal single-request streaming remains unchanged

_Found during the Codex Security repository scan, 2026-07-18. Verified against main at 5991d21195ace8cb0a554728e208f8c02778d882._

comments.body:
Two related streaming-receiver findings were filed from a Claude Security scan (2026-07-22, against 627c8b0):

- #228 — single-request CPU DoS via quadratic JSON re-parse in `unwrap` (`internal/stream/stream.go:800`).
- #229 — single-body memory amplification (~50x) via unbounded per-request record count in `extractRecords` (`internal/stream/stream.go:714`).

These are complementary to this issue, not duplicates. This issue targets *aggregate concurrency* (many valid in-limit bodies summing past the memory budget) and notes that "the per-request decompression limit prevents one oversized body." #229 refutes that specific assumption: a single 64 MiB body of tiny concatenated objects amplifies into multi-GB allocation because the cap is on bytes, not record count. A complete fix for the receiver's resource-exhaustion surface wants all three: an aggregate/concurrency budget (this issue), a per-request record cap (#229), and bounded unwrap depth + a processing deadline (#228).

Fixed in 992d7f6 (pushed to `main`), together with #228 and #229 — your comment on this issue was right that a complete fix for the receiver's resource-exhaustion surface needs all three.

A weighted semaphore (`streaming.max_concurrent_requests`, **default 4**, negative disables) is acquired **before** any body is buffered and released via `defer` on every exit path, so worst-case buffered memory is bounded at `max_concurrent_requests × max_body_bytes` regardless of how many senders arrive at once. Over-limit requests get **503** + `Retry-After: 1` + `rejected{reason=overloaded}` after a bounded 250 ms wait for a slot (which absorbs a normal burst without the queue itself becoming the backlog); the wait also aborts early if the client disconnects.

Two implementation notes worth recording:

**The slot is taken *after* the auth check, not before.** Otherwise an unauthenticated attacker could occupy the entire admission budget and deny service to legitimate senders holding a valid token — which would have turned an aggregate-memory control into a cheaper DoS than the one it fixes.

**This is the one new operator-tunable knob.** The other limits added across the three issues (record cap, unwrap depth, processing deadline) are hard-coded constants — nobody should need to tune them. This one is exposed because the correct value genuinely depends on the process memory limit, and `docs/configuration.md` says so explicitly: raise it only alongside `resources.limits.memory`.

Acceptance criteria:

- [x] Concurrent streaming requests are subject to a server-wide admission limit
- [x] Rejected/timed-out requests return a clear bounded-resource response (503 + `Retry-After`)
- [x] The existing per-request compressed and decompressed body limits remain in place
- [x] Focused tests cover concurrent requests at and beyond the limit — `TestAdmissionControl_{BeyondLimitRejectedWith503,SlotReleasedAfterRequest,NegativeDisablesLimit}`
- [x] Normal single-request streaming unchanged

Also wired through the Helm chart (`config.streaming.max_concurrent_requests`, chart 0.9.0).

title: Add aggregate admission control to the streaming receiver body buffer

## Goal

Bring the admin/status page (`internal/app`) up to (and past) meraki-dashboard-exporter's comprehensiveness while preserving what already works: single self-contained embedded template, zero CDN/external assets (air-gapped-tailnet safe), one poll loop, redacted read-only posture, one-data-model-two-representations (HTML + `/api/status.json`).

Design brainstormed and specced (spec is local-only per repo convention, not committed). Decisions locked below.

## Decisions (locked)

- **Structure:** tabbed single page — one embedded template, one poll loop, JS tab-switch (hash-deep-linkable), no reloads. Persistent header on every tab.
- **Tabs (6):** Overview · Collectors · API · Cardinality · Inventory & Catalog · Config.
- **Read-only:** no new mutating controls. Per-collector "Run now" is a follow-up (see below). Existing rDNS purge unchanged.
- **Charts:** zero-dependency SVG + vanilla-JS charting helper we own (axes, gridlines, multi-series, hover crosshair/tooltip). No third-party library. Sparklines stay in dense tables.
- **Polish:** refreshed design-token system + light/dark auto (`prefers-color-scheme` + manual toggle, `localStorage`).
- **Multi-tailnet:** combined view + per-tailnet breakdown on Overview (today's model). No per-tailnet selector.
- **Cardinality:** full meraki-parity suite.
- **Label-level data:** extend the fingerprint `CardinalityTracker` to retain **bounded** per-label-key distinct values (cap default 100, "≥N (capped)" overflow), so label-level views work under `self_observability.enabled` alone — no second opt-in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tabbed single-page layout; persistent header; hash deep-linking; `<noscript>` still renders all sections stacked
- [ ] Refreshed design tokens + working light/dark toggle (persisted)
- [ ] Zero-dependency charting helper (axes/gridlines/multi-series/hover); used for total-series, runtime, and latency time-series; no third-party lib on the page
- [ ] Overview: new health roll-up strip (collectors ok/failing/stale, last export age, total active series)
- [ ] Collectors: new data-freshness column (age of last *successful* run, badged ok/warning/stale)
- [ ] API: new auth & throughput panel (auth method, token type, OAuth-refresh/API-key-expiry warning, total calls, total 429s)
- [ ] Cardinality suite: summary cards, real total-series chart, top-metrics, high-cardinality-labels, growth-rate, threshold recommendations + critical/warning alerts, drill-down (all-metrics / all-labels / per-metric label-values), JSON export
- [ ] `CardinalityTracker` extended: bounded per-label-key distinct values + per-metric history rings; nil-receiver no-ops preserved; self-exclusion + per-metric cap preserved
- [ ] `CardinalityConfig` gains `WarningThreshold` / `CriticalThreshold` / `LabelValueSampleCap`; wired into defaults + `Validate()`
- [ ] Config tab: redacted-config JSON download (read-only)
- [ ] All new cardinality panels degrade gracefully when self-obs off (existing "enable self-observability" prompt pattern)
- [ ] Four generated artifacts regenerated (`docs/metrics.md`, `docs/env-vars.md`, Helm README, `values.schema.json`); `config.example.yaml` + `docs/configuration.md` updated for new keys
- [ ] Full gate green: `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` + `golangci-lint run`; DTO builders + tracker + template render + config validation covered by tests

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Per-collector "Run now" / any mutating control
- Vendored charting library / interactive zoom-pan
- Per-tailnet selector/filter
- Sourcing label values from the Prometheus registry (chose tracker extension instead)

## Approach

Four disjoint build lanes, seams frozen first: (A) tracker + config + sampler; (B) DTO + status builders; (C) template + CSS + JS + charts; (D) read-only JSON handlers. One wiring pass regenerates artifacts and runs the full gate. One commit per feature per repo convention.

## Problem

The retry transport caps exponential backoff at `maxDelay`, then replaces that capped delay with an arbitrary positive `Retry-After` value.

Most collectors use an app-lifetime parent context, so an upstream response can park a collector inside one logical request for hours.

## Evidence

- `internal/tsapi/transport.go:228-233` computes capped backoff, then assigns `sleep = ra` without applying `maxDelay`.
- `internal/tsapi/transport.go:251-256` waits for that full duration unless the parent request context is cancelled.
- `internal/tsapi/transport.go:442-457` accepts both numeric seconds and future HTTP dates.
- The comment at `internal/tsapi/transport.go:65-68` confirms long `Retry-After` values are intentionally outside the per-attempt timeout.

## Failure scenario / impact

The API returns `429 Retry-After: 21600`. One collector sleeps for six hours while the process heartbeat and unrelated collectors continue running. The configured retry maximum does not protect it, and recovery depends on request-context cancellation or a restart.

## Suggested direction

Clamp parsed `Retry-After` values to `maxDelay`. If respecting a longer server delay is required, return a retryable error to the scheduler instead of sleeping inside the API request for that duration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Numeric `Retry-After` values are capped at `maxDelay`
- [ ] HTTP-date values are capped the same way
- [ ] Shorter valid values are still honoured exactly
- [ ] Malformed, zero and past values retain their current behavior
- [ ] Cancellation still interrupts the wait immediately
- [ ] Tests cover both header formats above and below the cap

_Found during the pre-major release review, 2026-07-17. Verified against main at bd93ee2._

comments.body:
## Documentation touchpoints

- Update the [HTTP retry semantics](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/blob/bd93ee2/docs/configuration.md#L208-L226) to state whether `Retry-After` is capped and what limit applies.
- Review the generated [`api.duration` and retry definitions](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/blob/bd93ee2/docs/metrics.md#L102-L120). The docs must say whether `Retry-After` wait remains included in `api.duration`.
- If any metric descriptions change, update the in-code catalog & regenerate `docs/metrics.md`; do not edit the generated section directly.
Picking this up now (Wave 2). Clamping parsed `Retry-After` (numeric and HTTP-date) to `max_delay`.

Done in d581993. Parsed `Retry-After` (numeric seconds and HTTP-date) is now clamped to `max_delay`: `sleep = min(ra, maxDelay)`. A short `Retry-After` is still honoured exactly; malformed/zero/past values keep falling through to the jittered exponential backoff; request-context cancellation still interrupts the wait. Tests cover both header formats above and below the cap. Docs note that the wait counts toward `api.duration`.

title: Cap Retry-After delays at the configured retry maximum

body:
## Problem

Webhook signature validation rejects timestamps older than the configured tolerance but accepts timestamps arbitrarily far in the future.

Using a two-sided clock-skew window would prevent a future-dated signed request from remaining replayable long after it was first accepted.

## Evidence

- `internal/webhook/webhook.go:395-399` checks only `ts.Before(now-tolerance)`.
- There is no matching `ts.After(now+tolerance)` check before signature validation.

## Failure scenario / impact

A correctly signed request with a timestamp one day in the future is accepted immediately. The same captured request remains valid until that future timestamp plus the configured tolerance, extending its replay window from minutes to more than a day.

The attacker still needs a legitimately signed request, but the one-sided timestamp check weakens replay protection.

## Suggested direction

Capture `now` once and reject timestamps before `now-tolerance` or after `now+tolerance`. Keep the comparison inclusive at the documented boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Timestamps older than the tolerance are rejected
- [ ] Timestamps newer than the tolerance are rejected
- [ ] Both exact tolerance boundaries are tested
- [ ] A timestamp within the allowed clock-skew window remains valid
- [ ] Rejection metrics and logs distinguish or consistently classify future timestamp failures

_Found during the pre-major release review, 2026-07-17. Verified against main at bd93ee2._

comments.body:
## Documentation touchpoints

- Update the [webhook tolerance documentation](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/blob/bd93ee2/docs/configuration.md#L640-L654) so it describes the allowed clock-skew window in both directions.
- Review the generated [webhook receiver signals](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/blob/bd93ee2/docs/metrics.md#L433-L450). If rejection reasons or descriptions change, update the in-code catalog & regenerate `docs/metrics.md`.

For #201 the durability decision is: atomic two-phase — reject structural truncation and known-record decode failures with a non-2xx (no partial emit), still skip genuinely-unknown future record types.

## Problem

Graceful shutdown gives every telemetry pipeline and every tailnet provider one shared 10-second context, then shuts them down sequentially.

A blocked metric exporter can consume the whole budget before logs, traces or later tailnets get a chance to flush.

## Evidence

- `internal/app/app.go:577-579` creates one 10-second shutdown context.
- `internal/telemetry/provider.go:370-375` shuts down metrics, logs and traces sequentially with that context.
- `internal/telemetry/providerset.go:93-104` shuts down the process provider and each tailnet provider sequentially with the same context.

## Failure scenario / impact

The first tailnet's metrics exporter blocks until the shared deadline. Every later shutdown call receives an already-expired context, so buffered logs, traces and telemetry for other tailnets are dropped even if their backends are healthy.

This undermines the receiver join and rollup flush immediately before shutdown.

## Suggested direction

Start independent pipeline and provider shutdowns concurrently under a bounded overall deadline. Use child budgets where needed so one pipeline cannot consume another pipeline's opportunity to flush.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A blocked metric exporter does not prevent logs or traces from shutting down
- [ ] A blocked provider does not prevent other tailnet providers from shutting down
- [ ] Total shutdown time remains bounded
- [ ] Errors from every attempted shutdown are retained with `errors.Join`
- [ ] A blocking-exporter test proves the independent pipelines are called before the deadline

_Found during the pre-major release review, 2026-07-17. Verified against main at bd93ee2._

Implementing against `main` with strict TDD; will land as a single `Closes #204` commit. For #201 the durability decision is: atomic two-phase — reject structural truncation and known-record decode failures with a non-2xx (no partial emit), still skip genuinely-unknown future record types.

Done in c7f4f1e. `shutdownAll` now runs the metric/log/trace pipelines and the process + per-tailnet providers concurrently under the single overall deadline, each with its own child context, joining every error — a blocked exporter can no longer consume another pipeline's flush budget. Added a `lockedWriter` so the three stdout exporters don't interleave/data-race now that they shut down concurrently. ## Problem

The Helm chart accepts any integer `replicaCount`, even though tailscale2otel is a singleton poller with no leader election or shared checkpoint coordination.

The chart warns operators not to scale it but still renders a multi-replica Deployment.

## Evidence

- `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/templates/deployment.yaml:8-11` calls the workload a singleton but passes `replicaCount` directly to `spec.replicas`.

Enforce exactly one replica in the generated schema and add a template-level failure as a second guard. Remove that restriction only after leader election and shared checkpoint semantics exist.

- [ ] The generated values schema carries the restriction

## Problem

A positive `max_window <= interval` guarantees that a backlogged flow-log or audit-log poller can never catch up, but configuration validation only emits a warning.

At equality, the backlog never shrinks. Below equality, it grows on every tick.

#52 deliberately implemented this as a warning. The next major release is the right boundary to turn the guaranteed-bad configuration into a validation error.

## Evidence

- `internal/config/validate.go:210-229` detects this configuration in `Warnings()`.
- The condition applies to both `flowlogs` and `auditlogs` using a polling source.
- `internal/config/validate.go:535-565` already hard-errors other timing combinations that make collection permanently incorrect, including invalid lookback and lag values.

## Failure scenario / impact

A collector with `interval: 1m` and `max_window: 30s` advances its checkpoint by at most 30 seconds each minute. Its exported data becomes another 30 seconds older on every cycle while the service remains healthy and ready.

With both values at one minute, it remains permanently behind after any outage or initial backlog.

## Suggested direction

Make this a validation error for the next major version. Keep `max_window: 0` as the explicit no-cap sentinel. If there is a valid reason to allow permanent lag, require a clearly named opt-in rather than accepting it by default.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Polling flow logs reject positive `max_window <= interval`
- [ ] Polling audit logs reject the same configuration
- [ ] `max_window: 0` remains valid
- [ ] Stream-only collectors are unaffected
- [ ] Tests cover equality, below, above and zero
- [ ] Configuration docs describe the hard validation rule

body:
## Problem

The stream receiver can discard part of a request and still return `200 Success`. Once acknowledged, the sender has no reason to retry the lost records.

This behavior is deliberate: #96 introduced valid-prefix salvage and #67 made skipped records observable. The durability contract needs an explicit decision before the next major version.

## Evidence

- `internal/stream/stream.go:607-682` preserves a valid prefix after mid-stream corruption and discards the suffix.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:328-344` accepts that partial result.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:350-410` skips unclassified records and records that fail typed decoding.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:382-386` explicitly says the request still returns 200.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:434` sends the success acknowledgement.

## Failure scenario / impact

A truncated concatenated batch contains 60 valid records followed by corruption. The receiver emits the 60, drops the suffix and returns success.

A wire-format change can also make known records fail typed decoding while every request continues to be acknowledged. Metrics expose the loss, but the records are permanently gone.

## Suggested direction

Prefer two-phase processing: parse and type-check the complete batch before emitting anything, then reject the request with a non-2xx response if the batch is structurally incomplete or a known record is malformed.

Decide the policy for genuinely unknown future record types separately. If success-after-drop remains intentional, document it as an at-most-once lossy contract and surface a degraded health state plus an alert, not only counters and logs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The stream batch delivery contract is explicit in code and user documentation
- [ ] A corrupt suffix cannot be acknowledged as full success without an explicit, documented product decision
- [ ] Atomic rejection does not emit a partial prefix before returning non-2xx
- [ ] Tests cover corrupt suffixes, known-record decode failures and the chosen unknown-record policy
- [ ] If lossy ACK behavior remains, health and shipped alerts expose active record loss

_Found during the pre-major release review, 2026-07-17. Verified against main at bd93ee2._

For #201 the durability decision is: atomic two-phase — reject structural truncation and known-record decode failures with a non-2xx (no partial emit), still skip genuinely-unknown future record types.

Done in cfa330a (breaking), per the agreed contract: **atomic two-phase + forward-compatible unknown types**. Phase 1 classifies and typed-decodes the complete batch, staging records without emitting. Structural corruption/truncation (`rejected{reason=malformed}`) or a known flow/audit record that fails typed decoding (`rejected{reason=decode_error}`) rejects the whole request with 400 and emits nothing, so the sender retries. Phase 2 emits only once the batch is fully understood. Genuinely-unknown future record types stay skipped+counted and the batch still returns 200. Replaces the #96 valid-prefix salvage. Reuses existing `rejected`/`decode_errors` signals (no new metric).

## Problem

The fix for #84 bounds connection setup, TLS and response headers, but not the token response body read. A token endpoint can send valid headers and then stall forever while `x/oauth2` reads the body.

This affects both OAuth client credentials and workload identity.

## Evidence

- `internal/tsapi/auth.go:99-110` returns an `http.Client` with transport timeouts but no `http.Client.Timeout`.
- Both token sources are built from `context.Background()` with that client.
- `x/oauth2` reads the token response body after headers have arrived.
- `oauth2.ReuseTokenSource` serialises refresh callers, so one stalled refresh blocks every caller sharing the source.
- `internal/tsapi/auth_test.go:12-64` and `internal/tsapi/workloadidentity_test.go:216-270` only test a server that never sends headers.

## Failure scenario / impact

The token endpoint returns `200`, flushes the headers and starts a chunked JSON body, then stops sending data. `ResponseHeaderTimeout` has already completed successfully, there is no overall deadline, and the refresh never returns.

All collectors using that token source then block behind the refresh mutex.

## Suggested direction

Set an overall timeout on the token-fetch client or give each token fetch a deadline that remains active through the complete response body read.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] OAuth client-credentials token fetches are bounded through the full body read
- [ ] Workload-identity token exchanges have the same bound
- [ ] Tests flush successful headers and a partial body, then prove the request times out
- [ ] Existing no-header timeout tests continue to pass
- [ ] Callers recover with an error instead of remaining blocked

body:
## Problem

The node-metrics collector drops labels before calculating cumulative deltas. If a dropped label distinguishes two source counters, both counters share one baseline and corrupt each other's output.

Targets with the same effective identity can collide for the same reason. Static duplicates are retained, and validation only requires a URL.

#98 fixed discovered instance-label churn. It did not address source-series baseline identity or duplicate static targets.

## Evidence

- `internal/collector/nodemetrics/nodemetrics.go:784-786` builds attributes, drops labels, then calls `delta`.
- `internal/collector/nodemetrics/nodemetrics.go:873-874` keys the baseline by metric name and those post-drop attributes.
- `internal/collector/nodemetrics/nodemetrics.go:603-618` appends every static target, including duplicates.
- `internal/config/validate.go:611-619` only checks that each enabled static target has a URL.

## Failure scenario / impact

Given:

- `requests_total{peer="a"} = 100`, then `110`
- `requests_total{peer="b"} = 200`, then `210`
- `drop_labels: ["peer"]`

Both source counters get the same baseline key. The first scrape can emit a false `100`; the next can be treated as a reset and emit `210`, instead of suppressing the first observation and emitting a combined delta of `20`.

The curated counter uses the same bad delta.

## Suggested direction

Key the baseline from the complete source label set plus a stable target identity. Apply `drop_labels` only to the emitted attributes. Validate or deduplicate static URLs and reject colliding effective target identities.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Baseline keys retain every source label, including labels omitted from output
- [ ] Baseline keys include a stable target identity
- [ ] Two source counters merging onto one emitted series produce the sum of their correct deltas
- [ ] Duplicate static targets and effective identity collisions are rejected or deterministically deduplicated
- [ ] Tests cover counters, histogram components and curated counters

_Found during the pre-major release review, 2026-07-17. Verified against main at bd93ee2._

## Problem

IP redaction only recognises a bare address. Values formatted as `host:port` fall through to the key's fallback category, even when the host is a Tailscale, internal or external IP.

The default node-metrics identity uses exactly this format.

## Evidence

- `internal/telemetry/pii/ipclass.go:29` only calls `netip.ParseAddr`.
- `internal/telemetry/pii/registry.go:41` marks `tailscale.node` as IP-valued.
- `internal/telemetry/pii/registry.go:49` falls back to `CatHostnames` when parsing fails.
- `docs/node-metrics.md:196-198` says an omitted `instance` defaults to the URL's `host:port`.
- `internal/collector/nodemetrics/nodemetrics.go:940-946` implements that default.

## Failure scenario / impact

With:

- `pii_filter.tailscale_ips: false`
- `pii_filter.hostnames: true`
- a default node identity of `<tailnet-ip-1>:5252`

`netip.ParseAddr` fails, the value is classified as a hostname, and the Tailscale IP is exported. The categories are documented as independent, but this combination leaks a category that was explicitly disabled.

Bracketed IPv6 values have the same problem.

## Suggested direction

Parse `netip.AddrPort` before falling back to `netip.ParseAddr`, including bracketed IPv6 and relevant zone forms. Classification must be based on the address portion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] IPv4 `host:port` values are classified by their address
- [ ] Bracketed IPv6 `host:port` values are classified by their address
- [ ] Bare IPv4 and IPv6 behavior is unchanged
- [ ] Category cross-product tests prove `tailscale_ips`, `internal_ips`, `external_ips` and `hostnames` remain independent

## Problem

`otelEmitter.LogEvent` applies the PII redactor to log attributes, then emits `Event.Body` unchanged. This breaks the documented contract that disabled PII categories remove those identifiers from logs and that every log body is fixed, generic and identifier-free.

#115 correctly fixed two safe body examples, but it also introduced that blanket claim. The claim does not match the other emit sites.

## Evidence

- `internal/telemetry/emitter.go:276-294` redacts `ev.Attrs` at line 277 and passes `ev.Body` directly to `SetBody` at line 284.
- `docs/configuration.md:665-713` says disabled categories remove identifiers from metrics and logs, and lines 692-713 say log bodies never contain free-text identifiers.
- `internal/flowlog/processor.go:384` puts the raw source and destination addresses in the body.
- `internal/webhook/webhook.go:438` uses the raw webhook message.
- `internal/collector/keys/keys.go:220-221` uses `keyLabel`, which prefers the key description and falls back to its ID.
- `internal/collector/oauthapps/oauthapps.go:113-115` includes the app name.
- `internal/collector/devices/devices.go:688` and `internal/collector/logstream/logstream.go:147` export upstream error text unchanged.

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator disables `tailscale_ips`, `node_ids`, `hostnames` or `free_text_details` based on the documented contract. The matching attributes disappear, but the same values still leave the process in the log body.

The result is a privacy and compliance defect.

## Suggested direction

Make log bodies generic and move variable detail into classified attributes. If variable bodies are a requirement, add category-aware body redaction before `SetBody`.

The generic-body approach matches the contract added in #115 and is easier to test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disabled PII categories remove matching values from both log attributes and bodies
- [ ] Every production log event is covered by sentinel tests that inject identifiers into all available fields
- [ ] Tests cover each PII category independently
- [ ] `docs/configuration.md` describes the implemented behavior accurately

body:
## Summary

#187 removed `service.version` from the **metrics** resource, so tailscale2otel's own series no longer
carry a `service_version` label. Verified live. But the fix deliberately **kept** `service.version` on
the **traces** resource, and Grafana Cloud's Tempo **metrics-generator** derives Prometheus series from
spans — promoting span resource attributes to labels. So the exact per-build churn #187 fixed still
happens, on the generated span metrics.

This was found while live-verifying #187 and is **not** a regression from it — it predates the fix. #187
just made it the only remaining surface.

## Live evidence (<host-1>, 2026-07-17)

Every series in the stack still carrying `service_version` for `job="tailscale2otel"`:

```
traces_spanmetrics_calls_total
traces_spanmetrics_latency
traces_spanmetrics_size_total
traces_target_info
```

All four are Tempo-generated. tailscale2otel's own metrics are clean — `target_info{job="tailscale2otel"}`
carries `service_name` / `service_instance_id` / `process_runtime_version` / `telemetry_sdk_version` and
**no** `service_version`, and `count({__name__=~"tailscale.*", service_version!=""})` returns empty.

The churn is real, not theoretical — `count by (service_version) (traces_spanmetrics_calls_total{job="tailscale2otel"})`
over 6h:

| `service_version` | series |
| --- | --- |
| `48b8ae5` (current) | 90 |
| `4ab2311` (previous) | 54 |

Both versions coexist, so `sum(rate(traces_spanmetrics_calls_total))`-style RED panels double across a redeploy
for the lookback window — the graph2otel#104 artifact, on a different metric family.

## Why it is NOT obviously a bug

`traces_target_info` carrying the version is **correct** — that is the info-metric pattern, the traces-side
equivalent of `target_info`. The question is only the `traces_spanmetrics_*` dimension. And unlike the
exporter's own metrics, version-on-RED is a legitimate, widely-used dimension (canary / cross-version
latency comparison). Dropping `service.version` from the traces resource would also lose per-span version
attribution in Tempo, which is genuinely useful when debugging "which build produced this trace".

Scope is also small: ~90 series per version here, only when `tracing.enabled` AND the metrics-generator
are on — versus the thousands of flow series #187 was protecting.

## Options

1. **Leave it (default recommendation).** Version on spans is useful; spanmetrics cardinality is small;
   `traces_target_info` is the correct info metric. Accept a brief RED-panel artifact on redeploy.
2. **Configure the generator.** The churn is a *backend* dimension choice. Excluding `service_version`
   from the Tempo metrics-generator dimensions keeps version on spans (useful) while dropping it from the
   generated series (the churn). This is the surgical fix, but it is Grafana Cloud tenant config, not repo code.
3. **Drop `service.version` from the traces resource** (logs-only, mirroring the metrics split). Kills the
   churn in-repo, but loses version on spans in Tempo and empties `traces_target_info`'s version. Least
   attractive — it trades a useful signal for a small artifact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Decide between the options above — **option 1 accepted** (Rob, 2026-07-17): "we can live with tempo adding the version to the labels those are just spanmetrics"
- [x] ~~If 2: confirm the generator dimension change~~ — N/A, option 2 not taken
- [x] Reasoning recorded in `internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md` next to the #187 note (`bd93ee2`)

comments.body:
## Decided: option 1 — accept, document, close

Rob, 2026-07-17: "we can live with tempo adding the version to the labels those are just spanmetrics."

If the redeploy artifact ever matters, the fix is backend-side (exclude `service_version` from the generator's dimensions), keeping it on spans and off the generated series.

## Summary

`scripts/regen-generated.sh` claims in its own header that it "mirrors CI exactly ... so local output
is byte-identical to what CI expects". That was **false** for both helm artifacts, and the failure mode
was silent corruption rather than an error.

Surfaced while working #187: running the script produced an unrelated diff in
`deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/README.md` (the version footer vanished), which would have been committed
as churn had it not been spotted.

## Root cause

The script invoked whatever `helm-docs` / `helm-values-schema-json` happened to be on `PATH`, with **no
version pin and no verification**, while CI pins the *actions* (which each install one specific tool
binary).

**The helm-docs ldflag trap (the interesting one).** The local binary was `go install`ed and was
*already the correct version* (v1.14.2) — so a naive version check would have passed. helm-docs takes
its version from a **build-time ldflag** (`var version string` in package main), not Go build info, so
`go install` leaves it **empty**. The README template's footer is guarded by
`{{ if .HelmDocsVersion }}`, so an empty version **silently drops the whole footer** — a
plausible-but-wrong README that differs from CI's. (Same reason `helm-docs --version` failed with
"unknown flag": cobra only registers `--version` when Version is non-empty.) Upstream release binaries
are built by goreleaser, whose default ldflags set `-X main.version={{.Version}}`.

**helm-values-schema-json** was simply not installed, so the script SKIPped it entirely — the artifact
was only ever gated in CI, never reproducible locally.

**Action version ≠ tool version.** `losisin/helm-values-schema-json-action@v3.0.1` installs tool
**v2.5.0** (baked into the action's `dist/index.js` as `version$1`). Nothing recorded that mapping.

## Change

- **Pin both tool versions** in `scripts/regen-generated.sh` (`helm-docs v1.14.2`,
  `helm-values-schema-json v2.5.0`), documented against the actions that install them.
- **New `tools` target** — `scripts/regen-generated.sh tools` installs exactly those, passing the
  helm-docs version ldflag goreleaser would. `all` deliberately does NOT install (stays
  side-effect-free for the pre-commit hook).
- **Verify before regenerating.** A missing, mismatched, or version-less tool is now a loud SKIP naming
  the exact fix, instead of writing a wrong file. This closes the silent-corruption path.
- Pointer comments in `.github/workflows/helm.yml` so a Renovate bump of either action prompts
  updating the pins; docs in root `CLAUDE.md` + `deploy/CLAUDE.md`.
- `.gitignore`: `__pycache__/` + `*.py[cod]` (created by running the dashboard/alert generators).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `scripts/regen-generated.sh` regenerates all four artifacts byte-identically to the committed copies
- [x] Both helm tools installable via a documented one-shot command, at the versions CI uses
- [x] A wrong/missing/version-less tool SKIPs loudly and does NOT modify the artifact
- [x] The action↔tool version mapping and the ldflag gotcha are recorded where they'll be found

comments.body:
Done in `48b8ae5`.

**Verified from a clean slate:** removed both binaries → `scripts/regen-generated.sh tools` installed the pinned pair → full regen reproduced all four artifacts byte-for-byte (`git diff --quiet` on `deploy/helm` + `docs/`).

**Failure modes exercised, not assumed** (via PATH shims) — each SKIPs with the exact fix and leaves the artifact untouched:

| case | result |
| --- | --- |
| helm-docs built without the version ldflag (the bug that bit us) | `SKIP … reports no version (likely 'go install'ed without the version ldflag) … Fix: scripts/regen-generated.sh tools` |
| helm-docs at a different version than CI | `SKIP … is 1.13.0 but CI uses 1.14.2 … (its output would differ)` |
| tool absent entirely | `SKIP … not installed (CI will gate it)` |

## Summary

`service.version` is promoted from the OTel resource to a **`service_version` label on every metric series** (see the `telemetry` package — the build-info catalog doc notes "the service version is promoted from the resource as `service_version`"). Per the OTel→Prometheus compatibility spec this is a deviation: version belongs on an **info metric** (`target_info` from the resource, or the existing `*_build_info` gauge), **never as a label on every series**.

## Why it matters (even though this repo doesn't visibly break)

Only `service.name`(+`service.namespace`)→`job` and `service.instance.id`→`instance` are meant to become labels; every other resource attribute — including `service.version` — goes to `target_info` by the spec. Putting version on every series means **each new build mints a whole new series set**; during the query-lookback window after a redeploy, the old-version and new-version series coexist, and any `sum`-style panel adds both → a transient multiplier.

This repo runs **stable release tags**, so it rarely restarts onto a *different* version and the artifact stays invisible — but it's the same anti-pattern, and it inflates active-series cardinality by the number of versions ever seen. (It surfaced loudly in the sibling `graph2otel`, which runs the `:main` per-commit build — see rknightion/graph2otel#104, which has the full OTLP→Prometheus spec analysis.)

## Change

- Keep `service.version` on the OTel **resource** (semconv-correct → flows to `target_info`).
- Stop promoting it to a per-series label; rely on the existing `*_build_info{version=...}` gauge (and/or `target_info`) for version, joined via `group_left` where a panel needs it.
- Audit dashboards/alerts for any query that aggregates over or filters on `service_version` and repoint them at the info metric.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `service_version` no longer appears as a label on ordinary metric series (see the closing comment: it is now on **neither** ordinary series **nor** `target_info`; the version's metrics home is `tailscale2otel_build_info{version=...}`)
- [x] Version remains queryable via the build-info gauge (+ a documented `group_left` example)
- [x] Dashboards/alerts updated if any referenced `service_version`
- [x] Note the OTLP→Prometheus resource-attribute convention in the telemetry package docs

Cross-repo consistency with rknightion/graph2otel#104 (which carries the detailed spec citations).

comments.body:
## Done in `1658133` — with one deviation from this issue as filed

### The filed premise was wrong: this repo never promoted `service.version`

`buildResource` only ever put `service.version` on the **OTel resource** — which is exactly what this
issue's Change bullet 1 ("keep `service.version` on the OTel resource") asks for as the fix. The local
Prometheus exporter (`internal/telemetry/prometheus.go:14`) has no `WithResourceAsConstantLabels`, so on
the `/metrics` pull endpoint it was already `target_info`-only.

The per-series `service_version` label came **entirely from Grafana Cloud's OTLP ingest**, which promotes
the whole `service.*` resource namespace. That is backend-side and has **no exporter lever**. So bullet 1
as written would have shipped a no-op: keeping the attribute on the metrics resource is precisely what
causes the promotion.

graph2otel#104 already resolved this fork — its own comment concedes "backend promotion isn't reliably
controllable per-service", and its **shipped** fix (`519c002`) did the opposite of bullet 1: drop
`service.version` from the metrics resource. Since this issue asks for cross-repo consistency with #104,
that is what landed here.

### What shipped

**Resource split** (`provider.go`): `buildResource(ctx, opts, includeServiceVersion)` — metrics get
`false`, logs/traces get `true`. Logs/traces are never summed and have no per-series label surface, so
version attribution stays there.

**`build_info` carries the version again.** `d82d71d` had removed it *because* it collided with the
promoted resource label (`otlp_parse_error`); with the resource attr gone, the collision is gone, so
`tailscale2otel_build_info{version=...}` is restored as the single metrics-side version surface. The key
is **`version`, not `service.version`** — the latter normalizes to `service_version` and would re-enter
the promoted namespace.

**`reservedPromotedLabels` drops `service_version`.** It listed labels GC promotes so the Emitter can
drop a colliding data-point attr; the metrics resource no longer carries `service.version`, so reserving
it would be stale (and would wrongly drop a legitimate attr citing a promoted label that doesn't exist).

**Dashboards.** The flagship generator's `sv()` helper existed only to strip the churning label
(`max without (service_version)`). Deleted, along with all **62** call sites — verified byte-identical to
an identity-`sv()` regeneration, so the unwrap is provably behaviour-preserving. Build info panels
(flagship + the legacy `tailscale-exporter-health.json`, which also read the old label) now read
`version`. `service_version` no longer appears anywhere in the dashboard JSON.

**Alerts.** No expr change needed — rules already aggregate with `max by (<real dims>)`, which is robust
regardless. Only the now-dangling rationale in the generator docstring was corrected.

### Deviation from AC1 — read this before querying

AC1 said `service_version` should remain "only on `target_info` / `*_build_info`". **It is now on
neither.** `target_info` is derived from the metrics resource, so dropping the attribute there removes it
from `target_info` too. That trade-off is inherent to the only implementable fix, and graph2otel accepted
the same. The version's metrics home is `tailscale2otel_build_info{version=...}`:

```promql
tailscale_devices_count_ratio * on (job) group_left(version) tailscale2otel_build_info_ratio
```

**Join on `job`, not `instance`** — `build_info` is emitted by the **process** provider while tailnet
signals come from per-tailnet providers with deliberately distinct `service.instance.id`, so
`on (job, instance)` matches nothing. Documented in `internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md`.

### Verification

Full gate green: `go build` · `go vet` · `go test -race ./...` · `golangci-lint run` (0 issues) ·
`metricscatalog -check` in sync.

Beyond the unit tests, the production pipeline was driven end-to-end (real emitter + reserved-label guard
+ real stdout exporter), since the recorder-based `build_info` tests have no reserved set and so never
exercise the guard that previously dropped this attribute:

```
METRICS RESOURCE carries service.version: false
build_info carries version label:        true
build_info version value present:        true
```

Regression guards: `TestProvider_MetricsResourceOmitsServiceVersion` (metrics resource omits it, logs
resource keeps it) and `TestApp_RunGracefulShutdown` now asserts the injected version reaches
`build_info` through real `newApp` wiring.

### Not done (deliberate)

`internal/app/profiling.go` still tags Pyroscope with `service_version`. That is a **profile** tag, not a
Prometheus series label — no series-doubling surface, and version attribution is the entire point of
diffing flamegraphs across builds. Out of scope.

## Verified live on <host-1> (2026-07-17)

Closing comment above noted the backend-side claim was unproven locally. Now confirmed against live Grafana Cloud data, with <host-1> running `48b8ae5`.

**The version moved to the info metric, and GC's promotion no longer picks it up:**

```
tailscale2otel_build_info_ratio{
  instance="<host-1>", job="tailscale2otel",
  service_instance_id="<host-1>", service_name="tailscale2otel",
  tailscale2otel_provider="tailscale",
  go_version="go1.26.5-X:goroutineleakprofile",
  version="48b8ae5"
}
```

`service_name` and `service_instance_id` ARE promoted from the resource — proving GC's promotion is active — while `service_version` is absent because the metrics resource no longer carries it. The `version` label is present and correct.

**AC1 confirmed:** `count({__name__=~"tailscale.*", service_version!=""})` → **empty**. No tailscale series carries the label.

**target_info:** `target_info{job="tailscale2otel"}` carries `service_name`, `service_instance_id`, `process_runtime_version`, `telemetry_sdk_version` — and no `service_version`. This is the AC1 deviation flagged above, now observed rather than predicted: the version is on `build_info` only.

**Dashboard:** the flagship dashboard was regenerated and pushed to the live stack (generation 13→14). It had been stale by 6 panels from earlier unpushed work; the push was purely additive (292→298 panels, 0 removed, no hand-edits present). Live spec now byte-matches the committed JSON and contains zero `service_version` references.

**One surface remains, filed as #195:** the Tempo metrics-generator still emits `service_version` on `traces_spanmetrics_*` (the traces resource deliberately keeps `service.version`). Live churn is real there — 6h window shows `48b8ae5` (90 series) and `4ab2311` (54 series) coexisting. Not a regression from this issue; it predates it and is arguably a legitimate dimension. See #195 for the decision.

title: Don't promote service.version to a per-series metric label (OTLP→Prometheus: version belongs on target_info/build_info)

body:
## What happened

The v2.0.1 release run ([job 86937330205](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/actions/runs/29285590705/job/86937330205)) had GoReleaser succeed end-to-end — binaries, archives, SBOMs, SHA256SUMS, and the cosign signature all published to the v2.0.1 release — but the **Attest build provenance** step failed with:

```
Error: Invalid digest: {"mediaType":"application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json", ...
```

## Root cause

In the shared reusable `rknightion/.github/.github/workflows/binaries.yml`, the "Locate checksums" step used `find dist ... -name '*SHA256SUMS*' | head -1`. Cosign writes `tailscale2otel_2.0.1_SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json` next to `tailscale2otel_2.0.1_SHA256SUMS`, both match the glob, and `find`'s ordering is unspecified — this run it picked the signature bundle and fed it to `actions/attest-build-provenance` as the checksums file.

## Fix

- [x] Shared workflow fixed upstream: exclude `*.sigstore.json`/`*.sig`/`*.pem`/`*.intoto.jsonl` and `sort` for determinism — rknightion/.github@d1c590b295b9d7f2535fadc7bc5e74f2eddbd512
- [ ] Repin this repo's `release-please.yml` `binaries` job to the fixed SHA

## Impact on v2.0.1

None worth re-cutting for: the release is complete (binaries, SBOMs, checksums, cosign `.sigstore.json` signature). Only the `.intoto.jsonl` provenance asset is missing for this one release; a job re-run would still use the old pinned SHA, and backfilling provenance from a different workflow run would record misleading builder identity. Future releases get it via the repin.

comments.body: Fixed. Shared workflow patched in rknightion/.github@d1c590b295b9d7f2535fadc7bc5e74f2eddbd512 (exclude `.sigstore.json`/`.sig`/`.pem`/`.intoto.jsonl` from the checksums glob + `sort`), repinned here in 622ff44. Also repinned opnsense-exporter (9fb6409) and transceiver-exporter (e7037d5) — they were on v1.3.1 (pre-attest, unaffected today) but would have hit both the missing `attestations: write` permission and this glob bug on their next Renovate bump; both got the permission + the fixed SHA. v2.0.1 stands as published (binaries, SBOMs, SHA256SUMS, cosign signature); only its `.intoto.jsonl` is missing, and backfilling it from a different run would record misleading builder identity, so future releases pick it up via the repin.

title: v2.0.1 provenance attestation failed: attest step handed the sigstore bundle instead of SHA256SUMS

The v2.0.0 release's `binaries` job failed: GoReleaser's `gomod.proxy: true` build proxies `github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel@v2.0.0`, and Go's semantic-import-versioning rejects it — a module with a go.mod tagged v2+ must have a module path ending `/v2`. Nobody flagged this consequence of the #161 major bump.

Impact: v2.0.0 shipped its GHCR image, Helm chart, and notices (all green); only the cross-compiled binary archives + checksums/signatures/SBOMs are missing from the release. Re-running the job can't help (it checks out the tag, which lacks the /v2 path).

Fix: bump the module path to `github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/v2` (mechanical import sweep + tools/* go.mod require/replace updates), keeping `gomod.proxy: true` verifiable builds intact — the alternative (dropping proxy mode) would permanently forfeit proxy verification for every v2.x tag and silently strand any `go install` user on v1. Lands as a `fix:` so release-please cuts v2.0.1, whose binaries job will succeed.
title: release: v2.0.0 binaries job fails — module path must be /v2 for v2+ tags

Parent tracker for the feature program synthesized from the 2026-07-13 six-lane research pass (API-surface audit vs the live OpenAPI spec, Tailscale product changes Jan–Jul 2026, competing exporters + client telemetry, OTel/Grafana ecosystem, product-gap audit). This issue is the implementation plan: an orchestrating session should be able to run the whole program from this body + the child issues alone.

## Mission

Close every telemetry gap worth closing on the Tailscale control-plane surface, curate the client-metric stream we already forward raw, align attribute naming with OTel semantic conventions in one breaking pass, and knock out the verified operator-polish gaps — shipping as a single v2.0.0.

## Decisions already made — do not re-litigate

- **No Headscale investment.** The Headscale v2-API upgrade and Headscale server-metrics collector lanes were researched and explicitly cut (Rob, 2026-07-13). The current adapter stays as-is.
- **Semconv alignment is a hard cutover** — attribute renames land breaking under a `feat!:` commit, major bump to v2.0.0. No duplicate-attribute deprecation window.
- **No Prometheus mixin.** Dashboards/alerts stay as Grafana dashboard v2 JSON + Grafana-managed alert rule JSON generated in-repo (`deploy/grafana`, `deploy/alerts`).
- **Verified skips** (researched, rejected — don't resurface): OTel collector-contrib `tailscalereceiver` donation; OTLP profiles (no stable Go SDK); OpAMP; peer-relay control-plane coverage (zero relay endpoints in the API — client metrics in #171 are the only relay signal); federated-identity key coverage (invisible to our OAuth auth model); per-device routes endpoint (N+1 vs bulk); services `addrs`/`comment` as telemetry (PII fence stands — #166 uses VIPs in-memory only).

## Operating rules

- Generated artifacts (`docs/metrics.md`, `docs/env-vars.md`, Helm README/schema) regenerate via `scripts/regen-generated.sh` whenever inputs change.
- Progress lives here: tick phase checkboxes, post a phase-completion comment with SHAs after each phase.

Phases are ordered so later work builds on final names; issues within a phase are parallelizable EXCEPT where they share files (noted).

Shared seams to freeze before any fan-out: catalog descriptor names (`internal/catalog`/`internal/appcatalog`), semconv attribute names (`internal/semconv`), config keys + defaults (`internal/config`). Wiring files (`internal/app/collectors.go`, shared config struct) are single-owner — edited by one lane or a dedicated wiring pass, never in parallel.

## Release plan

All phases accumulate on `main`; #161's `feat!:` makes the pending release-please PR a v2.0.0. Hold merging the release PR until the program completes so v2.0.0 ships everything at once (release PR merge is manual anyway).

Config hot-reload (SIGHUP/watcher) · shared checkpoint backends (S3/Redis) + multi-replica story · Prometheus HTTP-SD endpoint serving tailnet devices as scrape targets · Kubernetes operator · log-stream destination config-drift gauge.

body:
## Why

The `nodemetrics` collector forwards every scraped `tailscaled_*` series verbatim (plus a `tailscale_node` label) — so newer client metrics already flow through, but as anonymous raw series: no catalog entry, no docs, no dashboards, no alerts. Nobody querying Grafana would discover them. The high-value subset as of client v1.94+ (peer relays GA 2026-02-19):

- `tailscaled_health_messages` (gauge, by `type`) — a node self-reporting warnings; the single most alert-worthy client signal
- `tailscaled_home_derp_region_id` — home DERP region (new in v1.94.1)
- `tailscaled_peer_relay_forwarded_packets_total` / `_bytes_total` / `tailscaled_peer_relay_endpoints` — the only observability surface peer relays have (the control-plane API exposes nothing; verified zero "relay" matches in the OpenAPI spec)
- `tailscaled_inbound/outbound_dropped_packets_total` (by `reason`: acl, error, ...)
- `tailscaled_inbound/outbound_packets/bytes_total` (by `path`: direct/derp/peer_relay) — direct-vs-relayed traffic mix per node

## What

- Promote the subset above into curated `tailscale.node.*` catalog metrics (same hand-picking pattern as `tailscale.node.up`), keeping raw forwarding unchanged (additive — no breaking rename of forwarded series).
- Cardinality check per label set; record decisions here.
- Catalog + `docs/metrics.md` + `docs/node-metrics.md` updates.
- Dashboard panels + alert rules land in the companion deploy issue (health-message warning alert, relay throughput, direct-vs-DERP mix).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Curated metrics in catalog with Recorder-asserted mapping tests (fixture scrape payloads)
- [ ] Raw forwarding behaviour unchanged (guard test)
- [ ] `docs/metrics.md` + `docs/node-metrics.md` regenerated
- [ ] Full gate green

comments.body:
## Seam freeze — curated metric names + cardinality (2026-07-13)

Curation happens in the nodemetrics collector's emit path: when a scraped family matches the map below, the curated metric is emitted **in addition to** the verbatim raw forward (additive — raw forwarding byte-identical to today, guard-tested). Counters ride the existing delta-baseline pipeline; every curated series carries the `tailscale.node` identity attribute like `tailscale.node.up`.

| source family | curated metric | instrument | unit | extra attributes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tailscaled_health_messages` | `tailscale.node.health_messages` | gauge | `1` | `tailscale.health.type` (from `type`) |
| `tailscaled_home_derp_region_id` | `tailscale.node.derp.home_region` | gauge | `1` | — (value = region ID) |
| `tailscaled_peer_relay_forwarded_bytes_total` | `tailscale.node.peer_relay.io` | counter | `By` | labels verified from fixture scrape |
| `tailscaled_peer_relay_forwarded_packets_total` | `tailscale.node.peer_relay.packets` | counter | `{packet}` | ditto |
| `tailscaled_peer_relay_endpoints` | `tailscale.node.peer_relay.endpoints` | gauge | `1` | — |
| `tailscaled_inbound_bytes_total` + `tailscaled_outbound_bytes_total` | `tailscale.node.io` | counter | `By` | `network.io.direction` (inbound→receive, outbound→transmit), `tailscale.path` (from `path`: direct\|derp\|peer_relay) |
| `tailscaled_inbound_packets_total` + `_outbound_packets_total` | `tailscale.node.packets` | counter | `{packet}` | ditto |
| `tailscaled_inbound_dropped_packets_total` + `_outbound_dropped_packets_total` | `tailscale.node.packets.dropped` | counter | `{packet}` | `network.io.direction`, `tailscale.drop.reason` (from `reason`: acl, error, ...) |

**New frozen attribute keys** (added to `internal/semconv`): `tailscale.health.type`, `tailscale.path` (values `direct|derp|peer_relay`), `tailscale.drop.reason`.

**Cardinality decisions:**
- `tailscale.node.io`/`packets`: nodes × direction(2) × path(≤3) — trivial.
- `packets.dropped`: nodes × direction(2) × reason (small closed set in the client; scraped values come from tailnet-member nodes, i.e. semi-trusted — fold unrecognized reasons to `other` with a bounded admit-set, same defensive posture as flow `transportName`).
- `health_messages`: nodes × warning type (client-defined set, ~dozens max) — fold is unnecessary; types are code-defined in tailscaled, not attacker-controlled free text. Emit as-is.
- `home_derp_region`: one series per node.

Naming collision check done: `tailscale.node.io/packets/packets.dropped/health_messages/derp.home_region/peer_relay.*` collide with nothing in the catalog; Prometheus normalizations (`tailscale_node_io_bytes_total`, `tailscale_node_packets_total`, `tailscale_node_packets_dropped_total`, `tailscale_node_health_messages_ratio`, ...) are distinct from the raw forwarded `tailscaled_*` names.

Docs: catalog entries land in `docs/metrics.md` (regen) + a curated-metrics section in `docs/node-metrics.md`. Dashboards/alerts over these land in #172.

Shipped in c362a92 per the frozen seam (8 curated tailscale.node.* metrics, three new bounded attribute keys, filters bypass curation, raw forwarding byte-identical — guard-tested). Cardinality decisions as frozen; path fold sums the ipv4/ipv6 variants into one bucket with correct counter semantics. One honesty note: the drop-reason admit-set {acl, error} is reconstructed from docs, not captured from a live scrape — unknown reasons fold to `other` so a wrong guess degrades gracefully, but a live-scrape check of real reason values is recommended when convenient (the lab scraper targets are reachable only from inside the tailnet). Dashboards/alerts over these land in #172.

body:
## Why

Docker-secrets-style file-based credentials exist in exactly one place: `node_metrics` `bearer_token_file` (`internal/config/config.go:622`). Every other credential — Tailscale OAuth client secret, API key, OTLP auth, admin token, streaming token, webhook secret, Prometheus pull token — is env/YAML-value only. Plain docker-compose users who mount `/run/secrets` have no clean path.

## What

- Add a `*_file` sibling for every secret-bearing config field, following the `bearer_token_file` precedent: value XOR file (validation error if both set), file read at load, trailing-newline trimmed.
- Enumerate the full field list during design and record it here (sweep `internal/config/config.go` for secret-shaped fields).
- Docs + `config.example.yaml` + env-vars regen (each `*_file` field is also settable via `TS2OTEL_*`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All secret fields have `*_file` variants with XOR validation, table-driven tests
- [ ] Trailing-newline handling tested (the classic docker-secrets papercut)
- [ ] Docs/example/env-vars regenerated
- [ ] Full gate green

comments.body:
## Seam freeze — full `*_file` field list + semantics (2026-07-13)

Sweep of every `Secret`-typed field in `internal/config/config.go`:

| existing field | new sibling |
|---|---|
| `tailscale.auth.oauth.client_secret` | `client_secret_file` |
| `tailscale.auth.apikey` | `apikey_file` |
| `headscale.api_key` | `api_key_file` |
| `otlp.grafana_cloud.token` | `token_file` |
| `admin.auth.token` | `token_file` |
| `prometheus.auth.token` | `token_file` |
| `streaming.token` | `token_file` |
| `webhook.secret` | `secret_file` |
| `profiling.pyroscope.basic_auth_password` | `basic_auth_password_file` |

- `tailnets[]` entries inherit the `TailscaleAuth` struct → per-entry `client_secret_file`/`apikey_file` come for free (and that list is file-only config anyway).
- `collectors.node_metrics.targets[].bearer_token_file` already exists — it is the semantic precedent.
- **Excluded:** `otlp.headers` (map[string]Secret) — a map has no clean per-key `*_file` sibling; documented workaround is env vars or `grafana_cloud.token_file`. Recorded here as a deliberate skip, not an oversight.
- #168's `id_token_file` is inherently file-based (no value variant, re-read per call — different lifecycle from these load-once secrets).

**Semantics (frozen, per the `bearer_token_file` precedent + issue):** value XOR file — both set is a `Validate()` error naming the key pair; file read once at `Load` (after env layering, before validation of dependent rules); read content passed through `strings.TrimSpace` (kills the classic `echo`-appended trailing newline, and leading/trailing whitespace is never legitimate in these credentials); unreadable/missing file is a load error naming the path. Every `*_file` key is settable via the standard `TS2OTEL_*` env convention. Table-driven tests cover XOR violations + newline trimming per field.

Shipped in a474fb9 per the frozen seam: all 9 *_file siblings with value-XOR-file validation (error names the key pair), read-at-Load, whitespace-trimmed, missing-file = load error naming the path; tailnets[] entries inherit for free; otlp.headers deliberately excluded (map). One internal deviation from the seam wording, recorded in the lane brief: conflict detection runs in resolveSecretFiles at Load (before dependent Validate rules would see the resolved value in both fields) and Validate reports it first — end-to-end behavior matches the spec exactly. Also seeds collectors.oauth_apps config surface for #167. Example config + docs/configuration.md + env-vars regenerated.

body:
## Why

Workload Identity Federation went GA 2026-02-19: fully keyless auth via OIDC token exchange — no stored client secret at all. `tailscale-client-go/v2` supports it (`ClientID` + `IDTokenFunc`). We currently support `oauth` (preferred) and `api_key` (discouraged, expiring). For k8s/CI deployments with an OIDC issuer this is strictly better than a mounted secret.

## What

- New `auth.method: workload_identity` in `internal/config` + `internal/tsapi`: federated client ID + an ID-token source. Config surface: token file path (projected service-account token — the k8s-native shape) as the primary source; follow the `TS2OTEL_*` env convention. Confirm the client library's exact interface with `go doc` before wiring (standing repo rule).
- Validation: mutually exclusive with the other methods; sensible errors when the token file is missing/unreadable; token re-read per `IDTokenFunc` call (projected tokens rotate).
- Docs: `docs/configuration.md` + `config.example.yaml` + env-vars regen; note the k8s projected-token recipe in the Helm docs if trivial.
- Optional follow-up (not gating): move the live-contract CI lane to keyless workload identity, retiring the runner-held OAuth client credentials.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `workload_identity` auth method works against the lab tailnet (evidence in a comment)
- [ ] Config validation + unit tests (failing-first)
- [ ] Docs/env-vars/example config regenerated
- [ ] Full gate green

comments.body:
## Seam freeze — config keys + defaults (2026-07-13)

```yaml
tailscale:
  auth:
    method: workload_identity     # now oneOf: oauth | apikey | workload_identity
    workload_identity:
      client_id: ""               # federated OAuth client ID (required)
      id_token_file: ""           # path to the OIDC ID token (required) — k8s projected SA token shape
      scopes: ["all:read"]        # default matches the oauth least-privilege default (#127)
```

Env (standard convention): `TS2OTEL_TAILSCALE__AUTH__WORKLOAD_IDENTITY__CLIENT_ID`, `...__ID_TOKEN_FILE`, `...__SCOPES`. Multi-tailnet `tailnets[]` entries inherit the same `TailscaleAuth` struct, so per-entry workload identity comes for free (including the empty-scopes → `all:read` backfill in `ResolvedTailnets`, which must be extended to the new method).

**Validation (frozen):** `method` extended to `oneOf(oauth, apikey, workload_identity)`; when selected, `client_id` and `id_token_file` both required; token file must exist and be readable at `Validate()` time; the token is **re-read on every `IDTokenFunc` invocation** (projected tokens rotate — never cache the first read). Mutual exclusion follows the existing pattern (the method selector picks the block; stray other-method creds get the existing warnings treatment).

**Scopes caveat:** if `go doc` shows tailscale-client-go/v2's workload-identity path takes no scope parameter, drop the `scopes` key entirely rather than shipping a dead field — record the outcome here.

**File ownership note:** the `internal/config` changes (struct, defaults, validation) are implemented in the #169/#170 config lane (single owner of config.go/validate.go); this issue's lane implements the `internal/tsapi` auth wiring against the frozen struct above.

Live-verification caveat: no lab credentials are present on this workstation (`.secrets/` absent) — the "works against the lab tailnet" criterion will be attempted via the lab deployment host; if unreachable it gets parked with an explicit comment rather than faked.

Shipped in d55341a. **Seam amendment (recorded per the freeze comment's caveat): the `scopes` key is DROPPED.** Verified two ways — Tailscale's WIF docs (the token-exchange takes only `client_id` + `jwt`; scopes are fixed by the federated identity's admin-console config) and Tailscale's own `feature/identityfederation` implementation. The pinned tailscale-client-go/v2 has zero WIF support (confirmed via go doc + the pinned commit's source; the successor `tailscale.com/client/tailscale/v2` has `IdentityFederation` but swapping modules was out of scope), so the exchange is implemented directly in internal/tsapi, mirroring the canonical flow: ID-token file re-read on every exchange (rotation tested), access token cached via ReuseTokenSource, bounded token-fetch client (#84 posture), Bearer attachment integration-tested against a fake exchange server.

**Parked acceptance criterion — live lab verification.** Not possible from this workstation and not faked: it needs a federated identity configured in the tailnet admin console (trusted OIDC issuer + audience + claim rules) plus a real OIDC token from that issuer (k8s projected SA token / GitHub Actions OIDC / cloud workload identity). The exchange protocol itself is fully exercised by the test suite; the remaining risk is Tailscale-side trust configuration, which only a real environment can prove. The optional follow-up (moving the live-contract CI lane to keyless WIF) would be the natural vehicle when someone sets that up.

body:
## Why

The live OpenAPI spec (`https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2?outputOpenapiSchema=true`) now has 90 operations vs our vendored 85 (`spec/tailscale-api.json`). The delta is exactly one new family: **OAuth Apps** (`GET/POST /tailnet/{tailnet}/oauth-apps`, `GET/PUT/DELETE .../{appId}`) — OAuth Apps for Device Provisioning (alpha, 2026-06-30), returning name, scopes, `allowedNodeAttributes`, timestamps. Same telemetry shape as the existing keys collector: inventory + scope visibility.

Also suspicious: the daily `api-drift.yml` lane should have opened a deduped tracking issue for a 5-op addition, and the only open issue is #3. Either the lane is broken or the dedupe/labeling swallowed it — worth finding out while we're here.

## What

1. Re-vendor `spec/tailscale-api.json` per `spec/README.md` (note: the endpoint returns YAML despite the URL — the existing tooling handles this; keep JSON committed). Update `internal/tsapi/contract` manifest/fuzz inputs as needed.
2. Investigate why the api-drift lane stayed silent on the 85→90 drift; fix or file what's found.
3. New collector `internal/collector/oauthapps` per the recipe in `internal/collector/CLAUDE.md`: narrow client interface, count metric + per-app info signal (scopes label, `allowedNodeAttributes` count). Decide default-on vs gated (alpha API; check required scope) and record here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Spec re-vendored; contract/fuzz tests green against it
- [ ] api-drift silence explained (comment) and fixed if a lane bug
- [ ] Collector emits count + per-app info; Recorder-asserted tests; registered/gated in `internal/app/collectors.go`
- [ ] `docs/metrics.md` + `config.example.yaml`/`docs/configuration.md`/env-vars regenerated as applicable
- [ ] Full gate green

comments.body:
## Seam freeze — collector shape + gating decision (2026-07-13)

**Config:** `collectors.oauth_apps` (`SimpleCollector`: `enabled`, `interval`), default **enabled=true, interval 300s**. Rationale for default-on: every other inventory collector defaults on; the alpha-API risk is handled by response-code tolerance, not gating — a 403/404 (feature not enabled / no scope) is treated as feature-off idle (no error, precedent: flowlogs 403-idle), so tailnets without the alpha see a silent no-op. Required scope is covered by the default `all:read`.

**Frozen names:**

| signal | name | instrument/severity | unit | attributes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| aggregate count | `tailscale.oauth_apps.count` | gauge | `{app}` | — |
| per-app scope count | `tailscale.oauth_app.scopes` | gauge | `1` | `tailscale.oauth_app.id`, `tailscale.oauth_app.name` |
| per-app allowed node attrs | `tailscale.oauth_app.node_attributes` | gauge | `1` | `tailscale.oauth_app.id`, `tailscale.oauth_app.name` |
| per-app info log | `tailscale.oauth_app.info` | INFO event | — | id, name, `tailscale.oauth_app.scope_values` (comma-joined), node-attribute count |

Pattern precedent: keys collector (`tailscale.key.scopes` gauge + scope_values on the log). Per-app series bounded by OAuth-app count (small); no per-entity toggle added.

**Client (`internal/tsapi/oauthapps.go` or client.go-adjacent):** raw GET `/api/v2/tailnet/{tailnet}/oauth-apps` (list op only — the CRUD ops are not consumed), narrow `lister` interface in the collector.

Package: `internal/collector/oauthapps`, collector `Name() = "oauth_apps"` (matches the config key style of `posture_integrations`/`log_stream`).

Shipped in 8f2c3ca. Spec re-vendored (85→90 ops; delta = exactly the five OAuth-Apps ops + their schemas, plus one benign upstream doc-typo). listOAuthApps added to the contract manifest — the schema-driven fuzz decodes it with no quirk payload. Collector emits count + per-app scopes/node-attribute gauges + info log per the frozen seam; wire envelope (oauthApps) verified against a live lab capture; 403/404 = feature-off idle so **default-on** is safe (decision recorded per the issue ask).

**api-drift silence root cause: by design, not a lane bug.** tools/apidrift classifies drift only across operations the contract manifest consumes (its documented scope); a brand-new upstream endpoint family is invisible to it until vendored+consumed. No fix applied. If automated new-endpoint discovery is wanted, that's a deliberate Classify design change (e.g. an Info-severity "new operation not in manifest" kind) — say the word and it gets its own issue.

body:
## Why

Tailscale Services went GA on 2026-01-27 (remote/non-localhost backends, tsnet lifecycle-driven registration, declarative JSON config). The fresh OpenAPI spec shows no new fields on the operations we consume, but that should be confirmed against a live capture rather than blog prose. Separately, GA'd flow logs now correlate a service's VIP with the underlying proxy machine IP — which we can exploit for enrichment: today a flow whose peer is a service VIP resolves to `unknown`/`external`.

## What

1. **Drift verification**: capture the live services response from the lab tailnet into `.capture/` and diff against `internal/tsapi/services.go` + `internal/collector/services` expectations. Fix anything that drifted; otherwise note "verified, no drift" here and move on.
2. **Service-VIP enrichment**: map service VIPs to service names in flow-log enrichment so the peer shows as the service instead of unknown. Note the fence: `internal/tsapi/services.go:8-11` deliberately does not decode `addrs` "so they cannot become telemetry". Enrichment needs the VIPs **in-memory only** (extend the `enrich.DeviceCache` pattern) — the raw addresses must still never be emitted as attribute values themselves, only the derived service name. Keep the fence's intent; document the carve-out at the decode site.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live capture diffed; result recorded in a comment
- [ ] Flow logs resolve service-VIP peers to service names (Recorder-asserted test with fixture flows)
- [ ] Raw service addresses never appear as emitted attribute values (guard test)
- [ ] Full gate green

comments.body:
**Drift verification: done — verified, no drift (2026-07-13).** Captured the live services surface from the lab tailnet (creds recovered from the <host-1> deployment; captures in gitignored `.capture/`):

- `GET /tailnet/-/services` — 9 live services (k8s-operator-managed). Field census across all: `addrs`, `annotations`, `comment`, `name`, `ports`, `tags` — no new fields post-GA vs what `internal/tsapi/services.go` expects. The decode fence (name/ports/tags only) stands.
- `GET /tailnet/-/services/{name}/devices` — live returns `{}` for every lab service (hosts list empty/omitted for operator-managed services); the LIVE OpenAPI schema for the op is unchanged (`{hosts: [ServiceHostInfo]}`), and the existing decode tolerates the empty object. Data condition, not drift.
- Bonus: `GET /tailnet/-/oauth-apps` confirmed live with envelope key `oauthApps` (empty list in lab) — wire-shape evidence for #167.

Next: the service-VIP → name flow-log enrichment (step 2), scheduled after the semconv/#161 batch lands (in-memory VIP map only; raw addrs never emitted; guard test).

Enrichment shipped in f3669cd (drift verification was posted earlier — verified, no drift). Flow peers that are service VIPs now resolve to the service name via an independent service map in the device cache (device hit wins on collision); the services collector repopulates it each tick through the documented ServiceAddrs carve-out (in-memory only; fetch failures non-fatal, previous map kept). ## Seam freeze — owner/tags attribute design (2026-07-13)

**Decode (`internal/tsapi/keys.go`):** `UserID string` from wire `userId`; `Tags []string` from `capabilities.devices.create.tags` (sibling of the already-decoded reusable/ephemeral/preauthorized).

**Frozen attribute keys:**

Empty userId → attribute omitted. Deliberately TS-namespaced, NOT `user.id`: on a key-inventory signal the owner is metadata about the key, not the subject of the signal (post-#161 `user.id` is reserved for "the user this signal is about"). - `tailscale.key.tags` — sorted, comma-joined auto-applied tag set, on `tailscale.key.expiry` + `tailscale.key.preauthorized` (auth keys only — the only type carrying create capabilities) and the expiring WARN event. Empty → omitted. Joined-string keeps it one attribute; tag sets are small and stable (bounded by ACL tag count).
