body:
## Problem
`buildAttrs` unconditionally calls `resolveLabelCollisions` whenever an emission has non-empty attributes, which always allocates two maps plus a fresh string-builder-derived Prometheus label name per attribute key — even in the overwhelmingly common case where no reserved-label collision or duplicate normalized key exists.

## Evidence
- `internal/telemetry/emitter.go:272-303` (`buildAttrs`) — calls `resolveLabelCollisions(attrs, e.reserved)` whenever `len(attrs) != 0`.
- `internal/telemetry/emitter.go:367-393` (`resolveLabelCollisions`) — unconditionally allocates `chosen := make(map[string]string, len(attrs))` and `keep := make(map[string]struct{}, len(chosen))`, and calls `metricdoc.PromLabelName(k)` for every attribute key.
- `internal/metricdoc/metricdoc.go:96-116` (`PromLabelName`) — builds a `strings.Builder` and always returns a fresh string, with no fast-path for "already valid, return as-is."
- Context: default poll intervals are minute-scale (`internal/config/defaults_test.go` shows `30s`/`2m` as representative), and the same emit call already pays a comparable or larger allocation cost via `redactor.Merge` and `CardinalityTracker.Observe`'s per-point fingerprinting (`internal/telemetry/cardinality.go:88-103`) — so this is a legitimate but modest micro-optimization, not a standout hot spot.

## Failure scenario / impact
Per-device/per-user/per-key gauges (`cardinality.per_entity.*`) and per-flow-rollup metrics emit one attrs map per entity per collection tick. On a tailnet with hundreds-to-thousands of devices, this multiplies into a meaningful number of extra short-lived map/string allocations and GC pressure every collector interval, purely for a collision check that almost never finds anything to resolve.

## Suggested direction
Add a cheap fast-path check — iterate `attrs` once counting keys against `e.reserved` with no allocation, and only build the maps when a real collision/reservation is detected — so the common case is allocation-free. A benchmark on `buildAttrs` with a realistic per-device attrs map would quantify the win.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A no-allocation fast path exists for the common no-collision case in `buildAttrs`/`resolveLabelCollisions`
- [ ] The existing collision-resolution behavior is unchanged for the cases that do collide
- [ ] A benchmark demonstrates reduced allocations for the common case

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

Covered by new alloc/equivalence tests in emitter_internal_test.go.

body:
## Problem
`nodeDiscoverer.Discover` (used by the node-metrics collector's discovery mode) independently issues its own full `DevicesRich()` poll on a separate ticker, even though the `devices` collector — when enabled — already populates `enrich.DeviceCache` with the same rich-device snapshot at a shorter interval. This is an avoidable duplicate poll against the heaviest, most rate-limit-sensitive tailscale API endpoint.

## Evidence
- `internal/collector/devices/devices.go:413` — devices collector calls `DevicesRich(ctx)` on its own `Interval` (default 60s).
- `internal/app/nodediscovery.go:51` — `nodeDiscoverer.Discover` calls `DevicesRich(ctx)` independently, on `node_metrics.discovery.interval` (default 5m).
- `internal/app/tailnetruntime.go:68` — the devices collector already populates `enrich.DeviceCache` (`rt.cache`) with a full rich-device snapshot.
- `internal/tsapi/ratelimit.go`, `client.go:58-60` — a single shared token-bucket rate limiter backs the whole client, so this fetch competes for the same budget as every other collector.
- At default settings this adds one extra full-inventory fetch every 5 minutes on top of the ~5 the devices collector already made in that window — roughly +20% additional load on tailnets that enable both `devices` and `nodemetrics`-with-discovery.

## Failure scenario / impact
On tailnets with thousands of devices, the duplicate poll is a non-trivial, avoidable payload/CPU/GC cost, and it eats into the shared rate-limit budget for no new data (the cache is at most 60s stale). This is **not** a drop-in cache-read swap, though: `enrich.DeviceMeta` currently lacks an online/`ConnectedToControl` field (needed for `node_metrics.discovery.online_only`, which defaults to `true`) and lacks the raw device `ID` (needed for the emitted `HostID` label, which currently comes from `NodeID` only). It also depends on first landing the fix for populating `DeviceMeta.Tags` in `toMetas` (currently always empty, tracked separately), since `ExcludeTags`/`IncludeTags` filtering in `nodeDiscoverer.match` needs real tag data to work off the cache.

## Suggested direction
Extend `enrich.DeviceMeta` with online status and device ID, have `nodeDiscoverer.Discover` read from `enrich.DeviceCache.Snapshot()` when the devices collector is enabled (falling back to its own `DevicesRich()` call only when devices is disabled or the cache is empty/stale), and land the `Tags`-population fix first so tag-based filtering keeps working off the cache.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The `DeviceMeta.Tags` population fix lands before or alongside this change
- [ ] `enrich.DeviceMeta` carries the fields node-metrics discovery needs (online status, device ID)
- [ ] `nodeDiscoverer.Discover` uses the shared cache when the devices collector is enabled, with a documented fallback path when it isn't
- [ ] `online_only` filtering and `HostID` labeling behave identically to today's `DevicesRich()`-based implementation
- [ ] Test covering discovery via the cache path and the fallback (devices disabled) path

body:
## Problem
The OAuth token refresh used to authenticate against the Tailscale API is unbounded: a hung token fetch can stall every collector on that tailnet runtime forever, with no automatic recovery short of a process restart.

**Critical verifier correction to the mechanism:** the raw finding blamed `oc.Timeout = 0` (in `internal/tsapi/auth.go`) as the cause, and proposed restoring a whole-client timeout as the fix. That is factually wrong and would **not** fix the issue. `oauth2.Transport.RoundTrip` calls `Source.Token()` **before** invoking its base transport and **ignores the request's context entirely** — the clientcredentials token source is bound to `context.Background()` and runs on `http.DefaultClient`, which has no deadline. This means `http.Client.Timeout` (whether set to 60s, as `tsclient`'s helper does by default, or 0) never bounded the token fetch in the first place — the line the raw finding blames does not cause or worsen the behavior. The real, and only correct, fix is to bind the token source to a context carrying an `oauth2.HTTPClient` whose transport sets a `ResponseHeaderTimeout` (or to implement the token source directly in `tsapi` instead of relying on `tsclient`'s `Background()`-bound helper). Neither `client.Timeout` nor a scheduler per-tick deadline can cancel a context-ignoring `Source.Token()` call.

## Evidence
- `internal/tsapi/auth.go:41-51` — `oc := tsclient.OAuthConfig{...}.HTTPClient(); oc.Timeout = 0; oc.Transport = wrap(oc.Transport)`.
- `tsclient oauth.go:38-40` — the token source is built with `oauthConfig.Client(context.Background())`.
- `x/oauth2` `clientcredentials.go:110` — `RetrieveToken(c.ctx, ...)` uses that stored `Background()` context, ultimately hitting `http.DefaultClient` (no timeout).
- `x/oauth2` `transport.go:45` (`oauth2.Transport.RoundTrip`) — calls `t.Source.Token()` with no context and before the base `RoundTrip`.
- `oauth2.ReuseTokenSource` serializes all callers under a mutex, so one hung refresh blocks every API request sharing that client indefinitely.
- The scheduler passes the app-lifetime `ctx` straight to `Collect` with no per-tick deadline, so the collector goroutines never recover on their own.

## Failure scenario / impact
At token expiry (roughly hourly), a refresh POST to `api.tailscale.com` stalls after TCP/TLS establishment but before response headers arrive (a stalled proxy connection, a blackholed connection that stays `ESTABLISHED`). All collectors on that tailnet runtime block forever waiting on the token mutex; `scrape.*` metrics silently stop while the process heartbeat keeps reporting `up=1`. Only a restart recovers. This is a real latent reliability risk but requires a fairly narrow network pathology to trigger, and is a pre-existing property of `tsclient`'s `OAuthConfig.HTTPClient()` helper (shared by every `x/oauth2` clientcredentials consumer) rather than a regression introduced by this repo's code.

## Suggested direction
Bound the token fetch by constructing the clientcredentials source with a context carrying an `oauth2.HTTPClient` whose transport sets a `ResponseHeaderTimeout` (or implement the token source directly in `tsapi` rather than depending on `tsclient`'s `Background()`-bound helper). A per-tick deadline in the scheduler is reasonable defense-in-depth but is not itself sufficient, since it cannot interrupt a context-ignoring `Source.Token()` call.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The OAuth token fetch is provably bounded (a test with a stalling token server proves the fetch times out and returns an error rather than hanging).
- [ ] Collectors on the affected tailnet runtime recover (retry / surface an error) instead of blocking forever when a token refresh stalls.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by `086c9b5`. tsapi now constructs the clientcredentials source itself and binds it to a context whose `oauth2.HTTPClient` carries dial/TLS/response-header timeouts, so a stalled token refresh returns an error instead of blocking every collector on the shared ReuseTokenSource mutex forever. API-call transport is unchanged (no impact on large flow-log body reads). A stalling-token-server test proves the fetch is bounded (returns in ~0.3s, not a hang) — verified in isolation that `src.Token()` hits ResponseHeaderTimeout.

## Problem
`config.streaming.tls.cert_file`/`key_file` is a real, documented config surface for terminating TLS on the streaming (HEC) receiver, but the Helm chart has no way to place an arbitrary file (like a cert/key pair) on disk inside the pod — there is no `extraVolumes`/`extraVolumeMounts` escape hatch, and `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` closes off any other write path.

## Evidence
- `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/values.yaml:465-468` — `streaming.tls.cert_file`/`key_file` documented config surface.
- `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/values.yaml:47-53` — `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.
- Grep of `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/{values.yaml,templates/*.yaml}` for `extraVolume` — zero matches.
- `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/templates/deployment.yaml` — only two volumes are mounted: the ConfigMap/Secret-backed `config` (read-only, single `config.yaml` key) and `checkpoints`.
- Note: the webhook receiver has no TLS config at all (`internal/config/config.go` defines no `WebhookTLS` type), so this applies only to the streaming receiver, not "similarly for webhook TLS."
- `deploy/CLAUDE.md`'s "No Kubernetes Service (deliberate)" section documents the intended pattern of terminating TLS at an Ingress rather than app-level certs in Kubernetes; `docs/streaming-webhooks.md:100` recommends `tailscale cert` for the app-level cert, which targets the project's docker-compose-on-a-tailnet-host deployment model, not generic k8s pods.

## Failure scenario / impact
An operator sets `config.streaming.tls.cert_file`/`key_file` in the Helm chart's `values.yaml`, expecting to terminate TLS on the streaming receiver as the config schema advertises. There is no chart-native way to get the cert/key material onto disk in the pod, so the receiver fails to start with a file-not-found error (a loud failure, not silent misbehavior), forcing the operator to fork the chart to add the mount themselves.

## Suggested direction
Add `extraVolumes`/`extraVolumeMounts` values, rendered into `deployment.yaml`'s `volumes`/`volumeMounts` blocks, so TLS material (or other custom mounts) can be wired in without forking the chart.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `extraVolumes`/`extraVolumeMounts` values exist in `values.yaml` and render into the Deployment template
- [ ] `values.schema.json` and `helm-docs` regenerated to document the new keys
- [ ] A documented example shows mounting a TLS cert/key Secret for `streaming.tls`

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

body:
## Problem
The Helm chart's `podSecurityContext` sets `runAsNonRoot` and a seccomp profile but never sets `fsGroup`. This is not needed for the default `emptyDir`-backed checkpoint volume (the kubelet chmods `emptyDir` roots to 0777, and the image itself pre-seeds `/var/lib/tailscale2otel` owned by uid/gid 65532), but a freshly-provisioned block PVC under the opt-in `persistence.enabled=true` path is typically root:root 0755 at its root on many CSI drivers, which can leave the container unable to write to it.

## Evidence
- `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/values.yaml:39-42` (`podSecurityContext`) — no `fsGroup`.
- `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/values.yaml:47-53` — container `securityContext` runs as uid/gid 65532.
- `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/templates/deployment.yaml:85-90,93-96` — checkpoints volume is `emptyDir` by default, or a PVC when `persistence.enabled=true`.
- `internal/app/app.go:559-570` (`ensureWritableDir`) — probes writability with `os.CreateTemp` and falls back to `collector.NewMemoryStore()` (with a WARN log) on any error; this fallback is documented deliberate design (`deploy/CLAUDE.md:33-37`), not a crash.
- Default `emptyDir` path is unaffected: kubelet's `emptyDir` plugin chmods the volume root 0777, and `deploy/Dockerfile:20,44` pre-seeds `/var/lib/tailscale2otel` via `COPY --chown=65532:65532`.

## Failure scenario / impact
An operator sets `persistence.enabled=true` for durable checkpoint storage (as `deploy/CLAUDE.md` documents). On a CSI driver/provisioner that doesn't itself apply ownership adjustment, the freshly-provisioned PVC root is owned root:root, the uid-65532 container can't write to it, `ensureWritableDir` fails, and the checkpoint store silently falls back to memory (with a WARN log, not a crash) — defeating the point of enabling persistence, since cursors never survive a pod restart.

## Suggested direction
Add `fsGroup: 65532` (and consider `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` for larger PVCs) to `podSecurityContext` in `values.yaml`/`deployment.yaml`, scoped to making the opt-in PVC path reliably writable regardless of the underlying CSI driver's default ownership behavior. The default `emptyDir` path already works and needs no change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `fsGroup: 65532` is set in `podSecurityContext` (or made configurable, defaulting to set)
- [ ] `helm lint`/`template`, `values.schema.json`, and `helm-docs` regenerated to reflect the change
- [ ] Behavior verified/documented for both the default `emptyDir` path and the opt-in PVC path

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Done in 250b4c5 (pushed to main). Added `podSecurityContext.fsGroup: 65532` so the opt-in PVC persistence path is writable by the non-root user.

body:
## Problem
`nodemetrics.Collect` scrapes its discovered/static targets in a plain sequential loop with no worker pool and no overall per-tick deadline. Each target uses a per-target `*http.Client` with a 10s default timeout, and the scheduler never wraps a collector tick in `context.WithTimeout`. Because targets are scraped strictly in series, total `Collect` duration scales linearly with the number of slow/unreachable targets, and once a tick overruns its interval, Go's single-slot `time.Ticker` drops/collapses subsequent ticks rather than queuing them — the collector's actual cadence degrades as the unreachable-target count grows.

Note: adversarially verified and downgraded/corrected. `Discovery.OnlineOnly` defaults to `true`, so **offline** devices are never scrape targets by default — only **online-but-unreachable** nodes (ACL-denied, firewalled) block, a narrower population than "powered off" devices. Per-tick time is bounded (not unbounded) by `MaxTargets × Timeout`; the worst-case ~2.8-hour figure needs an extreme corner (1000 simultaneous online-and-unreachable targets). Both `node_metrics.enabled` and `discovery.enabled` default to `false`, so no default deployment is affected, and the degradation is observable and self-correcting (unreachable targets emit `tailscale.node.up=0`, `scrape.duration` grows, and `scrape.staleness` becomes alertable) rather than a silent fault. It remains a legitimate robustness/scalability gap — nodemetrics is the only collector in the codebase that fans out to N independent targets per tick.

## Evidence
- `internal/collector/nodemetrics/nodemetrics.go:392-397` — a plain `for` loop over targets, no `go func` anywhere in the package.
- `internal/collector/nodemetrics/nodemetrics.go:46-50` + `internal/config/defaults.go` — per-target `http.Client` `Timeout` defaults to 10s.
- `internal/config/defaults.go:159` — `discovery.max_targets` defaults to 1000.
- `internal/collector/scheduler.go` — the scheduler calls `Collect(ctx, ...)` with the bare ambient ctx, never wrapped in `context.WithTimeout`, driven off a `time.Ticker` on the collector's interval (default 60s).
- `internal/config/defaults.go:163` — `Discovery.OnlineOnly` defaults `true`; `nodediscovery.go:114`'s `match()` drops any device not `ConnectedToControl`.
- `internal/config/defaults.go:151,157` — `NodeMetrics.Enabled`/`Discovery.Enabled` both default `false`.

## Failure scenario / impact
A tailnet with node-metrics discovery enabled has a handful of devices that are online but unreachable across the tailnet (missing/incomplete ACL grant, firewalled). Each of those costs up to the full per-target timeout (10s default), one after another; enough of them mixed with reachable targets can push a single tick's duration past the configured interval, so every subsequent tick starts late and the collector's actual scrape cadence degrades as the unreachable-target count grows — up to the `MaxTargets × Timeout` bound in the extreme case.

## Suggested direction
Scrape targets concurrently with a bounded worker pool, and/or derive a per-tick `context.WithTimeout` bounded by the collector's own interval, so one slow/unreachable batch of targets can never push a tick past its scheduled cadence.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Nodemetrics scrapes targets concurrently with a bounded worker pool, and/or a per-tick deadline ≤ the configured interval is enforced.
- [ ] A test with deliberately slow/unreachable targets asserts the tick completes within its interval bound.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by `ff47ce3`. `Collect` now fans target scrapes through a bounded worker pool (`Options.Concurrency`, default 10) and wraps the batch in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, interval)`, so slow/hung targets can't push a tick past its cadence. Every target is still attempted and emits `tailscale.node.up` each tick; per-target timeout, discovery union, and filters unchanged. Tests TDD-verified against the old serial loop. _(Sonnet subagent; gated on main. Optional `max_concurrent_scrapes` config knob deferred — internal default suffices.)_

body:
## Problem
Setting an env var that indexes into `node_metrics.targets` (a list-of-structs, documented as file-only) is not rejected or flagged as unknown — instead it silently decodes into a slice containing an empty `NodeMetricsTarget{}`, dropping the actual value the operator tried to set.

## Evidence
- `internal/config/env.go:19-27` — documents `collectors.node_metrics.targets` as file-only ("Complex collections ... are not settable via flat env vars").
- `internal/config/env.go:104-114` (`unknownEnvVars`/`keyExtendsKnown`) — treat any env var extending the known key `collectors.node_metrics.targets` as valid (not flagged), because that leaf key is present in `validKeys` even though its default value is `nil`.
- Reproduced via `mapstructure.Decode` with the exact config decode settings: `TS2OTEL_COLLECTORS__NODE_METRICS__TARGETS__0__URL=http://x` decodes to a slice of length 1 whose single element is a completely empty `NodeMetricsTarget{}` — the nested `url` value is silently dropped.
- With `node_metrics` enabled, this currently surfaces as the confusing hard error `collectors.node_metrics.targets[0].url is required` (`validate.go:383-386`) rather than a message pointing at the real cause.

## Failure scenario / impact
An operator, following the documented `__`-nesting env convention, tries `TS2OTEL_COLLECTORS__NODE_METRICS__TARGETS__0__URL=http://tailscaled:5252/metrics` to add a scrape target without a YAML file. With `node_metrics` enabled, `Load` fails with the opaque `targets[0].url is required` error — looking like the URL was never set, when it was actually supplied but silently zeroed during decode. With `node_metrics` disabled, the same env var instead injects an inert phantom empty target with no warning at all.

## Suggested direction
Either reject any env var that resolves under a list-of-structs leaf key as an explicit config error, or extend `keyExtendsKnown`/`unknownEnvVars` to specifically flag attempts to index into `collectors.node_metrics.targets`, giving the operator an actionable message pointing at the file-only requirement.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An env var attempting to index into `node_metrics.targets` produces a clear, actionable error naming the file-only requirement
- [ ] The confusing `targets[0].url is required` error no longer appears for this specific misconfiguration
- [ ] Test covering both the enabled and disabled `node_metrics` cases with an indexed env var set

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Done in 5d43509 (pushed to main). `TS2OTEL_*` env vars that index into list-of-structs config (`node_metrics.targets`, `tailnets`) now produce an actionable load error naming the offending variable and explaining those lists are file-only, instead of being silently ignored.

body:
## Problem

`release-please-config.json:17` defines a changelog section keyed on commit *type* `"deps"`
(`{ "type": "deps", "section": "Dependencies" }`), but this repo's commit convention always uses
`deps` as the Conventional Commits *scope*, never the *type* (verified: 19 `chore(deps): ...`
commits, 4 `fix(deps): ...` commits, 0 bare `deps: ...` commits). release-please's parser buckets a
commit purely by its `type` field, not scope, so this rule can only match a commit literally
formatted as `deps(scope)?: subject` — a form Renovate/this repo never produces.

## Evidence

- `release-please-config.json:17` — `{ "type": "deps", "section": "Dependencies" }`
- Every generated `CHANGELOG.md` (0.3.0, 0.4.0, 0.5.0, and the earliest 0.1.0/0.2.0 entries) has zero
  `### Dependencies` sections.
- `chore(deps)` commits fall into the `chore`/`Miscellaneous` bucket (`hidden: true`); `fix(deps)`
  commits fall into `fix`/`Bug Fixes` — neither ever reaches the `Dependencies` section as intended.

## Failure scenario / impact

Every routine Renovate dependency bump (the majority of commits in this repo) is generated as
`chore` and therefore silently dropped from the changelog entirely (`hidden: true`), never surfacing
under the intended "Dependencies" section — the changelog under-reports dependency churn even
though the config author clearly intended those bumps to be visible.

## Suggested direction

release-please's `changelog-sections` config doesn't support scope-based matching directly, so
either stop hiding `chore` entries, or have Renovate commit with a bare `deps:` type instead of
`chore(deps):`/`fix(deps):`, so dependency bumps actually land in a visible section.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] dependency bumps visibly land in the generated changelog under a clear section (or the
      `deps` section is removed from `release-please-config.json` with a documented rationale)
- [ ] the fix is verified against a representative set of `chore(deps)`/`fix(deps)` commit messages

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Closed by `413b314`. Removed the dead `{ type: "deps", section: "Dependencies" }` changelog-sections entry — release-please matches on commit TYPE only (never scope), so `type: deps` could never match `chore(deps)`/`fix(deps)` (type=chore/fix, scope=deps). `fix(deps)` still appears under Bug Fixes; `chore(deps)` stays in the hidden chore bucket. No real changelog output changes; removes non-functional config. _(Sonnet subagent.)_

body:
## Problem
Metric attribute values derived from wire input on the stream-receiver path are used unbounded, unlike the webhook receiver which already caps its attacker-influenced event type. Specifically: audit `action`/`origin` are emitted raw on the events counter, and flow `proto` falls back to a raw string of any unrecognized integer.

## Evidence
- `internal/audit/processor.go:195-198` — emits `tailscale.config.audit.events` with raw `ev.Action`/`ev.Origin` values (only the separate *changes* counter normalizes via `classify.go`'s `normalizeAction`/`normalizeActorType`).
- `internal/flowlog/processor.go:548-556` — `transportName` returns `strconv.Itoa(proto)` for any unknown int; `proto` is an attacker-supplied JSON number via the stream receiver.
- `internal/webhook/webhook.go:88-99,453-467` — contrast: the webhook path already caps its attacker-chosen event type at `maxDistinctEventTypes=64` for exactly this reason.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:397-399` + `internal/config/validate.go:98` — the stream receiver fails open (authorizes all requests) when `streaming.token` is empty, a state the validator only warns against rather than rejects.
- Mitigating factor: `cardinality.metric_limit` defaults to 10000 SDK-wide (`provider.go:193`), so the failure mode is `otel_metric_overflow` degradation, not unbounded growth — this is a hardening gap, not an unbounded-resource bug.

## Failure scenario / impact
With the streaming receiver reachable and `streaming.token` unset (an explicitly warned-against but allowed misconfiguration, or after a token leak), a flood of crafted audit/flow records with unique `action`/`origin`/`proto` values saturates `tailscale.config.audit.events` / `tailscale.network.flows` up to the 10000-series cardinality cap, after which genuine audit/flow series get folded into `otel_metric_overflow` and become indistinguishable, alongside memory/export inflation up to the cap.

## Suggested direction
Apply the webhook's `boundType` pattern (a bounded admit-set with an "other" overflow bucket) to audit `action`/`origin` in the processor, and clamp `transportName` to the 0–255 IANA protocol-number range (folding out-of-range values to "unknown"). The `metric_limit` backstop already prevents unbounded growth; this closes the remaining inconsistency with the webhook path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Audit `action`/`origin` values are bounded to a fixed admit-set with an overflow bucket before use as metric attributes
- [ ] `transportName` clamps out-of-range/unrecognized protocol numbers to a fixed "unknown" value instead of echoing the raw wire integer
- [ ] Test covering a flood of distinct wire-supplied action/origin/proto values not exhausting per-instrument cardinality beyond the bounded set

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by `742e6c1`. Wire-derived metric attr values are bounded to fixed admit-sets: audit action/origin → `knownActions`/`knownOrigins` (OpenAPI enums) with an `other` bucket on `tailscale.config.audit.events`; flowlog `proto` clamped to `unknown` outside IANA 1..255. The stream path inherits this via the shared processors (no stream edit needed). Log records keep raw values (not a series-cardinality vector). Flood tests (2000 distinct values) assert the emitted attr set stays bounded. _(Sonnet subagent; gated on main. Static enum admit-set chosen over a dynamic cap, matching the acceptance.)_

body:
## Problem
`api.duration` conflates two different sources of latency into a single histogram: the client's own configured rate-limiter wait time and genuine API/network round-trip + retry-backoff time. An operator has no way to tell, from the metric alone, which one is driving elevated `api.duration`.

## Evidence
- `internal/tsapi/auth.go:20-26` — `limiter: newRateWaiter(opts.RateLimit)` wired directly onto `retryTransport`.
- `internal/tsapi/transport.go:162` — `retryTransport.RoundTrip` waits on that limiter before every attempt.
- `internal/app/selfobs.go:27-46` (`apiObserver`) — records the resulting wall-clock `dur` into `tailscale2otel.api.duration` (and `api.requests`/`api.retries`) with only `endpoint` and `status` attributes; no attribute distinguishes rate-limiter wait time.

## Failure scenario / impact
An operator enables many collectors at short intervals with a conservative `rate_limit` (tuned for a small tailnet that later grows). `api.duration` p99 climbs and dashboards suggest an API-side problem, when the real, cheap fix is raising the `rate_limit` config knob — the ambiguity costs real diagnosis time on every rate_limit misconfiguration.

## Suggested direction
Track the limiter's own wait duration separately (e.g. a `tailscale2otel.api.rate_limit.wait` histogram, or a `wait_seconds` value threaded through `RequestInfo`) so it can be subtracted out of the existing `api.duration` histogram's interpretation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Rate-limiter wait time is observable separately from round-trip/backoff time
- [ ] `docs/metrics.md` documents the new signal and its relationship to `api.duration`
- [ ] Test asserting the new signal reflects actual limiter wait time under a throttled scenario

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Done in 5d43509 (pushed to main). Client-side rate-limiter wait is now tracked as `RequestInfo.WaitDuration`, excluded from `api.duration`, and recorded as a new histogram `tailscale2otel.api.rate_limit.wait` (unit s, keyed by endpoint) — only when a request actually waited. Descriptor added to appcatalog; metrics.md regenerated.

body:
## Problem

`config.example.yaml:250`, `docs/configuration.md:511`, and `docs/env-vars.md:160` all say the
`streaming.token` is expected as `"Authorization: Splunk <token>"`, and the `Options.Token` godoc
(`internal/stream/stream.go:156-158`) repeats the same claim. But the code — and the pinned live
capture — say the opposite: `stream.go:17-19` documents "Authentication is HTTP Basic auth,
base64('<user>:<token>') — NOT 'Authorization: Splunk <token>'", and `authorized()`
(`stream.go:397-408`) checks Basic auth first, the Splunk scheme second (as a fallback). Because
`docs/env-vars.md` is generated *from* the stale `config.example.yaml` comment, the wrong text is
self-propagating. Separately, the `MetricRejected` const comment (`stream.go:104`) lists rejection
reasons "auth"/"unparsable" but omits "too_large", which `catalog.go:27` already has.

## Evidence

- `config.example.yaml:250`, `docs/configuration.md:511`, `docs/env-vars.md:160` — all state the
  wrong (Splunk-scheme-only) auth contract.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:17-19` — package doc pins the real behavior: HTTP Basic auth,
  password = token.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:397-408` (`authorized()`) — checks Basic first, Splunk second; both are
  accepted, so nothing breaks functionally, but the docs contradict verified behavior.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:104` (`MetricRejected` comment) vs `catalog.go:27` (has `too_large`).

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator debugging 401s from a custom HEC forwarder (or writing a proxy/auth layer in front of

body:
## Problem
`enduser.id` and `tailscale.user.login` — the two attributes the per-user gauges (`tailscale.user.devices`, `tailscale.user.connected`, `tailscale.user.last_seen`) key on — are classified in the PII registry (`CatUserIDs`/`CatEmails` respectively) but are missing from the separate `identityKeys` set that `Redactor.Identity` checks before deciding whether to *suppress* a gauge whose identity is fully redacted. Because neither key is in `identityKeys`, `Redactor.Identity` never fires its suppression branch for these gauges; instead each attribute is independently dropped once redacted, leaving an *empty* attribute set that is emitted rather than suppressed.

Note: this is **not** a PII leak — when both `pii_filter.user_ids` and `pii_filter.emails` are disabled, the identifiers ARE correctly dropped; nothing sensitive escapes. The defect is a correctness/observability one: the gauges collapse to a single last-write-wins series instead of being suppressed, per the documented contract ("gauges whose only meaningful identity is a redacted category are suppressed entirely").

## Evidence
- `internal/collector/users/users.go:126-144` — emits `docUserDevices`/`docUserConnected`/`docUserLastSeen` with `idAttrs := {enduser.id: u.ID, tailscale.user.login: u.LoginName}`.
- `internal/telemetry/pii/registry.go:52-65` — `identityKeys` map does not include `enduser.id` or `tailscale.user.login` (contrast `host.name`/`host.id`, which ARE registered for the device analog).
- `internal/telemetry/pii/pii.go:107-131` — `Redactor.Identity` only suppresses when `identityPresent > 0` and all present identity keys are redacted.
- Verified empirically: with `CatUserIDs=false` and `CatEmails=false`, calling `Redactor.Identity` on two different users' attrs (`{enduser.id:"user-A",...}` / `{enduser.id:"user-B",...}`) both returned `suppress=false` and an identical empty map.
- `docs/configuration.md:552` documents the intended contract this code fails to honor for user gauges (while honoring it correctly for the device analog — `TestIdentitySuppressesWhenAllIdentityRedacted`).

## Failure scenario / impact
An operator disables both `pii_filter.user_ids` and `pii_filter.emails` (a plausible privacy-hardening combination this feature exists for) with `cardinality.per_entity.user` still enabled. Every per-user gauge for every user in the tailnet then emits with an empty attribute set instead of being suppressed; a synchronous OTEL gauge with the same (empty) attribute set collapses to one series per collection interval, so all users' distinct device counts/connection states/last-seen times get silently merged into a single arbitrary last-write-wins series that looks like real per-user data but represents an undefined single user.

## Suggested direction
Add `enduser.id` and `tailscale.user.login` to the `identityKeys` map, mirroring how `host.name`/`host.id` are registered for devices, so `Redactor.Identity` suppresses these gauges entirely once both identifying categories are disabled.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `identityKeys` includes the user identity keys (`enduser.id`, `tailscale.user.login`).
- [ ] A test mirroring `TestIdentitySuppressesWhenAllIdentityRedacted` covers the per-user gauge case (both categories disabled → suppressed, not collapsed).

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by `7126f31`. `enduser.id` and `tailscale.user.login` are now in the PII `identityKeys` set, so `Redactor.Identity` suppresses the per-user gauges when both `user_ids` and `emails` are redacted, instead of emitting them with an empty attribute set that collapses all users into one series. Mirrors the device analog; test mirrors `TestIdentitySuppressesWhenAllIdentityRedacted`. _(Sonnet subagent; gated on main.)_

body:
## Problem
Two credential-bearing config fields — OTLP headers and node-metrics per-target headers — are plain `map[string]string` instead of the `config.Secret` type every other credential in this codebase uses, leaving a gap in the project's "Secret redacts itself everywhere" guarantee.

## Evidence
- `internal/config/config.go:264` — `Headers map[string]string` (`OTLPConfig`).
- `internal/config/config.go:570` — `Headers map[string]string` (node-metrics targets).
- Every other credential field already uses `Secret`: `api_key`, `client_secret`, `grafana_cloud.token`, `streaming.token`, `webhook.secret`, admin/prometheus tokens, pyroscope password, `bearer_token` (`config.go:97,115,145,179,233,239,272,568,595,622`).
- `secret.go:38` — states the design goal explicitly: "a future debug endpoint or config dump must not become a credential leak."
- `internal/app/status.go:527-534` — the status page currently only emits header *key* names, so nothing leaks today; this is a latent gap, not an active leak.

## Failure scenario / impact
The documented way to authenticate OTLP against a non-Grafana-Cloud gateway is `otlp.headers: {Authorization: ...}`; per-node scrape auth can use a target `headers` map. A future contributor adds a debug log or config-dump endpoint that serializes `Config`, relying on the established "Secret redacts itself everywhere" guarantee — every credential is redacted except the OTLP/node-metrics header values, which land in logs or the endpoint output verbatim.

## Suggested direction
Change both `Headers` maps to `map[string]config.Secret` (calling `Reveal()` at the two consumption points in `internal/app/options.go`), or wrap them in a redacting type; add the fields to the `secret_test.go` redaction guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] OTLP `headers` values are typed as `config.Secret`
- [ ] Node-metrics target `headers` values are typed as `config.Secret`
- [ ] Both consumption points call `Reveal()` where the raw value is needed
- [ ] `secret_test.go`'s redaction guard covers both fields

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

OTLP `headers` and node-metrics per-target `headers` values are now typed `map[string]config.Secret`, so they redact in any config dump/log; `Reveal()` is called at the two consumption points in options.go. secret_test.go's end-to-end redaction guard now covers both fields (and asserts Reveal still returns the real value).

body:
## Problem

`internal/tsapi/services.go:40-44` tags the decoded field `NodeID string \`json:"nodeId"\`` on
`ServiceHost`, but Tailscale's own OpenAPI spec for this exact endpoint (`spec/tailscale-api.json`,
schema `ServiceHostInfo` for `GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/services/{serviceName}/devices`) names the wire
field `stableNodeID`, not `nodeId`. `encoding/json` falls back to case-insensitive matching only, not
fuzzy/substring matching, so `nodeId` never matches the wire key `stableNodeID` and `ServiceHost.NodeID`
always decodes to the empty string. `internal/tsapi/contract/manifest.go` has no `listServiceHosts`
entry at all, so this endpoint is excluded from the decode-fuzz/contract drift tests that would
otherwise catch a field-name mismatch like this.

## Evidence

- `internal/tsapi/services.go:40-44` — `NodeID string \`json:"nodeId"\``
- `spec/tailscale-api.json` — `ServiceHostInfo` schema names the field `stableNodeID`
- `internal/tsapi/contract/manifest.go` — no `listServiceHosts` entry (grep-confirmed)
- `internal/collector/services/services.go:114-125` — only reads `h.ApprovalLevel`/`h.Configured`
  today, so the bug is currently latent/harmless

## Failure scenario / impact

The bug is harmless today because nothing reads `NodeID`. But if a future change adds a per-host
node-identity metric or log field (a natural next step, since `NodeID` already exists on the
struct), it would silently emit an empty string for every host rather than erroring, because there
is no test or contract check on this endpoint to flag the mismatch.

## Suggested direction

Fix the JSON tag to `stableNodeID` per the OAS schema, and add a `listServiceHosts` contract-fuzz
entry (with a fixed/fake service name) so future field additions on this endpoint get the same
drift protection as other endpoints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ServiceHost.NodeID`'s JSON tag matches the OAS wire field (`stableNodeID`)
- [ ] a `listServiceHosts` contract-fuzz entry is added to `internal/tsapi/contract/manifest.go`
- [ ] a test confirms `NodeID` decodes correctly from a representative fixture

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

Corrected `ServiceHost.NodeID`'s JSON tag to `stableNodeID` (the OAS ServiceHostInfo wire field), added a `listServiceHosts` contract-fuzz manifest entry (LiveSkip, placeholder service name) for drift protection, and fixed the test fixture which had used the fictional `nodeId` and masked the bug.

body:
## Problem
The webhook receiver's pre-authentication body buffering is capped at a hardwired 64 MiB with no config knob to lower it, unlike the streaming receiver which exposes `max_body_bytes` and authenticates via a header bearer token *before* reading the body. Because the webhook's HMAC signature covers the whole body, some pre-auth buffering is structurally unavoidable — but there's no way for an operator to tighten the cap to match real (KB-scale) Tailscale webhook payloads.

- **Config knob gap:** `webhook.Options.MaxBodyBytes` exists (`webhook.go:149-152`) but `internal/app/collectors.go:212-220` (`webhookOptions()`) never sets it from config, and `config.WebhookConfig` has no `max_body_bytes` key at all — unlike `streaming`, which has one (`config.go:605-608`).
- **Default too high:** `defaultMaxBodyBytes = 64 << 20 // 64 MiB` (`webhook.go:77`) is sized for the streaming receiver's batch flow logs, not the webhook's KB-scale event payloads.

## Evidence
- `internal/webhook/webhook.go:77` — `defaultMaxBodyBytes = 64 << 20 // 64 MiB`.
- `internal/webhook/webhook.go:304-323` (`handle`) — body is fully read via `readBody`/`MaxBytesReader` (webhook.go:350-358) *before* `verify()` (webhook.go:317) runs, because HMAC requires the whole body.
- `internal/app/collectors.go:212-220` — `webhookOptions()` never wires `MaxBodyBytes` from config.
- `internal/config/config.go:610-628` (`WebhookConfig`) — no `max_body_bytes` key, unlike `config.go:605-608` for streaming.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:279,287` — streaming's `authorized()` runs before `readBody()`, since its auth is a header token, not a body HMAC.
- Existing test: `TestHandler_MaxBodyBytesTooLargeRejectedBeforeSignature` (`webhook_test.go:177`) confirms the cap already fires and bounds memory today — this is a hardening/consistency gap, not an unbounded-memory bug.

## Failure scenario / impact
The webhook listener must be internet-reachable for Tailscale's control plane to deliver events. An operator who wants to reduce the pre-auth buffering ceiling below 64 MiB (to better match KB-scale real payloads and reduce the per-connection worst case under N concurrent requests) currently has no config surface to do so, and the default itself is far higher than any real payload requires.

## Suggested direction
Wire `webhook.Options.MaxBodyBytes` to a new `webhook.max_body_bytes` config key, mirroring streaming's existing knob, and consider lowering the shipped default from 64 MiB to something proportionate to real event payloads (e.g. ~1 MiB), while keeping the knob available for outliers. Note: rejecting requests missing the signature header before reading the body is *not* a valid mitigation — it's trivially bypassed by sending any dummy signature header, since verification structurally requires the full body first. The cap itself remains the real defense.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `webhook.max_body_bytes` config key exists, is documented, and is wired through to `webhook.Options.MaxBodyBytes`
- [ ] The shipped default is lowered to a value proportionate to real Tailscale webhook payload sizes
- [ ] Existing `MaxBodyBytes`-cap test coverage still passes with the new config-driven value
- [ ] docs/env-vars.md and configuration.md regenerated/updated to reflect the new key

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus/sonnet._

comments.body: Done in 5d43509 (pushed to main). Added the `webhook.max_body_bytes` config knob (wired through webhookOptions) and lowered the pre-signature-verification default from 64 MiB to 1 MiB. config.example.yaml + env-vars.md updated.

body:
## Problem
The checkpoint store has two related robustness/truthfulness gaps:

- **A corrupt checkpoint file crash-loops startup instead of degrading gracefully.** `NewFileStore` returns the `json.Unmarshal` error as-is when the file content is corrupt/truncated/incompatible; that propagates straight through `app.New` to a fatal `os.Exit(1)` in `main()`. This is the *opposite* of the deliberate degrade-to-memory policy already applied one code path over, for an unwritable checkpoint directory. In a Kubernetes deployment (the default Helm config uses `store=file`), this is a `CrashLoopBackOff` until someone execs into the volume and deletes the file. Verified real: `os.Rename`'s atomic write means a hard kill/SIGKILL/OOM/panic *cannot* cause this — the only real triggers are true power loss / kernel panic within the fsync-ordering gap, or manual edit / bit-rot / restoring an incompatible-schema backup. The corrupted data is non-critical window-cursor state; graceful degrade just means a cold start from `initial_lookback`.
- **The status page and checkpoint reporter report the config value, not the effective store.** `checkpointStore()` silently falls back to an in-memory store (WARN log only) when the file path is unwritable or empty — but `ConfigSummary`/the status page report the raw config value (`"file"`), and `Run()` gates `RunCheckpointReporter` on that same config value rather than the effective store, so the reporter points at a file the fallback store will never write and reports stale/no data.
- Additionally the atomic temp-file+rename write path has no `fsync` — a minor durability nit for otherwise-disposable cursor state.

## Evidence
- `internal/collector/checkpoint.go:60-64` — `NewFileStore` returns the raw unmarshal error.
- `internal/app/app.go:147-151` → `cmd/tailscale2otel/main.go:40-43` — propagates to `os.Exit(1)`.
- `internal/app/app.go:547-552` — contrast: the unwritable-directory case degrades gracefully to `collector.NewMemoryStore()` with only a WARN.
- `internal/collector/checkpoint_test.go` — only tests valid-JSON persistence and a missing file; no corrupt-file test.
- `internal/app/app.go:543-554` (`checkpointStore()`) — silent fallback to memory on an unwritable path or empty `FilePath`.
- `internal/app/status.go:513-518` — `ConfigSummary` reports the raw `c.Checkpoint.Store` config value, not the effective store.
- `internal/app/app.go:412-414` — `RunCheckpointReporter` gated on `a.cfg.Checkpoint.Store == "file"`, not the effective store.
- `internal/collector/checkpoint.go:83-89` — `os.WriteFile` + `os.Rename` with no `fsync` of the file or its directory.

## Failure scenario / impact
A `checkpoints.json` that fails to unmarshal (bit-rot, manual edit, incompatible-schema restore) makes `tailscale2otel` unable to start at all — a single-binary production tool with no persistence safety net for this one failure mode, and zero test coverage for it. Separately: a container redeployed with a read-only filesystem and no volume WARNs once at startup, then the status page claims file-backed checkpoints indefinitely; on the next restart, flowlogs/auditlogs cold-start from `initial_lookback`, re-emitting an hours-long window the operator believed was checkpointed, with no correct signal telling them why.

## Suggested direction
On unmarshal failure, WARN, optionally rename the corrupt file aside, and start empty — matching the unwritable-dir fallback (add a test for this). Record the effective store kind (and fallback reason) on `App` at build time; use it — not the raw config value — in `ConfigSummary`/the status page and to gate `RunCheckpointReporter`. Optionally add an `fsync` of the temp file (and ideally its directory) before/after rename for crash durability.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A corrupt-checkpoint-file test asserts a WARN + in-memory fallback, not a fatal `os.Exit(1)`.
- [ ] The status page and `ConfigSummary` show the effective checkpoint store, not the raw config value.
- [ ] `RunCheckpointReporter` gates on the effective store.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Closed by 38dfcaa. `NewFileStore` returns `ErrCorruptCheckpoint` on decode failure; `checkpointStore` catches it, renames the file to `.corrupt` and starts empty (cold start) rather than crash-looping. It now also returns the effective store kind ("file"/"memory"), which `ConfigSummary`/status page and the `RunCheckpointReporter` gate use instead of the raw config value. The atomic write path now fsyncs the temp file + directory. Tests cover the corrupt-file degrade, the unwritable→memory effective report, and Keys/Delete persistence.

body:
## Problem

Three metric/log catalog descriptions are factually wrong or incomplete:

- **device-invite `host.id`**: `internal/collector/devices/catalog.go:278`'s
  `docDeviceInviteLog.Description` states `host.id` is "the sharing device's nodeId". Every
  `semconv.HostID` assignment in `devices.go` (lines 472, 507, 516, 525, 558, 590, 661, 682, 866,
  928, 964, 995) actually uses `d.ID` (the numeric RichDevice device ID), never `d.NodeID` — the
  inline comment at `devices.go:866` correctly says "device id, consistent with every other device
  signal", directly contradicting the generated-docs description one field over. `nodeId` and `id`
  are different identifier spaces, so a consumer trying to join this log's `host.id` to flow-log
  `tailscale.src.node`/`tailscale.dst.node` (which *are* nodeId-keyed) per the documented claim
  fails to correlate.
- **logstream `_ratio` caveat**: `internal/collector/logstream/catalog.go:16-23,80-87`
  (`docConfigured`/`docError`) describe plain `1`/`0` flags with no mention of Prometheus naming.
  `webhooks/catalog.go:18` explicitly notes "a **count**, despite `_ratio`" for the analogous
  unit-1 gauge. `metricdoc.PromName()` appends `_ratio` to any unit-"1" gauge regardless of whether
  the value is a fraction, and `docs/metrics.md:352,354` confirm the resulting names
  `tailscale_logstream_configured_ratio`/`tailscale_logstream_error_ratio` — logstream's docs don't
  carry the same disambiguating caveat webhooks' do.
- **acl `last_changed` restart semantics**: the metric's true meaning is "wall-clock time this
  process first observed the current ETag" (documented in code at `acl.go:57-58`), not a true
  policy-modification timestamp — the Tailscale API (`RawACL`) exposes only HuJSON + ETag, no real
  last-modified field, so on every process restart the very next `Collect()` treats the current ETag
  as newly observed and resets `lastChanged` to the restart time. `docs/metrics.md:278` documents
  the metric with no such caveat.

## Evidence

- `internal/collector/devices/catalog.go:278` vs `devices.go:866` (contradicting inline comment)
- `internal/collector/logstream/catalog.go:16-23,80-87` vs `internal/collector/webhooks/catalog.go:18`
- `internal/collector/acl/acl.go:57-58,98-102` (state is in-process only, resets `!haveETag` on
  every restart) vs `docs/metrics.md:278` (no restart/first-observed caveat)

## Failure scenario / impact

- A user reads `docs/metrics.md`, sees `host.id` described as a `nodeId`, and tries to join it to
  node-id-keyed flow/audit data — the join silently returns nothing because the value is actually
  the numeric device ID.
- An operator building a "log stream health" alert queries `tailscale_logstream_configured_ratio`
  and either misinterprets it as a computed fraction or wonders if it's a naming bug.
- An operator alerting on `tailscale.acl.last_changed` for "flag if ACL changed outside a
  maintenance window" gets a false positive on every restart/rollout, with no documented caveat
  explaining why.

## Suggested direction

Correct the device-invite `host.id` description to say "device id" (matching every other usage in
the package); mirror the webhooks "(despite `_ratio`)" wording into logstream's
`docConfigured`/`docError` descriptions; add a "resets to process-start time on restart / means
first-observed, not true modification time" caveat to the acl `last_changed` description
(`catalog.go` `docACLLastChanged`) and `docs/metrics.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docDeviceInviteLog.Description` says "device id", not "nodeId"
- [ ] logstream's `docConfigured`/`docError` descriptions carry the same `_ratio`-caveat wording as
      webhooks
- [ ] the acl `last_changed` description documents the restart/first-observed semantic
- [ ] `docs/metrics.md` regenerated and reflects all three corrections

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus/sonnet._

## Problem
Stream-receiver records that classify as unrecognized/unclassifiable are only logged at Debug level with a count, not exposed as a metric — and records dropped inside `unwrap` (a non-object HEC "event" value) aren't counted at all. The receiver still acks 200 regardless.

## Evidence
- `internal/stream/stream.go:372-374` — `if skipped > 0 { s.logger.Debug("stream: skipped unrecognized records", "count", skipped) }`, no counter.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:610-625` — `unwrap` returns `nil` for a non-object HEC "event" value; those drops are never added to `skipped`.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:386` — the request still acks 200 `{"text":"Success"}` regardless of how many records were dropped.

## Failure scenario / impact
Tailscale changes a flow-record field name (e.g. renames `nodeId`) — `classify` returns `kindUnknown` for every record, flow telemetry silently flatlines, and there is zero rejected/decode-error signal for an operator to alert on; the only trace is a Debug-level log most deployments won't have enabled.

## Suggested direction
Emit a skipped-records counter (e.g. a new reason on `MetricRejected` or a dedicated `tailscale.stream.skipped`) that also includes records dropped during `unwrap`; consider a rate-limited Warn-level log in addition to (or instead of) Debug.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Skipped/unclassifiable stream records are counted in a metric, not just logged
- [ ] Records dropped inside `unwrap` are included in that count
- [ ] Test asserting the metric increments for both classify-unknown and unwrap-drop cases

## Problem
`tsapi.Options.UserAgent` is defined and honored by the request helpers, but nothing ever populates it, so every raw tsapi request goes out with the default Go HTTP client user-agent instead of identifying itself as tailscale2otel.

## Evidence
- `internal/tsapi/client.go:27` — `UserAgent string` field defined.
- `internal/tsapi/logs.go:46-48` — `getJSON`/`putJSON`/log requests honor `UserAgent` when set.
- `internal/app/options.go:126-142` (`tsapiOptionsFor`) — never sets `UserAgent`; no other caller does either (only tests reference it).

## Failure scenario / impact
All raw-doer requests (`devices?fields=all`, `logging/network`, `logging/configuration`, `keys` — the highest-volume calls) are sent as `Go-http-client/2.0`. During a rate-limit incident or abuse investigation, Tailscale support has no way to attribute traffic to tailscale2otel, and the running version (already injected into `main` via ldflags) isn't visible on the wire either.

## Suggested direction
Set `UserAgent` to `"tailscale2otel/<version>"` in `tsapiOptionsFor` — the version is already threaded into `app.New`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All raw tsapi requests carry a `tailscale2otel/<version>` User-Agent header
- [ ] Version string matches the one reported elsewhere (status page / ldflags-injected `main.version`)
- [ ] Test asserting the header is present on outgoing requests

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

body:
## Problem

Four in-code comments have drifted from actual behavior:

- **providerset.go target_info claim**: `internal/telemetry/providerset.go:17,23-26` still describe
  `tailscale.tailnet` as riding along in a Resource attribute / `target_info` ("plus one Provider
  per tailnet (each Resource carries tailscale.tailnet=<name>)"). This was superseded by the
  const-attr redesign (`emitter.go:61-66`, `provider.go:410-436`): tailnet/provider are now
  per-signal const attrs, deliberately *not* Resource attributes.
- **appcatalog `_ratio` claim**: `internal/appcatalog/catalog.go:395-397` claims the unit
  `"{series}"` annotation is dropped under Prometheus normalization, leaving
  `tailscale2otel_series_by_group_ratio`. `metricdoc.PromName` only appends `_ratio` to unit-`"1"`
  gauges — annotation units get no suffix — and every real reference (deploy/, docs/metrics.md) uses
  the unsuffixed `tailscale2otel_series_by_group`.
- **telemetry/CLAUDE.md Emitter sketch**: lists the `Emitter` interface without `Histogram`/
  `HistogramCtx`, even though `types.go:47-65` defines six methods.
- **checkpoint persist-failure re-poll claim**: `internal/collector/selfobs.go:41-45`'s comment on
  `MetricCheckpointPersistErrors` claims "the next tick re-polls the same window" on a checkpoint
  persist failure. In fact both store implementations (`checkpoint.go`: `memoryStore.Set` and
  `fileStore.Set`) advance the in-memory cursor *before* the disk write can fail, so the scheduler's
  next `Get` sees the new value and polls the *next* window — the failed window is only re-polled
  after a process restart, as the separate comment at `selfobs.go:111-113` correctly states. This
  wrong text is confined to the internal Go source comment; the generated, user-facing
  `docs/metrics.md:116` (from `catalog.go:69-75`) is already correct and makes no re-poll claim.

## Evidence

- `internal/telemetry/providerset.go:17,23-26`
- `internal/appcatalog/catalog.go:395-397`
- `internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md` interface snippet (missing `Histogram`/`HistogramCtx`, vs
  `internal/telemetry/types.go:47-65`)
- `internal/collector/selfobs.go:41-45` (wrong) vs `selfobs.go:111-113` (correct) vs
  `docs/metrics.md:116` (correct, unaffected)

## Failure scenario / impact

A contributor extending multi-tailnet naming follows providerset.go's stale Resource description
and misses the const-attr path, or writes an alert on `tailscale2otel_series_by_group_ratio` from
the appcatalog comment — the query silently matches nothing. Separately, a future contributor
reading the internal checkpoint comment could misjudge duplicate/gap behavior on persist failure
(though no operator-facing doc carries this particular error, since `docs/metrics.md` is already
correct).

## Suggested direction

Update all four comment sites to match the current const-attr design, the real Prometheus name, the
full six-method `Emitter` interface, and the correct in-memory-advances-regardless-of-disk-outcome
checkpoint semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `providerset.go:17,23-26` describes the const-attr placement, not Resource/`target_info`
- [ ] `appcatalog.go:395-397` states the correct (unsuffixed) Prometheus name for this metric
- [ ] `internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md`'s `Emitter` interface sketch lists all six methods
- [ ] `internal/collector/selfobs.go:41-45`'s comment correctly describes in-memory-advance /
      restart-triggered re-poll semantics

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Closed by `33942fe` (Phase 6 code/security). See the commit body for specifics.

body:
## Problem
The Headscale adapter zero-fills several fields that Headscale's API simply doesn't provide, but the downstream collectors then emit those zero values as real telemetry rather than omitting the signal — conflating "Headscale doesn't report this" with "this is genuinely false/zero". Sub-items:

- **Spent preauth keys look identical to live keys.** `adaptPreAuthKey` never reads Headscale's `used` field, so a non-reusable one-time key that has already registered a node keeps reporting a live `tailscale.key.expiry` gauge and can still trigger the `tailscale.key.expiring` "take action" WARN, even though it's permanently spent.
- **`authorized` is always false for Headscale devices.** `adaptNode` never sets `RichDevice.Authorized` (Headscale has no such concept), so every Headscale device is bucketed as unauthorized in `tailscale.devices.count`'s `authorized` dimension — a misleading value, not an absent one, since it's a dimension on an always-emitted aggregate.
- **`tailscale.user.devices`/`tailscale.user.connected` are fabricated zeros.** `adaptUser` never sets `DeviceCount`/`CurrentlyConnected`, and unlike `LastSeen` (which the users collector correctly gates with `if !u.LastSeen.IsZero()`), these two gauges are emitted unconditionally — every Headscale user shows exactly 0 devices and disconnected, regardless of reality.
- **Security/hygiene booleans are zero-filled and emitted as real values.** `adaptNode` never sets `UpdateAvailable`/`IsEphemeral`/`IsExternal`, and `devices.go` emits them unconditionally: `tailscale.device.update_available` always reports 0 (docs already say this should be "no data" — the code contradicts the doc), and the `authorized`/`external`/ephemeral rollups are computed the same way as `authorized` above.
- **The `adaptNode` doc comment doesn't enumerate every zeroed field**, so gaps are easy to silently rediscover later.

## Evidence
- `internal/hsapi/adapt.go:69-79` (`adaptPreAuthKey`) never reads `p.Used`; `internal/hsapi/types.go:55` decodes it. `internal/collector/keys/keys.go:146-181` gates purely on `k.Revoked`/`k.Invalid`/`k.Expires`, with no reference to consumption.
- `internal/hsapi/adapt.go:38-54` (`adaptNode`) never sets `Authorized`. `internal/collector/devices/devices.go:562,694` buckets `tailscale.devices.count` by `authorized`. `docs/configuration.md:134-140` lists Headscale "no data" signals but doesn't mention `authorized`.
- `internal/hsapi/adapt.go:58-66` (`adaptUser`) never sets `DeviceCount`/`CurrentlyConnected`. `internal/collector/users/users.go:131-139` emits both unconditionally, in contrast to the `LastSeen` gate at line ~141.
- `internal/hsapi/adapt.go:38-54` also never sets `UpdateAvailable`/`IsEphemeral`/`IsExternal`. `internal/collector/devices/devices.go:500-501` (update_available), `:562` (authorized/external count dims), `:565-573` (ephemeral/untagged rollups) all emit unconditionally. `docs/configuration.md:137-139` already documents `update_available` as "no data" under Headscale — the code contradicts this.
- `internal/provider/provider.go:40` — `users` is a fully-supported (not gated) Headscale collector; `internal/config/defaults.go` — `Cardinality.PerEntity.User` defaults `true`, so these gauges fire out of the box.

## Failure scenario / impact
A Headscale operator builds an "update compliance" dashboard/alert off `tailscale.device.update_available` — it reports every node as fully up to date forever, silently. A "devices by authorized" panel shows 100% of Headscale nodes as unauthorized permanently. A "users with 0 devices" cleanup report or "no users currently connected" idle-tailnet alert silently shows false data for every Headscale tailnet. An operator provisions a one-time preauth key that gets used within minutes — for the rest of its expiration window it still counts as live and can still trigger an actionable-looking expiry WARN.

## Suggested direction
Map `p.Used` (for non-reusable keys) into `tsapi.Key.Invalid` (or a dedicated bucket), and exclude used one-time keys from the expiry warning. Either default `Authorized=true` in `adaptNode` (Headscale nodes are registered by definition), drop the dimension under Headscale, or document it. Gate `user.devices`/`user.connected` like `LastSeen` already is. Gate the zero-filled device booleans (`update_available`, etc.) the same way, or explicitly document them as no-data (fixing the code/doc contradiction). Enumerate every zeroed field in the `adaptNode` comment so this class of gap doesn't get silently rediscovered.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No Headscale-backed gauge emits a fabricated value for a field Headscale doesn't provide (preauth key `used`, `authorized`, `update_available`, `user.devices`/`user.connected`, and any other zero-filled boolean/count).
- [ ] `docs/configuration.md`'s Headscale gap list is complete and matches the code exactly.
- [ ] Adapter tests (`adaptPreAuthKey`, `adaptNode`, `adaptUser`) cover the zero-value/no-data cases.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Closed by `3b4cbbb`. All five sub-items: used one-time preauth keys → `Key.Invalid` (expiry gauge + expiring WARN now gated on `!Invalid`); `Authorized=true` for Headscale nodes (registered by definition); new `devices.WithUpdateAvailableData`/`WithEphemeralData` + `users.WithActivityData` options suppress `update_available`, `devices.ephemeral`, `user.devices`, `user.connected` under Headscale (wired in `collectors.go` gated on `provider==headscale`; Tailscale path unchanged, options default true); `adaptNode`/`adaptUser`/`adaptPreAuthKey` comments enumerate every zeroed field; `docs/configuration.md` gap list now matches code. Adapter + collector tests cover the no-data cases. _(Implemented by a Sonnet subagent; the collectors.go wiring + integration gate done on the main thread.)_ Note: gating expiry on `!Invalid` also correctly stops a revoked-but-unexpired Tailscale key from reporting a live expiry — a same-direction correctness improvement, no test regressions.

body:
## Problem
A split-DNS domain with a null/empty resolver list is counted in the aggregate `tailscale.dns.split_zones.count`, but the per-resolver loop never emits a point for it, so there is no way to identify, from the per-resolver series, which counted domain is the empty one.

## Evidence
- `internal/tsapi/dns.go:16-18` — comment: "A domain whose wire value is null decodes to a present key with an empty slice."
- `internal/collector/dns/dns.go:92-93` — `tailscale.dns.split_zones.count = len(cfg.SplitDNS)` counts the domain key regardless of whether its resolver slice is empty.
- `internal/collector/dns/dns.go:112-124` — the per-resolver loop (`for domain, resolvers := range cfg.SplitDNS { for _, r := range resolvers {...} }`) emits zero `tailscale.dns.resolver` points for a domain with an empty resolver slice.

## Failure scenario / impact
An admin configures split DNS with 3 domains, one of which intentionally has a null resolver list (a legitimate Tailscale feature for excluding a subdomain from a broader override). `tailscale.dns.split_zones.count` reports 3, but `tailscale.dns.resolver{kind="split"}` only ever shows 2 distinct `domain` values — with no metric surfacing which domain has no resolvers or why the counts don't reconcile.

## Suggested direction
Emit a `tailscale.dns.resolver` (or similar) info point for domains with an empty resolver list too (e.g. `address=""`), so every domain counted in `split_zones.count` has a corresponding identifiable series.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every domain counted in `tailscale.dns.split_zones.count` has at least one corresponding identifiable series/point
- [ ] A split-DNS domain with an empty resolver list is distinguishable from one with real resolvers
- [ ] Test covering a split-DNS config with a mix of populated and empty resolver lists

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Done in 5d43509 (pushed to main). Split-DNS zones with an empty resolver list now emit an identifiable per-domain signal instead of being indistinguishable from absent config. metrics.md regenerated.

body:
## Problem

`internal/telemetry/selfobs.go:28-39` installs a global OTEL error handler that logs every
`otel.Handle(err)` call as `"OTLP export failed"` and increments `tailscale2otel.export.failures`.
But the `Emitter` itself routes instrument-creation errors through that same hook
(`emitter.go:112-117`, e.g. `otel.Handle(err)` on a `Float64Counter` construction failure, same for
gauge/updown/histogram). The OTEL SDK returns a perfectly usable instrument *plus*
`ErrInstrumentName` for names outside `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-/]*` — it doesn't actually fail to
export anything.

## Evidence

- `internal/telemetry/selfobs.go:28-39` — global handler treats every `otel.Handle` call as an
  export failure.
- `internal/telemetry/emitter.go:112-117` — instrument-creation errors (e.g. bad Prometheus name)
  also go through `otel.Handle`.
- `sdk/metric@v1.44.0/meter.go:250-260` (`validateInstrumentName`) — the SDK returns a working
  instrument alongside the name-validation error; nothing is actually dropped.

## Failure scenario / impact

A forwarded node-metrics sample whose Prometheus name contains a colon (legal in Prometheus
exposition, e.g. a recording-rule-style name) fails OTEL name validation on first emit. The handler
logs `"OTLP export failed"` (WARN) and bumps the export-failure counter even though no export was
ever attempted and the metric still records and exports correctly. Operators alerting on
`tailscale2otel_export_failures_total` get a spurious failure with `error.type="export"` and a
misleading log line, sending them to debug backend connectivity instead of the metric name.

## Suggested direction

Classify errors in the handler — e.g. `errors.Is(err, sdkmetric.ErrInstrumentName)` → a distinct
`error.type` and a non-export log message — or route instrument-creation failures to the diag
logger instead of `otel.Handle` in the first place.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] instrument-name/creation errors are classified distinctly from real OTLP export failures
- [ ] `tailscale2otel.export.failures` only increments for genuine export failures
- [ ] a test exercises an invalid instrument name and asserts it is not counted as an export failure

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Closed by 16246da. The global OTEL error handler now checks `errors.Is(err, sdkmetric.ErrInstrumentName)` first: such errors are logged distinctly ("metric still records/exports") and NOT counted against `tailscale2otel.export.failures`, since the SDK returns a usable instrument and nothing is dropped. Test asserts an instrument-name error produces zero export-failure points while a genuine export error still increments the counter.

body:
## Problem
The devices collector's `lastPosture` map (`devices.go:220-223`), used by the default `postureLogChanges` mode to remember each device's last posture signature, is only ever written to (`devices.go:956`) and never pruned when a device disappears from a later `DevicesRich()` response. It grows for the life of the process, keyed by every distinct device ID ever seen — not the current fleet.

## Evidence
- `internal/collector/devices/devices.go:220-223` — `lastPosture map[string]string`, initialized once in `New` (line 388).
- `internal/collector/devices/devices.go:956` — `c.lastPosture[d.ID] = sig`, write-only, no delete path.

## Failure scenario / impact
A tailnet with high device churn (ephemeral CI/cloud nodes — `ephemeral=true` devices are explicitly supported elsewhere in this collector) running with `collect_posture: true` over an extended period sees `lastPosture`'s memory footprint grow roughly proportional to the cumulative distinct device count ever observed, not the current fleet size.

## Suggested direction
Rebuild/prune `lastPosture` each tick to only the device IDs present in the current `DevicesRich()` response — e.g. build a fresh map from the current pass instead of mutating the long-lived one in place.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `lastPosture` no longer retains entries for devices absent from the current tick's inventory
- [ ] Posture-changed detection still works correctly across ticks for devices that remain in the fleet
- [ ] Test covering a device leaving the fleet and its posture entry being pruned

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Done in 5d43509 (pushed to main). The devices collector now prunes its `lastPosture` map to the current fleet each tick, so departed devices no longer leak memory / stale posture state.

body:
## Problem

In multi-tailnet mode, `internal/app/app.go:186-189` pins the app's dedup self-obs state to
`runtimes[0]` only:

```go
a.flowDedup = a.runtimes[0].flowDedup
a.auditDedup = a.runtimes[0].auditDedup
```

(the field comments at `app.go:75-76` explicitly say "runtimes[0] ... retained for the dedup
self-obs reporter"). `Run()` feeds only these two sets into `runDedupReporter` (`app.go:405-409`),
and the status page's `dedupInfo` (`status.go:363-375`) reports the same pair. But every tailnet
runtime maintains its own independent flow/audit dedup sets (`tailnetruntime.go:86,94`), which
suppress inclusive-window poll overlap for that specific tailnet.

## Evidence

- `internal/app/app.go:186-189` — dedup fields aliased to `runtimes[0]` only.
- `internal/app/app.go:75-76` — comment documenting the (incomplete) intent.
- `internal/app/app.go:405-409` — `runDedupReporter` only sees the aliased sets.
- `internal/app/status.go:363-375` — status page `dedupInfo` mirrors the same limited view.
- `internal/app/tailnetruntime.go:86,94` — each runtime owns its own flow/audit dedup sets.
- `internal/appcatalog/catalog.go:313-320` — `dedup.evictions` doc: "sustained growth means the
  set is undersized" — precisely the signal that goes dark for tailnets 1..N-1.

## Failure scenario / impact

Two tailnets configured, the second much busier: its 16384-entry flow dedup set churns and evicts
keys inside the inclusive-window poll overlap, re-emitting boundary connections every tick.
`dedup.size`/`dedup.evictions` stay flat (they describe tailnet #1's quiet set), so the operator has
no way to see why tailnet #2's flow bytes run hot — double-counted flow/audit data with zero
observable signal.

## Suggested direction

Iterate `a.runtimes` in both `runDedupReporter` and `dedupInfo`, keying each set by name+tailnet
(e.g. via the existing dedup-set attribute plus the per-tailnet emitter), instead of pinning to
`runtimes[0]`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tailscale2otel.dedup.*` self-obs metrics are emitted per tailnet runtime in multi-tailnet
      mode, not just for `runtimes[0]`
- [ ] the admin status page's dedup info section shows per-tailnet dedup set stats (size,
      evictions, hits) keyed by tailnet name
- [ ] a multi-tailnet test asserts dedup self-obs/status data is reported for every runtime, not
      only the first

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body:
**From the v1 bug-bash round-2 sweep:**

In multi-tailnet mode, only `runtimes[0]`'s flow/audit dedup sets are wired into the self-obs reporter and the status page — `internal/app/app.go:186-189` explicitly does `if len(a.runtimes) > 0 { a.flowDedup = a.runtimes[0].flowDedup; a.auditDedup = a.runtimes[0].auditDedup }` (comment at `app.go:75-76` confirms this is intentional: "runtimes[0] ... retained for the dedup self-obs reporter"). Each tailnet runtime actually constructs its own flow (16384) and audit (4096) sets (`tailnetruntime.go:86,94`), but only the first configured tailnet's sets are ever observable.

This means the emitted `dedup_set="flow"` series silently means "first configured tailnet only" — every other tailnet's dedup fill/evictions/hits are unmeasured, with no attribute distinguishing which tailnet a data point covers even if that were fixed. A deployment monitoring, say, a 20-device tailnet (first in config) alongside a 500-device tailnet would see only the small tailnet's healthy dedup panel, with no signal that the larger tailnet's flow set (potentially under capacity pressure) isn't covered at all.

Suggest emitting the reporter per-runtime with a tailnet attribute stamped on each series (not just runtimes[0]'s), and listing every runtime's sets in `dedupInfo()` — or, at minimum, documenting the runtimes[0]-only limitation in `docs/metrics.md` until the full per-tailnet fix lands.

_cx=straightforward → verified adversarially by sonnet._

Closed by `eb2700d`. flow/audit dedup self-obs is no longer pinned to runtimes[0]: each runtime's sets are reported on its own emitter (stamping tailscale.tailnet), and `dedupInfo` lists every runtime's sets (tailnet-prefixed in multi mode, bare in single). webhook_cross stays process-global. Tests cover the multi-runtime listing + single-tailnet bare names.

body:
## Problem
`registerCollectors` runs once per runtime, and in multi-tailnet mode each registration passes the same global static `node_metrics.targets` list. With N tailnets configured, N independent nodemetrics collectors each scrape every static target every interval and re-emit the identical samples through their own tailnet emitter. Because each tailnet provider has a distinct `service.instance.id`, the duplicates don't collide as OTEL series — they land as N parallel copies of every sample, N-1 of which attribute the node to the wrong tailnet.

## Evidence
- `internal/app/collectors.go:154-160` — `registerCollectors` runs per runtime (`tailnetruntime.go:101`), passing the same shared `cfg.Collectors.NodeMetrics.Targets` (mapped via `nodeMetricsOptions`, `options.go:161-181`) to every runtime's registration.
- `internal/app/status.go:411-413` already acknowledges the fan-out: "node-metrics is process-global in practice; in multi-tailnet it runs per tailnet".
- `internal/app/options.go:148-156` — each tailnet provider gets a distinct `service.instance.id`, so the duplicate emissions don't collapse into one series.

## Failure scenario / impact
With `tailnets: [a.com, b.com]` plus `node_metrics.targets: [one jump host]`, the host is scraped twice per interval (2x load on `tailscaled`'s `:5252`) and its metrics are exported twice — once under tailnet `a.com` and once under `b.com` — doubling DPM cost and making per-tailnet dashboards show the same node in both tailnets.

## Suggested direction
Register static targets on only one runtime (or a process-level nodemetrics collector) in multi-tailnet mode, keeping per-tailnet discovery as-is; alternatively, document and validate that static targets and multi-tailnet are mutually exclusive.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A static `node_metrics` target is scraped and emitted once per interval, process-wide, in multi-tailnet mode — not once per tailnet.
- [ ] Alternatively, `node_metrics.targets` combined with multi-tailnet is rejected or explicitly documented as unsupported, with a test asserting the chosen behavior.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Closed by `f0e20d1`. Static `node_metrics.targets` (process-global) are now registered on the FIRST runtime only in multi-tailnet mode via a `primary` flag on runtimeDeps, so a shared jump host isn't scraped + emitted once per tailnet (2x tailscaled load, duplicate/mis-attributed samples). Per-tailnet discovery still runs on every runtime. Test asserts only the primary runtime owns the static node_metrics collector when discovery is off.
