body:
## Problem
`Registry.Register` (`internal/collector/collector.go:59-64`) accepts the base `Collector` interface (just `Name`/`DefaultInterval`) instead of the typed `SnapshotCollector`. `RegisterWindow` already takes the typed `WindowCollector`, giving that path a compile-time guarantee, but `Register` has no equivalent — so a collector that fails to properly implement `Collect` (wrong receiver, missing method) still compiles and registers successfully.

## Evidence
- `internal/collector/collector.go:59-64` — `Register(c Collector, interval time.Duration)` takes the base interface.
- `internal/collector/scheduler.go:254-256` — the scheduler's default switch branch only logs `collector implements neither SnapshotCollector nor WindowCollector`; `runErr` stays `nil`.
- `internal/collector/scheduler.go:216-244` — the deferred block still emits `scrape.success=1` and records a successful run in the `StatusTracker` on every tick regardless.

## Failure scenario / impact
A new collector is added with `Collect` defined on the wrong receiver type (or omitted). It passes the build and every registration test, runs forever as a silent no-op, and reports `scrape.success=1` across dashboards and the status page — the only signal is a WARN log line once per tick, easy to miss in practice.

## Suggested direction
Change `Register`'s parameter type to `SnapshotCollector` (mirroring `RegisterWindow`), turning this failure mode into a compile error. The scheduler's default branch then becomes unreachable defensive code.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Registry.Register` requires `SnapshotCollector` at compile time
- [ ] All existing collector registrations still compile unchanged
- [ ] A regression test/comment documents why the scheduler's "neither interface" branch is now defensive-only

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

body:
## Problem
The `/readyz` endpoint is wired to the exact same unconditional 200-"ok" handler as `/healthz` (`internal/app/admin.go:19-27`), so it never reflects real readiness. The Helm chart's `readinessProbe` points at `/readyz` (`deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/templates/deployment.yaml:72-77`), but nothing feeds receiver-startup failures or first-tick health into it — `deriveHealth` (`health.go:52-79`) already computes a real degraded/starting/healthy verdict, but only for the status page.

## Evidence
- `internal/app/admin.go:19-27` — `registerProbes` wires the same handler to `/healthz` and `/readyz`.
- `deploy/helm/tailscale2otel/templates/deployment.yaml:72-77` — readinessProbe targets `/readyz`.
- `internal/app/app.go:451` + `selfobs.go:97-103` (`recordReceiverStop`) — a receiver goroutine dying is only logged/counted, never fed back into readiness.
- `internal/app/health.go:52-79` — `deriveHealth` already computes a real starting/degraded/healthy verdict, but it's status-page-only today.

## Failure scenario / impact
Streaming enabled behind a Kubernetes Service; the HEC listener fails to bind (e.g. a missing TLS cert file). The stream receiver's goroutine terminates permanently, but `/readyz` keeps returning 200 forever. The Service keeps routing traffic to the pod, and Tailscale's HEC pushes get connection-refused indefinitely instead of the deployment being rolled back or the pod pulled from rotation.

## Suggested direction
Derive `/readyz` from live app state that already exists: whether receivers bound successfully (or terminally failed) and optionally `deriveHealth`'s starting/degraded verdict. Keep `/healthz` as pure process liveness, unaffected by receiver/collector state.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/readyz` returns non-200 (or a distinguishable body) while the app is still starting up (before first successful tick / receiver bind)
- [ ] `/readyz` returns non-200 if an enabled receiver (stream/webhook) has terminally failed to bind or has stopped unexpectedly
- [ ] `/healthz` remains pure liveness (always 200 once the process is up), independent of receiver/collector health
- [ ] Test coverage for both the ready and not-ready `/readyz` cases

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Done in 5d43509 (pushed to main). `/readyz` now reflects real readiness: 503 while any registered collector is still pending its first tick, or when an enabled stream/webhook receiver has terminally failed/bound-failed (tracked via a thread-safe receiverHealth populated by recordReceiverStop). `/healthz` stays pure liveness. Covered by readiness_test.go + admin_status_test.go.

body:
## Problem
The `tailscale.device.posture` log event's dynamic attributes bypass PII classification entirely. `emitPosture` copies every key of the full, arbitrary posture attribute map (raw provider-namespaced keys like `intune:...`, `custom:...`) verbatim into the log event's attrs, without routing them through the same classified `attribute`/`value` keys the separate `tailscale.device.attribute{,.info}` metric path already uses. None of these raw keys are registered in the PII registry, so the redactor's `redactKey` always falls through to "never redact" for them (unless the value happens to be a bare IP string) — regardless of any `pii_filter.*` toggle.

Note: adversarially verified and downgraded from the raw finding — this is a **documented, opt-in** log event (`collect_posture` defaults false, and there's a clean `posture_log_mode: off` switch), and the docs' `free_text_details` "posture values" claim is separately honored on the **metric** path (via the classified `value` label). The gap is specifically that the posture **log** signal isn't covered by the same redaction discipline the docs imply applies to "posture values" generally, and the completeness test doesn't catch it because it only walks declared `Attributes`, not dynamic ones.

## Evidence
- `internal/collector/devices/devices.go:962-968` (`emitPosture`): `evAttrs := telemetry.Attrs{semconv.HostName: d.Hostname, semconv.HostID: d.ID}; for k, v := range attrs { evAttrs[k] = fmt.Sprint(v) }` — `attrs` is the full, arbitrary map from `DevicePostureAttributes`.
- `internal/collector/devices/catalog.go:194-200` — `docPosture.Attributes` declares only `[HostName, HostID]`; the dynamic keys are never declared, so `internal/catalog/pii_completeness_test.go` (which only walks declared `catalog.Metrics()/LogEvents()` Attributes) never sees them.
- `internal/telemetry/pii/registry.go` — no raw posture keys are present in `keyCategory`/`nonIdentifier`.
- `internal/telemetry/pii/pii.go:58-82` — `redactKey` falls through to `return false` (never redact) for any unclassified, non-IP-valued key.
- `docs/configuration.md:570` — documents `pii_filter.free_text_details` as covering "...posture values" (honored on the metric path via the classified `value` label, per `devices.go:1004` + `registry.go:26`, but not on the log path).

## Failure scenario / impact
An operator enables `collect_posture: true` (a mainstream reason to do so — pulling MDM/EDR compliance data from Intune/Jamf/CrowdStrike/etc. via Tailscale device posture) and sets `pii_filter.free_text_details: false`, believing per the documented table that this redacts posture values. Every posture change still emits a `tailscale.device.posture` log record containing the full raw posture map — potentially including provider-specific identifiers or other posture-specific data — with no way to gate it short of `posture_log_mode: off` (which also drops the actionable, non-PII part of the signal).

## Suggested direction
Route the posture log's dynamic attribute merge through the same classified `attribute`/`value` keys (or a dedicated classified key) used by `emitAttributes`, so the existing `pii_filter.free_text_details` toggle and redactor actually see and gate them. Extend the completeness guard (`internal/catalog/pii_completeness_test.go`) to cover dynamic-attribute emitters, since it currently only walks declared `Attributes`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Posture log values are gated by `pii_filter` (via a classified key or a registered raw-posture-key class), consistent with the metric path.
- [ ] `pii_completeness_test` (or an equivalent) covers dynamic-attribute emitters, not just declared catalog `Attributes`.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by `6035361`. The posture LOG's arbitrary posture map is now JSON-encoded under one classified attribute `tailscale.device.posture.details` (registered `CatFreeTextDetails`) instead of spread as raw top-level keys that bypassed the redactor — so `pii_filter.free_text_details` gates it. Tests prove raw keys never appear and `Redactor.Log()` drops the key when the category is off. _(Sonnet subagent; gated on main.)_

body:
## Problem
Synchronous OTEL gauges under the project's forced cumulative temporality never truly disappear once an entity (device, node, DNS resolver, etc.) stops being emitted — the SDK's `cumulativeLastValue` aggregation keeps every attribute set it has ever seen and re-exports its last value with a refreshed timestamp on every export interval, forever. There is no staleness/eviction path for synchronous instruments in OTEL-Go (this is the SDK's documented behavior, tracked upstream as issue #3006) — it is not something the project's own code can trivially work around, and it is not fixed by switching to observable/async gauges either, since the same shared `cumulativeLastValue` aggregator is used underneath.

Note: adversarially verified and reframed. The only place the project *documents* drop-out semantics ("a source metric that stops emitting drops out rather than lingering at a stale value") is the self-obs `series.active`/`series.overflowing` gauges, which are keyed by a fixed, low-cardinality `metric.name` set that doesn't churn during a running config and which self-corrects (`series.overflowing` re-emits 0 every interval while the metric is active) — so the documented-contradiction framing doesn't actually apply there. The real, un-documented impact lands on **per-entity gauges** that carry no drop-out promise at all: `tailscale.device.online`, `tailscale.node.up`, `tailscale.dns.*`, and similar. Severity is inherent SDK/design-tradeoff behavior under sustained entity churn, not a discrete coding mistake.

## Evidence
- `internal/telemetry/provider.go:492` — `CumulativeTemporality` pinned for every instrument kind.
- `internal/telemetry/cardinality.go:107-112` and `internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md:70-72` — the "resets all sets so a source metric that stops emitting drops out" claim (applies only to `series.active`/`series.overflowing`, not the per-entity gauges below).
- `otel-go sdk/metric@v1.44.0/internal/aggregate/lastvalue.go:158-188` — `cumulativeLastValue.collect` ranges over every ever-seen attribute set with `Time: now()`; upstream TODO references issue #3006 (values map never cleared).
- Empirically verified in a scratchpad program: a `Float64Gauge` recorded once is returned with a fresh timestamp on every subsequent `Collect` (3/3 collections).
- Affected per-entity emit sites: `internal/collector/devices/devices.go:487` (`tailscale.device.online`), `internal/collector/dns/dns.go:105/117/130` (per-resolver/search-path info gauges), `internal/collector/nodemetrics/nodemetrics.go:579-582` (`tailscale.node.up`).
- `internal/telemetry/provider.go:193` — `WithCardinalityLimit` (default 10000): dead series permanently consume per-instrument cardinality slots until new live series collapse into `otel_metric_overflow`.

## Failure scenario / impact
A device is removed from the tailnet (or renamed, changing its attribute set). Its `tailscale_device_online` series keeps being exported at its last value every interval indefinitely — dashboards count ghost devices, `device.online==1` alerts can point at hardware that no longer exists, and DPM cost grows monotonically with churn. Under sustained churn, dead series can also exhaust the 10000-series-per-instrument cardinality limit, silently collapsing new live series into `otel_metric_overflow`.

## Suggested direction
A **design decision is needed** before implementation: either (a) document the real backend behavior and stop implying exported-series drop-out anywhere it doesn't apply, and clearly document the churn-driven ghost-series/cardinality-exhaustion consequence for operators of per-entity gauges; or (b) implement a real entity-delete/eviction mechanism for per-entity gauges (note: switching these to observable/async gauges alone will **not** fix this in OTEL-Go v1.44, since the underlying `cumulativeLastValue` aggregator behaves identically either way).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A decision is recorded (document-only vs. build a real eviction mechanism) and referenced from this issue.
- [ ] The `Report`/`CLAUDE.md` prose in `cardinality.go`/`internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md` is corrected to stop implying exported-series drop-out where it doesn't apply (self-obs gauges only).
- [ ] The churn consequence for per-entity gauges (`device.online`, `node.up`, `dns.*`, etc.) is documented for operators, or a real eviction mechanism is implemented.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by c421491. **Decision (document-and-warn, not build eviction).** Per-entity eviction isn't feasible in otel-go v1.44 under forced cumulative temporality (the shared `cumulativeLastValue` aggregation re-exports last values forever — upstream #3006 — and observable gauges behave identically), so v1 documents the behavior rather than fighting the SDK. Changes: corrected the `cardinality.go` `Report` comment and `internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md` to make clear the 'drops out' behavior applies only to the self-obs tracker's own measurement, NOT the exported per-entity gauges; added an operator-facing 'Ghost per-entity series under churn' note to `docs/metrics.md` covering the dashboard/alert and cardinality-exhaustion consequences and the restart-to-clear mitigation. _(Maintainer was away when the decision fork was surfaced; proceeded on the non-destructive documented default — revisit if you'd prefer a custom eviction mechanism.)_

Reopening — a real code fix is now feasible and its mechanism has landed (ac22409, pushed to main).

**The premise this issue was closed on was wrong for the pinned otel-go v1.44.0.** It was closed document-only because "observable gauges behave identically" under the shared `cumulativeLastValue`. They don't: the two gauge kinds route to *different* aggregators —
- synchronous `Gauge` → `LastValue()` → `cumulativeLastValue.collect` (never clears; #3006 TODO — ghosts forever)
- observable gauge → `PrecomputedLastValue()` → `precomputedLastValue.cumulative()` → `copyAndClearDpts` which **clears stale sets every cycle** ("Do not report stale values"; builder doc: "always only return values from the previous collection cycle")

(`sdk/metric@v1.44.0/pipeline.go:517-520`, `internal/aggregate/lastvalue.go`.)

**Landed in ac22409:** `Emitter.GaugeSnapshot(name, unit, desc, []GaugePoint)` — an observable gauge with atomic snapshot-replace, same PII/collision/const-attr pipeline as `Gauge`. Proven by `emitter_snapshot_test.go` against a real ManualReader (cumulative): a departed series **drops out**; an empty snapshot clears all. This is the reusable mechanism only — no collector uses it yet.

**Remaining (the actual fix): migrate the per-entity gauge emit loops to GaugeSnapshot.** Open scope decision:
- (a, recommended) all churning per-entity gauges in devices/nodemetrics/dns — `device.online` **and** its ~10 siblings (`last_seen`, `key_expiry`, `update_available`, `derp_latency`, `routes`, `conn_*`), `node.up`, all `dns.*` per-resolver/search-path. Consistent + complete; restructures 3 collectors' emit loops.
- (b) only the 3 named health gauges (`device.online`, `node.up`, `dns.*`) — smaller but leaves siblings ghosting.

Also TODO on completion: fix the now-false "observable gauges behave identically" line in `internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md` + the ghost-series note in `docs/metrics.md`.

Fully fixed and closed by 479575e (pushed to main) — the observable-gauge migration is complete, not just the mechanism.

Every churning (attribute-keyed) gauge across the three affected collectors now emits via an observable-gauge snapshot (`telemetry.GaugeSnapshotBuilder` → `Emitter.GaugeSnapshot`), so a departed entity's series drops out of the export on the next scrape instead of ghosting at its last value — and stops consuming a cardinality-limit slot:

- **devices** — all ~24 attribute-keyed gauges: per-device `online`/`last_seen`/`key_expiry`/`update_available`/DERP-latency/routes/`conn.*`/version-skew/exit-node/posture, plus the by-version / by-tag / by-region / by-CIDR / client-supports / invites / exit-node rollups.
- **nodemetrics** — `tailscale.node.up` (routed through the builder despite the concurrent scrape worker-pool: `scrapeTarget` returns its instance, `scrapeAll` gathers per-target results at disjoint indices, and `Collect` Adds + Flushes single-threaded on every path incl. zero-targets/all-failed).
- **dns** — the per-resolver and per-search-path info gauges.

Only **nil-attr single-series** gauges (counts/totals/flags) stay synchronous — they can't churn. One deliberate, documented exception: nodemetrics' forwarded passthrough samples (`emitSample`) stay synchronous because their names are dynamic and include monotonic counters, where snapshot semantics don't fit — noted in `docs/metrics.md`.

Each collector gained a TDD drop-out test proving a removed entity's series is gone (not ghosting) on the next collection, driven against the real SDK reader. The now-false "observable gauges behave identically" claim in `internal/telemetry/CLAUDE.md` and the ghost-series note in `docs/metrics.md` were corrected.

Full gate green on HEAD (479575e): `go build`/`vet`/`test -race ./...` · golangci-lint 0 issues · `metricscatalog -check` in sync (catalog descriptors unchanged — still gauges) · env-vars in sync.

body:
## Problem
Under `provider: headscale`, the single runtime is registered with the *same* cardinality tracker and `ExportStats` method value as the process-level provider (`rt.card == a.procCard`, `rt.emitter == a.procEmitter`). `Run()` unconditionally starts both the process-level self-obs reporters AND the per-runtime reporter loop, with no guard for the case where they alias the same objects — so under Headscale, two independent `runExportReporter`/`runCardinalityReporter` pairs run over identical state:

- Each `runExportReporter` keeps its own private `last` baseline and emits the *full* delta of the shared cumulative `ExportStats` every interval, so `tailscale2otel.export.datapoints`/`.log_records` are inflated to ~2x the true value.
- Each `runCardinalityReporter` calls `Report`, which drains-and-resets the shared tracker's sets; two reporters at unsynchronized phases each see roughly half an interval's distinct series, so `tailscale2otel.series.active`/`.series.by_group` undercount and flap.
- The admin status page and sparkline (`aggregateCardSnapshot`, `cardinalityTotal`) additionally add the process snapshot and the per-runtime snapshot together, exactly doubling the same value a third way.

Verified adversarially: this is real and reachable (self-observability defaults on), but confined to the **self-observability meta-metrics** (`tailscale2otel.export.*`, `tailscale2otel.series.*`) and the admin status page under `provider: headscale` only — core device/flow/audit/user telemetry is emitted through the emitter exactly once and is **not** affected, since collector signals flow through per-collector instrument caching independent of this aliasing.

## Evidence
- `internal/app/app.go:160-165` — the Headscale runtime is built with `ps.Process().Cardinality()`/`ps.Process().ExportStats` — the same pointer/method value assigned to `a.procCard`/`a.procExportStats` at `app.go:153-155`.
- `internal/telemetry/provider.go:349` — `Provider.Cardinality()` returns the one `p.card` pointer, confirming `rt.card == a.procCard`.
- `internal/app/app.go:410-411` — process-level reporters started unconditionally.
- `internal/app/app.go:418-421` — the per-runtime reporter loop started unconditionally, with no guard for aliasing.
- `internal/app/export_reporter.go:30-38` — each reporter's own private `last` baseline, emitting the full delta.
- `internal/telemetry/cardinality.go:113-136` — `Report` drains-and-resets the tracker's sets.
- `internal/app/status.go:48-51` and `internal/app/sampler.go:66-77` — `aggregateCardSnapshot`/`cardinalityTotal` add the process snapshot and the runtime snapshot together.
- `internal/config/defaults.go:189-191` — `self_observability.enabled` defaults to `true`.
- The `newApp` test seam (`app.go:346-349,364`) wires these hooks nil, so no existing test exercises the headscale two-reporter-alias case.

## Failure scenario / impact
Any `provider: headscale` deployment with the default `self_observability.enabled: true`: the operator's cost/volume dashboards read `export.datapoints`/`export.log_records` as ~2x reality, `series.active`/`series.by_group` show roughly halved and flapping cardinality, and the admin status page shows the total exactly doubled — three mutually inconsistent, all-wrong views of the same self-observability signal. Core tailnet telemetry is unaffected.

## Suggested direction
In `Run()`'s per-runtime reporter loop, skip runtimes whose `card`/`exportStats` alias the process provider's (or construct the Headscale runtime with nil `card`/`exportStats` since the process-level reporters already cover it, mirroring the documented intended design for the Tailscale multi-tailnet path where each tailnet gets a distinct provider). Apply the same identity guard in `aggregateCardSnapshot` and `cardinalityTotal`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Exactly one reporter pair (cardinality + export) runs per distinct tracker/stats identity — not one per runtime when a runtime aliases the process provider.
- [ ] `aggregateCardSnapshot` and `cardinalityTotal` don't double-count the same snapshot.
- [ ] A headscale-mode test exercising the real `New()`/`Run()` path (not the `newApp` nil-hook seam) asserts `export.datapoints`/`series.active` are correct under headscale.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by `543b336`. The Headscale runtime is now built with nil `card`/`exportStats` (it shares the process emitter), so only the process-level self-obs reporters run — no more ~2x-inflated `export.datapoints`/`log_records` or flapping `series.active`, and the status-page snapshot/total no longer double-count. Mirrors the `newApp` seam + multi-tailnet design (shared provider ⇒ no per-runtime reporter). A `New()`-path test asserts the headscale runtime's card/exportStats are nil.

body:
## Problem
`Run()`'s shutdown ordering never joins the receiver goroutines (stream/webhook), so in-flight HEC/webhook records can be ACKed to the sender but dropped from telemetry after the final flush. After `<-ctx.Done()`, `Run` waits only for the scheduler goroutines, then performs the "authoritative final flush" of each runtime's rollup accumulator and immediately shuts the telemetry pipeline down — while the receivers' own graceful `srv.Shutdown` (with its drain window) is still running in an untracked goroutine nobody waits for.

Note: verified adversarially and downgraded from the raw finding. Streaming and webhook receivers are **opt-in and disabled by default** (default ingestion is poll), so the default deployment is unaffected. This is a **timing-dependent race**, not a guaranteed loss on every restart — loss is limited to whatever request happens to be in flight at the SIGTERM instant. The admin and metrics (Prometheus) servers are **not** data-loss contributors — they serve probes/scrapes, not ingested data — so joining them is for tidiness only, not because they lose telemetry; the `app.go:498-500` comment claiming "the schedulers have stopped (so no connections are still being processed)" is incomplete for the receiver path and should be corrected alongside the fix.

## Evidence
- `internal/app/app.go:449-475` — receivers launched as untracked goroutines (`go func() { a.recordReceiverStop(...) }()`).
- `internal/app/app.go:484-488` — after `<-ctx.Done()`, `Run` joins only the scheduler goroutines.
- `internal/app/app.go:497-500` — the final rollup drain, with the incomplete comment about connections no longer being processed.
- `internal/app/app.go:505-507` — `a.shutdown(shutdownCtx)` tears down the OTEL providers immediately after.
- `internal/stream/stream.go:735-739` and `internal/webhook/webhook.go:262-266` — graceful `srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)` with a 10s drain, never joined.
- `internal/collector/scheduler.go:113-124` — contrast: `Scheduler.Run` does `wg.Wait()` so poll ticks drain before the flush; the receivers get no equivalent join.
- `cmd/tailscale2otel/main.go:48-52` — `main()` returns/exits right after `Run()`.

## Failure scenario / impact
Streaming enabled with an active Tailscale HEC sender; a k8s rolling restart sends SIGTERM while a batch POST is in flight. The handler finishes processing ~1-2s later and returns 200 (HEC success), so the sender marks the batch delivered and never resends — but the flow/audit records and rollup counts it produced were emitted after the final flush and are dropped. This can happen on any graceful restart with streaming/webhook traffic in flight at the SIGTERM instant; it is a race, not a guarantee.

## Suggested direction
Track the receiver goroutines with a `WaitGroup` (or per-server done channels) and join them after `ctx` cancellation, before the final `FlushRollup` and `a.shutdown`. Fix the `app.go:498-500` comment to accurately describe the ordering once receivers are joined. Joining admin/metrics servers as well is reasonable for consistency, but is not required to fix any data-loss path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Stream and webhook receiver goroutines are tracked and joined before `FlushRollup`/`a.shutdown` run.
- [ ] The `app.go:498-500` comment is corrected to reflect the real ordering.
- [ ] A test simulates an in-flight stream/webhook handler at SIGTERM and asserts its record is flushed, not dropped.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by `f0e20d1`. Stream/webhook receiver goroutines are tracked in a WaitGroup and joined after the schedulers stop but BEFORE `a.shutdown()` tears down the exporters (and before the deferred rdns Close) — their graceful HTTP shutdown lets an already-ACKed in-flight request finish emitting instead of being dropped. Also satisfies #121's receiver-join criterion. Verified by inspection + the existing `TestApp_RunGracefulShutdown` staying green; a dedicated in-flight-drain integration test is a reasonable follow-up (the ordering fix itself is small and the existing shutdown test guards regressions).

body:
## Problem
Several independent `Validate()`/`Warnings()` gaps let the config layer accept combinations that silently produce zero ingestion, permanently stalled window collectors, or dead HTTP listeners — with no startup error, no warning, and a healthy-looking status page/scrape metrics. Sub-items:

- **(a) `source: stream` with streaming disabled.** An enabled `flowlogs`/`auditlogs` collector configured with `source: stream` while `streaming.enabled: false` has no ingestion path at all: the poller isn't registered (source != poll/both) and the HEC receiver doesn't exist. `Validate()` only checks the enum value, not this cross-field combination. In multi-tailnet mode `source: stream` is strictly dead (streaming is forbidden entirely with >1 tailnets) yet still accepted.
- **(b) `otlp.endpoint` scheme under `protocol: http`.** The endpoint shape is validated only for `protocol: grpc`. Under `http`, a scheme-less `host:port` endpoint (the shape grpc requires) parses as an opaque URL with an empty host, silently zeroing the OTLP endpoint at runtime instead of failing at load time the way grpc does.
- **(c) `initial_lookback <= 0` permanently stalls window collectors.** On cold start, `from = to.Add(-initialLookback)`; with `initial_lookback` zero (the more realistic trigger — an operator reading "cold-start reach-back" naturally tries 0 meaning "start from now") or negative, `from >= to` forever, so `nextWindow` returns `ok=false` on every tick, the checkpoint is never bootstrapped, and the collector is permanently idle while `scrape.success=1`.
- **(d) negative `lag`.** `to = now.Add(-lag)`; a negative lag pushes `to` into the future, so the persisted high-water mark is in the future and records that later arrive with timestamps inside the already-consumed window are permanently skipped.
- **(e) `max_window <= interval` never catches up.** Catch-up advances at most `max_window` per tick; if `interval` exceeds `max_window`, the checkpoint falls further behind every tick, unboundedly, with no warning. (Note: `max_window <= 0` is an intentional "no cap" sentinel and must stay valid — only warn when `max_window` is positive but ≤ `interval`.)
- **(f) only one listener pair is bind-collision checked.** `Validate()` checks only the admin/prometheus pair for a duplicate `listen` address, despite four independent HTTP listeners (admin, prometheus, streaming, webhook). Any other colliding pair fails silently at runtime: one server loses the `net.Listen` race, logs an ERROR, and the process keeps running looking healthy while that surface is dead.
- **(g) no advisory lint for partial tailnet credentials.** `Validate()` never checks that the tailnet(s)' selected auth method actually has its credential populated (contrast the explicit `headscale.api_key` required-check). This surfaces later as an opaque `tsapi.NewClient` error or a silent OAuth 401, rather than a targeted config error naming the tailnet index. Any such lint must be advisory-only (not a hard require) since rendered/checked-in configs legitimately carry no credentials by design (credentials come from env vars at runtime — see `tools/configcheck`'s Helm CI check).

## Evidence
- (a) `internal/app/collectors.go:161-174` (poller/receiver registration); `internal/config/validate.go:331-334` (enum-only check); `validate.go:35-58` (dual-ingestion warning gated on `streaming.enabled==true`); `validate.go:304-306` (streaming forbidden with >1 tailnets, but `source: stream` still accepted).
- (b) `internal/config/validate.go:263-269` (grpc-only endpoint check); `internal/telemetry/provider.go:507`; oconf's `WithEndpointURL` (`otlpmetrichttp@v1.44.0/internal/oconf/options.go:288-302`) parsing a scheme-less endpoint to an empty host.
- (c) `internal/collector/window.go:15-28` (`nextWindow`); `internal/collector/scheduler.go:264-268` (`runWindow` returns `nil` on `!ok`, treated as success); no lower-bound check in `validate.go`.
- (d)/(e) `internal/config/validate.go` has no checks on `Lag`/`InitialLookback`/`MaxWindow` (only `otlp.metric_interval` and `node_metrics.discovery.interval` are checked); `internal/collector/window.go:16,25-27`.
- (f) `internal/config/validate.go:273-275` (admin/prometheus-only check); `internal/app/admin.go:124-140` and the analogous stream/webhook runners only log an ERROR on `ListenAndServe` failure, never terminate the process.
- (g) `internal/config/validate.go:276-317` (method-enum checks, no credential-presence check); `internal/config/validate.go:250-252` (the existing headscale precedent); `internal/tsapi/auth.go:35-55` (the opaque runtime failure this would prevent).

## Failure scenario / impact
- (a) An operator sets `collectors.auditlogs.source: stream` intending to switch to streaming but forgets `streaming.enabled: true`. Startup is clean, `config.valid=1`, no warnings — audit log coverage is silently zero until someone notices.
- (b) An operator switches `otlp.protocol` from `grpc` to `http` but keeps the grpc-shaped `host:port` endpoint. Startup succeeds; no metrics/logs ever arrive; only anonymous `export.failures` warnings, with no mention of the endpoint mis-shape.
- (c) An operator sets `initial_lookback: 0s` meaning "don't backfill, start from now." Flow/audit logs are never fetched — zero records, zero errors, all self-obs healthy — until someone notices the data is simply absent.
- (d)/(e) A user tunes `collectors.flowlogs.interval: 2h` without touching `max_window` (default 1h): delivery lag grows by 1h per tick forever while `scrape.success` stays 1.
- (f) `webhook.listen` is accidentally left equal to `streaming.listen` (e.g. after a copy-pasted Helm values override) — whichever server starts second never binds, silently killing that ingestion surface.
- (g) A multi-tailnet config has one entry missing its `auth.oauth.client_secret` (copy-paste without updating the secret env reference); the failure only surfaces at first API call for that tailnet, as a generic auth error rather than a targeted config error.

## Suggested direction
Add each rule to `Validate()` (hard errors for (a)/(b)/(c)/(d)/(f)) or `Warnings()` (advisory for (e)/(g), scoped carefully so it never requires a credential to be present in a checked-in/rendered config). For (c), an alternative to a hard reject is to bootstrap the checkpoint at `to` on the first `ok=false` cold-start tick instead of rejecting the value outright. Update `docs/env-vars.md`/`docs/configuration.md` wherever these semantics are documented.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] (a) An enabled flowlogs/auditlogs collector with `source: stream` and `streaming.enabled: false` errors or warns; `source: stream` is rejected outright in multi-tailnet mode.
- [ ] (b) `otlp.endpoint` under `protocol: http` (or empty) is validated for an http/https scheme and non-empty host, mirroring the grpc check.
- [ ] (c) `initial_lookback <= 0` is rejected in `Validate()`, or the window collector bootstraps its checkpoint on the first cold-start `ok=false` tick instead of stalling forever.
- [ ] (d) Negative `lag` is rejected in `Validate()`.
- [ ] (e) `max_window > 0 && max_window <= interval` produces a `Warnings()` entry for flowlogs/auditlogs.
- [ ] (f) The bind-collision check is generalized to all enabled listener pairs (admin, prometheus, streaming, webhook).
- [ ] (g) A scoped advisory `Warnings()` lint flags the common case of one tailnet credential field set and its counterpart empty, without requiring credentials to be present.
- [ ] Each rule has a dedicated `Validate()`/`Warnings()` test.
- [ ] `docs/env-vars.md` and `docs/configuration.md` updated wherever these semantics are documented.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus/sonnet._

All seven sub-items landed in `internal/config/validate.go`: (a) `source: stream` requires `streaming.enabled` and is rejected in multi-tailnet mode; (b) `otlp.endpoint` under `protocol: http` must be a full http/https URL with a host; (c) `initial_lookback <= 0` rejected; (d) negative `lag` rejected; (e) positive `max_window <= interval` warns; (f) bind-collision check now covers all four listeners; (g) advisory for a partially-set per-tailnet OAuth pair (never fires on both-empty). body:
## Problem
Root `CLAUDE.md` claims the live-contract CI lane authenticates "keylessly via GitHub OIDC (no stored token)." That is not what the workflow does: it mints a short-lived Tailscale API token via OAuth client-credentials, using a long-lived OAuth client id/secret pair stored in the environment of a dedicated self-hosted runner — not OIDC federation, and not credential-free.

## Evidence
- Root `CLAUDE.md:130`: "The live lane auths keylessly via GitHub OIDC (no stored token)."
- `.github/workflows/live-contract.yml:8-14`: "No id-token/OIDC: there is no published OIDC->Tailscale-API action. Instead we mint a short-lived token from Tailscale's documented OAuth endpoint using a READ-ONLY (all:read) OAuth client whose credentials live in the environment of a DEDICATED self-hosted runner (label `tailscale-api`) — NOT in GitHub secrets."
- The workflow's `permissions` block requests `contents: read, issues: write, pull-requests: write` — no `id-token: write` at all.

## Failure scenario / impact
An engineer or security reviewer trusting CLAUDE.md would believe the live-contract lane has zero standing credential exposure (typical of OIDC-based auth), and would miss that compromising or inspecting the `tailscale-api`-labeled self-hosted runner exposes a live, reusable (though read-only) Tailscale OAuth client secret — a real credential-handling detail that should be reflected accurately in the docs used to reason about the repo's threat model.

## Suggested direction
Correct the CLAUDE.md line to describe the actual mechanism (self-hosted runner env vars + Tailscale OAuth client-credentials exchange, read-only scope), matching the accurate comment already in `live-contract.yml`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Root `CLAUDE.md`'s description of the live-contract lane's auth mechanism matches `live-contract.yml`'s comment (self-hosted runner env OAuth client, read-only scope, no OIDC).
- [ ] No remaining claim in tracked docs that this lane uses GitHub OIDC.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

body:
## Problem
The `notices` job in `.github/workflows/publish.yml` runs `scripts/notices.sh` without ever installing `go-licenses`. Every other caller of this script installs the tool immediately beforehand — this job is the one exception.

## Evidence
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml:43-68` — the `notices` job runs only `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-go`, then directly `bash scripts/notices.sh`; no step installs `go-licenses`.
- `scripts/notices.sh:27-30`: `command -v "$GO_LICENSES" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "notices: go-licenses not found ..." >&2; exit 1; }`.
- GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runners do not ship `go-licenses`.
- Contrast: the `binaries` job's `pre-cmd` in `release-please.yml` runs `go install .../syft@... && go install github.com/google/go-licenses@v1.6.0 && bash scripts/notices.sh`, and `deploy/Dockerfile`'s build stage also installs `go-licenses` before running the equivalent step.

## Failure scenario / impact
On the next real release (release-please merges a release PR, `release_created=true`), `release-please.yml`'s `publish` job calls `publish.yml` with a non-empty `release_tag`, which runs the `notices` job. That job fails at the "Generate + attach third-party notices" step on every release — the job shows red in Actions (though nothing depends on it) — and the standalone `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` release asset is never generated or uploaded to the GitHub Release.

## Suggested direction
Add a `go install github.com/google/go-licenses@v1.6.0` step (pinned to match the `binaries` job's version) before the "Generate + attach third-party notices" step in the `notices` job.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The `notices` job in `publish.yml` installs `go-licenses@v1.6.0` before invoking `scripts/notices.sh`.
- [ ] A dry-run/manual trigger of the `notices` job succeeds and produces `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

comments.body: Closed by `413b314`. `publish.yml` now runs `go install github.com/google/go-licenses@v1.6.0` before the notices step. Note (follow-up, out of scope): go-licenses v1.6.0 appears to error against the Go 1.26 toolchain locally — pre-existing for every invocation of that pinned version (Dockerfile, binaries job), not introduced here; worth a separate issue if CI shows it failing. _(Sonnet subagent.)_

body:
## Problem
`docs/node-metrics.md` states that "Node identity = the `instance` label" and that every forwarded series carries an `instance` label. That is wrong: the code deliberately emits the per-node identity under `tailscale.node` (normalizes to `tailscale_node`), specifically to avoid Grafana Cloud's OTLP→Prometheus translation promoting the resource attribute `service.instance.id` to the `instance` label — which would clobber any per-series `instance` attribute and collapse `tailscale.node.up` to a single series. The doc describes exactly the pre-fix behavior the code was changed to avoid.

## Evidence
- `docs/node-metrics.md:196-199`: "**Node identity = the `instance` label.** Every forwarded series carries an `instance` label (your `instance:` value, or the URL `host:port` if omitted)."
- `docs/node-metrics.md:279`: "A value of `1` per `instance` means the last scrape of that node succeeded."
- `internal/collector/nodemetrics/nodemetrics.go:54-62` — `attrInstance = "tailscale.node"`, with an explicit comment that it is deliberately NOT `"instance"` for the resource-promotion-collision reason above.
- A regression test guards exactly this: "Regression guard for the service.instance.id resource-promotion collision: the per-node identity must NOT be emitted under the old `instance` key" (asserts `p.Attrs["instance"]` is absent).
- `docs/metrics.md:417,531` correctly document the real attribute as `tailscale_node`.

## Failure scenario / impact
An operator follows `docs/node-metrics.md` and writes `sum by (instance) (rate(tailscaled_outbound_bytes_total[5m]))` expecting a per-node breakdown. Because the real `instance` label on Grafana Cloud is the collector's own resource-promoted value (identical across every node), the query silently collapses ALL nodes into one series instead of erroring — producing a dashboard/alert that looks correct but reports the wrong per-node data.

## Suggested direction
Correct the "Node identity" bullet and the up-gauge sentence to say the identity/grouping label is `tailscale_node` (Prometheus-normalized) / `tailscale.node` (OTEL), and clarify that `instance:` in config only names the operator-facing config field, not the resulting attribute key.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/node-metrics.md`'s "Node identity" bullet corrected to reference `tailscale_node`/`tailscale.node`.
- [ ] The up-gauge sentence corrected to match.
- [ ] Doc clarifies that `instance:` is only the config field name, not the emitted attribute key.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by sonnet._

body:
## Problem
`internal/tsapi/devices.go`'s raw `richDevice` wire struct decodes `created`, `lastSeen`, and `expires` as plain `time.Time` fields. Tailscale's own OpenAPI spec documents that `created` is empty for external devices (a headline, supported feature — `RichDevice` even carries an `IsExternal` flag and the devices collector buckets by it), and the official `tailscale-client-go/v2` package wraps exactly these fields in a custom `tsclient.Time` type specifically to tolerate an empty-string wire value. The raw decoder in `internal/tsapi` does not use that tolerant type.

## Evidence
- `internal/tsapi/devices.go:120-122` — `Created time.Time \`json:"created"\`` / `LastSeen time.Time` / `Expires time.Time` on the raw wire struct.
- `spec/tailscale-api.json` (`Device.created`): "The date on which the device was added to the tailnet; this is empty for external devices."
- `tailscale-client-go/v2`'s `Time` type doc: "allows for unmarshalling timestamps that represent an empty time as an empty string ... this is used by the tailscale API when it returns devices that have no created date."
- Reproduced directly: `json.Unmarshal` of `{"devices":[{"created":""}]}` into a plain `time.Time` field errors with `parsing time "" as "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00"`.
- The contract fuzz tests (`TestFuzz_EdgeVariants`) cover `{}`/null devices but never an empty-string timestamp.

## Failure scenario / impact
An operator shares an external device into the tailnet. The API returns `created:""` for it, so the entire `/devices?fields=all` response fails to decode — every `devices` tick errors, `tailscale.device.*` metrics go absent, and because `enrich.DeviceCache` is populated by the devices collector, flow/audit IP→name resolution silently degrades to `unknown`/`external` as well.

## Suggested direction
Decode `created`/`lastSeen`/`expires` with an empty-string-tolerant wrapper (like `tsclient.Time` or a custom `UnmarshalJSON`), and add an empty-timestamp payload to the contract fuzz edge-variant tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Empty-string `created`/`lastSeen`/`expires` decode without error in `internal/tsapi/devices.go`.
- [ ] A contract fuzz edge-variant test covers an empty-timestamp payload.
- [ ] The devices collector completes a tick successfully when an external device with `created:""` is present.

_Found by automated v1 bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially by opus._

comments.body: Closed by `bb4d575`. richDevice Created/LastSeen/Expires now decode via `tsclient.Time` (empty-string tolerant), so an external device's `created:""` no longer fails the whole /devices?fields=all decode. Added a contract fuzz edge-variant for empty timestamps and a decode regression test asserting they decode to zero time.

Part of the fleet-wide docs effort tracked in **rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28** (Phase 2). This repo's doc site is served under the m7kni.io hub at `/tailscale2otel/`, so its own Zensical build + theme overrides determine what search engines and LLMs see for these pages.

Two things are bundled here because they touch the same files:

1. **Redesign & rebrand alignment** — adopt the new m7kni.io brand and colour scheme (light-first, the shared wordmark / palette / type tokens) so the whole fleet reads as one product family. **Tune it for documentation, not marketing:** unlike the vibrant hub *landing* page, these are end-user **product documentation** sites — prioritise a clean, professional, highly readable, documentation-friendly presentation (sensible density, strong nav/TOC/search, scannable reference content) while staying on-brand in palette, type, and logo. Brand-consistent, docs-first. The exact spec follows from the hub redesign — treat the visual details as **pending finalization in rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28** and don't front-run them.
2. **SEO / LLM discoverability** — the metadata improvements below, fully specified now and able to proceed independently of the visual spec.

## Why (SEO/LLM part)

Like the hub, this site's `docs/overrides/main.html` is an empty passthrough, so OpenGraph/Twitter/JSON-LD/robots meta are either absent or (if copied from the hub) injected client-side and invisible to non-JS crawlers and LLMs (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot, social unfurlers). Render them server-side.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Redesign & rebrand alignment** — apply the finalized hub brand/scheme in a professional, documentation-friendly way (spec via rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28). Brand-consistent palette/type/logo; docs-first layout, density, and navigation.
- [ ] **Server-render head tags** — `main.html` `extrahead` override emitting canonical, `theme-color`, OpenGraph, Twitter (`summary_large_image`), and `robots` meta server-side, reading `config.extra.*` + `page.meta.*`. Mirror the hub's implementation once #29 lands (reuse the same override pattern). ⚠️ MiniJinja — no Python string methods.
- [ ] **JSON-LD** — per-page `Article` (not `TechArticle`) + a repo-level `SoftwareSourceCode`/`SoftwareApplication` node (name, description, `programmingLanguage`, `codeRepository` → this GitHub repo). `Organization` site-wide.
- [ ] **Remove any client-side `seo.js`** if this repo carries a copy; server-side supersedes it.
- [ ] **GEO content-shape pass** on the docs prose (biggest evidence-backed LLM-citation win): definition-first sentences (lead a config option with what it does), self-contained/chunkable `##`/`###` sections (restate the subject, don't rely on "it"/"this"), config/flag/env reference as **tables** not prose, language-tagged code fences (```yaml/```bash), strict one-H1-per-page hierarchy.
- [ ] **robots.txt** — ensure this repo's `docs/robots.txt` allows the current AI UAs (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent`, plus user-action bots). (Note: the hub regenerates per-site `robots.txt` at merge time — keep the source consistent with the hub's policy.)
- [ ] **Align zensical version** — match the fleet's pinned zensical version and Renovate handling as decided in Phase 1 (rknightion/m7kni-net-site#29). Depending on that decision this repo may drop zensical from its own CI entirely (if the hub build is the only consumer) or keep it pinned + Renovate-grouped for local/preview builds — follow the fleet approach from #29, don't invent a per-repo variant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Site is on-brand with the new m7kni.io scheme while reading as a clean, professional product-documentation site.
- [ ] `curl` of a deployed page under m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/ (no JS) shows server-rendered OG/Twitter/canonical/JSON-LD/robots meta.
- [ ] Docs pages follow the GEO content-shape checklist above.
- [ ] zensical version handling matches the fleet decision in #29.
- [ ] Site build green; renders correctly under the hub.

## Notes

- llms.txt / llms-full.txt / sitemaps for this site are generated centrally by the hub's scripts over this repo's Markdown — **not** per-repo work here.
- Do the SEO/LLM + version tasks whenever useful; gate only the visual-redesign task on the hub spec.
title: Docs site: redesign & rebrand alignment + SEO/LLM discoverability

Stale false-positive — already fixed.

This run failed on `open ../../tailscale-api.json: no such file or directory` (the `internal/oas` and `internal/tsapi/contract` spec-reading tests), **not** on anything in `tailscale-client-go`. The OpenAPI spec only existed in a gitignored root `tailscale-api.json`, so CI's clean checkout couldn't find it.

Fixed by 4f5f665 (landed ~6 min after this issue was filed): a tracked `spec/tailscale-api.json` baseline was vendored and the tests repointed at it. Every scheduled `clientlib-main` run since has been green (Jun 15, Jun 22).

The reason this issue stayed open is that the drift lanes upserted a tracking issue on failure but never closed it on a later clean run. Hardened that in the same change: a new `resolve-drift` composite action now auto-closes the lane's tracking issue on the next green run (for `clientlib-main`, only when both `main` and `latest` matrix legs pass), so this won't recur.
